Abl.AutoFilter~.use_when: Live's Auto Filter as a panel: a stereo filter with circuit models plus its own LFO, envelope follower and sidechain. Reach for it for moving filter sweeps you would otherwise build from abl.device.autofilter~, an LFO and an envelope follower. Five inlets: MC stereo audio, sidechain audio (MC or MSP), mod A, mod B, messages. Drive it with `Freq 800`, `Res 0.6`, `Type 1` (LP HP BP Notch Morph DJ Comb Resamp Notch+LP Vowel), `Circuit`, `Drive`, `LFOAmount`, `LFORate`, `LFOWave`, `Env 0.5`, `SCExternal 1`, `Mix`; `recall <n>` loads presets such as Envelope+, LFO and Sidechain.

Abl.ChannelEQ~.digest: Stereo semi-parametric 3-band channel EQ incorporating the EQ algorithm from Ableton Live's native Channel EQ device
Abl.ChannelEQ~.use_when: The simplest stereo EQ in the package: Live's Channel EQ with low, sweepable mid and high bands and a highpass switch. Use it to shape a whole stereo track quickly. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Low` / `High` (±15 dB), `Mid` (±12 dB), `MidF` (120–7500 Hz), `HighPass 1`, `Gain` (±12 dB); presets Low, Mid, High, Loudness.

Abl.Chorus~.digest: Stereo chorus effect incorporating the chorus algorithm from Ableton Live's native Chorus-Ensemble device
Abl.Chorus~.use_when: Stereo chorus from Live's Chorus-Ensemble, with a panel and presets (Fast, Slow, Wide, Deep, Sliding). Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Rate` (0.1–15 Hz), `Mod`, `Feed`, `Width`, `Mix` (all 0.–1.), `Invert 1`, `Gain` (dB). For signal-rate control of rate or depth use abl.dsp.chorus~ directly (its inlets 2–4 are rate, mod, feedback).

Abl.Compander~.digest: A compressor/expander incorporating the ALaw compression/expanding compander algorithm from various Ableton Live's native compression devices
Abl.Compander~.use_when: A-law compressor or expander that colours a signal more than a normal compressor; the module runs one mono abl.dsp.compander~ per side. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Mode 0` compress / `Mode 1` expand, `Shape` (0.–1., amount), `Gain` (-70 to 18 dB); presets DefaultComp, MidComp, HighComp, DefaultExp, MidExp, HighExp.

Abl.Compressor~.digest: Stereo compressor incorporating the compressor algorithm from Ableton Live's native Compressor device
Abl.Compressor~.use_when: Live's Compressor as a stereo panel: the quickest good-sounding compressor for a student patch. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Thresh` (-70 to 6 dB), `Ratio` (1–64), `Att`, `Rel`, `Gain` (make-up, dB); presets Default, Punchy, Spongy. The module has no sidechain and hides the compressor's envelope outlet; use abl.device.compressor~ directly (outlet 1 = envelope) when you need either.

Abl.DFM~.digest: A digitally modeled analog lowpass filter
Abl.DFM~.use_when: Digitally modelled analog lowpass filter with drive, one abl.dsp.dfm~ per side. Use it for a warm resonant lowpass on a stereo signal. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Freq` (20–20000 Hz), `Reson`, `Drive` (0.–1.), `Gain` (dB); presets Default, Reson, Drive. Automate `Freq` through mod A/B from Abl.LFO~ or Abl.EnvFollower~ for sweeps.

Abl.DarkHall~.digest: Stereo reverberator incorporating the "dark hall" algorithm from Ableton Live's native Hybrid Reverb
Abl.DarkHall~.use_when: Dark, long hall reverb from Live's Hybrid Reverb. Good default when you want a big, soft room. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Decay` (0.1–60 s), `Size`, `Damp`, `Shape`, `Mod`, `Mix` (0.–1.), `Bass` (0.25–4 multiplier) with crossover `XBass` (80–1000 Hz), `Freeze 1`; presets Small, Long, Large, Huge, Dark, Bright, Flat, Warm.

Abl.Delay~.digest: Stereo delay incorporating the delay algorithm from Ableton Live's native Delay device
Abl.Delay~.use_when: Live's Delay as a stereo panel: separate or linked left/right times, feedback, a band-pass filter in the loop, time modulation, ping-pong and freeze. The quick way to a musical delay without building tapin~/tapout~ feedback by hand. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `DelL` / `DelR` (1–5000 ms), `Link 1`, `Feed` (0–0.95), `Filter 1`, `Freq`, `Width`, `MTime`, `MFilt`, `MFreq`, `PingPong 1`, `Freeze 1`, `Smooth` (0 Repitch, 1 Fade, 2 Jump), `Mix`.

Abl.Distortion~.digest: Tight and aggressive guitar pedal distortion incorporating the "distort" algorithm from Ableton Live's native Pedal device
Abl.Distortion~.use_when: Tight, aggressive guitar-pedal distortion from Live's Pedal device (one mono abl.dsp.distortion~ per side). Pick it over Abl.Overdrive~ (smoother) or Abl.Fuzz~ (heavier). Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Gain` (drive, 0.–1.), `Bass` / `Mid` / `Treble` (-1.–1.), `MidRange` (0 low, 1 mid, 2 high), `Sub 1`, `Mix`; presets More, Sharp, Heavy.

Abl.Doubler~.digest: Stereo doubler incorporating the algorithms from Ableton Live's native Phaser-Flanger device
Abl.Doubler~.use_when: Short stereo doubling delay (20–150 ms) from Live's Phaser-Flanger, to thicken a voice or instrument. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Time`, `LFOFreq`, `LFOMod`, `LFOWaveform`, `LFOSpin`, `EnvOnOff 1` with `EnvAmount` / `EnvAttack` / `EnvRelease`, `Warmth`, `BassFreq`, `Mix`; `View` switches the panel page. Presets Presence, Envelope, Wobbling, Unstable.

Abl.DrumBuss~.use_when: Live's Drum Buss: drive, crunch, compression, transient shaping and a tuned low 'boom' for a drum group. Use on a stereo drum mix; its 19 presets copy Live's. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Drive`, `Crunch`, `Dist` (0 Soft, 1 Medium, 2 Hard), `Comp 1`, `Trans` (-1.–1.), `Boom`, `Freq` (30–90 Hz), `Decay`, `Solo 1` (hear the boom only), `Damp` (Hz), `Trim`, `Gain`, `Mix`.

Abl.Echo~.digest: Modulation delay effect that lets you set the delay time on two independent delay lines, while giving you control over envelope and filter modulation - incorporating the algorithm from Ableton Live's native Echo device.
Abl.Echo~.use_when: Live's Echo: a character delay with two delay lines, noise and wobble, reverb, ducking, gate and modulation. Choose it over Abl.Delay~ for lo-fi or evolving echoes. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages include `DelL` / `DelR` (1–2500 ms), `Link`, `Feed` (0–1.5), `Channel` (0 Stereo, 1 Pingpong, 2 Mid/side), `Reverb`, `NAmt` / `WAmt` (noise, wobble), `Ducking 1`, `Gate 1`, `MFreq`, `MWave`, `Input`, `Output`, `Mix`; `View` flips its 4 pages.

Abl.Ensemble~.digest: Stereo ensemble effect incorporating the chorus/vibrato algorithm from Ableton Live's native Chorus-Ensemble device
Abl.Ensemble~.use_when: Lush three-voice stereo ensemble chorus from Live's Chorus-Ensemble; richer than Abl.Chorus~. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Rate` (0.1–15 Hz), `Mod`, `Feed`, `Width`, `Warm`, `Shape`, `Mix` (0.–1.), `Invert 1`, `Gain`; presets Fast, Slow, Wide, Deep, Warm, Whistling.

Abl.EnvFollower~.digest: Stereo envelope follower and shaper incorporating algorithms from various Ableton Live's native devices such as Auto Filter
Abl.EnvFollower~.use_when: Turns the loudness of a stereo input into two 0.–1. control signals, for making one module react to another sound. 4 inlets (MC audio, mod A, mod B, messages) and 5 outlets: left envelope, right envelope, mod A, mod B, reports. Wire an envelope outlet into another module's mod inlet and pick the target parameter in that module's menu. Messages: `Rise`, `Fall` (smoothing), `Gain` (-30 to 30 dB), `Shape` (-1.–1. curve), `Min` / `Max`; presets Reactive, Smooth, Invert.

Abl.Fade~.digest: A small utility for panning of 2 stereo signals
Abl.Fade~.use_when: Crossfades two stereo inputs and pans the result between two stereo outputs, with ramps. Use it for A/B source switching or dry/wet routing between module chains. 5 inlets (MC stereo in 1, MC stereo in 2, mod A, mod B, messages) and 5 outlets (MC out 1, MC out 2, mod A, mod B, reports). Messages: `InBal` / `OutBal` (-50 to 50); presets name the routes, e.g. 'A > B', 'AB > AB'.

Abl.Filther~.digest: A filter that has two distortion stages. The first is a hard diode clipper on the input, and the second is a soft saturation on the output to add harmonics to the filtered resonant output.
Abl.Filther~.use_when: Resonant lowpass with a hard diode clipper before it and soft saturation after, one abl.dsp.filther~ per side. Use it when a filter should also get dirty. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Freq` (20–20000 Hz), `Reson`, `Drive` (0.–1.), `Gain` (dB); presets Default, Reson, Drive.

Abl.Flanger~.digest: Stereo flanger incorporating the flanging algorithm from Ableton Live's native Phaser-Flanger device
Abl.Flanger~.use_when: Stereo flanger from Live's Phaser-Flanger, with two LFOs and an envelope. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Time` (0.1–20 ms), `LFOFreq`, `LFOMod`, `LFOFeedback`, `LFOWaveform`, `LFOSpin`, `LFO2` / `LFO2Freq`, `EnvOnOff 1` with `EnvAmount`, `Warmth`, `Mix`; `View` switches pages. Presets More, Fast, Stereo, Random, S&H, LFO 2, Envelope, Percussive.

Abl.Fuzz~.digest: Heavy and broken guitar pedal distortion incorporating the fuzz algorithm from Ableton Live's native Pedal device
Abl.Fuzz~.use_when: Heavy, broken fuzz-pedal distortion from Live's Pedal device (one abl.dsp.fuzz~ per side); the most extreme of the three pedal modules. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Same messages as Abl.Distortion~: `Gain`, `Bass` / `Mid` / `Treble`, `MidRange`, `Sub`, `Mix`; presets More, Sharp, Heavy.

Abl.Input~.digest: Stereo soundfile player & live audio stereo input
Abl.Input~.use_when: The start of an ABL chain: plays sound files (drag files onto its mc.playlist~) or brings in a live stereo input pair, with gain and a DSP button. 3 inlets (MC audio thru, one mod input, messages) and 3 outlets (MC stereo, mod out, reports); the audio at inlet 0 is passed on only while the module is inactive. Messages: `Play 1` / `Play 0`, `Source 0` file / `Source 1` input, `Adc <n>` (1 = inputs 1/2, 2 = 3/4 …), `Gain` (-70 to 18 dB), `Active`.

Abl.LFO~.digest: Stereo low frequency oscillator incorporating an algorithm from various Ableton Live's native devices such as Auto Filter or Shifter
Abl.LFO~.use_when: Stereo LFO whose two outlets make 0.–1. control signals for other modules' mod inlets. 3 inlets (mod A, mod B, messages) and 5 outlets (left LFO, right LFO, mod A, mod B, reports). Messages: `Freq` (0–100 Hz), `Waveform` (0 Sine … 9 Random S&H), `Duty`, `Phase`, `Offset` (0–360), `Spin` with `SpinOnOff`, `Min` / `Max` output range. For audio-rate LFOs patch abl.dsp.stereolfo~ directly.

Abl.Limiter~.digest: A mastering-quality dynamic range processor that ensures that the output does not exceed a specified level, incorporating the limiting algorithm from Ableton Live's native Limiter device
Abl.Limiter~.use_when: Live's mastering Limiter as a stereo panel; put it last in a chain to stop clipping. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Ceil` (-24 to 0 dB), `Gain` (±24 dB), `Rel`, `AutoRelease 1`, `Lookahead` (0 = 1.5 ms, 1 = 3 ms, 2 = 6 ms); presets More, Sharp, Pump. Abl.Output~ already contains an optional limiter (`Limiter 1`).

Abl.Matrix~.digest: A small utility for routing and mixing 4 stereo signals
Abl.Matrix~.use_when: A 4×4 router and mixer for stereo signals: any of four MC stereo inputs to any of four outputs, 10 ms ramps. 5 inlets (4 MC stereo ins, messages) and 5 outlets (4 MC stereo outs, reports). Click cells in its matrixctrl; `Mode 1` lets you drag a cell to set that connection's gain. Presets In1 > All, All > Out1, Diagonal, Gains, Empty; `recall <n>` from a message.

Abl.MeldFilter~.digest: wraps all filters used in Live's Meld synthesizer
Abl.MeldFilter~.use_when: Every filter from Live's Meld synth in one module: combs, crunchy lowpass, Filther, membrane and plate resonators, EQ peak/notch, phaser, redux, SVF 12/24 dB, switched-resonance LP, vowel. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Filter <0–13>` chooses the type, `Freq` (20–20000 Hz), `Macro1` / `Macro2` (0.–1., meaning changes with type). The preset menu lists the 14 types.

Abl.Mix~.digest: A small mixing utility that makes minimal use of the abl.device.utility~ object
Abl.Mix~.use_when: Minimal stereo channel control: gain, pan and on/off, built on abl.device.utility~. Use one per source before summing. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Gain` (-70 to 6 dB), `Pan` (-50 to 50), `Enable 0` to mute; presets PanL, PanR, Mute. For width, mono, phase or DC use Abl.Utility~.

Abl.ModScaler~.digest: Mono modulation signal scaler incorporating a signal shaping algorithm from various Ableton Live's native devices
Abl.ModScaler~.use_when: Reshapes a 0.–1. modulation signal before it reaches a mod inlet: gain, curve, smoothing and output range. In 0 is a mono modulation signal and out 0 the scaled 0.–1. signal; the other ports follow the standard layout (mod A/B, messages, reports). Messages: `Gain` (0–10), `Shape` (-1.–1., exponential to logarithmic), `Rise` / `Fall` (smoothing), `Min` / `Max`. Typical use: Abl.EnvFollower~ → Abl.ModScaler~ → a delay's mod inlet.

Abl.ModalReson~.digest: A stereo resonator using a modal filter bank
Abl.ModalReson~.use_when: Tuned modal resonator (plate or membrane) that makes any input ring at a pitch. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `FreqL` / `FreqR` (20–20000 Hz) with `Link 1`, `Type 0` plate / `Type 1` membrane, `Decay`, `Damp`, `Ratio` (0.–1.); presets Stereo, Bright Plate, Damped Plate, Bright Membrane, Damped Membrane.

Abl.Output~.use_when: The end of an ABL chain: sends MC stereo to a chosen output pair with gain, meters, a scope, an optional safety limiter and a DSP button. 3 inlets (MC stereo, one mod input, messages) and 3 outlets; outlet 0 passes the input through before the gain stage, so you can chain a recorder or a second output. Messages: `Dac <n>` (1 = outputs 1/2, 2 = 3/4 …), `Gain` (-70 to 18 dB), `Limiter 1`, `Active`.

Abl.Overdrive~.digest: Warm and smooth guitar pedal distortion incorporating the OD algorithm from Ableton Live's native Pedal device
Abl.Overdrive~.use_when: Warm, smooth overdrive-pedal distortion from Live's Pedal device; the gentlest of the three pedal modules. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Gain` (drive, 0.–1.), `Bass` / `Mid` / `Treble` (-1.–1.), `MidRange` (0–2), `Sub 1`, `Mix`; presets More, Sharp, Heavy.

Abl.Phaser~.digest: Stereo phaser incorporating the phasing algorithm from Ableton Live's native Phaser-Flanger device
Abl.Phaser~.use_when: Stereo phaser from Live's Phaser-Flanger, from gentle to 42-notch sweeps. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `PhaserNotches` (1–42), `PhaserCenter` (70–18500 Hz), `PhaserSpread`, `PhaserBlend`, `LFOFreq`, `LFOMod`, `LFOFeedback`, `LFOWaveform`, `LFOSpin`, `EnvOnOff 1` with `EnvAmount`, `Warmth`, `Mix`; `View` switches pages. Presets Soft, Wide, Fast, Deep, Alea, Envelope, LFO2, S&H, Perc.

Abl.PitchShifter~.digest: Stereo pitch shifter incorporating the pitch shifting algorithm from Ableton Live's native Shifter device
Abl.PitchShifter~.use_when: Stereo real-time pitch shifter from Live's Shifter device, for octave or fifth doubling and detune. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Coarse` (-24 to 24 semitones), `Fine` (-100 to 100 cents), `Win` (10–350 ms grain window; longer suits low sounds), `Wide 1`, `Mix`; presets OctDown, OctUp, FivthDown, FivthUp, Detune.

Abl.Pitch~.digest: Estimates the pitch/frequency of a given input signal
Abl.Pitch~.use_when: Tracks the pitch of a monophonic input and outputs it as a MIDI note number. 2 inlets (MC audio, messages) and 3 outlets: audio passed through, pitch as a float MIDI number, reports. Output only happens when the estimator's confidence is above a threshold and the pitch changes, so it can drive notes directly; examples/Abl.Special.maxpat sends it through an integer number box into `makenote 127 100` → `noteout`. For a signal-rate frequency and confidence, use abl.dsp.pitchestimator~ directly.

Abl.PlateReverb~.digest: Stereo plate reverb incorporating the reverb algorithm from Ableton Live's native Reverb device
Abl.PlateReverb~.use_when: Live's classic Reverb algorithm as a plate. The input is summed to mono, then spread to pseudo-stereo, so it adds space but keeps no stereo image. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Decay` (0.–1.), `DampF` (20–20000 Hz), `PreDel` (0–10), `Mix`; presets Short, Long, Large, Huge, Bright, Dark.

Abl.PrismReverb~.digest: Stereo reverberator incorporating the "prism" algorithm from Ableton Live's native Hybrid Reverb
Abl.PrismReverb~.use_when: Bright, spectral-sounding reverb ('Prism') from Live's Hybrid Reverb, with separate low and high decay multipliers. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Decay` (0.1–60 s), `Size`, `Low` / `High` (0.1–5 multipliers) around `Xover` (400–5500 Hz), `Freeze 1`, `Mix`; presets include Gated.

Abl.QuartzReverb~.digest: Stereo reverberator incorporating the "quartz" algorithm from Ableton Live's native Hybrid Reverb
Abl.QuartzReverb~.use_when: Clear, dense 'Quartz' reverb from Live's Hybrid Reverb, with distance and diffusion controls. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Decay` (0.1–60 s), `Size`, `Dist`, `Diff`, `Mod`, `HDamp` / `LDamp`, `Freeze 1`, `Mix`; presets include Mod and Delay.

Abl.Redux~.digest: Downsampling and bit-reduction effect incorporating the algorithm from Ableton Live's native Redux device
Abl.Redux~.use_when: Live's Redux: sample-rate reduction and bit crushing with jitter and optional filters, for lo-fi and aliasing sounds. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Rate` (40–40000 Hz), `Bits` (1–16), `Jitter`, `Shape`, `PreFilter 1`, `PostFilter 1` with `Octave`, `DCShift 1`, `Quality` (0 Eco, 1 High), `Mix`; presets Degraded, Atari, AM, CB, Damaged.

Abl.Remote~.digest: A small utility that sends or receives signals without patch cords
Abl.Remote~.use_when: Sends or receives a stereo signal by name, with gain and pan: the cordless send/return of an ABL rack. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Mode 0` send / `Mode 1` receive, `Target <name>` (default Signal1), `Gain` (dB), `Pan` (-50 to 50); presets 'Signal1>' … (send) and '>Signal1' … (receive). The bus name is global, so any Remote~ in any patch with the same Target shares it.

Abl.RingMod~.digest: Stereo ring modulator incorporating the ring modulator algorithm from Ableton Live's native Shifter device
Abl.RingMod~.use_when: Stereo ring modulator from Live's Shifter device, from tremolo (low frequency) to metallic clangs. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Freq` (1–10000 Hz), `DriveOnOff 1` with `Drive` (0–24), `Gain` (dB), `Mix`; presets High, Low, Drive, Tremolo.

Abl.Saturator~.digest: Waveshaping saturation incorporating the waveshaping algorithm from Ableton Live's native Saturator device
Abl.Saturator~.use_when: Live's Saturator: waveshaping warmth or clipping with oversampling and DC blocking. A safer everyday colour than the pedal modules. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Drive` (-36 to 36 dB), `Curve` (0 Analog Clip, 1 Soft Sine, 2 Medium Curve, 3 Hard Curve, 4 Sinoid Fold, 5 Digital Clip), `PostClip 1`, `Oversampling 1`, `DCBlock 1`, `Gain`, `Mix`.

Abl.ShimmerReverb~.digest: Stereo reverberator incorporating the "shimmer" algorithm from Ableton Live's native Hybrid Reverb
Abl.ShimmerReverb~.use_when: Hybrid Reverb's 'Shimmer': a reverb whose tail is pitch-shifted, for ambient pads. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Pitch` (-12 to 12 semitones, default 12), `Shimm` (amount), `Decay` (0.1–60 s), `Size`, `Diff`, `Damp`, `Mod`, `Freeze 1`, `Mix`; presets Long, Far, Down, Octaver, Inharm, Delay, Falling, Rising.

Abl.SpectralReson~.digest: Spectral processor which uses spectral resonances and pitched overtones to add tonal character to any audio source
Abl.SpectralReson~.use_when: Live's Spectral Resonator: adds pitched harmonic resonance to any sound, like tuning noise or drums to a note. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Pitch` (default 38), `Harms` (1–256), `Decay` (1–20000), `Stretch`, `Shift` (±48), `Voices` (1–8 menu) with `Unison`, `PitchMod`, `ModRate`, `Hdamp` / `Ldamp`, `Gain`, `Mix`; `View` flips pages. 23 presets such as HighBells, SlidingBells.

Abl.SpectralTime~.digest: Stereo spectral freeze and delay effect incorporating the algorithm from Ableton Live's native Spectral Time device
Abl.SpectralTime~.use_when: Live's Spectral Time: spectral freeze plus a frequency-shifting spectral delay. Use it for frozen chords, shimmering echoes and glassy textures. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages include `Freeze 1`, `Resol` (0 Low … 3 Ultra), `Order` (0 freeze→delay, 1 delay→freeze), `DTime` (10–3000 ms), `Feed`, `Shift` (±400), `Tilt`, `Spray`, `Mask`, `DMix`, `Mix`, `Gain`; `View` flips pages.

Abl.Switch~.digest: A small utility for fast routing of 2 stereo signals
Abl.Switch~.use_when: Routes either of two stereo inputs to either of two stereo outputs, with 10 ms ramps; a lighter Abl.Fade~ for hard switching. 3 inlets (MC stereo in 1, MC stereo in 2, messages) and 3 outlets (MC out 1, MC out 2, reports). Its only named parameters are `View` and `Active`, so the routing is set on the panel.

Abl.TidesReverb~.digest: Stereo reverberator incorporating the "tides" algorithm from Ableton Live's native Hybrid Reverb
Abl.TidesReverb~.use_when: Hybrid Reverb's 'Tides': a reverb whose tail is swept by a built-in modulator, for moving, wave-like space. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Decay` (0.1–60 s), `Size`, `Damp`, `Tide` (depth), `Rate` (0–100), `Phase` (0–180), `Wave` (shape), `Freeze 1`, `Mix`; presets Tight, Large, Waving, Stereo, Articule, Tremble, Halo.

Abl.Transient~.digest: Transient designer incorporating the "transient" algorithm from Ableton Live's native Drum Buss device
Abl.Transient~.use_when: One-knob transient designer from Live's Drum Buss: makes hits snappier or softer. Runs one abl.dsp.transientdesign~ per side. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Shape` (-1.–1.; one value sets both attack and sustain), `Gain` (-70 to 18 dB); presets Picky, Spongy.

Abl.Utility~.digest: A small swiss army knife for audio incorporating the algorithms from Ableton Live's native Utility device. This device can be used to change the gain, separate a single channel from a stereo signal, widen or narrow the stereo image or suppress DC offsets.
Abl.Utility~.use_when: Live's Utility for stereo housekeeping: gain, balance, mono, mid/side width, channel select or swap, phase invert, DC block and bass-mono. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Gain` (dB), `Bal` (-50 to 50), `Mono 1`, `MS 1` with `M/S` (-1.–1.), `Chans` (0 Left, 1 Stereo, 2 Right, 3 Swap), `InvertLeftPhase 1`, `InvertRightPhase 1`, `DC 1`, `BassMono 1` with `Freq` (50–500 Hz), `Mute 1`.

Abl.Vibrato~.digest: Stereo vibrato effect incorporating the vibrato algorithm from Ableton Live's native Chorus-Ensemble device
Abl.Vibrato~.use_when: Stereo pitch vibrato from Live's Chorus-Ensemble. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Rate` (0.1–15 Hz), `Mod` (depth), `Shape`, `Offset`, `Gain` (dB); presets Triangle, Wide, Fast, Slow, Detune, Beyond.

Abl.Vowel~.digest: A bank of five bandpass filters with frequencies and gains that correspond to the vowels AEIOU
Abl.Vowel~.use_when: Five-band formant filter that makes a sound say A-E-I-O-U; one abl.dsp.vowel~ per side. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Morph` (0.–1. across the vowels), `Freq` (20–20000 Hz, base pitch), `Reson`; presets E, I, O, U. Sweep `Morph` from Abl.LFO~ for talking effects.

Abl.Waveshaper~.digest: Waveshaping distortion incorporating a waveshaping algorithm from various Ableton Live's native distortion devices
Abl.Waveshaper~.use_when: Flexible waveshaping distortion with control of the transfer curve (curve, depth, linearity, period, damping), for designed rather than pedal-style dirt. Standard ABL ports: in 0 MC stereo audio (a mono MSP cord is doubled), in 1–2 mod A/B (0.–1.), in 3 messages; out 0 MC stereo, out 1–2 mod A/B, out 3 parameter reports. Messages: `Drive` (-36 to 36 dB), `SDrive`, `Curve`, `Depth`, `Linear`, `Period`, `Damp` (0.–1.), `PostClip 1`, `Oversampling 1`, `DCBlock 1`, `Gain`, `Mix`; presets Light, Heavy, Tight, NoisySynth, HardSynth, Destroyed, Noise.

flipflop~.digest: A Period-by-Period Synthesis oscillator that alternately receives the frequencies and the other parameters from two groups
flipflop~.use_when: A Period-by-Period Synthesis oscillator that alternately receives the frequencies and the other parameters from two groups.

jeyhisto.digest: Derives histograms (probability-distribution plots) from incoming numbers by means of Binning and Razoring
jeyhisto.use_when: Derives histograms (probability-distribution plots) from incoming numbers by means of Binning and Razoring.

jeyhistosliders.digest: A dimensions-responsive bpatcher-abstraction enclosing the jeyhisto, multislider, and other objects
jeyhistosliders.use_when: A dimensions-responsive bpatcher-abstraction enclosing the jeyhisto, multislider, and other objects.

jeyhistosliders~.digest: A dimensions-responsive bpatcher-abstraction enclosing the jeyhisto~, multislider, and other objects
jeyhistosliders~.use_when: A dimensions-responsive bpatcher-abstraction enclosing the jeyhisto~, multislider, and other objects.

jeyhisto~.digest: Derives histograms (probability-distribution plots) from incoming samples by means of Binning and Razoring
jeyhisto~.use_when: Derives histograms (probability-distribution plots) from incoming samples by means of Binning and Razoring.

jeynoisesliders~.digest: A dimensions-responsive bpatcher-abstraction enclosing the jeynoise~, multislider, and other objects
jeynoisesliders~.use_when: A dimensions-responsive bpatcher-abstraction enclosing the jeynoise~, multislider, and other objects.

jeynoise~.digest: A sine and cosine wave oscillator that works based on Period-by-Period Synthesis technique
jeynoise~.use_when: A sine and cosine wave oscillator that works based on Period-by-Period Synthesis technique.

jeyrand.digest: Redistributes numbers as specified by a user-defined list-style-Probability-Distribution-Function (PDF-list)
jeyrand.use_when: Redistributes numbers as specified by a user-defined list-style-Probability-Distribution-Function (PDF-list).

jeyrandsliders.digest: A dimensions-responsive bpatcher-abstraction enclosing the jeyrand, multislider, and other objects
jeyrandsliders.use_when: A dimensions-responsive bpatcher-abstraction enclosing the jeyrand, multislider, and other objects.

jeyrandsliders~.digest: A dimensions-responsive bpatcher-abstraction enclosing the jeyrand~, multislider, and other objects
jeyrandsliders~.use_when: A dimensions-responsive bpatcher-abstraction enclosing the jeyrand~, multislider, and other objects.

jeyrand~.digest: Redistributes samples as specified by a user-defined list-style-Probability-Distribution-Function (PDF-list)
jeyrand~.use_when: Redistributes samples as specified by a user-defined list-style-Probability-Distribution-Function (PDF-list).

aoo.client.use_when: AOO (Audio over OSC) peer client. It streams no audio itself and needs an `aoo.server`. `connect <host> <port>` connects to the server (outputs 1/0), `group_join <group> <group_pwd> <user> <user_pwd>` joins a group (the help uses `_` for unused passwords), `group_leave`, `disconnect`, `peer_list`. Once joined, `aoo.send~` / `aoo.receive~` created with the same port can address peers as `<group> <user> <id>` instead of `<host> <port> <id>`. Clients can also exchange messages, even across home routers: `send`, `broadcast`, `send_group`, `send_peer`, `target`. Argument is the port.

aoo.receive~.digest: Receive an AOO stream from an
aoo.receive~.use_when: AOO (Audio over OSC) sink: receives network audio from `aoo.send~` (or Pd/SuperCollider AOO). Arguments: channels, port, id. Without `@multichannel` it has one signal outlet per channel plus a message outlet; `@multichannel 1` gives one MC outlet. A source reaches it when the sender sends `add <host> <port> <id>` for it, or when it sends `invite <host> <port> <id>` (`uninvite` stops). `latency <ms>` (5-20 ms on a LAN) trades delay for fewer dropouts; `buffersize`, `resend`, `reset`, `source_list`, `dynamic_resampling`.

aoo.send~.digest: Send an AOO stream to an
aoo.send~.use_when: AOO (Audio over OSC) source: streams audio to `aoo.receive~` objects on other machines or apps. Arguments: channels, port, id. Without `@multichannel` it has one signal inlet per channel; `@multichannel 1` takes one MC inlet. Add a receiver with `add <host> <port> <id>` (or `<group> <user> <id>` via `aoo.client`), then send `start`; `stop` and `remove` end it. `format pcm|opus` (opus compresses for slow links), `buffersize`, `resend`, `redundancy`, `sink_channel`, `auto_invite`.

aoo.server.use_when: AOO (Audio over OSC) server that lets `aoo.client` objects find each other by group and user name. Argument is the port; clients `connect <host> <port>` to it. For internet use it must be publicly reachable. `relay 1` forwards data for peers that cannot connect directly. Not needed for plain `aoo.send~` → `aoo.receive~` streaming by host and port.

AudioEQ.use_when: Three-band 'double-shelving' EQ block for an AudioMix channel strip: two cross~ crossovers per channel split low, mid and high bands with separate gains. Ports: in 0 audio L, in 1 audio R, in 2 messages; out 0 L, out 1 R, out 2 dumpout. Messages: `lofreq` / `hifreq` (50–10000 Hz), `lo` / `mid` / `hi` (±24 dB), `active 0/1` (10 ms bypass crossfade). Name it (name field or arg 1) to control it remotely as `<name>-eq`, e.g. `; MyEQ-eq lo -12`.

AudioInput.digest: A stereo/dual mono audio input chooser.
AudioInput.use_when: Input block: adds a stereo or dual-mono hardware input to whatever audio arrives at its inlets. Ports: in 0 audio L, in 1 audio R, in 2 messages; out 0 L, out 1 R, out 2 dumpout. Pick the input in its live.menu, or send `input <n>` (index into '...', '1/2', '3/4' … then single channels). The first box argument becomes a receive name for remote messages. Input comes from the device chosen in Max's Audio Status.

AudioM4LEffect.digest: A container for Max For Live devices.
AudioM4LEffect.use_when: Container that hosts a Max for Live audio effect inside an AudioMix chain (default device SimpleGain). Ports: in 0 audio L, in 1 audio R, in 2 messages; out 0 L, out 1 R, out 2 dumpout. Drop a device onto it, click E to open its editor, D to unload it. Messages: `active 0/1` (10 ms crossfade bypass, also turns device processing off), `edit`, `delete`, `qlist`. Name it to send device parameters remotely, e.g. `; MyDevice Gain -6.`; the device's own parameter names are used.

AudioMix.digest: A simple stereo audio mixing module.
AudioMix.use_when: Channel-strip fader block: live.gain~ level with meter, constant-power pan, solo and on/off. Ports: in 0 audio L, in 1 audio R, in 2 messages; out 0 L, out 1 R, out 2 dumpout. Messages: `gain` (-70 to 24 dB), `pan` (-50 to 50), `solo 0/1`, `active 0/1`; `getgain`, `getstate`, `getattributes` report from out 2. `@type <symbol>` groups solo (default generic). Name it to control it as `<name>-mix` (e.g. `; MyTrack1-mix gain -12`); `; AudioMix <param> <value>` reaches every AudioMix at once.

AudioOutput.digest: A stereo/dual mono audio output chooser.
AudioOutput.use_when: Output block: sends its stereo input to a chosen hardware output pair (or one channel as dual mono) and passes the audio on. Ports: in 0 audio L, in 1 audio R, in 2 messages; out 0 L, out 1 R, out 2 dumpout. Pick the output in its live.menu or send `output <n>`. The first box argument becomes a receive name. Use it at the bottom of a strip; chain AudioRecord under it if needed.

AudioPlayer.use_when: Simple stereo sound-file player block: drop an AIFF/WAVE file or a folder, pick from its menu, play, loop. Adds the file's sound to the audio at its inlets. Ports: in 0 audio L, in 1 audio R, in 2 messages; out 0 L, out 1 R, out 2 dumpout. Messages: `play 0/1`, `loop 0/1`, `soundfile <index>` (menu). Built on sfplay~ 2; for many formats, clip editing and several channels use playlist~ instead.

AudioReceive.use_when: Receives a stereo bus (A–Z) sent by AudioSend and adds it to the audio at its inlets: the return of an aux send. Ports: in 0 audio L, in 1 audio R, in 2 messages; out 0 L, out 1 R, out 2 dumpout. Messages: `bus <n>` (0 none, 1 = A …), `gain` (dB), `active 0/1`. The bus is the global receive~ pair `AudioMix-<letter>-L~` / `-R~`.

AudioReceive2.use_when: Like AudioReceive but the bus is a name you type instead of a letter, so returns can be called 'Reverb' or 'Drums'. Ports: in 0 audio L, in 1 audio R, in 2 messages; out 0 L, out 1 R, out 2 dumpout. Messages: `gain`, `active 0/1`; the name field sets the bus (`AudioMix-<name>-L~` / `-R~`), matching an AudioSend2 with the same name.

AudioRecord.digest: Record a stereo soundfile in 24bit WAVE format.
AudioRecord.use_when: Records its stereo input to a 24-bit WAVE file and passes the audio on. Ports: in 0 audio L, in 1 audio R, in 2 messages; out 0 L, out 1 R, out 2 dumpout. Click File to choose a new file in a save dialog, then `rec 1` / `rec 0` to start and stop; `gain` (dB) sets the recording level. Built on sfrecord~ 2 with samptype int24; shows elapsed time.

AudioSend.use_when: Aux send block: copies its stereo input to a named bus A–Z at a set level, and passes the input on unchanged. Ports: in 0 audio L, in 1 audio R, in 2 messages; out 0 L, out 1 R, out 2 dumpout. Messages: `bus <n>` (0 none, 1 = A …), `gain` (dB), `active 0/1`. Box attributes set startup values: `AudioSend MySend @bus 3 @gain -3`. Pair with AudioReceive on the same letter.

AudioSend2.use_when: Like AudioSend but the bus is a typed name instead of a letter. Ports: in 0 audio L, in 1 audio R, in 2 messages; out 0 L, out 1 R, out 2 dumpout. Messages: `gain`, `active 0/1`; the name field sets the bus, matching an AudioReceive2 with the same name.

AudioVSTEffect.use_when: Container that hosts a VST, VST3 or Audio Unit effect inside an AudioMix chain, using vst~ 2 (stereo). Ports: in 0 audio L, in 1 audio R, in 2 messages; out 0 L, out 1 R, out 2 dumpout. Drop a plug-in onto it, click E for its editor, D to unload. Messages: `active 0/1` (10 ms crossfade; sends `disable` to the plug-in when off), `edit`, `delete`, `qlist`. Name it to set plug-in parameters remotely by their own names, e.g. `; MyPlugin "Dry/Wet Mix" 0.5`.

AudioXfaderIn.use_when: Constant-power crossfade from two stereo sources (A, B) into one stereo output, DJ-style. 5 inlets (A-L, A-R, B-L, B-R, messages) and 3 outlets (L, R, dumpout). Messages: `fade` (-50 = all A, 50 = all B); the A and B buttons jump to either end.

AudioXfaderOut.use_when: Constant-power crossfade of one stereo source between two stereo destinations (A, B), for example two effect chains. 3 inlets (L, R, messages) and 5 outlets (A-L, A-R, B-L, B-R, dumpout). Messages: `fade` (-50 = all to A, 50 = all to B); the A and B buttons jump to either end.

az.granulate~.use_when: Auzzie granular synthesis from a sample buffer — cloud-style granulator. Use for audio file granulation; reach for grainflow for explicit per-grain scheduling, or mubu.granular~ for descriptor-driven selection.

az.spectdelay~.use_when: Spectral delay processor — independent delay per FFT bin. Use for harmonic-tail / impulse-response-like effects you can't get from time-domain delay.

az.specteq~.use_when: Spectral EQ — frequency-domain shaping with arbitrary curve. Use when the response curve is too detailed for biquad/parametric chains.

az.strum~.use_when: Karplus-Strong plucked string, mono and one note at a time. One inlet for messages: a float plays a note at that frequency (Hz); a list of frequency, decay (ms) and optional squish plays with those values; bang replays with current settings. Messages decay, freq, glide (ms, for frequency changes during a note), squish (plectrum rigidity, int >= 0), nyqdecay (decay multiplier at Nyquist). Updated version of the old jg.strum~ external; ships with Auzzie.

butter_keys.digest: A kslider that can also mark, tint, slide and report
butter_keys.use_when: Drop-in replacement for `kslider` when the keyboard must also show or collect more than notes: type `butter_keys` in an object box (Max 9; the package maps it to `v8ui @filename butter_keys.js @border 0`), and every kslider message, attribute and outlet keeps its meaning (a number plays a note, `set`, `chord`, `clear`, `flush`, `bang`; `@mode` with an extra `z_mono` option, `@range`, `@inputmode`; right inlet = next velocity), except that `@offset` is the exact lowest note (default 1, with 48 keys). Additions: `@z_displaymode 1` turns each key into a vertical slider driven by multislider messages (`list`, `select <slider> <value>`, `fetch`, `setminmax`, `z_dump`, `z_setall`, plus `setval <note> <value>`), with values on outlet 3; `@z_mode` 1 or 2 lays the notes out as pads or numbered buttons (`@z_rows`). `setkeys <set> <notes...>` with `keycolor <set> r g b a` tints keys, and `setdots <set> <notes...>` with `dotcolor` draws marks on them. Outlet 4 reports `click <note> <velocity> <shift> <cmd> <option> <ctrl>` on every click (`@z_clicknotes 0` makes clicks report only); colors are set by message and are not saved as attributes.

2threshattack~.use_when: Two-threshold (Schmitt trigger) attack detector at signal rate. Left inlet: the signal to analyze. Right inlet: a reference level signal that both thresholds are multiplied by (1. leaves them unchanged). Arguments `<low> <high>`; runtime `low <float>` / `high <float>`; `tellmeeverything` posts state. An attack fires when the input goes above high × reference; the next attack is only recognized after the input drops below low × reference. Left outlet: a mostly-zero signal with a 1 at each attack sample. Right outlet: a two-item list at each attack (sample value, level multiplier). Use for onset detection that does not retrigger on the wobble just above one threshold; to measure how loud the attack was, look at the energy around the attack time (help file).

SDIF-buffer.digest: Store an SDIF stream in Max.
SDIF-buffer.use_when: In-memory SDIF stream container. Constructor arg: `<buffer-name>`. Load with `read-stream-number <filename> <stream>`; inspect with `framelist <filename>`, `streamlist <filename>`, `print` / `printall`; modify with `change-frametype <symbol>` / `change-streamID <int>` / `timeshift <seconds>`; `clear` empties; `debug <on/off>` for diagnostics. Use as the substrate for SDIF analysis data (resonance models, spectral envelopes) loaded from disk; pair with sdif-tuples to read and sdif-listpoke to write.

SDIF-fileinfo.digest: Report information about the streams in an SDIF file
SDIF-fileinfo.use_when: Report stream metadata about an SDIF file on disk. Constructor arg: `<buffer-name>`. `scan <filename>` reads metadata, `bang` re-emits, `clear` resets. Use to inspect SDIF files (stream count, frame types, time ranges) before loading them into a buffer.

SDIF-info.use_when: Report metadata about a loaded SDIF stream in an sdif-buffer. Constructor arg: `<buffer-name>`. `set <buffername>` retargets, `bang` queries, `tellmeeverything` dumps state. Use for stream-aware analysis pipelines — confirm the stream's frame type and timing before reading tuples.

SDIF-listpoke.digest: Poke (write) data into an SDIF-buffer with Max lists
SDIF-listpoke.use_when: Write Max-list data into an sdif-buffer. Constructor arg: `<buffer-name>`. `listpoke <values>` writes, `newmatrix` / `matrixtype` / `numcolumns` configure shape, `time <seconds>` sets timestamp, `set` updates buffer reference, `errorreporting <int>` for diagnostics. Use to programmatically construct SDIF data from Max-side lists.

SDIF-ranges.digest: Report ranges of values in an SDIF-buffer
SDIF-ranges.use_when: Report value ranges (min/max per dimension) of data in an sdif-buffer. Constructor arg: `<buffer-name>`. `column-range <col> <matrix-type>` queries one column, `column-ranges <matrix-type>` queries all, `max-columns` reports column count, `set <buffername>` retargets. Use for autoscaling visualisations or normalising SDIF feature streams to a known range.

SDIF-tuples.digest: Pull data out of an SDIF-buffer into Max lists
SDIF-tuples.use_when: Pull data tuples out of an sdif-buffer as Max lists. Constructor arg: `<buffer-name>`. `columns <col1> <col2?> <col3?>` selects which columns to extract, `interp <type>` chooses interpolation between frames, `direction <int>` plays forward/backward, `concatenate <id>` merges streams, `max_rows <n>` caps output, `outputinterval <ms>` paces emission, `reltime <phase>` reads at a relative time, `print` debug-dumps. Use as the read side of an SDIF pipeline — extract per-frame analysis data for control or resynthesis.

accumulate~.digest: Adds the current incoming sample to the previous output.
accumulate~.use_when: Signal accumulator: each input sample is added to the running output. Left inlet: signal to add. Right inlet: on (1) / off (0) signal (the refpage describes resetting by signal rather than by message, unlike +=~). Attributes: `@min` / `@max` bounds, `@start` initial value, `@scale` multiplies the last output (values between 0. and 1. make it leak), `@mode` clip (default, stop at the bound) / wrap (jump to the other bound) / reset (go back to start). Use for random walks, ramps and slow integrators at signal rate; the help file shows bounded and circular random walks.

bench.use_when: Control-rate timing utility used as a pair. Create one `bench in` before the chain you want to time and one `bench out` after it; connect the in object's right outlet (a timestamp) to the out object's right inlet. Any message passes through; when it arrives at `bench out` the elapsed CPU time is reported. `version` posts the version. Use to find which part of a message chain is slow.

bench~.use_when: Signal-rate timing utility used as a pair: `bench~ in` before and `bench~ out` after the part of the DSP chain you want to measure, with the in object's right outlet connected to the out object's right inlet. Outputs a signal giving how long that section takes to compute. Use to compare the CPU cost of alternative DSP chains.

bpf.digest: bpf - break point function editor, CNMAT-style.
bpf.use_when: Breakpoint function editor (UI) that holds several functions in one box. Input a float x to get the y values of all functions out the left outlet. Manage functions with `addfunction <id>`, `setfunction <id>`, `deletefunction <id>`, `clearfunction <id>`, `hidefunction <id>`, `setnumfunctions <n>`; enter points as `list <id> <x> <y>`; `dump` sends `[function point x y aux]` rows out the rightmost outlet; `clearregion <x1> <x2>`, `snap_all_points_to_grid`, `xminmax` / `yminmax` set the view. Attributes include `@step` (stepped display), `@snaptogrid`, `@lockinput`, `@drawposition`, grid and color attributes. Staff mode (`@displaymode 1`), signal input and `setfunctionname` are marked unsupported. Use when one editor must hold several related envelopes; for a single curve the built-in function is simpler.

cambio~.digest: Signal-to-event version of change, for mostly-constant signals
cambio~.use_when: Signal-rate change detector for mostly-constant signals — emits an event only when input value changes. Drive with a signal carrying control values (e.g. snapshot~ output, control bus). Use as a signal-domain equivalent of `change` for slowly-varying control signals carried at audio rate — avoids the cost of converting to event-rate just to detect changes.

cnmatrix~.digest: Signal routing with Jitter matrices as input
cnmatrix~.use_when: Audio matrix routing using a Jit.matrix as the routing pattern. Constructor args: `<inputs> <outputs> <interpolation_mode>`. Drive routing matrix via `jit_matrix <name>` messages. Smooth between matrix configurations with `slide <ms>` or `smooth`; `fast` and `frame` toggle update timing; `list` for direct gain table input. Use to drive a matrix~-style audio router with patterns generated as Jitter matrices — generative or visual routing without per-cell message scripting.

decaying-sinusoids~.use_when: Bank of exponentially decaying sine partials. Model as `freq gain decayrate` triples (the resonators~ / res-transform format), given as arguments or a list. A virtual time index drives the decay: `goto <seconds>` jumps to a time (0 is the start of the decay; negative times grow exponentially and are risky), `rate <scalar>` scales all decay rates, `min_vtime` / `max_vtime` limit the virtual time range, or send a signal to control virtual time directly. A float sets the overall output gain; `clear` removes all partials. Use for bells, plates and plucked tones from a resonance model, re-struck by jumping virtual time back to 0.

deinterleave.digest: "De-interleave" (aka delace) elements in one list into some number of smaller lists.
deinterleave.use_when: Split one interleaved list into multiple smaller lists (delace). Constructor arg: `<index-multiple>` sets stride N (creates N outlets). Send `list` to split; `bang` to re-emit last result. Use to separate stride-N elements from a list — e.g. extract odd/even indices, separate (x, y, z) triples into three streams. Inverse of interleave.

gridpanel.digest: Simple utility for drawing a UI grid.
gridpanel.use_when: UI utility — draws a grid (lines/cells) for visual layout. Configure with `divisions <n>` (uniform), or `xdivisions <n>` / `ydivisions <n>` independently; `linewidth <pixels>` sets stroke; `idlemousing <int>` toggles mouse-tracking on hover. Use to align controls or visualise a grid in custom UIs.

harmonics~.use_when: Bank of harmonic sine oscillators over one fundamental. Arguments: fundamental, then partial amplitudes. A float sets the fundamental; a list is the fundamental followed by amplitudes (`420. 0.1 0.2 0.3`); `first-amplitude <amp>` sets the fundamental's level; `wave <shape> <max-sinusoids>` loads pulse-train, sine, sawtooth, square or triangle; `noisiness <0.–1.>` adds noise to all partials (use sinusoids~ in bwe mode for per-partial noise); `clear` fades out and empties. Use for additive harmonic tones whose partial levels you control directly.

interleave.digest: Interleave (lace) separate list elements into a single list
interleave.use_when: Lace separate list elements into a single interleaved list. Constructor arg: `<number-of-inlets>` sets how many input streams to interleave. Use to combine parallel streams into one stride-N list. Inverse of deinterleave.

lcm.use_when: Least common multiple of integer inputs. Constructor arg: `<list-of-integers>` for static input; runtime `int` / `list` to evaluate; `bang` to re-emit last result; `tellmeeverything` for state dump. Use for rhythmic/cyclic-pattern length calculations — e.g. when do two polyrhythms align (lcm of bar lengths), or how long until a phase pattern repeats.

list-interpolate.use_when: Linear interpolation between two lists, one inlet. The first list received is stored; the second becomes the destination; each later list becomes the new destination. A float 0.–1. outputs the mix between the two; `bang` steps once from first to second, with the step count set by the first argument or `steps <n>`. Second argument: maximum list length. `zeropad 1` lets lists of different lengths work: the last list sets the length and the other is truncated or padded with zeros. Use for morphing between presets or spectra stored as lists.

migrator.digest: Spectral/harmonic transformation, based on David Wessel's "migrate" abstraction
migrator.use_when: Probabilistic migration of a set of frequencies toward a target, after David Wessel's migrate. Arguments: standard deviation (semitones), number of oscillators, base amplitude. `list` of freq/amp pairs sets the target; each `bang` (or `1` for automatic updates every 25 ms, `0` to stop) moves one step; `forcefeed <pairs>` jumps to a new set without migrating; `nOsc_smooth <n>` changes the oscillator count with smooth amplitudes. Attributes: `@fade` (updates to fade oscillators in/out), `@nOsc`, `@oscamp`, `@output` (0 = one concatenated list, 1 = each pair separately). Outlets per help: pairs for an oscillator bank, last changed frequency, index of the partial being updated, bang when the list wraps. Use to feed sinusoids~ or oscillators~ with gradually drifting harmonies, or to pick weighted random pitches from a timbre.

opensoundcontrol.digest: Translate between Max data and buffers in CNMAT's "OpenSoundControl" ("OSC") network protocol.
opensoundcontrol.use_when: Legacy CNMAT converter between Max messages and OSC packets (`FullPacket` messages); box text in the help file is `OpenSoundControl`. Argument: buffer size in bytes (default 1024). Build bundles with `openbundle` / `closebundle` (or `[` / `]`), set the time with `OSCTimeTag`; incoming packets are parsed to Max messages; `errorreporting`, `printcontents`, `debug` for diagnostics. **Deprecated** per its refpage in favour of the odot package. For new work: udpreceive and udpsend already decode and encode OSC; for bundles use odot's o.route / o.select to dispatch, o.expr.codebox for expressions, o.compose to write bundles as text, o.display to view them. odot's o.expr and o.message are themselves in odot's deprecated folder.

osc-route.digest: Dispatch OSC messages according to an address hierarchy stripping off the portion of the address that matched
osc-route.use_when: Dispatch OSC messages by address hierarchy, stripping matched prefix. **DEPRECATED** — use odot's o.route which handles full OSC bundles with types and timetags. Legacy: constructor args list addresses, runtime `set <outlet> <address>` reconfigures; `allmessages` enumerates patterns. For simple cases the native `route` works on plain symbols; for full OSC use odot.

osc-schedule.digest: Schedule delivery of an OSC packet/bundle at a future time using an encoded timestamp
osc-schedule.use_when: Schedule OSC packet/bundle delivery at a future time via OSC timetag. **DEPRECATED** — use odot's o.schedule. Legacy: `FullPacket <bytes> <pointer>` queues a packet, `reset` clears the queue; `@maxdelay` (ms ceiling), `@packetsize` (ceiling), `@queuesize` (queue depth), `@precision` (timing tolerance) tune behaviour.

osc-timetag.digest: Generate, transform, and manipulate OSC timetags.
osc-timetag.use_when: Generate, transform, and manipulate OSC timetags. **DEPRECATED** — use odot's o.timetag. Legacy: `OSCTimeTag <int1> <int2>` constructs a timetag, `FullPacket <bytes> <pointer>` extracts a timetag from a bundle, `now` returns current time, `immediate` returns the immediate-execution timetag; `@from` / `@to` / `@op` define conversion behaviour.

oscillators~.use_when: Bank of tabulated function oscillators — many wavetable oscillators in one object with per-voice frequency and amplitude. Constructor args: `<buffer-name> <frequency/amplitude-duples>` define the wavetable and initial bank state. Runtime: `list <freq/amp pairs>` updates bank, `set <buffer-index>` selects a wavetable buffer~, `noglissbirthmode <flag>` toggles glide-on-birth behaviour, `clear` zeros voices. Use for oscbank-style additive synthesis with arbitrary waveforms; cheaper than N parallel wave~ objects.

peqbank~.use_when: Bank of parametric EQ filters in one signal object. Arguments and messages can mix in any order: `maxelem <n>` (maximum filters), `peq <F0 Hz> <bandwidth oct> <G0 dB at DC> <G peak dB> <GB edge dB>` adds a peak/cut band, `shelf <low dB> <mid dB> <high dB> <low cutoff Hz> <high cutoff Hz>` is a 3-band shelf, `bank <...>` or a plain list sends several of these at once, `biquads a0 a1 a2 b1 b2 ...` loads raw coefficients. Output is smoothed by default (`smooth`); `fast` saves CPU without smoothing. `clear` refreshes the filter state if it blows up; `reset` restores the bank and maxelem 10. Right outlet: the full biquad coefficient list, which the help file routes to a filter graph display. Use for multi-band EQ driven by messages rather than a chain of biquad~ objects.

poly.bus~.digest: Receive audio over a virtual bus connection of a named
poly.bus~.use_when: Named audio bus receiver for poly~ voices. Arguments: `<name> <number of channels>`; outlets are the bus channels. poly.send~ objects inside poly~ voices send to it by `@name` and `@channel`. Its signal inlet carries no audio: it only fixes DSP order, and the help file wires it so poly.bus~ comes after poly.send~ in the DSP chain. Use when a poly~ needs many separate outputs or sends without the delay and cost of extra poly~ outlets.

poly.send~.use_when: Send audio over a virtual named bus to all matching poly.bus~ receivers. `@name` (symbol) sets bus name, `@channel` selects channel index. Pairs with poly.bus~. Use for one-to-many audio fanout without explicit cords; works across poly~ instance boundaries.

printit.digest: print out information that is normally hidden by Max
printit.use_when: Print info that's normally hidden by Max — internal object state, attribute details, list contents at full precision. Optional constructor arg: `<label>` prepends a prefix. Pass through `bang`, `int`, `float`, `list`, `anything` — all are printed. Use for debugging when native `print` truncates or omits detail.

rbfi.use_when: Radial Basis Function Interpolator (UI). Designs N-dimensional interpolations between named points. Add points with `add_point <name> <coords> <inner_radius> <outer_radius> <locked> <rgb>`; `delete_point`, `move`, `inner_radius`, `outer_radius` modify; `clear` empties; `dump` / `getnumpoints` query state; `pop` removes last. Many display attrs: `@always_draw_circles`, `@always_draw_labels`, `@bgcolor`, `@bordercolor`, `@font_size`, `@line_width_float`, `@enable_multiple_crosshairs`, plus more. Use for preset/parameter interpolation in 2D space — drag a cursor between named presets and get smoothly weighted parameter blends.

res-transform.use_when: Transforms a resonance model stored as `freq gain decayrate` triples (the resonators~ format). Load the model with an argument list, a `list`, `resonances`, `sinusoids` (freq/gain pairs) or `more` (append). Transformations: `frequency-scale`, `frequency-add`, `frequency-spread`, `frequency-base` with `pitch` / `midi-pitch` to transpose, `frequency-minimum` / `frequency-maximum`, `gain-scale`, `gain-range`, `attenuate <dB>`, `rate-scale`, `rate-spread`, `evenfrequencyscale` / `oddfrequencyscale` and `evengainscale` / `oddgainscale` (even- or odd-numbered partials), `spectral-corner` / `spectral-slope`, `cluster-size` with `frequency-around` and `attenuation-spread`, `setonefrequency` / `setoneamplitude` / `setonerate` / `setoneresonance`. `bang` outputs the transformed model; `clear` removes transformations but keeps the data. Help: messages to the right inlet queue parameters without output, a bang on the left applies them. Use between an analysis model and resonators~ or sinusoids~.

resdisplay.use_when: UI display for resonance or sinusoid models. `list` of `freq gain decayrate` triples, or `sinusoids` followed by freq/gain pairs, updates the graph; `bang` outputs the stored data; `clear` empties it; `displayrange <low Hz> <high Hz>` zooms. Attributes: `@freqmin` / `@freqmax`, `@ampmin` / `@ampmax`, `@log` with `@ampmin_log` / `@ampmax_log`, `@mode`, and colors `@bgcolor`, `@bordercolor`, `@datacolor`, `@selectioncolor`. Use to see a model before sending it to resonators~.

resonators~.use_when: Bank of 2-pole resonant filters with one input and a summed output. Arguments: optional `smooth` (interpolate when the model changes; use it for live changes), then `freq gain decayrate` triples. `list` of triples replaces the model; a float excites the model with an impulse of that amplitude; a signal input excites it continuously (the help notes inputs often need 1–200× gain); `outputgain <list>` sets per-resonance gains; `squelch` damps the model; `clear` zeroes filter state; `bang` sends sample rate, state and coefficients out the right outlet. Use for modal synthesis of struck or excited bodies from measured or transformed models (res-transform, SDIF-buffer).

roughness.use_when: Estimates perceptual roughness (dissonance) from partial data, based on Richard Parncutt's code. Send a `list` of frequencies and amplitudes, or point it at SDIF data: `set <SDIF-buffer name>`, `SDIFtime <seconds>`, then `process_SDIF`. `set-cbw-type 1` (Parncutt, Hutchinson and Knopoff bandwidth) or `2` (Moore and Glasberg) chooses the critical-bandwidth formula; `scIndex` is the exponent of the standard curve. It does not analyze live audio: get partials first from an analysis object or an SDIF file.

sinusoids~.use_when: Bank of sine oscillators set by frequency/amplitude pairs, as arguments or a `list` (`440. 0.1 442. 0.05`). With `bwe` as the first argument it runs in bandwidth-enhanced mode and takes freq/amp/noisiness triples, adding band-limited noise to each partial. `clear` fades all partials to zero and stops synthesis; `tellmeeverything` posts the oscillators; `verbose` prints diagnostics. There is no phase control. Use for additive resynthesis from analysis data (often via SDIF-tuples and threefates); oscbank~ is the built-in alternative.

slipOSC.use_when: SLIP-encoded OSC over serial. `FullPacket <bytes> <pointer>` sends a raw OSC packet over serial; receives accept `int` / `list` of bytes for SLIP framing; `printcontents`, `debug`, `errorreporting` for diagnostics. Use to send/receive OSC over a serial port (Arduino, microcontrollers) using the SLIP framing convention.

sphY.use_when: Spherical harmonics evaluator (Y_l^m functions). `eval <theta> <phi>` evaluates at a (declination, azimuth) point; `index` queries indexing; `@order` sets the spherical-harmonic order. Use for ambisonic encoding/decoding math, 3D directivity patterns, or any application needing Y_l^m functions.

thread.fork.digest: Thread-level parallelism for event domain computation
thread.fork.use_when: Fork message processing onto a separate thread. Pass through `bang`, `int`, `float`, `anything` — they continue on a worker thread. Pair with thread.join. Use to move expensive control-rate computations off the scheduler thread (computational graph processing, large list operations) without blocking audio.

thread.join.digest: Thread-level parallelism for event domain computation
thread.join.use_when: Join messages from a forked thread back to the main scheduler. Pass through `bang`, `int`, `float`, `anything` — they return to scheduler thread. Use as the merge point for thread.fork results before any further main-thread processing (UI updates, audio control).

thread.which.digest: Report information about which thread a given message lives in, and forward it.
thread.which.use_when: Report which thread (scheduler vs other) a message is currently in, then forward it. Use for debugging threading issues — confirm you're on the expected thread before a thread-sensitive operation. Pass through `bang`, `int`, `float`, `list`, `anything`; output includes thread identifier.

threefates.use_when: Manages births and deaths of sinusoidal partial tracks between SDIF-tuples and sinusoids~. Input: lists of `index frequency gain` triples. Output: `frequency gain` pairs in a stable order for an oscillator bank. A new index is a birth and starts at zero amplitude; a missing index is a death and ends at its last frequency with zero amplitude, so sinusoids~ ramps it to silence without a glissando. A one-frame delay is applied to everything because births need it. Arguments: maximum number of partials, number of parameters per partial besides the index (use 3 for sinusoids~ in bwe mode). Use in additive resynthesis whenever partials appear and disappear between frames.

trampoline.use_when: Tail-call optimization for Max message loops. Put it inside a recursive or feedback message chain; messages (bang, int, float, list, anything, FullPacket) pass through but are 'bounced' so the call stack does not keep growing, which avoids stack overflow in deep recursion. Argument: number of inlet/outlet pairs, each handled independently. Use when a patch loops messages back into itself many times in one call (recursion patterns, repeated OSC processing).

trend-report.digest: Keep track of trends in a stream of numbers and report about each one after it finishes.
trend-report.use_when: Reports each finished rising or falling run in a stream of ints or floats. It outputs only after a trend ends, that is, at the first value that goes the other way. Outputs (per help): the trend's initial value, final value, number of inputs, and direction. Argument: tolerance: a single value that breaks the trend by less than this is ignored unless the next value also breaks it. Use to turn a jittery controller stream into gesture events (the end of a rise, the end of a fall).

vsnapshot~.digest: Output a list representing the signal vector associated with a given signal's input, similar to
vsnapshot~.use_when: Outputs a whole signal vector as a list, like snapshot~ but with every sample of the vector. Argument: polling interval in ms. `1` / `0` or `start` / `stop` turn automatic polling on and off; `bang` polls once. Use to look at or process one vector of samples in the message domain.

waveguide~.use_when: Waveguide mesh physical model with stiffness: delay-line edges joined at nodes, in any layout you define. Set the counts at creation: `@nodes`, `@edges`, `@inputs`, `@outputs`, `@size` (delay buffer in samples, default 1024). Build the mesh with `connect edge <edge> <node> <node>`, `connect input <signal inlet> <node>`, `connect output <signal outlet> <node>`; set properties with `set delay <edge> <ms>`, `set fc <edge> ...` (damping, 0.–1.), `set nl <edge> ...` (stiffness, 0.–1.). Use `*` in place of an edge number to address all edges; several commands can go in one list. Excite with a signal at input nodes; `reset` zeroes the state if it blows up. Use for experimental struck or plucked meshes (strings, triangles, plates).

xydisplay.digest: Create a 2d path and traverse it
xydisplay.use_when: 2D point path editor (UI) you can traverse with a phase. Create points by clicking (Shift-click removes), with a `list` or `set` of x/y pairs; `movepoint <index> <x> <y>` / `setpoint` (no output), `moveselected` / `setselected`, `select` / `setselection <index>`, `findnearest <x> <y>` / `findnearestx` / `findnearesty` (select without output), `renumber`, `clear`. A float input from 0 to the last index outputs the interpolated x/y out the third outlet; `bang` outputs all points as a list; `dump` sends `index x y` lists out the rightmost outlet followed by `done`. Attributes: `@xmin` / `@xmax` / `@ymin` / `@ymax`, `@connect_points`, `@drawlabels`, `@drawpoint`, `@locked`, `@parameter_enable`, colors. Use for drawn trajectories, for example a panning path driven by a phasor.

CidLinkClient.digest: Send messages to a Cid network infrastructure
CidLinkClient.use_when: Send messages to a Cid network infrastructure.

CidLinkServer.digest: Server of a Cid network infrastructure
CidLinkServer.use_when: Server of a Cid network infrastructure.

CH-Client.digest: Connect to the Collab-Hub Server. Client Module for Collab-Hub.
CH-Client.use_when: Connect to the Collab-Hub Server. Client Module for Collab-Hub.

CH-Events.digest: Observe Published Events on the Collab-Hub Server.
CH-Events.use_when: Observe Published Events on the Collab-Hub Server.

ch.client-testing.use_when: Developer debugging version of the Collab-Hub client module, for inspecting the Node for Max side. The file is patchers/ch.client-testing.maxpat (type ch.client-testing); no CH-ClientTesting name mapping ships. Not needed for normal use - use CH-Client.

ch.controls.digest: Observe Published Controls on the Collab-Hub Server.
ch.controls.use_when: Show and manage controls published on the Collab-Hub server: AvailableControls, ObservedControls and MyControls displays, Observe / Stop menus to start or stop receiving a control, Clear to remove one you published. Only needed with publish mode. Needs CH-Client connected. The file is patchers/ch.controls.maxpat; the package's init mapping points CH-Controls at ch.control.maxpat, which does not exist, so type ch.controls.

ch.timer.use_when: Shared timer for collaborative performance: start, stop and reset are broadcast to all connected clients. Displays the Collab-Hub timer web app in a jweb, so it needs internet access. The file is patchers/ch.timer.maxpat (type ch.timer); no CH-Timer name mapping ships.

jit.gp.emitter.use_when: Particle source for the Compute package's GPU particle system (a v8 script). Needs a `jit.gp.world` and a `jit.gp.render` in the same context. Attributes: `position`, `rate`, `speed`, `life`, `mass`, `initialvelocity`, `massincrement`, `enable`, `type point|matrix` (matrix emits from geometry, e.g. `jit.gl.model @matrixoutput 1`), `mode constant|trigger` (trigger emits on bang). The refpage's `material` attribute is disabled in the script.

jit.gp.force.use_when: Force for the Compute package's GPU particle system (a v8 script); needs `jit.gp.world`. `type point_attractor|directional|drag|field`; `amount`, `position`, `direction`, `radius`, `radiussoftness`, `enable`. Field forces add `fieldtype forcefield|rotational|accelerative|dragging`, `noisefunction` (simplex, perlin, …), `fieldoctaves`, `fieldoffset`, `fieldscale`. The refpage's `materials` / `materialcount` are disabled in the script.

jit.gp.obstacle.use_when: Collision shape for the Compute package's GPU particle system (a v8 script); needs `jit.gp.world`. `shape plane|sphere|box`, `action kill|stick|bounce`, `position`, `direction`, `scale`, `radius`, `roughness`, `softness`, `enable`, `materials`.

jit.gp.render.use_when: Draws a `jit.gp.world` particle system as points (a v8 script driving `jit.gl.mesh`). Connect the `jit.gp.world` outlet to its inlet, as the help does. Attributes: `color` (rgba), `point_size`. No help file of its own.

jit.gp.world.use_when: Core of the Compute package's GPU particle system (a v8 script on `jit.gpu.compute`). Set `@count` (particles) and `drawto` your `jit.world`; bind `jit.gp.emitter`, `jit.gp.force` and `jit.gp.obstacle` in the same context and connect its outlet to `jit.gp.render`. `reset` clears particles, `enable` pauses. Handles a million particles (`@count 1000000` in the examples). Compute 0.1.4 needs Max 9.1.3+.

jit.gpu.bang.digest: Synchronize GPU compute submissions with rendering
jit.gpu.bang.use_when: Compute package: bangs in step with the `jit.world` render loop (`drawto`). Use it to drive `jit.gpu.compute` passes and `jit.gpu.submit` when a compute chain shares textures with an OpenGL context. `enable 0` stops the bangs. Outlets: bang, dumpout.

jit.gpu.buffer.digest: A buffer resource contains arbitrary data stored in GPU memory
jit.gpu.buffer.use_when: Compute package: a block of data in GPU memory for compute shaders. Fill it from a Jitter matrix (raw bytes), a dictionary (`dictionary <name>`, laid out by the shader block named by `passname` / `blockname`), or zero it with `allocitems <count>`; `allocfromdict`, `mirror_properties <other>`. Connect its outlet to a `jit.gpu.compute` bind-point inlet (sets passname/blockname automatically), or bind by `name`. Read back with `jit.gpu.tomatrix`.

jit.gpu.compute.use_when: Compute package: runs a GLSL compute shader (`.comp`) on `jit.gpu.image` / `jit.gpu.buffer` resources via Vulkan (MoltenVK on Mac). Load with `@shader` / `@file` / `read`, or double-click to edit an embedded shader. `bang` only queues the pass (outlet bangs when queued); nothing runs until `jit.gpu.submit` is banged. Inlets are added per shader bind point, so the inlet count varies; uniform-block fields become attributes and `param <path> <values>`. `bind <bindpoint> <resource>`; `@autoworkgroups <image bindpoint>` sizes dispatch automatically, else set `workgroups x y z`. Chain passes outlet→inlet for order. Package 0.1.4, Max 9.1.3+.

jit.gpu.image.digest: An image resource (also known as a texture) in GPU memory
jit.gpu.image.use_when: Compute package: an image/texture in GPU memory. Fill from a Jitter matrix (sets `format` automatically) or a `jit.gl.texture` name, or size it with `@dim` for shader output. Attributes: `dim`, `format` (e.g. rgba8_unorm, r32_float), `filter`, `wrap`, `array`, `miplevels` / `automiplevels`, `name`. Connect its outlet to a `jit.gpu.compute` bind-point inlet; `mirror_properties <other>` copies another image's setup.

jit.gpu.imageview.digest: A view into a GPU image with subresource selection
jit.gpu.imageview.use_when: Compute package, advanced: a view of chosen mip levels (`miplevel`, `miplevelcount`) or array layers (`arraylayer`, `arraylayercount`) of a `jit.gpu.image`, with its own `filter` / `wrap`. Its help notes `jit.gpu.tomatrix` can often read levels and layers directly without a view.

jit.gpu.submit.digest: Submit queued GPU compute work for execution
jit.gpu.submit.use_when: Compute package: `bang` sends all queued GPU passes to the GPU. Every compute patch needs one; without it nothing runs. Left outlet bangs on submission, middle outlet when the GPU finishes. `gl_dependency 1` waits for OpenGL when results feed `jit.gl.*` objects; `clear` drops the queue; `copy_graphviz` copies the render graph for debugging.

jit.gpu.tomatrix.digest: A pass to read GPU data back to a Jitter matrix
jit.gpu.tomatrix.use_when: Compute package: reads a `jit.gpu.image` or `jit.gpu.buffer` (right inlet or `source`) back to a Jitter matrix. `bang` queues the readback; the matrix leaves the middle outlet after `jit.gpu.submit` completes. Buffers come out as 1D char matrices. `layer`, `layercount`, `miplevel`. CPU readback is slow; use `jit.gpu.totexture` for display.

jit.gpu.totexture.digest: Pass to convert a GPU image to an OpenGL texture
jit.gpu.totexture.use_when: Compute package: turns a `jit.gpu.image` (right inlet or `source`) into a `jit.gl.texture` without a CPU copy. `bang` queues it; the texture name leaves the middle outlet after `jit.gpu.submit` completes, ready for `jit.gl.videoplane`. `drawto`, `flip` (on by default), `filter`, `layer`, `miplevel`.

jit.gpu.transfers.digest: Queue and execute GPU transfer operations between images and buffers
jit.gpu.transfers.use_when: Compute package, advanced: queues GPU copies — `copyimage`, `copybuffer`, `copyimagetobuffer`, `copybuffertoimage` (two resource names or one dictionary with regions), `blitimage <dict>`, `genmipmaps <image>`. `bang` emits the queue into the render graph; it runs on the next `jit.gpu.submit`. `clear` empties the queue.

Three arguments set table size, curve exponent and curve scale (e.g. dot.transfer 180 3 1); one argument names a saved table (e.g. exponential.table). Messages edit, open, write, revert. Built-in alternative: function — breakpoint curve you can also use for mapping. Digital Orchestra Toolbox abstraction (IDMIL), open it to read how it works.

dot.urn.use_when: Outputs random numbers without repeats until all are used. Inlets: 0 bang generates random number; 1 add numbers back to the pot. Outlets: 0 Random number output; 1 Bang if the pot is empty (all numbers have been chosen). Arguments: limit, seed. Messages: max, clear, seed. Built-in alternative: urn — same idea, fewer options. Digital Orchestra Toolbox abstraction (IDMIL), open it to read how it works.

dot.vector.distance.digest: Finds maximum or minimum distance between a scalar and a list.
dot.vector.distance.use_when: Finds the list item nearest to (or farthest from) a number. Inlets: 0 scalar; 1 list. Argument - finds the minimum distance, + the maximum (e.g. dot.vector.distance -). Left inlet: the number; right inlet: the list. Outlets: list index, distance. Digital Orchestra Toolbox abstraction (IDMIL), open it to read how it works.

dot.vector.dotproduct.use_when: Computes the dot product of two lists. Inlets: 0 left list; 1 right list. Outlets: 0 dot product. Built-in alternative: vexpr — list math, needs a summing step. Digital Orchestra Toolbox abstraction (IDMIL), open it to read how it works.

dot.vector.interpolate.2.digest: Interpolates/extrapolates between two lists of equal length.
dot.vector.interpolate.2.use_when: Blends between two equal-length lists with one coefficient. Inlets: 0 interpolation coefficient; 1 list 1; 2 list 2. Outlets: 0 interpolated output. Older name mapped to it: dot.interpolate2. Built-in alternative: vexpr — can do the math by formula. Digital Orchestra Toolbox abstraction (IDMIL), open it to read how it works.

dot.vector.interpolate.4.digest: Interpolates/extrapolates between four lists of equal length.
dot.vector.interpolate.4.use_when: Blends four equal-length lists from an XY position. Inlets: 0 2D interpolation coefficient; 1 list1; 2 list2; 3 list3; 4 list4. Outlets: 0 interpolated output. Older name mapped to it: dot.interpolate4. Digital Orchestra Toolbox abstraction (IDMIL), open it to read how it works.

dot.vector.normalize.digest: Normalizes a list of ints or floats, or a windowed stream.
dot.vector.normalize.use_when: Scales a list, or a windowed stream, into a 0–1 range. Inlets: 0 stream or list to normalize; 1 window size in samples. Outlets: 0 normalized input. Older name mapped to it: dot.normalize. Digital Orchestra Toolbox abstraction (IDMIL), open it to read how it works.

dot.window.timed.digest: Output a list of samples in a user-specified time window
dot.window.timed.use_when: Collects values from the last stretch of time into a list. Argument / right inlet: window length in ms (e.g. dot.window.timed 500). Left inlet: numbers to collect. Output: list of the values received within the window. Its refpage file carries the wrong name (dot.vector.scale). Built-in alternative: zl.stream — keeps the last N items, by count not time. Digital Orchestra Toolbox abstraction (IDMIL), open it to read how it works.

modal_analysis.digest: play notes in and click analyze. Modal_analysis filters out repetitions, orders notes and identifies the mode.
modal_analysis.use_when: Guess the mode of a set of notes. Send a list of MIDI pitches (or play notes in) and bang to analyze; it removes repeated pitch classes, orders them, and outputs the mode as scale degrees and degree distances (half steps). Use when a system should follow the tonal centre of what a player just played; feed the result to modal_change. Old-format .pat abstraction (only modal_change and modal_triad are compiled externals).

modal_analysis+.digest: play notes in and click analyze. Modal_analysis filters out repetitions, orders notes and identifies the mode.
modal_analysis+.use_when: modal_analysis with a mode-namer and related-mode suggestions: after analyzing, it can drive modal_change and trigger modal_mutation (modes sharing 6 of 7 notes with the same root) or modal_shift (modes sharing 6 of 7 notes).
