Use for exploring modes related to played material. Old-format .pat abstraction (only modal_change and modal_triad are compiled externals).

modal_change.digest: this patch filters all unrelated notes to ones from the selected mode
modal_change.use_when: Core of the EAMIR Modal Object Library. Send a tonic (pitch class 0-11 or a letter such as F#) to the left inlet and a mode name (ionian, dorian_b2, lydian_b7, harmonic_minor, melodic_minor, ...) or a list of degree distances such as 2 2 1 2 2 2 1 to the right inlet; it outputs the mode's pitch classes and scale lists. It does not filter notes itself: feed its output to modal_coll_filter, which fills a coll, and put modal_filter <coll name> on the note stream to snap notes into the mode. Other modal_* objects (modal_triad, modal_pc_match, modal_shift, modal_retune) also read its output. Compiled external.

modal_chord_analysis.digest: NOTE: there are often numerous functions for a given chord. This will output one of them.
modal_chord_analysis.use_when: Name tertian chords: send a list of MIDI notes to the left inlet; outlets give chord root, chord quality, function within a key, inversion, bass note, and a list for jit.cellblock. Added intervals are written M/m/P with # and b. Only one of several possible functions is reported. Right inlet takes coll messages (open) to edit the chord-name data. Beta.

modal_coll_filter.digest: works with modal_change and modal_filter to force notes into a tonal framework
modal_coll_filter.use_when: Build the pitch-class remapping data that modal_filter uses. Connect modal_change's output to its inlet (mode) and its outlet to a named coll; it writes a 12-entry table that maps every pitch class to a nearby note of the current mode (major, harmonic minor, melodic minor and harmonic major mode families). Then modal_filter <same coll name> snaps incoming notes.

modal_filter.digest: simple abstraction that filters all incoming notes to those specified by the Modal_Change object
modal_filter.use_when: Snap incoming MIDI notes into the current mode. Argument: the name of a coll filled by modal_coll_filter (e.g. modal_filter my_coll). A note in the inlet is split into pitch class and octave, the pitch class is looked up in the coll, and the octave is added back, so out-of-mode notes are remapped to an in-mode neighbour rather than blocked. One inlet (MIDI note), one outlet (filtered note). Use after notein/kslider for mode-locked playing.

modal_fuzzharm.digest: send a bang to the left inlet to yield a chord chosen from the specified weighted probabilites
modal_fuzzharm.use_when: Choose a chord for each scale degree by weighted probability. Send a scale degree/pitch (often via modal_pc_match), bang the left inlet to output a chord for modal_triad. Double-click to edit weights in a cellblock; read/write save the table; clear resets it (all weights start at 0). Old-format .pat abstraction (only modal_change and modal_triad are compiled externals).

modal_line.digest: If a non-diatonic number is sent to the first inlet, the entire list will be scanned through to see if that non-diatonic number exists somewhere in the list. HINT: it doesn't!!
modal_line.use_when: Like line, but ramps through only the notes of the current mode. Argument: ramp time in ms. Auto mode ramps over that time; manual mode steps one note per bang. Non-diatonic target notes are not found, so put modal_filter before it. Beta; author calls it a kludge. Old-format .pat abstraction (only modal_change and modal_triad are compiled externals). Needs modal_change in the patch for the current tonic and mode.

modal_mediant.digest: Note: you MUST select an initial tonic before you click get related modes. Then choose from the list--this will automatically effect the Modal Change Object and repopulate the list with new modes.
modal_mediant.use_when: Fill a umenu with modes in chromatic-mediant relation to the current mode; choosing one updates modal_change and refreshes the list. Select an initial tonic first. Old-format .pat abstraction (only modal_change and modal_triad are compiled externals).

modal_messiaen10.digest: send a MIDI pitch class number (C=0, C#=1, etc) in the left inlet or simply send a message box with a captial letter. This will determine the tonic of the 10 note mode
modal_messiaen10.use_when: Output the pitches of a 10-note mode of limited transposition (Messiaen mode 7 and its inverse). Left inlet: tonic as pitch class or capital letter; right inlet: degree-distance list or a messiaen_mode7 / messiaen_mode7_inverse message. Old-format .pat abstraction (only modal_change and modal_triad are compiled externals).

modal_messiaen6.use_when: Output the pitches of a 6-note mode of limited transposition, such as whole_tone or messiaen_mode5. Left inlet: tonic (like modal_change); right inlet: degree-distance list or a mode-name message. Old-format .pat abstraction (only modal_change and modal_triad are compiled externals).

modal_messiaen8.digest: send a MIDI pitch class number (C=0, C#=1, etc) in the left inlet or simply send a message box with a captial letter. This will determine the tonic of the 8 note mode
modal_messiaen8.use_when: Output the pitches of an 8-note mode of limited transposition, such as octatonic, octatonic_inverse, messiaen_mode6 or messiaen_mode4_inverse. Left inlet: tonic as pitch class or capital letter; right inlet: degree-distance list or mode-name message. Old-format .pat abstraction (only modal_change and modal_triad are compiled externals).

modal_messiaen9.digest: send a MIDI pitch class number (C=0, C#=1, etc) in the left inlet or simply send a message box with a captial letter. This will determine the tonic of the 9 note mode.
modal_messiaen9.use_when: Output the pitches of a 9-note mode of limited transposition (messiaen_mode3 and its inverse). Left inlet: tonic as pitch class or capital letter; right inlet: degree-distance list or mode-name message. Old-format .pat abstraction (only modal_change and modal_triad are compiled externals).

modal_mutation.use_when: Bang to find a mode that shares 6 of 7 notes with the current mode and keeps the tonic (or a semitone inflection of it); the result updates modal_change and reports which scale degree changed. Old-format .pat abstraction (only modal_change and modal_triad are compiled externals). Needs modal_change in the patch for the current tonic and mode.

modal_netreceive.digest: use these objects to easily transmit modal_change data over a network. Networking uses UDP features for port and IP address specification.
modal_netreceive.use_when: Receive modal_change tonic and mode data sent by modal_netsend over UDP, and pass it to a local modal_change. The help patch sets the network with an address and a port message. Pair with modal_netsend. Old-format .pat abstraction (only modal_change and modal_triad are compiled externals).

modal_netsend.use_when: Send the current modal_change tonic and mode to another computer over UDP. Set the destination with address <ip> and port <n>. Pair with modal_netreceive. Old-format .pat abstraction (only modal_change and modal_triad are compiled externals).

modal_pc_match.digest: if the input matches a chromatic scale degree between a whole step. Example, a C# played in the key of C Major (between scale degrees 1 & 2 - C & D - a whole step).
modal_pc_match.use_when: Report which scale degree an incoming pitch matches. Inlet 1: pitch; inlets 2-9: scale-degree pitch classes straight from modal_change. The first 7 outlets fire for diatonic degrees 1-7, the next 14 for chromatic degrees (#1, b2, ... b7), and the last outlets output the chromatic pitch classes. Use to harmonize or react differently to in-mode and out-of-mode notes.

modal_pentatonic_coll_filter.digest: this patch filters all unrelated notes to ones from the selected mode
modal_pentatonic_coll_filter.use_when: Pentatonic version of modal_coll_filter: takes modal_change output and writes a coll that maps every pitch class onto the current pentatonic mode; use with modal_filter <coll name>. One inlet, one outlet.

modal_prog.digest: With the optional argument '@immediate 1', a new list of chords triggered when a list is currently being played will sound as soon as each chord from the previous list is played.
modal_prog.use_when: Play a chord progression one chord per bang. Send it a list of chord functions (e.g. 1 5 6 4, or 1 4 5 V/5 5); bang the left inlet for each next chord; the outlet goes to modal_triad's first inlet. By default a new list starts on the next bang; @immediate 1 switches as soon as the current chord of the old list has played. Old-format .pat abstraction (only modal_change and modal_triad are compiled externals).

modal_retune.digest: Compensate effect's latency by delaying the audio input. If Delay Compensation option is turned on in Live, the relative timing of different audio tracks will also be aligned accordingly.
modal_retune.use_when: Turn modal_change output into scale settings for retune~. Connect it from modal_change as in the help patch; its outlet feeds a live.grid of enabled notes, and the help patch (based on the Auto-tuna Max for Live device) converts that selection into retune~ notebase and enablednotes messages.

modal_shift.use_when: Bang to find a related mode by changing just one scale degree of the current mode; the result updates modal_change. Old-format .pat abstraction (only modal_change and modal_triad are compiled externals). Needs modal_change in the patch for the current tonic and mode.

modal_shiftlist.digest: modal_shiftlist is like the Modal_Shift object but populate the related modes into a menu
modal_shiftlist.use_when: Like modal_shift, but fills a umenu with all modes one scale degree away; choosing one updates modal_change and refreshes the menu. Choose the initial mode from the menu to trigger the calculation (the tonic alone does not). Old-format .pat abstraction (only modal_change and modal_triad are compiled externals).

modal_strictmod.digest: takes current tonic (pitch class #) in right inlet and the tonic to be modulated to in the right inlet. the left outlet outputs the index of transposition to be added to incoming pitch data
modal_strictmod.use_when: Compute the transposition for a modulation. Send the current tonic (pitch class) and the tonic to modulate to (0-11), as in the help patch. The left outlet gives the number of semitones to add to incoming pitches (for example with +). Old-format .pat abstraction (only modal_change and modal_triad are compiled externals).

modal_triad.digest: modal_triad used here with modal_prog to play chord progressions
modal_triad.use_when: Build chords from function names in the current mode. First inlet: chord symbols - scale-degree numbers 1-8, Roman numerals (case-sensitive quality, e.g. I, ii, ii0, I+), letter names (C, Cdom7, Gdom7b9#11), secondary functions (V/5, 7/2) and alterations with # and b followed by a degree. 7ths, 9ths, 11ths and 13ths follow the mode. Outlets give the chord tones for makenote/noteout. Pairs with modal_prog and modal_change. Compiled external.

vj.VST_preset.digest: bpatcher version with arguments visible through inspector
vj.VST_preset.use_when: Choose the right plug-in and preset file for the current platform. Arguments: Mac plug-in, Windows plug-in, Mac preset, Windows preset. Send win32, win64 or osx (or set); the left outlet sends the load messages to a vst~, the right passes a umenu through. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.banger.digest: simple abstraction similar to Peter Elsea's banger object
vj.banger.use_when: Bang outlets in sequence, one per incoming bang. Argument: number of outlets (help uses 31). Right inlet sets direction: 0 left to right, 1 right to left, 2 back and forth; set <n> chooses the next outlet; an int bangs that outlet. Similar to Peter Elsea's banger. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.bankselect.digest: value greater than arg1 for arg2 seconds
vj.bankselect.use_when: Detect a press-and-hold: bangs when the incoming value matches argument 1 (help: a held MIDI note) for argument 2 seconds. Left outlet: bang when the hold time is reached; right outlet: seconds held so far. Name is misleading. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.buffer_cropper.digest: X = gated (lower sensititvty to allow more through gate)
vj.buffer_cropper.use_when: Trim silence from the start and end of a buffer~. Bang the left inlet to calculate; other inlets take the gate state (0/1), how many ms of silence may pass before cropping, and how much silence to add back at each end. The help patch sets gate sensitivity 0-5. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.countdown.use_when: Count beats up or down at a tempo, optionally after a delay. Inlets: start, tempo, number of beats, direction (0 up, 1 down), delay in seconds, secondary display. Outlets: bang when finished, and the current count. Use for count-ins. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.filedate.digest: year, month, day, hour, minute, seconds, AM/PM
vj.filedate.use_when: Bang to get the current date and time as one filename-safe symbol (year-month-day_hour-minute-second-AM/PM, e.g. 2016-8-20_5-11-50-PM); prepend a name to make a recording filename. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.filenamedaterecording.digest: By default, the recording path is the Desktop (arg 1)
vj.filenamedaterecording.use_when: Make dated file paths for sfrecord~. Argument 1: folder (default Desktop/); arguments 2-4: file names. Bang to generate; each outlet gives an open message with a date-and-time-prefixed file name. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.filepath_folder.digest: populates a umenu with a folder relative to the patch
vj.filepath_folder.use_when: Fill a umenu with the files in a folder next to the patch. Argument: folder path pattern (help: %smisc). Inlets: refresh, clear, output the selected path; outlets: to umenu, full file path. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.filepather.digest: drop a bunch of files in the "stuff goes here" folder and see them pop up in the umenu below. This patch loads them into the tempoary Max search path
vj.filepather.use_when: Add a folder beside the patch (default stuff_goes_here) to the search path and list its files in a umenu. Inlets: select file, step through files; outlets: file name, and file name with read prepended. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.fileplayer.use_when: Small sound/movie file player with gain and waveform display. Inlets: file path, gain (0-127), messages to jit.qt.movie; outlets: audio left and right. Uses the legacy jit.qt.movie; prefer playlist~ or jit.playlist in new patches. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.keysustainer.digest: Won't send a keyup message if another key is still held down or pressed within the argument value
vj.keysustainer.use_when: Turn computer-keyboard presses into a sustained on/off: it does not send key-up while another key is held or pressed again within the argument time (ms). One outlet. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.lockstate.digest: reports if patch is locked or unlocked
vj.lockstate.use_when: Show and toggle whether the patch is locked, using js scripts and a textbutton. No inlets or outlets. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.number_separator.digest: take consecutive numbers as a symbol and separate them
vj.number_separator.use_when: Split a symbol of digits (e.g. "15558675309") into separate numbers using regexp. One inlet, one outlet. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.open_folder.digest: opens a folder called "misc" relative to this help file in Windows Explorer or Mac Finder
vj.open_folder.use_when: Open a folder next to the patch in Finder or Explorer. Argument: folder name relative to the patch. Outlets: folder path, and the patch's own path. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.platform_detection.digest: detect if user is on a Mac or a PC
vj.platform_detection.use_when: Report the operating system at load: left outlet fires for Mac, right for Windows (the author used it to choose a VST folder). No inlets. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.prefs_loader_filepath.digest: Note: you must specify an app name (ex. "MY APP NAME") in a standalone object in the "Preferences File Name" (in Inspector)
vj.prefs_loader_filepath.use_when: Load a file path saved in a standalone app's preferences folder (~/Library/Application Support/<app name>). Argument: app name, which must match the standalone object's Preferences File Name. Inlets: bang to reload, path from dropfile, path from opendialog; outlet: stored path. Standalone-building helper.

vj.prefs_loader_mappings.digest: Note: you must specify an app name (ex. "MY APP NAME") in a standalone object in the "Preferences File Name" (in Inspector)
vj.prefs_loader_mappings.use_when: Load saved mappings from a standalone app's preferences folder. Argument: app name, which must match the standalone object's Preferences File Name. Bang to reload (loads on open). Standalone-building helper.

vj.prefs_loader_standalone.digest: creates space to store preferences files with a standalone object at ~/Library/Application Support/"MY APP NAME"
vj.prefs_loader_standalone.use_when: Create the preferences folder ~/Library/Application Support/<app name> for a standalone app, for use with vj.prefs_loader_filepath and vj.prefs_loader_mappings. Argument: app name. Note: closing its help patch quits Max. Standalone-building helper.

vj.quickscale.use_when: Play a scale. Arguments: tonic, mode name, tempo (e.g. vj.quickscale c major 120). Inlets: bang to start, velocity, transposition from pitch class (default +48); outlets: pitch and velocity for noteout. Uses modal_change inside. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.random_filename.digest: output has descriptive filename and random number in front. No more overwriting sfrecord~ files when batch recording in multiple sessions!!
vj.random_filename.use_when: Put a random number in front of a file name so repeated sfrecord~ recordings do not overwrite each other. Argument: descriptive file name (e.g. computer_audio.aif). Bang for a new name. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.switchtoggler.digest: turns all other switches off when one is on (clicked_
vj.switchtoggler.use_when: A group of live.toggle switches where turning one on turns the others off; seven outlets report each switch. No inlets. The built-in radiogroup does the same job. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.timetrial.use_when: Trial-version helper for standalone apps: after argument 1 minutes it shows a nag screen, after argument 2 minutes it quits. No inlets or outlets. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.toggler.digest: enable toggles according to master toggle sync
vj.toggler.use_when: Drive two sets of controls from one toggle: left outlet is enabled when the toggle is on, right outlet when it is off. Legacy V Objects helper.

vj.windowresizer.digest: ...when the patch reopens it will open in the specified size in the desired margin from the screen
vj.windowresizer.use_when: Save the patch window's size and position so it reopens that way: resize the patch in presentation mode, click the button, save. Optional arguments: screen position; optional @fullscreen 1. Uses thispatcher. Legacy V Objects helper.

fftz.bthresher~.use_when: Per-bin feedback with amplitude thresholds. Signal in left inlet; right two inlets accept threshold and damping signals (3 inlets total). Set per-bin parameters with `bin <bin#> <damping> <threshold>` or `alldamp <damping>` / `allthresh <threshold>` to set globally; `inf_hold <flag>` freezes feedback indefinitely; `max_hold <ms>` caps hold time. Use for buildup/feedback effects on individual frequency bins (loud bins ring, quiet bins stay clean) — native equivalent is a pfft~ with per-bin gate + delay loop, substantial.

fftz.burrow~.use_when: Cross-filter A's spectrum by B's spectral magnitude (B 'burrows into' A). 4 inlets: A signal, B signal, threshold signal, mult signal. `invert <flag>` swaps the cross-filter polarity (filter where B is quiet rather than loud); `mute <flag>` zeros output. Use for spectral cross-filtering effects where one sound shapes another's spectrum — no native equivalent.

fftz.cavoc27~.use_when: 27-rule cellular-automaton-driven oscillator-bank spectrum. Signal in left, signal out. Tunable via `@density` (initial CA density 0.–1.), `@holdtime` (ms between CA steps); messages `freeze <flag>` to halt evolution, `manual <flag>` to step on demand, `interpolate <flag>` for crossfaded transitions, `noalias <flag>` to suppress aliasing, `oscbank <flag>` to use oscbank resynthesis, `capture_spectrum <flag>` to seed CA from input audio. Use to generate evolving emergent spectral textures with no input audio required.

fftz.cavoc~.use_when: Generates evolving spectra from an 8-rule cellular automaton; needs no audio input. Set the rule with `rule <8 values>`; `bottomfreq` / `topfreq` constrain the band; `retune <min> <max>` sets random tuning factors (useful with `oscbank 1`, which is much louder); `external_trigger 1` makes it step on each `bang` instead of `@holdtime` ms. `@density` sets the initial fill. Start with very low gain. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.centerring~.use_when: Frequency-independent ring modulation in the spectral domain — modulates each bin's amplitude rather than the time-domain product. `randphases` randomises bin phases, `zerophases` zeros them, `seed <value>` sets the random seed. Use for spectral AM that doesn't introduce sidebands the way time-domain ring modulation does.

fftz.codepend~.use_when: Block convolution of two live input signals: multiplies their spectra (complex multiply), which can drop the level a lot. 4 inlets: two signals plus controls for a scaling exponent and an inverse threshold. `invert 1` divides the spectra instead, and `pad <dB>` rebalances gain in invert mode. This is cross-synthesis between two sounds, not an impulse-response reverb: use HIRT multiconvolve~ or hirt.convolver~ for IR convolution. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.cross~.use_when: Cross synthesis with a threshold: while the threshold condition holds it multiplies the two spectra, otherwise it keeps the last calculated magnitude/phase pair. 3 inlets: two sounds and a threshold (the help uses a voice as the filter and an orchestral sample as the driver). Output is peaky, so the help follows it with a compressor. `autonorm 1` matches output to input gain (loud, CPU-heavy). FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.dentist~.use_when: Punches out all but a chosen set of partials. `toothcount <n>` sets how many bins stay, `scramble` picks a new set, `setstate <bin list>` chooses bins directly and `showstate` reports them; `topfreq <hz>` caps where new teeth can go. `ramptime` sets the interpolation time between sets (per the help), and `interpolate_singles 0` applies toothcount changes instantly. Outlets: audio plus sync and state. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.disarrain~.use_when: Spectrum scrambler with smooth crossfaded bin reordering. `bang` to rescramble; `fadetime <ms>` controls crossfade length; `setstate <pattern>` / `isetstate <pattern>` (instant) / `showstate` save and inspect the permutation; `killfade` cancels in-progress fade. `@maxfreq` caps the scrambled band. Use for evolving spectral mangling with smooth transitions between rearrangements.

fftz.disarray~.use_when: Reorders a set number of frequency bins to transform timbre, with instant changes. `switch_count <n>` sets how many bins are swapped, `topfreq <hz>` the highest frequency that can move; `bang` makes a new arrangement, `setstate <list>` recalls one and `showstate` reports it (third outlet, list). For crossfaded changes use fftz.disarrain~. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.drown~.use_when: Spectral noise reduction (or increase): every bin below a threshold is multiplied by a factor, so low values quieten noise and values above 1 add noise; bins are scaled, not zeroed. 3 inlets: the signal plus threshold and weak-bin multiplier controls. The help toggles a relative threshold (tracking the signal peak) with `rel2peak $1`; the refpage lists `adaptive` for the same idea. For a band-limited version use fftz.scrape~. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.enrich~.use_when: Oscillator-bank resynthesis of the input using a custom waveform stored in a buffer~, useful for spectral distortion. Name the table with `@buffername` (the help switches with `buffername <name>`); the help says the buffer~ must be mono and 8192 samples long. `@lofreq` / `@hifreq` limit the resynthesized band. 3 inlets. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.ether~.use_when: Spectral compositing — for each bin, take whichever of two inputs has greater magnitude. `invert <flag>` flips to take the lesser (= vacancy~ behaviour). Use to combine two sounds where each occupies different spectral regions; complementary to fftz.vacancy~.

fftz.leaker~.use_when: Bin-level crossfader between two spectra. `upsieve` and `downsieve` shift the crossfade pattern up or down through bins; `randsieve` randomises which bins come from which source. Use for granular spectral morphing where you control the mix bin-by-bin via control or by the sieve patterns.

fftz.loopsea~.use_when: Records a sound into an internal spectral buffer, then loops each FFT bin with its own length, speed and (in oscbank mode) transposition. Argument: recording length (10000 in the help, for a sound of at least 10 seconds). `acquire_sample` records; `setloops <min ms> <max ms>` sets loop durations; `randspeed <min> <max>` randomises speeds in Hz; `setspeed` sets a global speed; `randtransp <min> <max>` or `transp_choose <values…>` set transpositions; `restart_loops`; `printloops` sends the loop data out the rightmost outlet for later `readloops`. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.mindwarp~.use_when: Warps the spectral envelope (formant-shifting style). Two control signals on additional inlets shape the warp. Use to transform timbre/formants while pitch is unaffected — vocal/instrument 'monster voice' or formant shifts. Minimal control surface beyond standard fft params and signal-driven warp.

fftz.morphine~.use_when: Morphs between the spectra of two input sounds. 3 inlets: two signals and the morph index (useful range 0 to 1). `transition <value>` sets the exponential scaling of the morph curve (the help loads -5; more negative values change the progression), it is not an on/off flag. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.multyq~.use_when: Four-band equalizer done in the frequency domain; type it as `fftz.multyq~`. 13 inlets: the signal, then frequency, bandwidth and gain for each of the four bands (the help unpacks each band's three values onto its own inlets). Bandwidth runs 0 to 1; gain below 0 cuts a notch, down to -1. CPU is the same however many bands are used. Being FFT-based, it is imprecise at low frequencies, so prefer biquad~/filtergraph~ or fffb~ for ordinary EQ. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.pileup~.use_when: Spectral accumulation: each bin keeps its amplitude and phase (with optional damping) until new information above a threshold replaces it, giving reverberant sustains and freezes. Messages: `persistence <factor>` (damping), `mode <n>` (operating mode), `clear`, `synthresh`, `transpose` and `oscbank 1` (oscillator-bank resynthesis), `inverse_gain`, `lowfreq` / `hifreq` to limit the band. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.pvcompand~.use_when: Spectral compander: expands or compresses the differences between bin amplitudes within each frame. Signal plus one threshold inlet in dB, useful from about -60 to +60: positive values make the sound peakier, negative values flatten it towards noise. `normalize 1` rebalances output level. It is a timbre effect, not a per-band level compressor. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.pvgrain~.use_when: Tracks the spectrum of an input sound and outputs control data for playing notes on a sampler or synthesizer (the help drives a groove~ sampler with it); despite its name and digest it is not an audio granulator. `framegrains <n>` sets the maximum data grains per FFT frame, `probability <0.-1.>` the odds that an active bin emits one, `basefreq <hz>` the base pitch of your sample, `topfreq <hz>` the highest frequency listened to. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.pvharm~.use_when: Phase-vocoder harmonizer: mixes two internally transposed copies of the input with the output. 4 inlets: the signal plus controls for the two transposition factors (T1, T2) and a synthesis threshold. `lowfreq` / `hifreq` set the band to resynthesize, `osclimit <n>` caps oscillators for CPU, and the help also toggles `compressor $1`. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.pvoc~.use_when: Phase vocoder resynthesis of a live input with transposition. Signal in the left inlet; the other two inlets take a transposition factor and a synthesis threshold (the help converts dB with dbtoa). `@lowfreq` / `@highfreq` limit the band that is resynthesized. It has no time-stretch or scrub control: to freeze, slow down or scrub a sound spectrally, use fftz.residency~. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.pvtuner~.use_when: Frequency-quantised resynthesis — snaps each spectral peak to the nearest scale degree. Many built-in scale messages: `eq12` (equal-tempered), `diatonic`, `eastern`, `dominant_seventh_chord`, `added_sixth_major` / `added_sixth_minor`, plus user-defined scales. `basefreq <hz>` sets reference; `binfo` reports bin-to-pitch mapping; `@scale_interpolation` smooths between scales. Use for autotune-like quantisation of polyphonic or inharmonic material to a scale.

fftz.pvwarpb~.use_when: Buffer-driven spectral warp — same idea as pvwarp~ but the warp curve comes from a buffer~. Required: `@buffername <symbol>` naming the buffer holding the warp function. Use when the warp curve needs to be precomputed, drawn (in waveform~), or animated as buffer contents.

fftz.pvwarp~.use_when: Spectral frequency warping — maps the frequency axis through a function defined by control values. `bottomfreq <hz>` / `topfreq <hz>` set the warped band; `autofunc <min> <max>` generates an automatic warp curve. Use for inharmonic transformations, formant shifts, alien retunings.

fftz.reanimator~.use_when: Audio texture mapping: first analyses a texture sound, then resynthesizes a driver sound by finding, for each driver frame, the closest frame in the texture. Argument sets the analysis length (the help uses 2000 with a texture of at least 2 seconds). Send `analyze` while the texture plays into the left inlet, then play the driver. Other messages: `freeze_and_march`, `resume`, `inverse`, `oscbank`, `framecount`, `meminfo`. Outlets: audio, record sync, current frame. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.resent~.use_when: Spectral sampler like fftz.residency~ but with independent speed and phase per bin; learn residency~ first. `acquire_sample` (or a bang, as in the help) records into memory sized by `@size`. Per-bin control: `bin <bin> <speed>`, `linespeed <startbin> <speed> <endbin> <speed>`, `linephase <startbin> <phase> <endbin> <phase>`, `randspeed <min> <max>`, `randphase <min> <max>`; global: `setspeed`, `setphase`, `addspeed`, `store_incr`. Speed 0 scrubs by phase. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.residency_buffer~.use_when: Like fftz.residency~ but stores the spectral analysis in a named buffer~ (`@buffername`), so several objects can share it. Size the buffer~ first: `calcbuf <ms>` reports the samples needed. A bang records the input; the second inlet sets speed and the third position (the help drives a second, slower reader from the same buffer). `oscbank`, `synthresh`, `transpose`, `playthrough`, `meminfo`. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.residency~.use_when: Spectral sampler: records input into internal memory (`@size`, in ms in the help), then resynthesizes it at any speed and pitch. `acquire_sample` starts recording, `acquire_stop` ends it early. The second inlet sets playback speed and the third position: set speed to 0 and move the position to scrub or freeze. `transpose`, `synthresh`, `oscbank 1`, `playthrough 1`, `meminfo`, `@interpolation`. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.schmear~.use_when: Smears the amplitude spectrum by convolving it across neighbouring bins with a kernel you supply. `schmimp <values…>` sets the kernel (`schmimp 1` = no smear), `shift <n>` moves bin energy up, `threshold <value>` sets the level used. FFT size strongly changes where the energy goes. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.scrape~.use_when: Noise reduction like fftz.drown~, but applied only between a knee and cutoff frequency and on up to Nyquist, with a transition in between. 6 inlets: the signal plus five controls for knee, cutoff, two thresholds and the weak-bin multiplier (see the help for their order). It does not learn a noise profile. Use when noise sits in the high range and lows must stay untouched. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.shapee~.use_when: Frequency shaping: shapes the frequency evolution of one signal with that of another. 3 inlets: first sound, second sound (a voice works well as the filter), shape width, which sets the amount. Its refpage description and digest were copied from fftz.scrape~ and are wrong; trust the help file. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.swinger~.use_when: Cross-synthesis combining magnitudes of A with phases of B (or vice versa). Use for the classic spectral cross-synthesis sound — A's pitch / phase structure with B's timbre, or vice versa.

fftz.taint~.use_when: Multiplies the spectra of two input sounds, which can drop the level a lot. 4 inlets: two signals plus controls for a scaling exponent and an inverse threshold. `invert 1` divides the spectra instead (lower threshold values intensify it) and `pad <dB>` rebalances gain in invert mode only. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.thresher~.use_when: Sustains amplitude and frequency in lower-energy bins, which then decay. 3 inlets: signal, threshold (0 lets every frame through, higher values sustain more) and damping factor (for example 0.985). `oscbank 1` switches to oscillator-bank resynthesis, with `synthresh` and `transpose`. For per-bin control use fftz.bthresher~. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

fftz.vacancy~.use_when: Spectral compositing — for each bin, take whichever of two inputs has lesser magnitude. `invert <flag>` flips to greater (= ether~ behaviour); `rms <flag>` switches comparison metric to RMS; `swapphase <flag>` exchanges phases between inputs. Inverse of fftz.ether~. Use to extract the 'quiet' parts of two sources.

fftz.xsyn~.use_when: Cross synthesis: filters the first input with the spectrum of the second. Two signal inlets and no other controls; use a rich driver sound on the left and a voice or other shaped sound on the right. FFT size and overlap are the `@fftsize` and `@overlap` attributes (powers of 2).

flowSwing.audioWarp.digest: NI Grid based time-warp of sound samples
flowSwing.audioWarp.use_when: Time-warp a sound in a buffer~ to Non-Isochronous (NI) Grids in real time: warp markers are pulled toward the beats of an uneven grid set by Formative/Target pulses and the S parameter, so timing can morph during performance. Four inlets (the second goes to the internal groove~, the third takes the buffer to stretch, the fourth parameters or a dict of markers); outlets include audio, trigger signal, original and warped phase, marker data, grid and pattr output. Warp markers can come from flowSwing.onsetDetect. Needs Max 9. Typing the dotted name loads the patch as a bpatcher (init/objectmappings.txt).

flowSwing.envelop.digest: NI Grid based sequencer and envelop generator
flowSwing.envelop.use_when: Sequencer and envelope generator on a Non-Isochronous (NI) Grid. Left inlet: a phasor signal for playback position. Right inlet: parameters - Formative / Target (beat counts), S (grid position between the two pulses), niRotation, breakpoints (dict), lock, morph, snapToNIGrid, chans / firstChannel (MC gate channels), offset, mute. Outlets: envelope signal, MC gate/trigger signal, phase, voice count, breakpoint index and values, shifted positions, grid, pattr output. Needs Max 9. Typing the dotted name loads the patch as a bpatcher (init/objectmappings.txt).

flowSwing.nested.digest: Sequencer with 2 hierarchically nested NI Grids
flowSwing.nested.use_when: Like flowSwing.envelop but with two hierarchically nested NI Grids (extra Formative2, Target2, S2, niRotation2 parameters). Left inlet: phasor signal; right inlet: parameters. Outlets: envelope, MC trigger signal, phase, voice count, breakpoint data, grid, pattr output. Needs Max 9. Typing the dotted name loads the patch as a bpatcher (init/objectmappings.txt).

flowSwing.noise.digest: Synthesizer with tone-to-noise control and mc based polyphony
flowSwing.noise.use_when: Polyphonic tone-to-noise synth driven by an MC gate signal (each channel triggers a voice's ADSR). Separate inlets for frequency, noiseF (period noise), noiseA (amplitude noise), skew, filter and Q (float, signal or MC signal), plus a parameter inlet (attack, release, envCurve, ampCurve, filterRange, Formative / Target / S for NI detune). Outlets: two audio channels and pattr output. Pairs with flowSwing.envelop gates. Needs Max 9. Typing the dotted name loads the patch as a bpatcher (init/objectmappings.txt).

flowSwing.onsetDetect.digest: Onset detection and automatic creation of warp markers
flowSwing.onsetDetect.use_when: Detect onsets in a buffer~ and turn them into warp markers for flowSwing.audioWarp. Requires the FluCoMa package (uses fluid.bufonsetslice~). Right inlet: buffer <name>, metric, threshold, continous 1 (re-detect on every parameter change); left inlet: bang or messages to fluid.bufonsetslice~. Outlets: list of onset positions in samples, dict of markers and parameters. Needs Max 9. Typing the dotted name loads the patch as a bpatcher (init/objectmappings.txt).

flowSwing.stepUI.use_when: Step-sequencer style editor for per-breakpoint values of flowSwing.envelop or flowSwing.nested. Left inlet: list of step times 0-1 (its inlet comment says to connect the third-from-right outlet of flowSwing.envelop); right inlet: list of y values or messages (range, grid, floatmode, format, color, zoom_x). Outlets: y values, the step being edited, parameter changes. Needs Max 9. Typing the dotted name loads the patch as a bpatcher (init/objectmappings.txt).

flowSwing.subDiv.digest: Non Integer subdivision of a phasor
flowSwing.subDiv.use_when: Divide a phasor~ ramp into segments of any relative lengths. Inlets: phasor ramp, list of ramp times (0-1), sliding factor (>= 0). Outlets: phase 0-1 within the current segment, segment index. Use when subdiv~'s equal divisions are too regular. Type flowSwing.subDiv (init/objectmappings.txt). Needs Max 9.

fluid.ampfeature~.use_when: Realtime amplitude differential feature — outputs a slow/fast envelope difference signal used as an onset/event indicator. `@highpassfreq` (default 85 Hz) high-passes input before envelope extraction (removes DC/rumble); `@fastrampup` / `@fastrampdown` (default 1 ms) and `@slowrampup` / `@slowrampdown` (default 100 ms) tune the two envelope time constants; `@floor` (default -144 dB) sets noise gate. Send `reset` to clear envelope state. Use as a low-cost activity detector before a full spectral onset analysis — cheaper than fluid.onsetfeature~ when amplitude is enough.

fluid.ampgate~.use_when: Amplitude-based gate detector with hysteresis and lookahead. Constructor arg: `<maxsize>` (sample buffer). Tune onset/offset thresholds (`@minlengthabove` / `@minlengthbelow`, both in ms), silence handling (`@minsilencelength`), and lookahead/lookback (`@lookahead` / `@lookback`) to avoid false triggers; `@highpassfreq` (default 85 Hz) pre-filters input. `reset` clears gate state. Use when you need event boundaries (note on/off) from a level threshold without false triggers — the lookahead lets the gate confirm sustain before opening.

fluid.ampslice~.use_when: Amplitude-based slicer — detects onsets via slow/fast envelope detrending and emits slice triggers. Same envelope-time-constant attrs as fluid.ampfeature~ (`@fastrampup/down`, `@slowrampup/down`, `@highpassfreq`, `@floor`); add `@onthreshold` / `@offthreshold` (dB) for slice gating and `@minslicelength` (ms) to suppress short slices. `reset` clears state. Use for realtime onset slicing on percussive or amplitude-modulated material.

fluid.audiofilesin.use_when: Abstraction that lists every audio file in a folder. Send the absolute folder path as a symbol to the inlet (the help file sends `C74:/media/msp` through `conformpath`); the outlet emits a list of filenames with full paths. Typical next step: fluid.concataudiofiles to load them all into one buffer~.

fluid.audiotransport~.use_when: Realtime optimal-transport spectral morph between two live sounds. Two signal inlets, one per source, and `@interpolation` (0–1, also settable by an `interpolation $1` message) morphs between them; standard FFT attributes (`@fftsettings <window> <hop> <fft>`, `@maxfftsize`). Larger FFT sizes blend spectra more smoothly but smear attacks (demonstrated in its help file). `reset` clears state. Offline version: fluid.bufaudiotransport~.

fluid.buf2list.digest: Copy the contents of a buffer~ to a list
fluid.buf2list.use_when: Copy buffer~ contents to a Max list (audio→list bridge). `@source <buffer-name>` and `@startframe` / `@startchan` define the read region; `@axis 0` reads frame-major, `@axis 1` reads channel-major. Send `bang` to copy; `buffer <name>` retargets source. Use to extract feature vectors, analysis frames, or short audio segments into list-domain processing chains.

fluid.bufampfeature~.use_when: Buffer-based amplitude differential feature — offline equivalent of fluid.ampfeature~. Same envelope attrs (`@fastrampup/down`, `@slowrampup/down`, `@highpassfreq`, `@floor`) plus buffer addressing (`@source`, `@startframe`, `@numframes`, `@startchan`, `@numchans`). `@features <buffer>` writes per-frame feature curve. `bang` runs analysis; `cancel` aborts long jobs. Use when audio is already in a buffer — typically faster and more accurate than realtime.

fluid.bufampgate~.use_when: Buffer-based amplitude gate detection — offline equivalent of fluid.ampgate~. Constructor arg: `<maxsize>`. Same gate attrs (`@minlengthabove/below`, `@lookahead/back`, `@minsilencelength`, `@highpassfreq`) plus `@indices <buffer>` to write slice-point pairs. Use to find event boundaries in a buffered audio file in one offline pass — the indices buffer gives you (start, end) pairs ready for fluid.bufcompose~ slicing.

fluid.bufampslice~.use_when: Buffer-based amplitude slicer — offline counterpart of fluid.ampslice~. Same envelope and threshold attrs plus `@indices <buffer>` for slice points and standard buffer addressing (`@source`, `@startframe/numframes`, `@startchan/numchans`). Produces a list of slice points for an entire file in one pass. Use for batch slicing where realtime accuracy isn't enough.

fluid.bufaudiotransport~.use_when: Offline optimal-transport spectral morph between two buffers. Sources are `@sourcea` and `@sourceb` (each with its own `@startframea` / `@numframesa` / `@startchana` / `@numchansa` and …b region attributes); `@destination` receives the result; `@interpolation` (0–1) sets the mix point; standard FFT attributes (`@fftsettings <window> <hop> <fft>`, `@maxfftsize`). `bang` runs, `cancel` stops. Use to render in-between timbres; realtime version: fluid.audiotransport~.

fluid.bufchroma~.digest: A histogram of pitch classes on a Buffer
fluid.bufchroma~.use_when: Pitch-class histogram (chroma vector) for a buffer. Constructor arg: `<numchroma>` (default 12 = chromatic); `@minfreq` / `@maxfreq` constrain analysis band, `@maxnumchroma` caps allocation, plus standard buffer addressing and `@features <buffer>` for output. Use for offline key/chord/harmonic-content analysis — feeds into corpus search by harmonic similarity.

fluid.bufcompose~.use_when: Buffer compositing — concatenate, layer, copy with sample-precise placement. `@source <buf>` and `@startframe`/`@numframes`/`@startchan`/`@numchans` define the read region; `@destination <buf>` and `@deststartframe`/`@deststartchan` define write position; `@gain` and `@destgain` mix existing destination content with source. `bang` runs; `cancel` aborts. Use as the FluCoMa swiss-army knife for assembling buffers programmatically — corpus prep, splicing, layering.

fluid.bufflatten~.use_when: Flattens a multichannel buffer into a single channel by laying its values out end to end — it does not mix audio down. `@source` / `@destination`, region with `@startframe`, `@numframes`, `@startchan`, `@numchans`; `@axis 1` (default) goes channel by channel, `@axis 0` frame by frame. Main use: turn a multichannel stats buffer (from fluid.bufstats~) into one flat point for `fluid.dataset~ addpoint`. `bang` runs.

fluid.bufhpss~.digest: Buffer-Based Harmonic-Percussive Source Separation Using Median Filtering
fluid.bufhpss~.use_when: Harmonic-percussive source separation by median filtering on a buffer. Constructor args: `<harmfiltersize> <percfiltersize>`. `@source`, `@startframe`, `@numframes`, `@startchan`, `@numchans` pick the region; `@harmonic`, `@percussive` and `@residual` name the output buffers. `@harmfiltersize` (default 17, odd, in spectral frames over time) and `@percfiltersize` (default 31, odd, in spectral bins across frequency). `@maskingmode` 0 soft (default), 1 binary (uses `@harmthresh`), 2 soft with residual (uses `@harmthresh` and `@percthresh`, fills `@residual`). standard FFT attributes (`@fftsettings <window> <hop> <fft>`, `@maxfftsize`). `bang` runs, `cancel` stops.

fluid.bufloudness~.digest: A Loudness and True-Peak Descriptor on a Buffer
fluid.bufloudness~.use_when: ITU-R BS.1770 loudness and true-peak descriptor on a buffer. Constructor arg: `<maxwindowsize>`. `@hopsize` (default 512) and window controls; `@kweighting 1` enables K-weighted loudness (LUFS standard); `@truepeak 1` enables true-peak detection; `@padding` adds analysis padding; standard buffer addressing. `@features <buf>` writes per-frame loudness/peak curves. Use as the standard loudness descriptor for ML features or normalisation — far more accurate than peak-amplitude.

fluid.bufmelbands~.digest: A Perceptually Spread Spectral Contour Descriptor on a Buffer
fluid.bufmelbands~.use_when: Mel-band spectral analysis on a buffer. Constructor arg: `<numbands>`. `@minfreq` / `@maxfreq` define analysis band (default 20–20000 Hz); `@maxnumbands` caps allocation; standard FFT and buffer attrs; `@features <buf>` writes per-frame mel-band curves. Use as a perceptually-spread spectral descriptor for offline analysis or as preprocessing for offline MFCC extraction.

fluid.bufmfcc~.digest: Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients as Spectral Descriptors on a Buffer
fluid.bufmfcc~.use_when: MFCC on a buffer. Constructor args: `<numcoeffs> <numbands>` (typical: 13 coefficients from 40 mel bands). `@maxnumcoeffs` and `@maxnumbands` cap allocation; `@minfreq` / `@maxfreq`; standard FFT and buffer attrs; `@features <buf>` writes the MFCC curve. Use as the standard timbral feature for offline corpus analysis — feeds into fluid.kmeans~/fluid.knnclassifier~ for similarity matching.

fluid.bufnmfcross~.digest: Resynthesise a target sound based on a source sound
fluid.bufnmfcross~.use_when: Cross-synthesis — resynthesise a target sound using bases extracted from a source. `@output <buf>` for resynthesis output; `@continuity` (default 7) constrains temporal continuity; `@iterations` (default 50) sets NMF iteration count; `@polyphony` (default 11) caps simultaneous bases; standard FFT attrs. Use for spectral hybridisation: 'play sound A using the spectral building blocks of sound B' — distinctive cross-synthesis aesthetic.

fluid.bufnmfseed~.digest: Non-Negative Double Singular Value Decomposition on a Buffer
fluid.bufnmfseed~.use_when: Non-negative double-SVD seeding for NMF — smarter initialisation than random. `@bases <buf>` and `@activations <buf>` write seed matrices; `@maxcomponents` (default 200) caps component count; `@coverage` (default 0.5) controls how much spectral variance the seed covers. Use as preprocessing for fluid.bufnmf~ when random initialisation produces unstable decompositions.

fluid.bufnmf~.digest: Buffer-Based Non-Negative Matrix Factorisation on Spectral Frames
fluid.bufnmf~.use_when: Non-negative matrix factorisation on spectral frames. `@components` (default 1) sets target rank; `@bases <buf>` and `@activations <buf>` name output matrices; `@basesmode` and `@actmode` control whether bases/activations are random-init, fixed, or seeded; `@iterations` controls NMF iteration count; standard FFT attrs. Use to decompose audio into a small number of recurring spectral templates and their activations — source separation, sound-pattern discovery, dictionary learning.

fluid.bufnoveltyfeature~.use_when: Buffer-based novelty curve. Constructor args: `<kernelsize> <filtersize>`. `@algorithm` selects novelty algorithm; `@kernelsize` (default 3) is similarity-matrix kernel size; `@filtersize` (default 1) smooths the novelty curve; standard FFT and buffer attrs; `@features <buf>` writes the novelty curve. Use to extract a continuous novelty signal from a buffer for offline visualisation, thresholding, or downstream slicing.

fluid.bufnoveltyslice~.use_when: Buffer-based novelty slicer — segments a buffer at points of structural change. Same `@algorithm` / `@kernelsize` / `@filtersize` controls as bufnoveltyfeature~ plus `@indices <buf>` for slice points and a threshold attr. Use for music-structure segmentation (sections, phrases) rather than note-level onsets — finds change-points in a similarity matrix.

fluid.bufonsetfeature~.use_when: Spectral-change onset curve computed over a buffer. `@source`, `@startframe`, `@numframes`, `@startchan`, `@numchans`; `@features <buf>` receives the curve. `@metric` picks one of ten measures: 0 Energy (default), 1 HFC, 2 SpectralFlux, 3 MKL, 4 Itakura-Saito, 5 Cosine, 6 PhaseDev, and further phase/complex-domain variants; `@filtersize` (default 5); `@framedelta` (default 0); standard FFT attributes (`@fftsettings <window> <hop> <fft>`, `@maxfftsize`). `bang` runs, `cancel` stops. Use to inspect or custom-threshold the detection function offline.

fluid.bufonsetslice~.use_when: Spectral-change onset slicer on a buffer: writes slice points to `@indices <buf>`. `@source`, `@startframe`, `@numframes`, `@startchan`, `@numchans`. `@threshold` (default 0.5), `@metric` (ten measures, 0 Energy default, 2 SpectralFlux, 5 Cosine, …), `@filtersize` (default 5), `@framedelta` (default 0), `@minslicelength` (default 2), standard FFT attributes (`@fftsettings <window> <hop> <fft>`, `@maxfftsize`). `bang` runs, `cancel` stops. The indices buffer feeds fluid.bufcompose~ or per-slice analysis loops.

fluid.bufpitch~.use_when: Pitch and confidence descriptor on a buffer, frame by frame. `@source`, `@startframe`, `@numframes`, `@startchan`, `@numchans` choose the region; `@features <buf>` receives two channels per source channel (pitch, confidence). `@algorithm` 0 = cepstrum, 1 = harmonic product spectrum, 2 = YinFFT (default); `@minfreq` / `@maxfreq` (defaults 20 / 10000); `@select`; `@unit`; standard FFT attributes (`@fftsettings <window> <hop> <fft>`, `@maxfftsize`). `bang` runs, `cancel` stops. Follow with fluid.bufstats~ to get one pitch per slice.

fluid.bufscale~.use_when: Linear remap of buffer values to a new range. `@inputlow` / `@inputhigh` define source range; output range via destination attrs (consult refpage); `@clipping 1` clips outliers; standard buffer addressing. Use to normalise buffer amplitude or rescale a feature curve buffer to a known range before downstream processing.

fluid.bufselectevery~.digest: Extract every N samples / channels from a buffer
fluid.bufselectevery~.use_when: Decimate — extract every Nth sample/channel from a buffer. `@framehop` (default 1) sets sample stride; `@chanhop` (default 1) sets channel stride; `@destination <buf>` for output, plus standard buffer addressing. Use for downsampling without filtering or to extract one channel of a multichannel buffer.

fluid.bufselect~.digest: Select and copy specific values from a buffer
fluid.bufselect~.use_when: Extract specific samples or channels from a buffer by index. `@indices` (list of frame indices, default [-1] = all) and `@channels` (list of channel indices, default [-1] = all); `@source` / `@destination`. Use to copy out an arbitrary subset of a buffer's data — e.g. extract only frames at known slice points into a corpus buffer.

fluid.bufsinefeature~.use_when: Sinusoidal peak tracking on a buffer — extract sinusoidal partial tracks. Constructor arg: `<numpeaks>`. `@detectionthreshold` (default -96 dB) gates peak detection; `@frequency <buf>` and `@magnitude <buf>` name output buffers; `@frequnit` and `@magunit` select Hz vs MIDI vs raw and dB vs linear; standard FFT and buffer attrs. Use for harmonic analysis, partial extraction, or as input to sinusoidal resynthesis.

fluid.bufsines~.use_when: Sinusoidal modelling and resynthesis on a buffer — separates audio into sinusoidal partials and a residual. `@detectionthreshold` (default -96 dB) gates peaks; `@birthlowthreshold` / `@birthhighthreshold` control track birth (-24 / -60 dB); `@bandwidth` (default 76 cents) sets tracking width; standard FFT and buffer attrs plus output buffer attrs (sinusoids and residual — consult refpage). Use for high-quality time-stretch/pitch-shift, harmonic isolation, or to extract just the inharmonic residual.

fluid.bufspectralshape~.digest: Seven Spectral Shape Descriptors on a Buffer
fluid.bufspectralshape~.use_when: Seven spectral-shape descriptors on a buffer in one pass: centroid, spread, skewness, kurtosis, rolloff, flatness, crest. `@minfreq` / `@maxfreq` constrain band; standard FFT and buffer attrs; `@features <buf>` writes a 7-column-per-frame analysis curve. Use as a one-stop offline timbral feature extractor — much cheaper than chaining seven separate descriptors.

fluid.bufstats~.digest: Statistically summarise a time series in a Buffer
fluid.bufstats~.use_when: Summarizes each channel of a buffer (usually a per-frame analysis) into seven statistics: mean, std, skewness, kurtosis, low, mid and high percentiles. `@stats <buf>` receives the result; `@select` chooses which statistics (default all seven); `@low` / `@middle` / `@high` set the percentiles (defaults 0, 50, 100); `@numderivs` (0–2) adds the same statistics for first and second derivatives; `@weights <buf>` weights frames (e.g. by loudness); `@outlierscutoff` drops outliers. `@source`, `@startframe`, `@numframes`, `@startchan`, `@numchans`. `bang` runs. Standard step between per-frame analysis and one data point per slice; follow with fluid.bufflatten~ before adding to a dataset.

fluid.bufstft~.digest: Perform a Short-Time Fourier Transform on one channel of a buffer
fluid.bufstft~.use_when: Short-time Fourier transform on one channel of a buffer. `@inverse 0/1` selects forward/inverse; `@magnitude <buf>` writes magnitudes (consult refpage for phase output too); `@padding` adds analysis padding; standard FFT and buffer addressing attrs. Use when you need direct STFT magnitudes/phases for custom analysis without writing a pfft~ subpatcher.

fluid.bufthreaddemo~.digest: A Tutorial Object to Experiment with Multithreading in FluidBuf* Objects
fluid.bufthreaddemo~.use_when: Tutorial object demonstrating multithreading in FluidBuf* objects. Tracks job time in `@time` and result symbol in `@result`. Skip in production — use only for learning the FluCoMa threading model.

fluid.bufthresh~.use_when: Gate processor for buffers — zero values below a threshold (consult refpage for threshold attr name). `@source` / `@destination`, plus standard buffer addressing. Use to clean low-level noise from a feature curve buffer or signal buffer before downstream analysis.

fluid.buftransientslice~.use_when: Transient-based slicer on a buffer — segments at sharp transients via order-statistic filtering. `@blocksize` (default 256) sets analysis block; `@order` (default 20) is autoregressive order; `@padsize` adds boundary padding; `@clumplength` (default 25) merges nearby transients; `@minslicelength` (default 1000) suppresses short slices; `@indices <buf>` writes slice points. Use for percussive note segmentation — complements onsetslice~ (spectral) and ampslice~ (amplitude).

fluid.buftransients~.use_when: Transient extractor on a buffer — separates transient and tonal components via AR modelling. Same `@blocksize` / `@order` / `@padsize` / `@clumplength` controls as buftransientslice~ plus output buffer attrs (transients, residual — consult refpage). Use to isolate clicks/attacks for separate processing or to remove them from a recording.

fluid.chroma~.digest: A histogram of pitch classes in Realtime
fluid.chroma~.use_when: Realtime pitch-class histogram. Constructor arg: `<numchroma>`. `@minfreq` / `@maxfreq`; `@maxnumchroma` caps allocation; `@normalize 0/1`; standard FFT attrs. `reset` clears state. Output is a chroma vector signal. Use for live key/chord detection or harmonic-aware control.

fluid.concataudiofiles.use_when: Concatenate audio files into one buffer. `@destination <buf>` names the output; send `list <file-paths>` to concatenate. Use as a corpus-prep utility — combine many short files into one long buffer with known segment boundaries (track the boundaries separately for indexing).

fluid.datasetquery~.use_when: Query/filter a FluidDataSet. Build query with `addcolumn <int>` (include a column), `addrange <start> <count>` (include a range), `filter <col> <condition> <value>` (predicate), `and <col> <condition> <value>` (chain conditions), `limit <n>` (cap result size); `clear` resets the query. Use to extract subsets of a dataset (e.g. all points within a feature range) before clustering or classification.

fluid.dataset~.digest: A set of data associated with identifiers.
fluid.dataset~.use_when: Dictionary-like container for ML feature vectors keyed by identifier. Constructor arg: `<name>`. Add/remove with `addpoint <id> <buf>` / `deletepoint <id>` (each point is one row, length determined by buffer size); `frombuffer <buf> <transpose> <labelset>` bulk-loads from a buffer; `dump` for full state; `cols` reports column count; `clear` empties. Use as the data substrate for FluCoMa's ML algorithms (kmeans, knn, mlp, pca, umap) — replaces ad-hoc coll/dict structures.

fluid.gain~.use_when: Realtime gain object whose refpage describes it as a sanity test of the FluCoMa realtime client wrapper. `@gain` multiplies the signal; `reset` exists. No practical use in patches — use `*~` or `live.gain~` for gain.

fluid.grid~.digest: Constrain a 2D DataSet into a Grid.
fluid.grid~.use_when: Constrain a 2D dataset to a regular grid. `@axis` selects which axis to grid first (0 or 1); `@extent` sets grid resolution; `@oversample` increases grid density. `fittransform <src> <dst>` fits and writes; `refer <name>` references an existing dataset by name. Use to snap clustered/embedded points to grid cells for sequencer-like or pad-like corpus browsing.

fluid.hpss~.digest: Harmonic-Percussive Source Separation Using Median Filtering
fluid.hpss~.use_when: Realtime harmonic-percussive source separation by median filtering. Constructor args: `<harmfiltersize> <percfiltersize>`. `@harmfiltersize` (default 17, odd, measured in spectral frames over time) and `@percfiltersize` (default 31, odd, measured in spectral bins across frequency) set the filter lengths; `@maxharmfiltersize` / `@maxpercfiltersize` reserve room for later changes. `@maskingmode` 0 soft masks (default, fewest artefacts), 1 binary masks (cleaner split, more artefacts, uses `@harmthresh`), 2 soft masks with a third residual stream (uses `@harmthresh` and `@percthresh`). standard FFT attributes (`@fftsettings <window> <hop> <fft>`, `@maxfftsize`). Outlets carry the harmonic, percussive and (mode 2) residual signals. The help notes a bigger harmonic filter adds latency. Offline version: fluid.bufhpss~.

fluid.jit.plotter.use_when: Jitter-accelerated 2D plotter for very large datasets. 2 inlets / 2 outlets (UI events). Configure with `colorscheme <name>`, `bgcolor <r> <g> <b> <a>`, `panfactor <factor>`; mark a point with `highlight <id>` and `highlightscale <scale>`; `clear` empties. Use when fluid.plotter is too slow for datasets with thousands of points — visualising a UMAP embedding of a corpus, or scatter-plotting hundreds of slices.

fluid.kdtree~.digest: Efficient lookup of data using a k-d tree.
fluid.kdtree~.use_when: K-d tree for efficient nearest-neighbour lookup on a FluidDataSet. Constructor arg: `<name>`. `fit <dataset>` builds the tree; `knearest <buf> <k?>` finds k nearest neighbours of a query buffer; `knearestdist <buf> <k?>` returns distances too; `@numneighbours` (default 1) and `@radius` set defaults; `cols` / `dump` / `clear` for inspection. Use when you need fast NN queries on a large dataset (corpus browsing by feature similarity) — much faster than fluid.dist for large N.

fluid.kmeans~.use_when: K-means clustering on a FluidDataSet. Constructor arg: `<name>`. `fit <dataset>` learns clusters; `fitpredict <dataset> <labelset>` learns and assigns each point to its cluster; `fittransform <src> <dst>` writes per-point distance-to-centroids; `@numclusters` (default 4), `@maxiter` (default 100). Use to group similar items in a corpus into k clusters — basic unsupervised classification.

fluid.knnclassifier~.use_when: K-nearest-neighbours classifier. Constructor arg: `<name>`. `fit <dataset> <labelset>` trains on labelled data; `predict <dataset> <labelset>` classifies new points; `@numneighbours` (default 3), `@weight 1` enables distance-weighted voting; `load <dict>` restores a saved model. Use for labelled-corpus classification — given a feature vector, predict which class it belongs to.

fluid.knnregressor~.use_when: K-nearest-neighbours regression. Constructor arg: `<name>`. `fit <source> <target>` trains; `predict <source> <target>` predicts continuous values; `@numneighbours` (default 3), `@weight 1` enables distance weighting. Use to predict continuous values (synthesis parameters) from a feature vector blended from k nearest training points — feature-driven cross-synthesis.

fluid.labelset~.digest: A set of labels associated with identifiers.
fluid.labelset~.use_when: Container for string labels keyed by identifier. Constructor arg: `<name>`. `addlabel <id> <label>` / `deletelabel <id>` to populate; `getids <labelset>` queries; `cols` / `dump` / `clear` for inspection. Use alongside fluid.dataset~ to attach class labels to feature vectors for supervised ML.

fluid.list2buf.digest: Copy a list to a buffer~
fluid.list2buf.use_when: Copy a Max list into a buffer~. `@destination <buf>`, `@startframe` / `@startchan` for write position; `@autosize 1` resizes destination to fit; `@axis` selects frame-major vs channel-major write. Send `list <values>` to copy. Use as a bridge from list-domain data (feature vectors, control sequences) into audio-domain processing.

fluid.loudness~.digest: A Loudness and True-Peak Descriptor in Realtime
fluid.loudness~.use_when: Realtime ITU-R BS.1770 loudness and true-peak. Constructor arg: `<maxwindowsize>`. `@windowsize` (default 1024), `@hopsize` (default 512), `@kweighting 1` (LUFS), `@truepeak 1`, `@select` lets you pick output channels (`loudness`, `peak`, or both). Use as the standard loudness descriptor for live monitoring or feature extraction — far more accurate than RMS / peak.

fluid.mds~.use_when: Multidimensional scaling of a fluid.dataset~: reduces dimensions while trying to keep distances between points. Only `fittransform <source dataset> <destination dataset>` (and `refer`) exist — it has no separate fit/transform, so it cannot place new points later; use fluid.umap~ or fluid.pca~ for that. `@numdimensions` (default 2); `@distancemetric` 0 Manhattan, 1 Euclidean (default), 2 squared Euclidean, 3 Minkowski max, 4 Minkowski min, 5 symmetric Kullback-Leibler.

fluid.melbands~.digest: A Perceptually Spread Spectral Contour Descriptor
fluid.melbands~.use_when: Realtime mel-band spectral descriptor. Constructor arg: `<numbands>`. `@minfreq` (default 20), `@maxfreq` (default 20000); `@normalize 1` for normalised output; `@maxnumbands` caps allocation; standard FFT attrs. Use for live perceptually-spaced spectral analysis.

fluid.mfcc~.digest: Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients as Spectral Descriptors in Realtime
fluid.mfcc~.use_when: Realtime MFCC. Constructor args: `<numcoeffs> <numbands>` (typical: 13 coeffs from 40 bands). Same `@minfreq`/`@maxfreq`/`@maxnum*` controls as fluid.melbands~ plus standard FFT attrs. Use for live timbral feature extraction — feeds into fluid.knnclassifier~ / fluid.mlpclassifier~ for live classification.

fluid.mlpclassifier~.use_when: Multi-layer perceptron classifier. Constructor arg: `<name>`. `fit <dataset> <labelset>` trains, `predict <dataset> <labelset>` labels a whole dataset, `predictpoint <buf>` labels one live point. `@hiddenlayers` (default 3 3), `@activation` 0 identity, 1 sigmoid, 2 relu (default), 3 tanh; `@learnrate` 0.01, `@momentum` 0.5, `@batchsize` 50, `@maxiter` 1000, `@validation` 0.2 (defaults). Changing layers or activation resets training. `write` / `read` save and load the model. Scale inputs first (fluid.normalize~ or fluid.standardize~). Use when fluid.knnclassifier~ boundaries are too crude.

fluid.mlpregressor~.use_when: Multi-layer perceptron regression. Constructor arg: `<name>`. `fit <source> <target>` trains a non-linear mapping between two datasets; `predict <source> <target>` evaluates. Same `@hiddenlayers`, `@activation`, `@learnrate`, `@momentum 0.9` (default), `@batchsize`, `@maxiter` controls as mlpclassifier. Use for non-linear feature-to-control mappings — ML-driven cross-synthesis, gesture-to-parameter learning.

fluid.nmffilter~.digest: Realtime Non-Negative Matrix Factorisation with Fixed Bases
fluid.nmffilter~.use_when: Realtime NMF filtering — uses pre-trained bases to filter incoming audio. Constructor arg: `<maxcomponents>`. `@bases <buf>` (required) names the pre-trained bases buffer; `@iterations` (default 10) sets per-frame NMF iterations; `@maxcomponents` (default 20). Use for live source separation when bases are learned offline (via fluid.bufnmf~) and applied to new audio.

fluid.nmfmatch~.digest: Realtime Non-Negative Matrix Factorisation with Fixed Bases
fluid.nmfmatch~.use_when: Realtime NMF matching — outputs activation strength of pre-trained bases on incoming audio. Same args/attrs as fluid.nmffilter~ but the output is per-base activation rather than filtered audio. Use to detect 'how much of each template is present' in live audio — pattern recognition, instrument identification by spectral signature.

fluid.nmfmorph~.use_when: Spectral morph between sounds via NMF bases. `@source <buf>` and a second-source attr (consult refpage); `@activations <buf>` provides the base-activation pattern; `@interpolation` (0.–1.) drives morph; `@autoassign 1` auto-pairs bases by similarity; standard FFT attrs. Use for spectral morphing constrained to a learned dictionary of components — more controllable than free spectral morphing.

fluid.normalize~.use_when: Linearly normalise a FluidDataSet to `[@min, @max]` (default [0, 1]). Constructor arg: `<name>`. `fit <dataset>` learns range; `fittransform <src> <dst>` learns and writes; `inversetransform <src> <dst>` reverses. Use to rescale feature columns before ML — required preprocessing for many algorithms.

fluid.noveltyfeature~.use_when: Realtime novelty curve. Constructor args: `<kernelsize> <filtersize>`. Same `@algorithm` / `@kernelsize` / `@filtersize` controls as fluid.bufnoveltyfeature~ plus standard FFT attrs. Use for live detection of structural change (section transitions) rather than note onsets.

fluid.noveltyslice~.use_when: Realtime novelty-based slicer. Same controls as fluid.noveltyfeature~ plus a threshold attr. Use for live segmentation at structural boundaries — phrase or section endpoints rather than notes.

fluid.onsetfeature~.use_when: Realtime spectral-change onset curve (the detection function behind fluid.onsetslice~). `@metric` picks one of ten measures: 0 Energy (default), 1 HFC, 2 SpectralFlux, 3 MKL, 4 Itakura-Saito, 5 Cosine, 6 PhaseDev, and further phase/complex-domain variants; `@filtersize` (default 5) smooths; `@framedelta` (default 0) sets the comparison distance; standard FFT attributes (`@fftsettings <window> <hop> <fft>`, `@maxfftsize`). Use when you want to threshold or display the curve yourself.

fluid.onsetslice~.use_when: Realtime spectral-change onset slicer: outputs a trigger when the onset curve crosses `@threshold` (default 0.5). `@metric` picks one of ten measures (0 Energy default, 1 HFC, 2 SpectralFlux, 3 MKL, 4 Itakura-Saito, 5 Cosine, 6 PhaseDev, …); `@filtersize` (default 5); `@framedelta` (default 0); `@minslicelength` (default 2) suppresses slices that are too close; standard FFT attributes (`@fftsettings <window> <hop> <fft>`, `@maxfftsize`). Catches pitched onsets that amplitude slicers (fluid.ampslice~) miss. `reset` clears state.

fluid.pca~.use_when: Principal component analysis on a FluidDataSet — linear dimensionality reduction. Constructor arg: `<name>`. `fit <dataset>` learns components; `fittransform <src> <dst>` projects; `inversetransform <src> <dst>` reconstructs. `@numdimensions 2` (default) sets target; `@whiten 0/1` toggles whitening (unit variance per component). Use for linear dim reduction when your features have strong linear structure — fast, interpretable, deterministic.

fluid.pitch~.use_when: Realtime monophonic pitch descriptor: outputs frequency and a 0–1 confidence (how harmonic the frame is). `@algorithm` 0 = cepstrum, 1 = harmonic product spectrum, 2 = YinFFT (default); `@minfreq` (default 20) and `@maxfreq` (default 10000) bound the search; `@select pitch confidence` picks outputs; `@unit` selects Hz or MIDI; standard FFT attributes (`@fftsettings <window> <hop> <fft>`, `@maxfftsize`). Low confidence means noise or polyphony — gate on it before using the pitch. `reset` clears state. Built-in alternative: fzero~. Offline: fluid.bufpitch~.

fluid.plotter.digest: Plot data in a two-dimensional graph.
fluid.plotter.use_when: JSUI 2-D scatter plot for datasets. `setpoint <id> <x> <y>` adds or moves a point; `pointcolor`, `pointsize`, `pointsizescale`, `shape`, `colorscheme` style them; `highlight <id>` marks points; `xrange` / `yrange` / `range` set the view; `bgcolor`; `clear` / `reset`. Outlet 0 reports the mouse position while clicking and dragging (not a point id) — send it to `fluid.kdtree~` to find the nearest point; outlet 1 reports zoom changes. For thousands of points use fluid.jit.plotter.

fluid.robustscale~.digest: Apply Robust Scaling to a FluidDataSet
fluid.robustscale~.use_when: Robust (median/IQR-based) scaling of a FluidDataSet. Constructor arg: `<name>`. `@low 25` and `@high 75` (default = IQR) set percentiles for scaling. `fit` / `fittransform` / `inversetransform` like fluid.normalize~. Use instead of normalize~ when features have outliers — robustscale~ is unaffected by extreme values that would skew min/max-based scaling.

fluid.sinefeature~.use_when: Realtime sinusoidal peak tracking. Constructor arg: `<numpeaks>`. `@detectionthreshold` (default -96 dB) gates peak detection; `@frequnit` and `@magunit` choose Hz vs MIDI and dB vs linear; `@maxnumpeaks` caps allocation; standard FFT attrs. Use for live harmonic analysis or partial-track-driven control.

fluid.sines~.use_when: Realtime sinusoidal modelling and resynthesis — separates input into sinusoidal partials and a residual live. Same `@detectionthreshold`, `@birthlowthreshold` / `@birthhighthreshold`, `@bandwidth` controls as fluid.bufsines~. Use for live time/pitch manipulation, harmonic isolation, or extracting just the residual for noise-only processing.

fluid.skmeans~.use_when: Spherical k-means — clusters using cosine similarity instead of Euclidean distance. Constructor arg: `<name>`. `fit <dataset>` trains; `encode <src> <dst>` projects to cluster activations; `encodepoint <src-buf> <dst-buf>` projects one point; `@numclusters 4`, `@encodingthreshold 0.25`, `@maxiter 100`. Use when feature magnitudes shouldn't matter (only direction), e.g. clustering MFCCs or normalised feature vectors.

fluid.spectralshape~.digest: Seven Spectral Shape Descriptors in Realtime
fluid.spectralshape~.use_when: Realtime version of fluid.bufspectralshape~ — seven spectral descriptors in one object. `@minfreq` / `@maxfreq` constrain band; `@power 0/1` switches power vs magnitude domain; `@rolloffpercent 95` (default) sets the rolloff threshold; standard FFT attrs. Use for live timbral feature extraction.

fluid.standardize~.use_when: Standardise a FluidDataSet (zero mean, unit variance per column). Constructor arg: `<name>`. `fit` / `fittransform` / `inversetransform` like normalize~ / robustscale~. Use as the standard preprocessing for ML algorithms that assume standardised input (PCA, MLP, etc.).

fluid.stats.digest: Rolling mean and standard deviation on control inputs
fluid.stats.use_when: Rolling mean and standard deviation on control-rate inputs. Constructor arg: `<inputsize>`. `@history` (default 2) sets window length; `@autosize 1` adapts to incoming list size. `clear` / `reset` zero state. Use to smooth or summarise a feature stream before downstream processing — list-domain version of average~ for control-rate work.

fluid.stftpass~.use_when: FFT/IFFT roundtrip with no processing. Standard FFT attrs (`@fftsettings`, `@maxfftsize`). Use as a baseline / sanity-check or as a starting template when building a custom spectral processor — the inputs/outputs and threading model match the rest of the FluCoMa real-time objects.

fluid.transientslice~.use_when: Realtime transient-based slicer. Same `@blocksize` / `@order` / `@padsize` / `@clumplength` / `@minslicelength` controls as fluid.buftransientslice~ plus `@skew` (default 0.0) for asymmetric detection and a threshold attr. Use for live percussive segmentation; complements fluid.onsetslice~ (spectral) and fluid.ampslice~ (amplitude).

fluid.transients~.use_when: Realtime transient extractor — separates transient and tonal components live via AR modelling. Same `@blocksize` / `@order` / `@padsize` / `@clumplength` / `@skew` / `@threshback` controls as fluid.buftransients~. Use for live click/attack isolation or removal — apply different processing to transients vs steady-state.

fluid.umap~.digest: Dimensionality Reduction with Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection
fluid.umap~.use_when: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection — non-linear dimensionality reduction. Constructor arg: `<name>`. `@numdimensions 2` (default) sets target; `@numneighbours 15` controls local-vs-global balance (lower = more local); `@mindist 0.1` controls cluster tightness; `@iterations 200`, `@learnrate 0.1` are SGD knobs. `fit <dataset>` and `fittransform <src> <dst>`; `load <dict>` restores. Use to embed a high-dim feature space in 2D/3D preserving local structure — typically the best embedding for browsing a sound corpus.

fluid.waveform~.use_when: JSUI display for buffers in FluCoMa workflows, built from layers. `waveform <buf>` draws a waveform; `features <buf>` overlays a feature curve (e.g. from fluid.bufonsetfeature~); `slices <buf>` draws slice markers from an indices buffer (they can be moved, added and deleted by hand); `image <buf>` draws a 2-D buffer such as a spectrogram; `remove <layer>` removes a layer; `clear` resets; `bgcolor` sets the background. Use instead of waveform~ when you want slices and analysis curves layered over audio.

fl.!=~.digest: Compares frame values for inequality (returns 1 or 0)
fl.!=~.use_when: Compares frame values for inequality (returns 1 or 0). Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.!~.digest: Calculates the logical not of each value in the input frame
fl.!~.use_when: Calculates the logical not of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.%~.digest: Calculates the left input frame values modulo the right input frame values
fl.%~.use_when: Calculates the left input frame values modulo the right input frame values. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.&&~.digest: Calculates the logical and of the left and right input frame values
fl.&&~.use_when: Calculates the logical and of the left and right input frame values. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.*~.digest: Multiplies values in the two input frames
fl.*~.use_when: Multiplies values in the two input frames. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.+~.digest: Adds values in the two input frames
fl.+~.use_when: Adds values in the two input frames. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.-~.digest: Subtracts the right input frame values from the left input frame values
fl.-~.use_when: Subtracts the right input frame values from the left input frame values. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl./~.digest: Divides the left input frame values by the right input frame values
fl./~.use_when: Divides the left input frame values by the right input frame values. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.<=~.digest: Compares input frames using a less than or equal to operation (returns 1 or 0)
fl.<=~.use_when: Compares input frames using a less than or equal to operation (returns 1 or 0). Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.<~.digest: Compares input frames using a less than operation (returns 1 or 0)
fl.<~.use_when: Compares input frames using a less than operation (returns 1 or 0). Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.==~.digest: Compares frame values for equality (returns 1 or 0)
fl.==~.use_when: Compares frame values for equality (returns 1 or 0). Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.>=~.digest: Compares input frames using a greater than or equal to operation (returns 1 or 0)
fl.>=~.use_when: Compares input frames using a greater than or equal to operation (returns 1 or 0). Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.>~.digest: Compares input frames using a greater than operation (returns 1 or 0)
fl.>~.use_when: Compares input frames using a greater than operation (returns 1 or 0). Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.abs~.digest: Calculates the absolute value of each value in the input frame
fl.abs~.use_when: Calculates the absolute value of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.accumpos~.digest: Finds the index where the cumulative sum reaches a specified percentage of its total
