fl.accumpos~.use_when: Finds where a frame's running sum reaches a set percentage of its total. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/percentage`, `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.acosh~.digest: Calculates the hyperbolic arccosine of each value in the input frame
fl.acosh~.use_when: Calculates the hyperbolic arccosine of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.acos~.digest: Calculates the arccosine (in radians) of each value in the input frame
fl.acos~.use_when: Calculates the arccosine (in radians) of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.asinh~.digest: Calculates the hyperbolic arcsine of each value in the input frame
fl.asinh~.use_when: Calculates the hyperbolic arcsine of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.asin~.digest: Calculates the arcsine (in radians) of each value in the input frame
fl.asin~.use_when: Calculates the arcsine (in radians) of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.atan2~.digest: Calculates the arctangent using two arguments (left operand is y, right operand is x)
fl.atan2~.use_when: Calculates the arctangent using two arguments (left operand is y, right operand is x). Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.atanh~.digest: Calculates the hyperbolic arctangent of each value in the input frame
fl.atanh~.use_when: Calculates the hyperbolic arctangent of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.atan~.digest: Calculates the arctangent (in radians) of each value in the input frame
fl.atan~.use_when: Calculates the arctangent (in radians) of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.audiotrigger~.digest: Schedules frames based on non-zero audio input
fl.audiotrigger~.use_when: Scheduler that emits an empty trigger frame for every non-zero input sample (not a level threshold). Feed it an impulse train or a gated signal (e.g. clicks) to start frames at audio-determined times. As a scheduler it accepts `@id`, `@rt`, `@buffer` and, in non-realtime mode, `reset` / `process <samples>`.

fl.biquadcoeff~.use_when: Calculates biquad filter coefficients from frequency, gain and Q. The filter mode is set by the mode parameter. Filter settings may be made either via parameters or per sample via inputs. The type of input and output is determined by the coefficients parameter. If set to dynamic then inputs are created for per sample values. Output will be at least one sample or as long as the longest input frame. Frames of per sample values are padded to length with their final value if required. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/freq`, `/gain`, `/qs`, `/mode`, `/coefficients`.

fl.biquad~.digest: Applies a biquad filter to the input
fl.biquad~.use_when: Filters each frame with a biquad using given coefficients. Output is the same length as the input. Filter settings may be made either via parameters or per sample via inputs. The dynamic parameter is set to create the inputs for per sample values. Frames of per sample values are padded to length with their final value if required. Additional values are ignored. In this mode the parameter value is used if no corresponding input is provided. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/a1`, `/a2`, `/b0`, `/b1`, `/b2`, `/dynamic`, `/reset`.

fl.cartopol~.digest: Converts from cartesian values at the inputs to polar values at the outputs
fl.cartopol~.use_when: Converts cartesian frames (x, y and optionally z) to polar or spherical frames (radius and angles). `/dimensions` chooses 2D or 3D; `/angles` sets radians or degrees. Outputs match the longest input; shorter inputs are zero-padded. In spectral work, feed the real and imaginary outputs of fl.fft~ to get magnitude and phase; convert back with fl.poltocar~.

fl.cbrt~.digest: Calculates the cube root of each value in the input frame
fl.cbrt~.use_when: Calculates the cube root of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.ceil~.digest: Calculates the ceiling function of each value in the input frame
fl.ceil~.use_when: Calculates the ceiling function of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.centroid~.digest: Calculates the centroid of the input frame
fl.centroid~.use_when: Calculates the centroid (center of mass) of a frame. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.chain~.digest: Schedules frames in the future at times specified times in the input frame
fl.chain~.use_when: Schedules future frames at times listed in an input frame. The output is an empty trigger frame. Inputs interact with previously scheduled frames according to time and mode parameters. The remaining count output can be used to track the number of currently scheduled frames. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/units`, `/time`, `/mode`. A scheduler: it can start a network. Attributes `@id` (context), `@rt`, `@buffer`; in non-realtime mode send `reset` then `process <samples>`.

fl.chop~.digest: Chops input frames into equally sized output frames of a specified size
fl.chop~.use_when: Cuts a frame into several equal-length frames. The size can be set in samples or as a ratio of the length of the input frame. Outputs are formed by chopping the input into consecutive slices of the same length. Any additional input values once all outputs are formed are ignored. If there are insufficient input values to complete all outputs later outputs will be shortened. It is possible for the final output(s) to be empty in this case. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/num_outs`, `/size`, `/units`.

fl.clip~.digest: Clips the incoming frame to the range delimited by the two parameters
fl.clip~.use_when: Clips the incoming frame to the range delimited by the two parameters. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.combinetags~.digest: Combines a number of tagged input frames into a single tagged output frame
fl.combinetags~.use_when: Merges several tagged frames into one tagged frame. The number of inputs is set using a parameter. All inputs trigger output. Tagged frames arriving asynchronously are sent to the output. Tagged frames arriving synchronously are combined at the output. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/num_ins`.

fl.complex.*~.digest: Multiplies complex values in the two pairs of input frames
fl.complex.*~.use_when: Multiplies complex values in the two pairs of input frames. FrameLib complex-frame analogue of `fl.times~` (see package_concepts.md FrameLib section for complex-frame protocol).

fl.complex.+~.digest: Adds complex values in the two pairs of input frames
fl.complex.+~.use_when: Adds complex values in the two pairs of input frames. FrameLib complex-frame analogue of `fl.plus~` (see package_concepts.md FrameLib section for complex-frame protocol).

fl.complex.-~.digest: Subtracts complex values in the right input frame pair from those in the left pair
fl.complex.-~.use_when: Subtracts complex values in the right input frame pair from those in the left pair. FrameLib complex-frame analogue of `fl.minus~` (see package_concepts.md FrameLib section for complex-frame protocol).

fl.complex./~.digest: Divides complex values in the left pair of input frames by those in the right pair
fl.complex./~.use_when: Divides complex values in the left pair of input frames by those in the right pair. FrameLib complex-frame analogue of `fl.divide~` (see package_concepts.md FrameLib section for complex-frame protocol).

fl.complex.conj~.digest: Calculates the complex conjugate of each complex value at the inputs
fl.complex.conj~.use_when: Calculates the complex conjugate of each complex value at the inputs. FrameLib complex-frame analogue of `fl.conj~` (see package_concepts.md FrameLib section for complex-frame protocol).

fl.complex.cosh~.digest: Calculates the hyperbolic cosine of each complex value at the inputs
fl.complex.cosh~.use_when: Calculates the hyperbolic cosine of each complex value at the inputs. FrameLib complex-frame analogue of `fl.cosh~` (see package_concepts.md FrameLib section for complex-frame protocol).

fl.complex.cos~.digest: Calculates the cosine of each complex value at the inputs
fl.complex.cos~.use_when: Calculates the cosine of each complex value at the inputs. FrameLib complex-frame analogue of `fl.cos~` (see package_concepts.md FrameLib section for complex-frame protocol).

fl.complex.expr~.digest: Calculates the result of a mathematical expression involving complex numbers
fl.complex.expr~.use_when: Like fl.expr~ for complex numbers: each input and the output are real/imaginary frame pairs. Inputs are written `in1`, `in2` … (help: `fl.complex.expr~ sinh(in1) * log(in1)`). Parameters `/expression`, `/mismatch`, `/trigger_ins` (creation only). Use for spectral maths on the paired outputs of fl.fft~.

fl.complex.exp~.digest: Calculates the exponent base e (e^x) of each complex value at the inputs
fl.complex.exp~.use_when: Calculates the exponent base e (e^x) of each complex value at the inputs. FrameLib complex-frame analogue of `fl.exp~` (see package_concepts.md FrameLib section for complex-frame protocol).

fl.complex.log10~.digest: Calculates the logarithm base 10 of each complex value at the inputs
fl.complex.log10~.use_when: Calculates the logarithm base 10 of each complex value at the inputs. FrameLib complex-frame analogue of `fl.log10~` (see package_concepts.md FrameLib section for complex-frame protocol).

fl.complex.log~.digest: Calculates the logarithm base e of each complex value at the inputs
fl.complex.log~.use_when: Calculates the logarithm base e of each complex value at the inputs. FrameLib complex-frame analogue of `fl.log~` (see package_concepts.md FrameLib section for complex-frame protocol).

fl.complex.pow~.digest: Raises left operand values to the power of right operand values (both complex)
fl.complex.pow~.use_when: Raises left operand values to the power of right operand values (both complex). FrameLib complex-frame analogue of `fl.pow~` (see package_concepts.md FrameLib section for complex-frame protocol).

fl.complex.sinh~.digest: Calculates the hyperbolic sine of each complex value at the inputs
fl.complex.sinh~.use_when: Calculates the hyperbolic sine of each complex value at the inputs. FrameLib complex-frame analogue of `fl.sinh~` (see package_concepts.md FrameLib section for complex-frame protocol).

fl.complex.sin~.digest: Calculates the sine of each complex value at the inputs
fl.complex.sin~.use_when: Calculates the sine of each complex value at the inputs. FrameLib complex-frame analogue of `fl.sin~` (see package_concepts.md FrameLib section for complex-frame protocol).

fl.complex.sqrt~.digest: Calculates the square root of each complex value at the inputs
fl.complex.sqrt~.use_when: Calculates the square root of each complex value at the inputs. FrameLib complex-frame analogue of `fl.sqrt~` (see package_concepts.md FrameLib section for complex-frame protocol).

fl.complex.tanh~.digest: Calculates the hyperbolic tangent of each complex value at the inputs
fl.complex.tanh~.use_when: Calculates the hyperbolic tangent of each complex value at the inputs. FrameLib complex-frame analogue of `fl.tanh~` (see package_concepts.md FrameLib section for complex-frame protocol).

fl.complex.tan~.digest: Calculates the tangent of each complex value at the inputs
fl.complex.tan~.use_when: Calculates the tangent of each complex value at the inputs. FrameLib complex-frame analogue of `fl.tan~` (see package_concepts.md FrameLib section for complex-frame protocol).

fl.constant~.use_when: Outputs a single constant such as pi or e, optionally scaled. Output is a single value. The constant can be multiplied before output as set by the multiplier parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/constant`, `/multiplier`.

fl.contextcontrol~.digest: Controls a named context via Max messages.
fl.contextcontrol~.use_when: Controls an existing FrameLib context without processing frames itself. Point it at the context with `@id <name>` (matching the scheduler's `@id`). Messages: `multithread 1/0` (off by default), `timeout <relative> <absolute>` (no arguments turns timeouts off), `export <classname> <folder>` (writes C++ code for the network). Realtime versus non-realtime is not set here but with each network's `@rt` attribute; non-realtime time is advanced by sending `reset` and `process <samples>` to schedulers and IO objects such as fl.interval~ and fl.sink~.

fl.convert~.digest: Converts the input vector according to a specified conversion
fl.convert~.use_when: Converts frame values between units such as dB, MIDI and frequency. The output length matches the input length. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/mode`.

fl.convolve~.digest: Convolves two inputs (either real or complex)
fl.convolve~.use_when: Convolves two real or complex frames. The output length depends on the edges parameter, which sets the edge behaviour. Output length is M + N - 1 for linear convolution (M and N are the input lengths). For other edge behaviours the output length is the maximum of M and N. In complex mode pairs of inputs and outputs are used to represent complex values. If one of a pair of inputs is shorter than the other it is zero padded to match. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/max_length`, `/mode`, `/edges`.

fl.copysign~.digest: Copys the signs of the right input frame onto the magnitudes of the left input frame
fl.copysign~.use_when: Copys the signs of the right input frame onto the magnitudes of the left input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.correlate~.digest: Correlates two inputs (either real or complex)
fl.correlate~.use_when: Cross-correlates two real or complex frames. The output length depends on the edges parameter, which sets the edge behaviour. Output length is M + N - 1 for linear correlation (M and N are the input lengths). For other edge behaviours the output length is the maximum of M and N. In complex mode pairs of inputs and outputs are used to represent complex values. If one of a pair of inputs is shorter than the other it is zero padded to match. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/max_length`, `/mode`, `/edges`.

fl.cosh~.digest: Calculates the hyperbolic cosine of each value in the input frame
fl.cosh~.use_when: Calculates the hyperbolic cosine of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.cos~.digest: Calculates the cosine (for arguments in radians) of each value in the input frame
fl.cos~.use_when: Calculates the cosine (for arguments in radians) of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.crest~.digest: Calculates the crest factor of the input frame
fl.crest~.use_when: Calculates the crest factor (peak over RMS) of a frame. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.diff~.digest: Calculates the absolute differences between values in the two input frames
fl.diff~.use_when: Calculates the absolute differences between values in the two input frames. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.dispatch~.digest: Dispatches multiple inputs dynamically to multiple outputs
fl.dispatch~.use_when: Sends each of several inputs to any of several outputs. Each output can be independently connected to any one input. The number of inputs and outputs is variable. The selected input for each output is changed with a parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/num_ins`, `/num_outs`, `/input_01...32`.

fl.erfc~.digest: Calculates the complimentary error function of each value in the input frame
fl.erfc~.use_when: Calculates the complimentary error function of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.erf~.digest: Calculates the error function of each value in the input frame
fl.erf~.use_when: Calculates the error function of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.exp2~.digest: Calculates the exponent base 2 (2^x) of each value in the input frame
fl.exp2~.use_when: Calculates the exponent base 2 (2^x) of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.expr~.digest: Calculates the result of a mathematical expression
fl.expr~.use_when: Evaluates a math expression element-wise across input frames. Inputs are written `in1`, `in2` … (not `$f1`), e.g. `fl.expr~ in1 * 2 - 1`; the number of inputs follows the expression. Constants e, pi, epsilon, inf; the usual operators; functions such as sin, log, sqrt, abs, pow, min, max, clip, wrap, fold. Parameters `/expression`, `/mismatch` (wrap by default), `/trigger_ins` are creation-only. Constant parts are pre-computed, so one fl.expr~ is efficient and replaces chains of fl.* math objects.

fl.exp~.digest: Calculates the exponent base e (e^x) of each value in the input frame
fl.exp~.use_when: Calculates the exponent base e (e^x) of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.fft~.digest: Calculate the real or complex Fast Fourier Transform of the input(s)
fl.fft~.use_when: Forward FFT of a frame. There is no size parameter: the transform size follows the input frame, zero-padded to a power of two, so set size upstream (e.g. `fl.source~ /length 4096` or fl.window~). `/mode` (creation only): `real` (default; real input, output N/2+1 bins), `complex` (two input frames, real and imaginary), `full_spectrum`. Outputs are separate real and imaginary frames; get magnitude and phase with fl.cartopol~. `/normalise` and `/max_length` are the other parameters. Invert with fl.ifft~ and overlap-add with fl.sink~.

fl.filtertags~.digest: Filters tagged frames using a set of specified tags
fl.filtertags~.use_when: Passes on only the tagged items whose tags match a list. The filtered output contains any items from the input that match the given tags. The residual output contains any items from the input that do not match the given tags. The number of tags can be set explicitly by parameter. Alternatively, it can be set implicitly by the tag parameters present at instantiation. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/num_filters`, `/tag_01...10`.

fl.firphase~.digest: Transform FIR coefficients to preserve the amplitude spectrum but alter the phase
fl.firphase~.use_when: Changes the phase of FIR filter coefficients without changing their amplitude response. The phase can be directly specified using the phase parameter. Output frames will be the length of the FFT size used internally for processing. Inputs which are not a power of two are zero-padded before processing. Additionally the input can be further zero-padded to avoid time aliasing. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/max_length`, `/phase`, `/time_factor`.

fl.flatness~.digest: Calculates the flatness (as a ratio) of the input frame
fl.flatness~.use_when: Calculates the flatness (noisiness) of a frame. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.floor~.digest: Calculates the floor function of each value in the input frame
fl.floor~.use_when: Calculates the floor function of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.fold~.digest: Folds the incoming frame into the range delimited by the two parameters
fl.fold~.use_when: Folds the incoming frame into the range delimited by the two parameters. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.framedelta~.digest: Outputs the deltas between consecutive frames
fl.framedelta~.use_when: Outputs the change in each value since the previous frame. Frames are expected to be of uniform size otherwise the object will reset. The first output frame (and those after a reset) will consist entirely of zero values. The output is the same size as the input.

fl.framemax~.digest: Calculates the maximum value of the input frame
fl.framemax~.use_when: Outputs the largest value in a frame. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.framemin~.digest: Calculates the minimum value of the input frame
fl.framemin~.use_when: Outputs the smallest value in a frame. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.frommax~.use_when: Turns Max messages (int, float, list, anything) into frames. `/mode values` (default) outputs the last received value(s) as a vector; `/mode params` collects messages into one tagged frame, used to set parameters of other FrameLib objects. Output only happens when a frame arrives at the trigger input, so wire a scheduler to it. Counterpart of fl.tomax~.

fl.gaussian~.digest: Generates frames of normally distributed random values
fl.gaussian~.use_when: Generates frames of normally distributed random values. Mean and standard deviation can be set per sample or by parameter. Per-sample mean and standard deviations are passed in by input. The length of the output is dependent on the mode parameter. Output length may be set by parameter or based on that of the trigger input. When input and output lengths are mismatched the result depends on the mismatch parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/mode`, `/length`, `/units`, `/mean`, `/deviation`, `/mismatch`.

fl.geomean~.digest: Calculates the geometric mean of the input frame
fl.geomean~.use_when: Calculates the geometric mean of a frame. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.hypot~.digest: Calculates the length of a hypotenuse given the two operands as the other lengths
fl.hypot~.use_when: Calculates the length of a hypotenuse given the two operands as the other lengths. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.ifft~.digest: Calculate the real or complex inverse Fast Fourier Transform of the inputs (real and imaginary)
fl.ifft~.use_when: Turns real and imaginary spectrum frames back into a time-domain frame. All FFTs use a power of two size, with zero-padding applied at the inputs if necessary. The expected input lengths depend on the mode parameter. The mode selects either real or complex iFFTs and also the input and the output type. In complex mode, real and imaginary values are output as separate frames. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/max_length`, `/normalise`, `/mode`.

fl.info~.digest: Outputs the sample rate, number of channels and length of a specified buffer
fl.info~.use_when: Reports the sample rate, channel count and length of a buffer~. The units for reporting length can be set with the units parameter. If the named buffer is not found all outputs are given as zero. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/buffer`, `/units`.

fl.interval~.digest: Schedules frames at regular intervals set by the interval parameter
fl.interval~.use_when: The usual scheduler at the head of a FrameLib network: emits an empty trigger frame at a regular interval, and nothing downstream runs without a scheduler. Set the period as the first argument or `/interval` (default 64), with `/units` samples, ms, seconds or hz (`fl.interval~ 500 ms`). FrameLib parameters use `/name value`, not `@`; the Max attributes are `@id` (context name), `@rt` (0 = non-realtime) and `@buffer`. `/switchable 1` at creation lets `/on` start and stop it. In non-realtime mode (`@rt 0`) drive it with `reset` then `process <samples>`. Other schedulers: fl.once~, fl.perblock~, fl.audiotrigger~, fl.chain~.

fl.join~.digest: Concatenates all input frames into a single output frame
fl.join~.use_when: Joins several frames end to end into one frame. Each input may trigger output (or not), as set by the triggers_in parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/num_ins`, `/trigger_ins`.

fl.kernelsmooth~.digest: Smooth an input based on a provided smoothing kernel
fl.kernelsmooth~.use_when: Smooths a frame using a supplied smoothing shape. The kernel is interpolated to the specified width(s) to perform smoothing. If the kernel is symmetric only the right-hand side should be provided. The edge behaviour can be set as appropriate for the application. The output is the same length as the frame at the first input. Internally kernels are always stretched across a whole number of samples. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/smooth`, `/scale`, `/symmetric`, `/edges`, `/max_fft`.

fl.kurtosis~.digest: Calculates the kurtosis of the input frame
fl.kurtosis~.use_when: Calculates the kurtosis (peakiness) of a frame. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.lag~.digest: Delay vector type input by a whole number of frames
fl.lag~.use_when: Delays uniform-length frames by a whole number of frames. Frames are expected to be of a uniform length. The output is the same length as the input. If the input length changes then the internal storage is reset. The object can also be reset by sending a frame to the reset input. The start parameter controls behaviour when insufficient frames are stored. The underlength output indicates that insufficient frames are stored. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/max_frames`, `/num_frames`, `/pad`, `/start`.

fl.length~.digest: Calculates the length of the input frame
fl.length~.use_when: Outputs the number of values in a frame. The output is a single value.

fl.log10~.digest: Calculates the logarithm base 10 of each value in the input frame
fl.log10~.use_when: Calculates the logarithm base 10 of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.log2~.digest: Calculates the logarithm base 2 of each value in the input frame
fl.log2~.use_when: Calculates the logarithm base 2 of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.log~.digest: Calculates the logarithm base e of each value in the input frame
fl.log~.use_when: Calculates the logarithm base e of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.lookupstring~.digest: Lookup a specified string from an internally stored list of strings
fl.lookupstring~.use_when: Picks one stored text string by index for tagging. The string can be specified by index or normalised value. The first number at the input is used to specify the string. The number of stored items can be set explicitly by parameter. Alternatively, it can be set implicitly by the parameters present at instantiation. Items may be dynamically updated by parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/num_items`, `/tag`, `/scale`, `/empty`, `/item_01...32`.

fl.lookup~.digest: Lookup values from one input using a table provided at another
fl.lookup~.use_when: Reads values from a table frame at positions given by another frame. The first input is interpreted as the positions to read from the table at the second. The output is the same length as the frame at the first input. The scale, edges and bound parameters control the mapping of the input to the table. The lookup can be performed with different types of interpolation (or none). Only the first input triggers output. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/scale`, `/edges`, `/bound`, `/interp`.

fl.makestring~.digest: Creates a tagged string by concatenating strings and numbers
fl.makestring~.use_when: Builds a tagged string from text and numbers. Items for concatenatation are set as parameters and can be altered dynamically. Numeric inputs are indicated as in1 to inx (where x is the number of inputs created). Only a single number is read from each input, interpreted as an integer. Numbers can be optionally zero-padded. The number of items to concatenate can be set explicitly by parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/num_items`, `/tag`, `/trigger_ins`, `/padding`, `/item_01...10`.

fl.makewindow~.digest: Generates a specified window function across each output frame
fl.makewindow~.use_when: Generates a window shape such as Hann as a frame. The length of the output is dependent on the mode parameter. Output length may be set by parameter or based on that of the trigger input. Gain compensation can be applied using the compensate parameter. The included endpoints are controllable so as to fit different applications. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/mode`, `/length`, `/units`, `/window`, `/exponent`, `/compensate`, `/parameters`, `/endpoints`.

fl.map~.digest: Maps values from input to output via a specified scaling
fl.map~.use_when: Scales frame values from one range to another, with curves. The output length matches the input length. Scaling maps the specified range of input values to a corresponding specified output range. Different shapes and types of scaling are available. Values may be optionally constrained within the specified output range. The values specfying the ranges may be in either order for both input and output. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/mode`, `/in_1`, `/in_2`, `/out_1`, `/out_2`, `/clip`, `/exponent`.

fl.maxpos~.digest: Calculates the index of the maximum value of the input frame
fl.maxpos~.use_when: Outputs the index of the largest value in a frame. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.max~.digest: Calculates the maximums of pairs of values in the two input frames
fl.max~.use_when: Calculates the maximums of pairs of values in the two input frames. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.mean~.digest: Calculates the mean of the input frame
fl.mean~.use_when: Calculates the average of a frame. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.medianfilter~.digest: Applies a median or other specified percentile filter to the input
fl.medianfilter~.use_when: Replaces each value with the median of its neighbours. The default percentile is 50% which returns the median. The output is the same length as the input. Each output value is the specified percentile of the surrouding area in the input. The width of the filtering and the edge behaviour are both controllable. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/width`, `/pad`, `/edges`, `/percentile`.

fl.minpos~.digest: Calculates the index of the minimum value of the input frame
fl.minpos~.use_when: Outputs the index of the smallest value in a frame. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.min~.digest: Calculates the minimums of pairs of values in the two input frames
fl.min~.use_when: Calculates the minimums of pairs of values in the two input frames. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.movingaverage~.digest: Calculates per sample moving averages and standard deviations
fl.movingaverage~.use_when: Tracks a smoothed average and deviation for each value across frames. The moving average and standard deviations are exponentially weighted. An alpha value [0-1] controls the rate of update from static to immediate. Alphas may be set per sample using the corresponding input or by parameters. Parameters allow different alphas when the average increases or decreases. Frames are expected to be of a uniform length. The output is the same length as the input. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/alpha_up`, `/alpha_down`, `/average`, `/deviation`.

fl.multitaper~.digest: Calculates a multitaper power (or amplitude) spectrum from a real input
fl.multitaper~.use_when: Calculates a low-variance power spectrum using multiple tapers. The spectrum is calculated using the sine tapers. All FFTs use a power of two size, with zero-padding applied at the input if necessary. Output frames will be (N / 2) + 1 in length where N is the FFT size used. The number of tapers and their weighting are both controllable. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/max_length`, `/num_tapers`, `/normalise`, `/output`, `/weighting`.

fl.nanfilter~.digest: Filter NaNs from the input either by replacing or by removing them
fl.nanfilter~.use_when: Replaces or removes invalid (NaN) values in a frame. The length of the output depends on the mode parameter. The length of the output will be no longer than the input. The value for replacement can be specified using the value parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/mode`, `/value`.

fl.nonzero~.digest: Outputs the indices of input samples that are non-zero
fl.nonzero~.use_when: Outputs the positions of non-zero values in a frame. The length of the output frame depends on the number of non-zero items in the input. The output is an ordered list of indices for all non-zero input values (counting from zero)

fl.now~.use_when: Outputs the current FrameLib time. Time is reported in the specified units. Output is a single value. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/units`.

fl.once~.digest: Schedules a single frame at the begining of time that lasts forever
fl.once~.use_when: Starts a single frame at the beginning of time. The output is an empty frame. A scheduler: it can start a network. Attributes `@id` (context), `@rt`, `@buffer`; in non-realtime mode send `reset` then `process <samples>`.

fl.onepolezero~.digest: Applies a one-pole with one-zero filter to the input
fl.onepolezero~.use_when: Filters each frame with a one-pole, one-zero filter. Output is the same length as the input. The filter can output a single specifed mode at a time. Alternatively, in multi-output mode all modes are output simultaneously. Filter settings may be made either via parameters or per sample via inputs. The dynamic parameter is set to create the inputs for per sample values. Frames of per sample values are padded to length with their final value if required. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/freq`, `/mode`, `/multi_output`, `/dynamic`, `/reset`.

fl.onepole~.digest: Applies  a one-pole 6dB/octave filter to the input
fl.onepole~.use_when: Filters each frame with a gentle 6 dB per octave filter. Output is the same length as the input. The filter can output a single specifed mode at a time. Alternatively, in multi-output mode all modes are output simultaneously. Filter settings may be made either via parameters or per sample via inputs. The dynamic parameter is set to create the inputs for per sample values. Frames of per sample values are padded to length with their final value if required. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/freq`, `/mode`, `/multi_output`, `/dynamic`, `/reset`.

fl.pack~.digest: Packs multiple frame streams into a multistream output
fl.pack~.use_when: Combines several frame streams into one multistream connection. Inputs may be single stream or multistream. All inputs are concatenated in order, with blank inputs ignored. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/num_ins`.

fl.pad~.digest: Pads the input frame with a repeated specified value
fl.pad~.use_when: Adds a repeated value to the start or end of a frame. Padding may be applied to either the start or the end of the frame or both. Padding amounts may be set in samples, or as a ratio of the input length. The output length is at least the size of the input. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/pad`, `/start`, `/end`, `/units`.

fl.pattern~.digest: Step through a frame of values (or pattern) one at a time
fl.pattern~.use_when: Steps through a frame of values one value per trigger. The pattern input takes the pattern frame without triggering output. Triggers step through the pattern either forwards or backwards. The pattern can be run (once), looped, paused or stopped. Triggers at the reset input set the position in the pattern using the reset parameter. The position is also reset whenever a new pattern is received. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/mode`, `/direction`, `/reset`, `/idle`.

fl.peaks~.digest: Finds peaks in the input frame
fl.peaks~.use_when: Finds and interpolates peaks in a frame. The input frame is searched for peaks (values greater than the surrounding values). Each input sample is assigned to a peak. Peaks positions and values are also interpolated and output. The first output is the same length as the input. Other outputs are as long as the number of detected peaks. Peaks are detected if a value exceeds its neighbours and a fixed threshold. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/neighbours`, `/threshold`, `/pad`, `/edges`, `/refine`, `/boundaries`, `/always_detect`.

fl.perblock~.digest: Schedules one frame at the start of each host audio block
fl.perblock~.use_when: Starts one frame at the start of each audio block. The output is an empty trigger frame. A scheduler: it can start a network. Attributes `@id` (context), `@rt`, `@buffer`; in non-realtime mode send `reset` then `process <samples>`.

fl.percentile~.digest: Calculates a specified percentile of the input frame (by default the 50th or median)
fl.percentile~.use_when: Outputs a chosen percentile of a frame, the median by default. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/percentile`, `/interpolate`, `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.poltocar~.digest: Converts from polar values at the inputs to cartesian values at the outputs
fl.poltocar~.use_when: Converts polar or spherical frames into x, y (and z) frames. Conversion may be in 2D or 3D (using spherical coordinates). The outputs are frames of the same length as the longest input. Shorter inputs are padded with zeros prior to conversion. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/dimensions`, `/angles`.

fl.pow~.digest: Raises left input frame values to the power of right input frame values
fl.pow~.use_when: Raises left input frame values to the power of right input frame values. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.prioritise~.digest: Apply a fixed priority ranking to synchronous input frames
fl.prioritise~.use_when: Passes only the highest-priority frame when several arrive at once. Frames arriving asynchronously are sent to the output. When frames arrive synchronously only one is sent to the output. The input number is used to proritise synchonous inputs. Either higher or lower numbered inputs can be prioritised. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/num_ins`, `/order`.

fl.product~.digest: Calculates the product of the input frame
fl.product~.use_when: Multiplies all values in a frame together. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.ramp~.digest: Generates a linear ramp across each output frame
fl.ramp~.use_when: Generates a straight-line ramp across a frame. The scale parameter is used to set the range of the ramp. The length of the output is dependent on the mode parameter. Output length may be set by parameter or based on that of the trigger input. The range of the output ramp is determined by the scale and edges parameters. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/mode`, `/length`, `/units`, `/scale`, `/endpoints`.

fl.random~.digest: Generates linearly distributed random values in the range [0-1]
fl.random~.use_when: Generates frames of random values between 0 and 1. The length of the output is dependent on the mode parameter. Output length may be set by parameter or based on that of the trigger input. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/mode`, `/length`, `/units`.

fl.read~.digest: Reads from a specified host buffer given an input frame of positions
fl.read~.use_when: Reads a buffer~ at the positions given by an input frame (the core of FrameLib granulators: ramp of positions in, grain out). Set the buffer as argument or `/buffer`; `/channel`, `/units` (e.g. ms), `/interp`, `/edges` (e.g. wrap) and `/bound` control reading. Output length equals the input length. Typical chain: fl.ramp~ → fl.read~ → fl.window~ → fl.sink~.

fl.recall~.digest: Recall a remotely stored frame for use
fl.recall~.use_when: Reads a frame stored under a name by fl.store~. The frame to be recalled is determined by the storage specifed by the name parameter. The ordering input can be used to explicitly control ordering between related objects. In a multistream scenario each stream has separate storage for a given name. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/name`.

fl.register~.use_when: Stores a frame and outputs it again when triggered. The left input triggers recall, whilst the right input stores a frame. The mode parameter is used to set whether the right input causes output. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/mode`.

fl.reverse~.digest: Computes the reverse of the input frame
fl.reverse~.use_when: Reverses the order of values in a frame. The output is the same length as the input.

fl.rms~.digest: Calculates the rms of the input frame
fl.rms~.use_when: Calculates the RMS level of a frame. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.round~.digest: Calculates the rounded value of each value in the input frame
fl.round~.use_when: Calculates the rounded value of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.route~.digest: Routes the input to one of a number of outputs
fl.route~.use_when: Sends a frame to one of several outputs. The number of outputs is variable. The selected output can be changed with a parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/num_outs`, `/output`.

fl.samplerate~.digest: Convert or output values based on the sample rate
fl.samplerate~.use_when: Outputs the sample rate or converts values based on it. For output modes the output is a single value. For conversion modes the size matches the input size. The sample rate or the nyquist frequency can be requested. Alternatively, a number of sample rate related conversions are offered. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/mode`, `/normalisation`.

fl.select~.digest: Selects output from a number of inputs
fl.select~.use_when: Passes one of several input frames to the output. The number of inputs is variable. The selected input can be changed with a parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/num_ins`, `/input`.

fl.shift~.use_when: Shifts values left or right within a frame. The output is the same length as the input. Output can be shifted left or right in comparison to the input. The edge behaviour can be set as appropriate for the application. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/shift`, `/pad`, `/edges`, `/units`.

fl.sinh~.digest: Calculates the hyperbolic sine of each value in the input frame
fl.sinh~.use_when: Calculates the hyperbolic sine of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.sink~.digest: Outputs frames to the host environment as audio by overlap-adding into an output buffer
fl.sink~.use_when: Main exit from FrameLib to MSP audio: overlap-adds incoming frames into its output with no added latency. `/buffer_size` (creation only, default 250000 samples) limits the longest frame; `/delay` adds optional delay (reducing the maximum frame length); `/units` sets samples, ms or seconds; `/interp` sets interpolation. A first argument like `=2` makes a multistream sink. In non-realtime mode use `@rt 0 @buffer <name>` and drive with `reset` / `process <samples>`.

fl.sin~.digest: Calculates the sine (for arguments in radians) of each value in the input frame
fl.sin~.use_when: Calculates the sine (for arguments in radians) of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.skewness~.digest: Calculates the skewness of the input frame
fl.skewness~.use_when: Calculates the skewness (lopsidedness) of a frame. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.sort~.digest: Sorts an input frame into ascending or descending order
fl.sort~.use_when: Sorts a frame in ascending or descending order. The sort can either be on values or indices as set by the indices parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/order`, `/indices`.

fl.source~.digest: Captures audio from the host environment and outputs the most recent values as frames
fl.source~.use_when: Main entry from MSP audio into FrameLib: captures the most recent audio as a frame whenever triggered (usually by fl.interval~). `/length` sets the frame size (e.g. `fl.source~ /length 4096`) and adds matching latency; `/delay` adds more; `/buffer_size` limits the maximum; `/interp` interpolates capture. Non-realtime: `@rt 0 @buffer <name>` reads from a buffer~.

fl.spatial~.digest: Generates multiplication factors for a set of speakers positioned in 3D
fl.spatial~.use_when: Computes speaker gains for a 3D position using distance-based panning. The core underlying algorithm is DBAP (distance-based amplitude panning). Input may use cartesian [x, y, z] or spherical [radius, azimuth, elevation] coordinates. Angles may be set using degrees or radians. 2D operation can be achieved by setting all z or elevation values to zero. Missing values at any input are assumed to be zero. Note that the orientation of the spherical coordinates can be adjusted as required. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/angles`, `/orientation`, `/input_coords`, `/speaker_coords`, `/constrain`, `/speakers`, `/weights`, `/rolloff`, `/blur`, `/max_speakers`, `/point_factor`.

fl.split~.digest: Splits input frames into two frames, given a specified split point
fl.split~.use_when: Splits a frame into two at a given point. The split point may be specified in samples or as a ratio of the length of the input frame. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/split`, `/units`.

fl.spread~.digest: Calculates the spread of the input frame
fl.spread~.use_when: Calculates the spread of a frame around its centroid. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.sqrt~.digest: Calculates the square root of each value in the input frame
fl.sqrt~.use_when: Calculates the square root of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.stddev~.digest: Calculates the standard deviation of the input frame
fl.stddev~.use_when: Calculates the standard deviation of a frame. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.store~.digest: Stores frames remotely for later recall
fl.store~.use_when: Stores a frame under a name for fl.recall~. The storage location is determined by the name parameter. The output / ordering input can be used to explicitly control ordering between related objects. In a multistream scenario each stream has separate storage for a given name. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/name`.

fl.streamid~.digest: Outputs the stream id for each stream in a multistream connection
fl.streamid~.use_when: Outputs which stream number each stream of a multistream is. Any input triggers a single value output - the stream id (counting from one).

fl.subframe~.digest: Output a specified segment of an input frame
fl.subframe~.use_when: Outputs a chosen section of a frame. The subframe is specified by a start and end point in the input frame. The start point is included in the output frame but the end point is not. Points may be specified in samples or as a ratio of the length of the input frame. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/start`, `/end`, `/units`.

fl.sum~.digest: Calculates the sum of the input frame
fl.sum~.use_when: Adds up all values in a frame. The output is a single value. When the input frame is empty then the output is determined by the empty parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/empty`, `/default`.

fl.svf~.digest: Applies a state variable filter to the input
fl.svf~.use_when: Filters each frame with a state-variable filter. Output is the same length as the input. The filter can output a single specifed mode at a time. Alternatively, in multi-output mode all modes are output simultaneously. Filter settings may be made either via parameters or per sample via inputs. The dynamic parameter is set to create the inputs for per sample values. Frames of per sample values are padded to length with their final value if required. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/freq`, `/res`, `/mode`, `/multi_output`, `/dynamic`, `/reset`.

fl.tag~.digest: Adds tags to vectors either in order to set parameters or for routing purposes
fl.tag~.use_when: Adds tags (parameter names) to vectors so a single tagged frame can set parameters on other FrameLib objects, or be used for routing. One input per tag, set implicitly by the `/tag_01` … parameters present at creation or explicitly with `/num_ins`; a further input takes already-tagged frames to append. Read tagged frames back with fl.untag~ or fl.filtertags~; merge them with fl.combinetags~.

fl.tanh~.digest: Calculates the hyperbolic tangent of each value in the input frame
fl.tanh~.use_when: Calculates the hyperbolic tangent of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.tan~.digest: Calculates the tangent (for arguments in radians) of each value in the input frame
fl.tan~.use_when: Calculates the tangent (for arguments in radians) of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.ticks~.use_when: Counts incoming frames up or down to a limit. Counting is between zero and one less than the limit parameter. Counting can be either up or down. Counting can be run (once), looped, paused or stopped. Triggers at the reset input set the count to the value of the reset parameter. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/limit`, `/direction`, `/reset`, `/mode`, `/idle`.

fl.timedelta~.digest: Calculates the time interval between consecutive incoming frames
fl.timedelta~.use_when: Outputs the time between consecutive frames. Time is reported in the specified units. Output is a single value. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/units`.

fl.timemean~.digest: Calculates the mean per sample over the most recent frames
fl.timemean~.use_when: Averages each value over the most recent frames. The output is the same length as the input. Input frames are expected to be of a uniform length. If the input length changes then the internal storage is reset. The object can also be reset by sending a frame to the reset input. The start parameter controls behaviour when insufficient frames are stored. The underlength output indicates that insufficient frames are stored. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/max_frames`, `/num_frames`, `/pad`, `/start`.

fl.timemedian~.digest: Calculates the specified percentile per sample over the most recent frames
fl.timemedian~.use_when: Takes the median (or other percentile) of each value over recent frames. The default percentile is 50% which returns the median. The output is the same length as the input. Input frames are expected to be of a uniform length. If the input length changes then the internal storage is reset. The object can also be reset by sending a frame to the reset input. The start parameter controls behaviour when insufficient frames are stored. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/max_frames`, `/num_frames`, `/percentile`, `/pad`, `/start`.

fl.timer~.digest: Calculates the time elapsed between the each trigger input and the previous reset
fl.timer~.use_when: Outputs time elapsed since the last reset frame. A frame in the reset input starts the timer. Frames in the trigger input cause the elapsed time to be reported. Time is reported in the specified units. Output is a single value (output is empty if no reset frame has yet been received). Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/units`.

fl.timestddev~.digest: Calculates the standard deviation per sample over the most recent frames
fl.timestddev~.use_when: Calculates each value's standard deviation over recent frames. The output is the same length as the input. Input frames are expected to be of a uniform length. If the input length changes then the internal storage is reset. The object can also be reset by sending a frame to the reset input. The start parameter controls behaviour when insufficient frames are stored. The underlength output indicates that insufficient frames are stored. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/max_frames`, `/num_frames`, `/pad`, `/start`.

fl.tomax~.use_when: Turns frames into Max messages (a list per frame) so FrameLib results can drive ordinary Max objects. It does not output audio: for audio use fl.sink~ (overlap-add), and for an audio-rate control signal use fl.trace~. No parameters. Long frames may exceed Max's message length limit. Counterpart of fl.frommax~.

fl.trace~.digest: Outputs values from the input as audio, continuing the last value till a new frame arrives
fl.trace~.use_when: Outputs frame values as an audio-rate signal, holding the last value until a new frame arrives; intended for control signals rather than audio. `/mode`: `full` (whole frame, default), `first`, `last`, `specified` or `ratio` (with `/position`). `/buffer_size`, `/units`, `/delay` as fl.sink~.

fl.trunc~.digest: Calculates the truncated value of each value in the input frame
fl.trunc~.use_when: Calculates the truncated value of each value in the input frame. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.uniform~.digest: Generates frames in which all values are identical
fl.uniform~.use_when: Generates frames where every value is the same. The output value is set with a parameter. The length of the output is dependent on the mode parameter. Output length may be set by parameter or based on that of the trigger input. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/value`, `/mode`, `/length`, `/units`.

fl.unpack~.digest: Unpacks multistream input into individual streams
fl.unpack~.use_when: Splits a multistream connection into single streams. Multistream inputs are unpacked in order across the outputs. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/num_outs`.

fl.untag~.digest: Retrieves vectors from a tagged frame according to a specified set of tags
fl.untag~.use_when: Pulls named values out of a tagged frame. Each output deals with one tag and outputs vectors at the input with that tag. Outputs will be empty if the tag is not present at the input with a vector value. The number of outputs can be set explicitly by parameter. Alternatively, it can be set implicitly by the tag parameters present at instantiation. Parameters (write as `/name value` or as arguments): `/num_outs`, `/tag_01...10`.

fl.window~.digest: Multiplies the input frame by a specified window
fl.window~.use_when: Multiplies each incoming frame by a window; the output has the input's length. Set the window as the first argument or `/window` (e.g. `fl.window~ hann`), not `@window`. `/compensate` applies gain compensation for overlap-add (help uses `reconstruct`, `linear`, `square`); `/size`, `/exponent`, `/parameters`, `/endpoints` refine the shape. Standard step before fl.fft~. To generate a window frame with no input, use fl.makewindow~.

fl.wrap~.digest: Wraps the incoming frame into the range delimited by the two parameters
fl.wrap~.use_when: Wraps the incoming frame into the range delimited by the two parameters. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

fl.||~.digest: Calculates the logical or of the left and right input frame values
fl.||~.use_when: Calculates the logical or of the left and right input frame values. Element-wise FrameLib operator on input frames.

bufconvolve~.use_when: Convolve or deconvolve two buffers offline (non-realtime). Operation is selected by message: 'convolve' for forward convolution, 'deconvolve' for inverse. Deconvolution mode supports several attribute-driven options (deconvmode, deconvphase, deconvfilter, deconvrange, deconvdelay) for regularised inverse-filter design. For realtime convolution use multiconvolve~ instead. Native Max has no offline convolution — rolling this yourself is a long pfft~ + complex-multiply + ifft chain.

bufresample~.digest: Resample the contents of a buffer~ to transpose or change sample rate
bufresample~.use_when: Rewrite a buffer at a new sample rate or transposition with high-quality offline resampling. Four message modes: 'resample' (target sample rate), 'transpose' (cents/ratio), 'both' (combined), and 'filter' (apply only the antialiasing filter). Different from groove~/sfplay~, which play back at a rate without altering the source — bufresample~ produces a new buffer.

bufreverse~.digest: Reverse the contents of a buffer
bufreverse~.use_when: Reverse the contents of a buffer~ and write the result to another buffer~ (triggered by `process`; bangs when done). `readchan`, `writechan` and `resize` control which channels are read and written.

hirt.convolutionreverb~.digest: The HIRT Convolution Reverb for Max
hirt.convolutionreverb~.use_when: Turnkey convolution reverb abstraction with built-in IR file loading. Optional 'reverbname' arg sets the instance name. Messages: 'open' / 'close' to toggle the GUI window, 'iradd' / 'irfolder' / 'irmenu' to load IRs, 'irmode' for impulse-handling mode. Use instead of building a multiconvolve~-based reverb when you want a self-contained reverb unit. For non-reverb convolution (cabinets, time-domain filtering, custom IRs from a buffer) use hirt.convolver~ or multiconvolve~ directly.

hirt.convolver~.use_when: General-purpose realtime convolver abstraction — convolve any signal with any IR. Optional 'convolvername' arg. Messages mirror the reverb version: 'open' / 'close' for GUI, 'iradd' / 'irfolder' / 'irmenu' to load IRs. Choose this over hirt.convolutionreverb~ when you're not building a reverb (cabinet IRs, EQ-as-IR, time-domain filtering).

hirt.irmaker~.digest: HIRT Impulse Response Maker - Impulse Response Measurement and Auditioning
hirt.irmaker~.use_when: All-in-one IR measurement: plays the excitation, records the response and makes the IR. `sweep` (best for rooms and analog gear) or `impulse` (digital systems) starts a measurement; `stop` aborts; `save` writes the IR to disk; `settings` sets all parameters; `left`, `right`, `centre` choose which input channel's response is auditioned; `open` / `close` the window. Outlets 0-1 go to the system being measured, 2-3 to your monitors, then progress and a done bang. For custom multichannel chains use irmeasure~ with irextract~.

iralign~.use_when: Time-align multiple IRs so their direct-sound peaks coincide. Messages: 'align' (mutual alignment) or 'alignto' (align to a reference). Reach for this before iraverage~ or comparison work where IRs were captured at different distances or with different latencies.

iraverage~.digest: Average multiple IRs in the time or frequency domain
iraverage~.use_when: Average several impulse responses to reduce measurement noise. `average` works in the time domain; `process` works in the frequency domain, with `smoothmode` / `smoothamount` for smoothing and `phase` for the output phase. `readchan`, `writechan` and `resize` control buffer I/O. Align the IRs first with iralign~.

irextract~.digest: Process recorded measurements from the irmeasure~ object
irextract~.use_when: Companion to irmeasure~ — turns a recorded sweep response into the actual IR. Sweep type is set by message: 'sweep' (exponential sine sweep), 'mls' (max-length sequence), 'pink' / 'white' / 'brown' (noise variants). Messages: 'getir' to retrieve the result, 'dump' for raw data, 'clear' to reset. Use when irmeasure~ has captured raw measurement data and you need to extract the IR from it.

irinvert~.use_when: Build an inverse filter from an IR. Messages: 'invert' for the basic case, 'mimo' / 'mimoto' for multi-input multi-output (matrix) inversion. Use for room correction, speaker equalisation, or any 'undo this system's response' workflow.

irmeasure~.digest: Measure IRs of single or multichannel systems using a range of excitation signals
irmeasure~.use_when: Generate excitation signals and record a system's response to measure IRs of single or multichannel systems. Arguments: number of measurement inputs and outputs. Excitations: `sweep`, `mls`, `white`, `pink`, `brown`; `tone` outputs a test tone. `activeins` / `activeouts` choose channels, `stop` cancels, `getir` retrieves the IR, `reprocess` recomputes with new deconvolution settings, `extract` copies the raw recording of one input so irextract~ can process it later, `dump`, `clear`. Lower level than hirt.irmaker~.

irnonlin~.digest: Transform IRs for harmonics of system into those required by a Hammerstein model
irnonlin~.use_when: Hammerstein-model decomposition of harmonics from a system measurement — for modeling weakly nonlinear systems (tubes, distortion). Messages: 'convert' (in-place) or 'convertto' (separate destination). Niche; reach for this only when doing nonlinear system identification.

irphase~.digest: Change the phase of an IR
irphase~.use_when: Convert an IR's phase characteristic while preserving its magnitude response. Phase mode is selected by message: 'minphase' (minimum-phase, no pre-ringing), 'maxphase' (maximum-phase), 'linphase' (linear-phase, symmetrical impulse), 'mixedphase' (blended), 'allpass' (allpass component only). Use when you need a specific phase property — e.g. zero pre-ringing for a linear-phase EQ from a measured curve.

irplapprox~.digest: Approximate the frequency response of an IR with a set of freq/dB pairs
irplapprox~.use_when: Distil an IR's frequency response into a compact set of frequency/dB pairs (piecewise-linear approximation). Triggered by 'approx' message. Use when you need a parametric description of a response, e.g. to drive a parametric EQ from a measured curve.

irreference~.digest: Estimate system IRs by relative comparison of two recorded inputs
irreference~.use_when: Derive an IR by comparing a reference signal to a recorded system output, when you can't drive the system with a controlled sweep. Optional num_ref_ins arg. Workflow messages: 'rec' to start recording, 'finish' to stop, 'extract' / 'reprocess' / 'getir' to compute and retrieve, 'activeins' / 'clear' / 'dump' / 'stop'. Use when measurement is in-situ and the reference signal is whatever happens to be playing.

irstats~.digest: Calculate room acoustic parameters and measurements from an IR
irstats~.use_when: Compute room-acoustic measurements from an impulse response. Send `stats <buffer> <names…>` with any of t20, t30 (reverb time), edt (early decay time), onset, directend, directexists, mixing (early-to-late transition), center (centre time), clarity and rms; results come out as one list in the order requested. `timeinsamps`, `clipmixing` and `readchan` refine the output.

irsweeps~.digest: Generate measurement signals to a buffer
irsweeps~.use_when: Write a measurement excitation signal into a buffer. Signal type by message: 'sweep' (exponential sine sweep), 'invsweep' (inverse sweep, paired with 'sweep' for deconvolution), 'mls', 'pink', 'white', 'brown'. First step of a manual IR measurement workflow that pairs with irmeasure~ and irextract~.

irtransaural~.digest: Generate filters for the playback of binaural material over speakers
irtransaural~.use_when: Generate crosstalk-cancellation filters so binaural recordings play back correctly over loudspeakers. Two algorithm choices by message: 'lattice' (lattice-form filter) or 'shuffler' (shuffler-form filter). Use only for transaural / loudspeaker-binaural playback — niche but specific.

irtrimnorm~.digest: Trim (by RMS level), crop, or pad multiple IRs, with or without group normalisation
irtrimnorm~.use_when: Trim, crop, pad, and normalise multiple IRs as a batch, with optional group normalisation. Each operation has 'in-place' and 'to-destination' variants: 'trim' / 'trimto', 'crop' / 'cropto', 'pad' / 'padto'. Standard cleanup step before using captured IRs in convolution.

iruser~.digest: Create an IR with a specified frequency response and a given output phase
iruser~.use_when: Synthesise an IR from a target frequency response and a chosen output phase. Triggered by 'make' message. Use to build EQ-curve IRs, target-response filters, or any case where you want to specify a response and get an IR.

irvalue~.digest: Return dB amplitude of IR from frequency input
irvalue~.use_when: Query an IR's magnitude (in dB) at a given frequency. 'set' message loads the IR, then a float to the inlet returns the dB value at that frequency. Use as a measurement utility — read out a specific frequency's level from an IR rather than visualising the whole curve.

morphfilter~.use_when: Apply time-varying filtering to a buffer with morphing gain (offline). Messages: 'addfilter' to push filter stages, 'clear' to reset, 'process' to run. Use when you need a filter whose response changes over the duration of a buffer in a controlled way — e.g. spectral fades, EQ automation baked into a sample.

multiconvolve~.digest: Multichannel realtime zero- or low- latency convolution
multiconvolve~.use_when: The main HIRT realtime convolver for one or many signals. Arguments: number of inputs, number of outputs, latency mode: `zero` (0 samples, least efficient, default), `short` (128 samples) or `medium` (512 samples, most efficient). Load IRs with `set`, empty with `clear`; `@fixedsize` fixes the impulse length in samples. `mc.multiconvolve~` is also available. For a ready-made reverb use hirt.convolutionreverb~.

spectrumdraw~.digest: Display spectra from realtime inputs or buffers
spectrumdraw~.use_when: Display realtime or buffer-based spectra in a Max UI without rolling your own pfft~ → jit.matrix chain. Messages: 'set' to assign a buffer, 'select' to choose a curve, 'freeze' to hold the display. Use for IR/spectrum visualisation in HIRT-based or general spectral patches.

jit.gl.isf.digest: Render ISF files to GL textures
jit.gl.isf.use_when: Render ISF files to GL textures.

link.audio.receive~.digest: Receive stereo audio over Link Audio from other peers in the session
link.audio.receive~.use_when: Receive a stereo audio stream from another application on the Link session, synchronized to the Link beat grid with cubic interpolation. Argument or `@channel` names the stream; `channel <peer> <channel>` or `@peer` disambiguates when two peers use the same name. Outlets: left signal, right signal, discovery messages, and a bang when the channel list changes. Discovery: `getchannels` (also `bang`), `getpeers`, `getchannelswithpeers`, `getcount`, `getstatus` output lists prefixed `channels` / `peers` / `channelswithpeers` / `count` / `status`; wire through `route channels` into a `umenu`, then `prepend channel` back to the inlet. `@autopollchannels 1` (and `autopollpeers`, `autopollchannelswithpeers`, `autopollstatus` with `statuspollinterval`) push updates automatically. `latency` (ms) trades delay against dropouts; `enable 0` stops receiving. Read-only `status` stays at connected until audio arrives and the Link transport is playing. Only between separate applications, never within one Max (use `receive~`). Requires Link package 2.0 (Max 9+).

link.audio.send~.digest: Send stereo audio over Link Audio to other peers in the session
link.audio.send~.use_when: Stream stereo audio from Max to another application (any Link Audio peer) on the same Link session, synced to the Link beat grid. Argument or `@name` sets the channel name other peers see. Both inlets (left, right) must carry signal; there is no mono fallback, so feed a mono source to both. No outlets. Several `link.audio.send~` objects with the same name share one stream: their audio is summed, and `quantum` (beat mapping, typically bars, 1-64) and `announce` are shared across all of them. `announce 0` hides the stream from peers while keeping the name; `enable 0` silences only this object's contribution. Only works between separate applications: to move audio inside one Max, use `send~` / `receive~`. Requires Link package 2.0 (Max 9+); all link.* objects share one Link peer.

link.beat.digest: Synchronize beats with a Link timeline
link.beat.use_when: Synchronize beats with a Link timeline.

link.phasor~.digest: Synchronize phase with a Link timeline
link.phasor~.use_when: Synchronize phase with a Link timeline.

link.session.digest: Start/stop a session, change the tempo, or be notified about these events
link.session.use_when: Start/stop a session, change the tempo, or be notified about these events.

nw.cppan~.digest: Pan mono input across two outputs
nw.cppan~.use_when: Pan mono input across two outputs.

nw.gateplus~.digest: Route a signal with zero-crossing awareness
nw.gateplus~.use_when: Route a signal with zero-crossing awareness.

nw.grainbang~.digest: Trigger grains with a bang message
nw.grainbang~.use_when: Trigger grains with a bang message.

nw.grainphase~.digest: Control grains with a phase signal
nw.grainphase~.use_when: Control grains with a phase signal.

nw.grainpulse~.digest: Trigger grains with a pulse signal
nw.grainpulse~.use_when: Trigger grains with a pulse signal.

nw.grainstream~.digest: Generate grains at a given frequency
nw.grainstream~.use_when: Generate grains at a given frequency.

nw.pulsesamp~.digest: Trigger sample playback with a pulse signal
nw.pulsesamp~.use_when: Trigger sample playback with a pulse signal.

db.geneural.digest: < Forward propagates input buffer through network and assigns results to output buffer
db.geneural.use_when: Small neural network for list-to-list mapping, from the geneural study. Arguments: input size, output size. Left inlet takes the input list (and runs the trained net in a gen patcher), middle inlet the target list, right inlet messages: `addset` stores the current input/target pair, `learn` trains (in classic `js`, default 9000 iterations), plus `learningrate`, `learningiterations`, `hiddenlayers` (1–82), `hiddenunits` (1–15), `activation` (0 linear, 1 sigmoid, 2 htan, 3 reLu), `resetweights`, `clearsets`, `download weights` / `download learningset` (dict out the right outlet) and `upload weights dictionary <name>`. A teaching demo; for real work reach for the FluCoMa or ml.star packages.

db.mc.channelhandling.digest: Allocate channels and create a channel lookup table
db.mc.channelhandling.use_when: Internal helper — the voice allocator behind the studies' `gui.main` panels. Arguments: channel count, busy map name. Takes a list of 0/1 voice on/off states, runs `mc.voiceallocator~ <n> @name <busymap>` with an `mc.sig~ @bzname` busy signal, and broadcasts a voice-index-to-channel table to `channelmap_<busymap>` for `db.mc.channelmap`. Use `mc.voiceallocator~` directly in new patches.

db.mc.channelmap.digest: Reorders a list to match it's allocated channels. (use with db.mc.channelhandling)
db.mc.channelmap.use_when: Internal helper — reorders a parameter list so item N lands on the MC channel that voice N was given. Argument: busy map name (must match a `db.mc.channelhandling` in the same session). It is `zl 1024 indexmap` whose right inlet is fed by an unnamed `[r]` set to `channelmap_<name>`. Only useful together with `db.mc.channelhandling`.

db.mc.clicklessdelay~.digest: (Arguments: Busymap name, Crossfade rate (Hz)) Using 2 MC delay lines and a sine oscillator to crossfade between them, we can have a clickless delay by updating the delay times only when the volume is near zero.
db.mc.clicklessdelay~.use_when: MC delay line whose delay time can jump without clicks. Arguments: busy map name, crossfade rate in Hz. Left inlet: MC audio; right inlet: MC delay-time signal in ms (max 5000). Inside, two `mc.tapin~ 5000` / `mc.tapout~` lines are crossfaded by a `cycle~` and each line picks up a new time through `mc.sah~` only while its own gain is near zero, so a new time takes effect within one crossfade cycle. Reach for it when delay times are sequenced or randomized; for smooth sweeps a plain `mc.tapout~` is fine.

db.mc.filterdelaystereo~.digest: (Arguments: #Channels, Busymap name) We use mc.reson~ to bandpass filter the MC signal. Look inside "db.mc.clicklessdelay~" to see a clickless MC delay line.
db.mc.filterdelaystereo~.use_when: Bank of band-passed, delayed, panned copies of a sound, mixed to stereo. Arguments: channel count, busy map name. Left inlet: source signal (duplicated with `mc.dup~`); right inlet: list messages `filterCenters <Hz list>`, `filterQ <list>`, `delayTimes <ms list>`, `delayFbs <list>`, `pans <0–1 list>` (each list is smoothed into an MC signal by `ltomc`). Output: 2-channel MC. Uses `mc.reson~`, `db.mc.clicklessdelay~` (5 Hz crossfade) and `mc.stereo~`. Needs `ltomc`, which only exists inside the study folders.

db.mc.fmwavetable~.digest: (Arguments: #Channels, BusyMap Name) MC FM wavetable synthesis
db.mc.fmwavetable~.use_when: Per-channel two-operator FM with wavetable oscillators. Arguments: channel count, busy map name. Inlets: 1 wave messages prefixed `carrier` or `modulator` and passed to that `mc.wave~` (for instance `carrier setvalue 3 set wavetable.5` via `mc.target`); 2 carrier frequency (Hz); 3 modulator frequency (Hz, drives an `mc.phasor~`); 4 modulation index, as a ratio of the carrier frequency. Outlets: carrier MC signal, modulator MC signal. Pair with `db.wavetable2polybuffer` to fill a `polybuffer~` with frames.

db.mc.geneural~.digest: < This gen patcher outputs an mc signal reading from a buffer. Each channel is an ascending sample index (starting at 0)
db.mc.geneural~.use_when: Signal-rate version of `db.geneural`: each MC channel is one input or output value. Arguments: input size, output size. Left inlet: MC input signal; middle: MC target signal; right: the same messages as `db.geneural` (`addset`, `learn`, `hiddenlayers`, `activation`, `download`/`upload`, ...). Inside, `mc.gen~` pokes each channel into a buffer by `mc_channel` and the network only recomputes when an input changes. Outlet 0 is the MC result, outlet 1 the dict dump. Demo-grade.

db.mc.oneshotphasor~.digest: (Arguments: #Channels, Busymap name) Outputs a one shot MC phasor
db.mc.oneshotphasor~.use_when: Starts a 0–1 ramp on a free MC channel for every incoming message, then frees the channel when the ramp ends. Arguments: channel count, busy map name. Left inlet: any message (claims a channel via `mc.voiceallocator~ @name <busymap>`); right inlet: ramp length in ms. Outlets: MC ramps (`mc.line~ @bzname`), and a `[input, channel]` list. Useful as a per-grain or per-note phase for `mc.wave~`, `mc.gen~` or envelopes.

db.mc.oneshotramp~.digest: (Arguments: #Channels, BusyMap Name) Use mc.voiceallocator~ to manage channels as voices and send out a linear one shot ramp as an MC signal
db.mc.oneshotramp~.use_when: Attack/decay envelope on a newly allocated MC channel per message. Arguments: channel count, busy map name. Inlets: any message (new voice), attack ms, decay ms. Outlets: MC envelope, the message, the channel number. The envelope itself holds the voice busy. Caution: the allocator inside is typed `mc.voiceallocator~ #1 #2`, and the refpage documents only one argument, so the busy map name is probably not applied (use `@name`). Not verified in Max.

db.mc.periodiconeshot~.digest: (Arguments: #Channels, Busymap name, init rate) Periodically outputs a one shot MC phasor based on a list of 0/1 (off/on) values.
db.mc.periodiconeshot~.use_when: Step sequencer that fires `db.mc.oneshotphasor~` ramps on steps marked 1. Arguments: channel count, busy map name, step time in ms. Messages to the only inlet: `active 0/1`, `rate <ms>`, `steps <n>`, `length <ms>` (ramp length), `activeSteps <0/1 list>`. Outlet 0: MC ramps; outlet 1: `step <n>`, `activeStep <input> <channel>`, and a bang at the end of each pass.

db.mc.stereodelay~.digest: (Arguments: #Channels, MaxDelayTime, Glide time) Basic MC delay line with random panning and delay time gliding
db.mc.stereodelay~.use_when: Multichannel feedback delay with random panning. Arguments: channel count, max delay (ms), glide time (ms). Inlets: stereo MC input, delay-time list (ms), feedback list. Output: 2-channel MC via `mc.stereo~ @autogain 1`; pan positions come from `mc.sig~` sent `deviate 0.5 0.5` at load. Caution: the internal `ltomc` boxes are typed with 32 channels, not the channel-count argument, and `ltomc` is missing from the `shared` folder.

db.mc.vox~.digest: (Arguments: #Channels) Create a simple MC Vocoder using 2 mcs.fffb~ for convenient filter banks
db.mc.vox~.use_when: Channel vocoder built from two `mcs.fffb~` filter banks. Argument: number of bands. Inlets: 1 modulator (voice, loop); 2 carrier (for instance `mc.saw~`); 3 filterbank messages sent to both banks (`freq 0 <Hz list>`, `QAll <q>`, `gain 0 <list>`); 4 attack ms; 5 decay ms. The modulator bands are squared and smoothed with `mc.slide~`, multiplied onto the carrier bands, and mixed to one channel with `mc.mixdown~ 1 @autogain 1`. The simplevox study sends band frequencies as `freq 0 <list>` from an exponential `vexpr` map; do the same.

db.wavetable2polybuffer.digest: (Arguments: Polybuffer name, Size of waveforms (in samples)) This patch takes a wavetable file, extracts the waveforms from it and puts each one on a buffer in a polybuffer~
db.wavetable2polybuffer.use_when: Splits a single-file wavetable (all frames end to end) into one `buffer~` per frame inside a `polybuffer~`. Arguments: polybuffer name, frame size in samples (for instance `db.wavetable2polybuffer wavetable 256`). Send a file name (or bang for a file dialog); it outputs the frame count. The frames are named `<name>.1`, `<name>.2`, ... as `polybuffer~` always does, so any `mc.wave~` / `wave~` channel can be sent `set <name>.<n>`.
