dp_osc.use_when: Internal helper — the voice patcher oscillator of the dynamicpoly study: 0–1 signal times 127 → `mc.mtof~` → `mc.cycle~` → `mc.stereo~ @autogain 1`. Write the three objects directly instead.

gui.main.digest: < MC voice allocating with active busymap setting. Uses busymap name "forces" to control a specific set of MC objects
gui.main.use_when: Internal helper — the control panel bpatcher of one study. Four different patchers share this name (attraction, cellularautomata, magnetism, particlegrains), each with its own dials, presets and voice allocation. Not reusable; do not place it by name in your own patch.

ltomc.digest: (Arguments: #Channels, Busymap name) Convert a list to an MC signal with smoothing.
ltomc.use_when: Turns a number list into an MC signal, one value per channel, with glide. Arguments: channel count, busy map name, glide time in ms (for instance `ltomc 32 sound 20`). A one-item list takes a separate plain `sig~` path. Otherwise it is `mc.sig~ @chans <n>` fed `applyvalues`, then `mc.rampsmooth~`. Three identical copies live inside the study folders; for new patches `mc.sig~` with `applyvalues` or `mc.list~` does the job without the name clash.

mctomatrix.digest: (Arguments: #Channels, Matrix name, Plane Destination, Dim 1 Destination) Original patch and idea by Timo Hoogland
mctomatrix.use_when:
Writes an MC signal into one row or plane of a named `jit.matrix`, one cell per channel, without leaving the audio thread. Arguments: channel count, matrix name, plane, row (dim 1). The trick: `count~ 0 ` walks the channels one sample at a time, `mc.==~` passes only the matching channel, `mc.mixdown~ 1` merges them, and `jit.poke~ @plane

` writes the cell. Idea credited to Timo Hoogland. Use it to draw MC control data with Jitter.

MIAP.use_when: Manifold-Interface Amplitude Panning for control data: interpolate across a map of nodes you place (speakers, parameter presets, data points) and output node gains as a message. Optional name argument binds it to a MIAP.map GUI (get_name reports it). Build maps with node_create, node_create_ring, node_create_grid, polyset_create, link_create, or read_mapA / read_mapB JSON files; move the point with coords x y; crossfade two maps with @pan; @gainsmode 0 linear / 1 dB. Trajectories: set_trajectory, record_trajectory, start / stop. Use for multi-parameter mapping as well as panning; the built-in nodes object is a simpler alternative. Real names are capitalized (externals, refpages, init/miap-objectlist.txt). macOS 10.15+ / Windows 10+.

MIAP.map.use_when: GUI for MIAP and MIAP~: draw and edit node maps, polysets and links, and drag the listening point. Binds to a MIAP or MIAP~ with the same name; @reporthints and @reportmessages output interaction info. Edits create undo snapshots in the bound object. Real names are capitalized (externals, refpages, init/miap-objectlist.txt). macOS 10.15+ / Windows 10+.

MIAP.meyer.digest: Convert Meyer D-Mitri projects to MIAP JSON map and trajectory files
MIAP.meyer.use_when: Convert Meyer Sound Matrix-3 / D-Mitri project files into MIAP JSON map and trajectory files: read_project <file>, map <n> / trajectory <n> to choose, write_map / write_trajectory <file> to save. Real names are capitalized (externals, refpages, init/miap-objectlist.txt). macOS 10.15+ / Windows 10+.

MIAP~.use_when: Manifold-Interface Amplitude Panning for audio: pan a signal across any speaker layout drawn as a map of nodes (speaker, virtual, derived, silent). Arguments: optional name (binds a MIAP.map), optional max channel count (without it, one MC outlet). Same map, polyset, trajectory and undo messages as MIAP; @pan crossfades map A and B, @divergence spreads the source, @report 1 outputs gains. Real names are capitalized (externals, refpages, init/miap-objectlist.txt). macOS 10.15+ / Windows 10+.

byte-cast.digest: For casting a list of byte data
byte-cast.use_when: For casting a list of byte data.

FungibleData.use_when: Demo patch (loads as an abstraction but has no inlets/outlets) showing ways to copy numbers between `table`, `coll`, lists, `multislider` and Jitter matrices, using Peter Elsea's Lobjects-style `Util.*` helper abstractions that ship in the same folder (`Util.List2Table`, `Util.Table2List`, `Util.Coll2Table`, `Util.Table2Coll`, `Util.TableCopy`, `Util.Multislider2Table`, `Util.Table2Multislider`). Open it as a reference, not as a building block. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

PattrSave.digest: this autopattr connects all named UI objects in this patch to pattrstorage.
PattrSave.use_when: Demo patch (by Charles Veasey) showing presets with `autopattr` and `pattrstorage @greedy 1 @fileusagemode 1 @savemode 2`: store values, `writeagain` to `settings.json`, and reload them automatically when the patch opens. Not a reusable object; copy its pattern. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

average.digest: gives an average tempo of the last bangs
average.use_when: Demo patch comparing ways to average data (median, bucket average, list average, tap tempo) plus two galvanic-sensor helpers (`imi.avgmap`, `imi.splitscale`). Not an object despite the name. Several boxes need third-party externals that are not in the package (`St.Average`, `laverage`, `f0.average_tempo`, `dot.median`). Built-ins: `mean`, `zl.median`. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

coll_duplicates.use_when: Remove duplicate numbers from a coll and renumber it. Abstraction, 2 inlets / 1 outlet; see its help file for wiring. Numbers only. Internally uses colls named `master`, `buf` and `end`, so two copies in one Max session interfere. For lists, built-in `zl.unique` or `array.unique`. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

deltachange.digest: bang if delta over a certain number
deltachange.use_when: Split a stream of ints by size of change: values whose change from the previous one exceeds the threshold (argument) go out one outlet, smaller changes out the other. Abstraction, 1 inlet / 2 outlets. Use to react differently to small and big sensor jumps. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

fxwdmxusbpro.use_when: Send DMX to an Enttec DMX USB Pro interface over `serial`. Abstraction (Olivier Pasquet, modified by fxw), 2 inlets / 1 outlet: left inlet takes a list of channel values (channels 1–512, values 0–255; the help packs them with `pak`); right inlet takes port selection from the umenu fed by its outlet (`print`/`refresh`, `getport`, `close`). Uses the Enttec packet format 126 6 … 231. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.apploader.digest: use the coll document : IMIMovies to load a movie or a sound (add open at the end)
imi.apploader.use_when: Open an application stored in the package's `apps` folder. Abstraction, 1 inlet; args: folder name, application name (e.g. `imi.apploader faceOSC FaceOSC.app`). Uses the third-party `shell` external (Intel-only binary on the curating machine) and a hard-coded Max 7 path (`/Users/Shared/Max 7/Packages/`), so it is unlikely to work in Max 9. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.apploader2.digest: use the coll document : IMIMovies to load a movie or a sound (add open at the end)
imi.apploader2.use_when: Open an application in the package's `apps` folder via `;max launchbrowser` with a file:// URL. Abstraction, 1 inlet; args: folder, application (spaces as %20). Its paths are hard-coded to Max 7's shared Packages folder, so it is unlikely to work in Max 9. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.avgmap.digest: wait for the average (3 s) then add and substract 50 to it.
imi.avgmap.use_when: For galvanic-skin sensors: wait 3 seconds for an average, then map incoming values (0–1024) around that average to 0–10. Abstraction, 1 inlet / 2 outlets. Needs `dot.smooth` (not installed on the curating machine) and uses global `value` names `avg`, `plus`, `minus`, so two copies share state. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.bounce.use_when: Fold a moving x/y position back and forth between 0 and a limit (args: x limit, y limit), for bouncing drawings. Abstraction, 1 inlet (pair) / 1 outlet. Uses `Lrem` (from the RTC-lib package). Built-in `pong @mode fold` does the same for single values. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.counter.digest: arguments : staring number (0), iteration (20) and optionally grain (default 1) and speed (default 100 ms)
imi.counter.use_when: Count through a range at a set speed, or instantly. Abstraction, 1 inlet / 1 outlet; args: start (0), iterations (20), step/grain (1), speed in ms (100). Normally counts with `metro`; message `fast` counts instantly with `uzi`. Built-ins: `counter` + `metro`, `uzi`. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.debug.digest: date stamp the send and receive for easy debug
imi.debug.use_when: Print a message to the Max console with a time stamp (hh:mm:ss) for debugging sends and receives. Abstraction, 1 inlet. Built-in `print` without the time. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.desktop.digest: open  / read / import a document from the desktop
imi.desktop.use_when: Prefix a file name with the user's Desktop path and a message. Abstraction, 1 inlet / 1 outlet; argument = message to prepend (`importmovie`, `read`, `open`), then send a file name symbol. Built on `conformpath`. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.docloader.digest: use the coll document : IMIMovies to load a movie or a sound (add open at the end)
imi.docloader.use_when: Open a document found in the Max search path with its default application (e.g. an Arduino sketch). Abstraction, 1 inlet; send the file name. Uses `absolutepath`, `conformpath` and the third-party `shell` external (Intel-only binary on the curating machine, so not native Apple Silicon). From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.draw.digest: lcd drawing help : use with paintoval, frameoval, framerect, paintrect
imi.draw.use_when: Convert `x y width height` into jit.lcd rectangle coordinates measured from the centre or the corner (argument `center` or `corner`). Abstraction, 1 inlet / 1 outlet; prepend the drawing message (`paintrect`, `framerect`, `paintoval`, `frameoval`) and send to `jit.lcd`. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.encoder.use_when: Turn rotary-encoder pulses into movie frame numbers (argument = number of frames, e.g. 4000); resets to the last frame after 5 seconds regardless of position. Abstraction, 1 inlet / 2 outlets; send the result as `frame $1, bang` to a movie player. Uses a global `value a`. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.fullscreen.digest: simple fullscreen abstraction with position (x,y) and scale (x,y)
imi.fullscreen.use_when: Position and size a `jit.window` and toggle fullscreen with Escape (also hides cursor and menu bar). Abstraction, 1 inlet / 1 outlet to the window; args: x, y, width, height. For new work, `jit.world` has `fullscreen` and `esc_fullscreen` attributes. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.looptheloop.digest: universal frame converter to make loop points easier to use. It has two modes wait (wait for the end of the loop to be reached) or go (immediate jump). Accepts normal loop (1) or palindrome (2)
imi.looptheloop.use_when: Set movie loop points by frame number. Abstraction, 2 inlets / 3 outlets placed between a movie player and its controls; send `looppoints <start> <end> <go|wait> <1|2>` (go = jump now, wait = at loop end; 1 = normal loop, 2 = palindrome). Converts frames to time using the movie's fps and timescale. Help uses the old `jit.qt.movie`; use `jit.movie`. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.matrix2cell.digest: copies a matrix to a cellblock (you can now use multiple instances)
imi.matrix2cell.use_when: Display a Jitter matrix in a `jit.cellblock`, resizing rows and columns to fit. Abstraction, 1 inlet / 1 outlet (to jit.cellblock). Built-in `jit.cellblock` can also take a `jit_matrix` directly. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.matrixinfo.use_when: Report a matrix's planecount, type and dimensions from three separate outlets (1 inlet / 3 outlets). Wrapper around built-in `jit.matrixinfo`. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.matrixset.digest: record / playback a set of matrix (10 in the example) of 1 plane with auto-dim
imi.matrixset.use_when: Record and play back a set of 1-plane matrices whose dimensions adapt to the input. Abstraction, 2 inlets / 4 outlets; argument = number of matrices (e.g. 10); bang to record/step, `reset` to clear. Wrapper around built-in `jit.matrixset`. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.mgra.digest: jit.mgraphics drawing help : use with rectangle, ellipse, ...
imi.mgra.use_when: Convert `x y width height` into `jit.mgraphics` shape messages (`rectangle`, `ellipse`…) measured from the centre or corner (argument `center` or `corner`). Abstraction, 1 inlet / 1 outlet; needs `imi.wh_to_center` from the same folder. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.minus.use_when: Subtract with both inlets triggering output (a value in the right inlet also outputs the result). Abstraction, 2 inlets / 1 outlet. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.movieloader.digest: load applications and documents from Max (compatible with package)
imi.movieloader.use_when: Load a movie or sound by index from a coll file list named `IMIMovies`: send an index, get `read <file>` (or `open` for sounds) for the player. Abstraction, 1 inlet / 2 outlets; one outlet bangs for an automatic read. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.oneint.use_when: Pass one integer, then block until reopened; one inlet takes integers, the other reopens the gate. Abstraction, 2 inlets / 1 outlet; `onebang` for integers. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.past.use_when: Bang when a value rises past a threshold (argument), and report falling back below on the second outlet. Abstraction, 2 inlets (value, threshold) / 2 outlets. Built-in `past` covers the rising case. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.plus.use_when: Add with both inlets triggering output (a value in the right inlet also outputs the result). Abstraction, 2 inlets / 1 outlet. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.pushcount.digest: when a number hits the threshold (120), send a bang after a delay (2000 ms or 2 seconds in the example below)
imi.pushcount.use_when: Bang after a delay once a value passes a threshold (e.g. threshold 120, delay 2000 ms), for button or sensor 'hold' triggers. Abstraction, 3 inlets (the value plus threshold and delay settings) / 2 outlets. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.seqbang.digest: bang left then right and back
imi.seqbang.use_when: Alternate bangs between its two outlets (left, right, left…). Abstraction, 1 inlet / 2 outlets. Built-in `cycle 2` does the same with bangs. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.slide.digest: slide for matrix (arguments : on (default) / off, speed (default 20 ms)
imi.slide.use_when: Smooth changes in a matrix over time with `jit.slide` driven by an internal `qmetro`. Abstraction, 2 inlets / 1 outlet; args: on/off (default on), slide amount / speed (default 20 ms). Built-in `jit.slide` alone is usually simpler. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.splitscale.digest: takes an init value (500) and a range value (450-500) and strictly map to values of the output  (0.1 to 0.75 in the example).
imi.splitscale.use_when: Map values below and above a centre point to two output ranges (e.g. `imi.splitscale 500 50 0.1 0.75`: input around 450–550, output 0.1–0.75). Abstraction, 1 inlet / 1 outlet; args: centre, range, output low, output high. Part of the input range is hard-coded to 450/550. Built on `split` + `scale`. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

imi.through.use_when: Wrap a moving x/y position around between 0 and a limit (args: x limit, y limit), so drawings leaving one edge re-enter at the other. Abstraction, 1 inlet (pair) / 1 outlet. Built-in `pong @mode wrap` does it for single values. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

iterate.digest: simple iterate abstraction : pick up a method then click iterate
iterate.use_when: Apply a chosen math expression repeatedly to a starting number: left inlet = starting number, right inlet = the expression (e.g. `$f1 * 3`), bang iterate. Abstraction, 2 inlets / 1 outlet; rewrites its internal `expr` box by scripting when the expression changes. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

max_messaging.digest: with a comma between the values, the first one (30) is sent first then the second one (50), see the Max window
max_messaging.use_when: Demo patch (not an object) on building messages with `pack`/`pak`, `zl.group`, `zl.join`, `sprintf`, and storing text with `coll`, `text` and `dict`, drawing results in `jit.mgraphics`. Open it as a reference. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

maxuino.digest: 5. If you still have troubles, mail to chris.d.coleman@gmail.com/batchku@gmail.com or try someone from the readme, or the Arduino Forums.
maxuino.use_when: Maxuino: control an Arduino running StandardFirmata from Max (pin modes, digital/analog read and write, PWM, servos). The abstraction is `maxuino` (2 inlets / 3 outlets); its help file is named `maxuin.maxhelp`. Arguments set the serial port (e.g. `maxuino c`); messages such as `pinMode <pin> <mode>` (0 digital in, 1 digital out, 2 analog in, 3 PWM, 4 servo), `analogWrite <pin> <value>`, `digitalWrite <pin> <value>`. Upload StandardFirmata to the board first. A Max for Live device version is included. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

messenger.use_when: Talk to an Arduino running the Messenger library over serial with Arduino-like commands: `p m 13 1` (pinMode), `w d 13 $1` (digitalWrite), `r d` / `r a` (read all digital / analog pins). Abstraction, 1 inlet / 1 outlet; args: port letter, baud rate (e.g. `messenger c 115200`); messages `port`, `baud`, `print`. Needs the matching sketch (basic_communication.ino). Built on `serial`. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

mmf-fs.core.digest: keep this patch opened, or place [mmf-fs.core] as an abstraction or in a bpatcher anywhere in your patch
mmf-fs.core.use_when: MMF-Fantastick (Mathieu Chamagne, Max Multitouch Framework): receives touch data from the Fantastick app on iPhone/iPad over UDP and sends it interface images. The loadable abstraction is `mmf-fs.core` (keep it open, or place it as an abstraction or bpatcher anywhere in the patch); it has no inlets/outlets and communicates by `send`/`receive` (e.g. `toFantaStick`). Configure UDP ports, device IP and web-server address in its preferences. Needs the Fantastick app. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

nothing-detector.digest: toggled when nothing is happening for 1 second
nothing-detector.use_when: Detect when a data stream stops changing: outputs 1 while values change and 0 after the timeout (argument, ms) passes with no change. Abstraction by Mattyo, 2 inlets (data, threshold ms) / 1 outlet. Use for 'nobody is interacting' states in installations. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

o.list.crossover.digest: (default) @mix = 0.5 : equal distribution, 50% from parent A and 50% from parent B
o.list.crossover.use_when: Genetic-algorithm crossover: breed an offspring list from two parent lists. Abstraction, 1 inlet taking `A <list>` / `B <list>` (the help prepends `A` and `B`), `size`, and bang to generate. Attributes: `@mix` (0 = all A … 1 = all B, default 0.5), `@mutation` (0. = none), `@points` (crossover points); mutation ranges via `min`/`max`, `imin`/`imax`, `fmin`/`fmax`. Works with ints, floats and symbols and lists of different sizes. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

o.midi.prob-rhythm.use_when: Probabilistic rhythm (zeroth-order Markov): each step plays with the probability stored in a weight table. Abstraction, 4 inlets / 2 outlets. Inlet 1: int = output that step, bang = iterate, `set <n>` = jump without output; inlet 2: step weights as a list (0.–1., e.g. from `multislider`); inlet 3: max velocity 0–127; inlet 4: overall probability 0–100. Outlets: velocity (0–127), step number. Attributes `maxvel`, `overall_prob`, `seed`. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

o.num2list.digest: This object will output a list comprised of N elements. Each element is equal to the input.
o.num2list.use_when: Repeat an incoming value N times as a list (e.g. `5` → `5 5 5 5`); works with symbols. Abstraction, 2 inlets (value, list size) / 1 outlet; argument = list size (default 32). Handy before `vexpr` to multiply a list by one number. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

past2.use_when: Bang when a float value rises past a threshold (argument), and report falling back below on the second outlet. Abstraction, 2 inlets / 2 outlets; float version of `imi.past`. Built-in `past` covers the rising case. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

randomness.digest: predicts the future from the past
randomness.use_when: Weighted random choice: outputs values according to a list of probabilities. Abstraction (by digiology), 3 inlets / 1 outlet: left = bang to output, middle = list of values, right = list of probabilities in percent. Built on `table` (whose bang gives a weighted random index). Its help file is instead an index of random, Markov-chain and flocking demos. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

shell2UTCtime.use_when: Convert a Unix timestamp (seconds, e.g. from `date +%s` via the `shell` external) into a readable GMT date and time string. Abstraction by Italo Lombardo, 1 inlet / 1 outlet. Built-in `date` gives the local date and time directly. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

textcoordmagic.digest: apply a texture (texture) onto a 3d object and use texcoordmagic to change the size, anchor and position .
textcoordmagic.use_when: Zoom, rotate and position a texture on a 3D GL shape by generating `tex_plane_s` / `tex_plane_t` messages. Abstraction by Wes Smith; 3 inlets set zoom, anchor and angle; 1 outlet to a GL object using `@tex_map 1` (e.g. `jit.gl.gridshape`); args set initial zoom, anchor and angle. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

threshold~.digest: threshold~ monitors its input signal and outputs bangs when the signal exceeds a specified "trigger" value, and also when the signal recedes below a "rest" value. You can specify debounce times in milliseconds, for the threshold~ to wait after the two event types before triggering again.
threshold~.use_when: Bang when a signal rises above a 'trigger' level and again when it falls below a 'rest' level, with separate debounce times — a port of Pd's `threshold~`. Abstraction, 5 inlets (signal, low threshold, high threshold, low debounce ms, high debounce ms) / 2 bang outlets. Built on `thresh~` + `edge~`. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

tweening.use_when: Demo patch showing easing (tweening) between two values with the `tween.js` script from the same folder, driven by `metro` + `counter`; choose ease type and direction from menus. Not a reusable object. From Max for the Visual Arts (Nicolas Maréchal's teaching toolkit).

mira.channel.digest: Send and receive arbitrary data between Max and a browser.
mira.channel.use_when: Send and receive arbitrary data between Max and a browser.

mira.status.digest: Report status of all Mira clients.
mira.status.use_when: Report status of all Mira clients.

gf.digest: Real-time following and recognition of time profiles
gf.use_when: Real-time following and recognition of time profiles. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

imubu.digest: MuBu container with a graphical user interface
imubu.use_when: Interactive editor for a mubu container. UI for visualizing and editing tracks, markers, descriptors.

mc.mubu.concat~.use_when: MuBu concatenative synthesis engine. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

mc.mubu.granular~.use_when: MuBu granular synthesis engine. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

mimo.normalize.use_when: Mimo module (not a standalone box) that learns per-column statistics of a MuBu track and normalizes data with them. Train offline with `mubu.model <mubu> <track> normalize @name <outtrack>`; send `getmodel` to get the model as JSON (the help file copies it into a `dict` with `dict.deserialize`). Apply to live streams with `pipo normalize @normalize.model <dict>`. `@normalize.type` chooses minmax (scale to 0–1) or meanstd (center and divide by standard deviation). The MuBu equivalent of FluCoMa’s fluid.normalize~ / fluid.standardize~.

mimo.pca.use_when: Mimo module (not a standalone box) that performs Principal Component Analysis by singular value decomposition. Train with `mubu.model <mubu> <track> pca @name <outtrack>` (`@pca.rank -1` picks the rank automatically, a positive value sets it); copy the trained model to a `dict` with `getmodel`. Apply live with `pipo pca @pca.model <dict> @pca.direction forward` to reduce dimensions, or `@pca.direction backward` to reconstruct. `@pca.threshold` also available.

mimo.stats.use_when: Mimo module (not a standalone box) that computes basic statistics over all data of a MuBu track. Run it with `mubu.model <mubu> <track> stats @name <outtrack>`; send `getmodel` to get the statistics as JSON (the help file copies them into a `dict`). `@stats.alpha` sets the normalization step factor per training iteration.

mubu.use_when: Multi-buffer container — root object. Holds multiple named tracks (audio, MIDI, descriptors, markers). See package_concepts.md MuBu section. Use as the central data structure for time-tagged multi-modal content; reach for plain `buffer~` if all you need is mono/stereo audio.

mubu.additive~.use_when: MuBu additive synthesis engine. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

mubu.concat~.use_when: MuBu concatenative synthesis engine: plays whole segments of a MuBu audio track, where each segment is defined by a marker track (onset time, optionally duration and offset). Args: number of output channels, MuBu name, marker track id — e.g. `mubu.concat~ 2 <mubu> @audio audio @markers descr` as in camu.voice; the outlet count grows with the channel count. It plays the segment you address (`markerindex`, `bufferindex`, `position`, a `list`, or `bang` to trigger); it does not choose segments by sound — that is done upstream by `mubu.knn` (see camu.select). Key attributes: `@play 1` with `@period` / `@periodvar` for periodic playing, `@autotrigger 1` to play when a new index arrives, `@allowrepeatmarkers 0`, `@duration`, `@attack` / `@release`, `@resampling`, `@duplicatechannels 1`, `@outputstate 1` (reports marker, buffer and play state, needed by camu.cont and camu.random). MC version: mc.mubu.concat~. Core engine of catart-mubu.

mubu.dtw.use_when: Dynamic time warping object. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

mubu.gmm.digest: Gaussian Mixture Models for real-time recognition
mubu.gmm.use_when: Gaussian Mixture Models for real-time recognition. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

mubu.gmr.digest: Gaussian Mixture Regression for motion-sound mapping
mubu.gmr.use_when: Gaussian Mixture Regression for motion-sound mapping. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

mubu.granular~.use_when: MuBu granular synthesis engine: plays asynchronous grains from an audio track of a MuBu container, or synchronous (pitch-period) grains when a marker track marks the waveform periods. Args: number of output channels, MuBu name, marker track id — e.g. `mubu.granular~ 2 <mubu> @play 1 @positionvar 3 @duplicatechannels 1`. Grains are placed by position (`position` message or `list`; the help file also drives position from a signal for sample-accurate sync), not selected by descriptors. Key attributes: `@play`, `@period` / `@periodvar` (ms), `@duration` / `@durationvar`, `@positionvar`, `@resampling` / `@resamplingvar`, `@attack` / `@release`, `@reverse`, `@filtermode` / `@filterfreq`, `@outputposition` (reports actually played grain position). Outlet count follows the channel count. MC version: mc.mubu.granular~.

mubu.gvf.use_when: Gesture Variation Follower. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

mubu.hhmm.digest: Hierarchical Hidden Markov Models for real-time continuous gesture recognition
mubu.hhmm.use_when: Hierarchical Hidden Markov Models for real-time continuous gesture recognition. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

mubu.knn.use_when: K-NN unit selection. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

mubu.model.use_when: Process MuBu tracks. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

mubu.play.use_when: Play track. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

mubu.play~.use_when: MuBu audio track player: plays an audio track of a MuBu container as signal, or a plain buffer~ when the track id is `[audio]` (e.g. `mubu.play~ <buffername> [audio]`). Args: MuBu name, track id. `@channels` sets the number of signal outlets (shown in the help file; missing from the refpage). `@play 1` / `0` starts and stops, `@loop` loops the current region, `@bufferindex` / `@trackid` choose what to play, `pause` / `resume`. Use to audition corpus files or play regions selected in imubu. For playing non-audio track data as messages use mubu.play.

mubu.process.use_when: Process MuBu tracks. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

mubu.record.use_when: Record data. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

mubu.record~.use_when: Record audio into a mubu container's audio track at runtime.

mubu.scroll.use_when: Reverse Time Scroll of Vectors. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

mubu.track.use_when: Access MuBu track. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

mubu.xmm.digest: Hierarchical Multimodal Hidden Markov Models for continuous recognition and mapping
mubu.xmm.use_when: Hierarchical Multimodal Hidden Markov Models for continuous recognition and mapping. MuBu container operation — see package_concepts.md MuBu section.

pipo.digest: Simple PiPo host receiving and outputting lists
pipo.use_when: PiPo host for lists: runs a chain of PiPo modules on incoming data frames (sensor data, descriptors) and outputs the processed frames. Args: frame width, frame size, then the PiPo definition — module names without the `pipo.` prefix, joined with colons, e.g. `pipo median:scale @median.size 13`, `pipo 1euro`. Module attributes carry the module prefix (`@median.size`); a module can be renamed in the chain, e.g. `savitzkygolay(sg)` → `@sg.size`. Host attributes: `@framerate` (set it to the real data rate — time-based modules otherwise assume 1000 Hz), `@dims`, `@labels`, `@timetagged`. `reset` clears module state; `getoutdims` / `getoutlabels` report the output format. Saved boxes have 2 inlets and 3 outlets. Mimo models trained with mubu.model can be applied here, e.g. `pipo normalize @normalize.model <dict>`.

pipo.1euro.use_when: PiPo module (not a standalone box) implementing the 1€ filter (Casiez et al. 2012): a cascaded lowpass whose cutoff rises with the signal's speed, so slow or still input is smoothed hard while fast movement keeps little lag. Use it by name without the `pipo.` prefix inside a PiPo host: `pipo 1euro` for live lists (sensor frames), or `mubu.process <mubu> <track> 1euro @name <outtrack> @samplerate <rate>` to filter a recorded track offline. Attributes carry the module prefix: `@1euro.fcmin` (minimum cutoff frequency — the smoothing at rest), `@1euro.beta` (speed factor: how quickly the cutoff opens as the input moves), `@1euro.order` (number of cascaded filter passes), `@1euro.bypass`. Give the host the real data rate (`@framerate` on `pipo`, `@samplerate` on mubu.process / mubu.track); otherwise 1000 Hz is assumed and the cutoffs are wrong. Use for IMU, gyroscope, touch or mouse data where fixed smoothing either lags or jitters; for a fixed amount of smoothing `slide` is simpler.

pipo.bands.use_when: PiPo module (not a standalone box) that groups FFT bins into bands on a chosen frequency scale (`@bands.mode`, e.g. mel). Use it by name, without the `pipo.` prefix, inside a PiPo host: `pipo` (lists), `pipo~` (live audio), `mubu.process` (MuBu tracks, offline) or `mubu.model`; chain modules with colons. Example based on the help files: `mubu.process <mubu> audio slice:fft:bands @fft.mode power @bands.mode mel @bands.num 24`. Attributes carry the module prefix: `@bands.mode`, `@bands.eqlmode`, `@bands.num`, `@bands.log`, `@bands.power`, `@bands.limits`.

pipo.basic.use_when: PiPo module (not a standalone box) that computes basic audio descriptors: f0, periodicity, loudness and spectral moments. Use it by name, without the `pipo.` prefix, inside a PiPo host: `pipo` (lists), `pipo~` (live audio), `mubu.process` (MuBu tracks, offline) or `mubu.model`; chain modules with colons. Attributes carry the module prefix: `@basic.winsize`, `@basic.hopsize`, `@basic.minfreq`, `@basic.downsampling`, `@basic.threshold`. Same description as pipo.descr, and its help file actually demonstrates the `descr` module; prefer `descr`.

pipo.bayesfilter.use_when: PiPo module (not a standalone box) that extracts a smooth envelope from EMG muscle-sensor data by non-linear Bayesian filtering. Use it by name, without the `pipo.` prefix, inside a PiPo host: `pipo` (lists), `pipo~` (live audio), `mubu.process` (MuBu tracks, offline) or `mubu.model`; chain modules with colons. Example based on the help files: `pipo bayesfilter @bayesfilter.logjumprate -10`. Attributes carry the module prefix: `@bayesfilter.logdiffusion`, `@bayesfilter.logjumprate`, `@bayesfilter.mvc`, `@bayesfilter.levels`, `@bayesfilter.clipping`, `@bayesfilter.alpha`, `@bayesfilter.beta`, `@bayesfilter.rectification`.

pipo.biquad.use_when: PiPo module (not a standalone box) that filters a data stream (not audio) with a biquad filter. Use it by name, without the `pipo.` prefix, inside a PiPo host: `pipo` (lists), `pipo~` (live audio), `mubu.process` (MuBu tracks, offline) or `mubu.model`; chain modules with colons. Example based on the help files: `pipo biquad @framerate 200 @biquad.filtermode bandpass @biquad.frequency 5 @biquad.Q 1`. Attributes carry the module prefix: `@biquad.b0`, `@biquad.b1`, `@biquad.b2`, `@biquad.a1`, `@biquad.a2`, `@biquad.biquadtype`, `@biquad.filtermode`, `@biquad.gain`, `@biquad.frequency`, `@biquad.Q`. For audio signals use `biquad~`.

pipo.chop.use_when: PiPo module (not a standalone box) that cuts the stream into fixed-size segments and outputs per-segment statistics (`@chop.mean`, `@chop.stddev`, `@chop.min`, `@chop.max`, `@chop.duration`). Use it by name, without the `pipo.` prefix, inside a PiPo host: `pipo` (lists), `pipo~` (live audio), `mubu.process` (MuBu tracks, offline) or `mubu.model`; chain modules with colons. Example based on the help files: `pipo~ loudness:chop @chop.size 242 @chop.mean 1`. Attributes carry the module prefix: `@chop.offset`, `@chop.size`, `@chop.segtimes`, `@chop.segdurations`, `@chop.duration`, `@chop.min`, `@chop.max`, `@chop.mean`, `@chop.stddev`. The standard segmentation in catart-mubu: `descr:chop`.

pipo.const.use_when: PiPo module (not a standalone box) that adds a column holding a constant value, named with `@const.name`. Use it by name, without the `pipo.` prefix, inside a PiPo host: `pipo` (lists), `pipo~` (live audio), `mubu.process` (MuBu tracks, offline) or `mubu.model`; chain modules with colons. Example based on the help files: `mubu.process <mubu> audio descr:chop:const @name descr`. Attributes carry the module prefix: `@const.value`, `@const.name`. catart-mubu uses it to reserve a named column (e.g. `@const.name FilenameNoteNumber`) that camu.filenamenotenumber fills.

pipo.cqt.use_when: PiPo module (not a standalone box) that computes a constant-Q spectrum with musically spaced bins. Use it by name, without the `pipo.` prefix, inside a PiPo host: `pipo` (lists), `pipo~` (live audio), `mubu.process` (MuBu tracks, offline) or `mubu.model`; chain modules with colons. Example based on the help files: `pipo~ cqt`. Attributes carry the module prefix: `@cqt.hop`, `@cqt.mode`, `@cqt.numbins`, `@cqt.minfreq`, `@cqt.octavebins`, `@cqt.threshold`, `@cqt.scale`, `@cqt.window`, `@cqt.minkernelsize`, `@cqt.zerophase`.

pipo.dct.use_when: PiPo module (not a standalone box) that computes a discrete cosine transform of each frame. Use it by name, without the `pipo.` prefix, inside a PiPo host: `pipo` (lists), `pipo~` (live audio), `mubu.process` (MuBu tracks, offline) or `mubu.model`; chain modules with colons. Example based on the help files: `pipo~ slice:dct`. Attributes carry the module prefix: `@dct.order`, `@dct.weighting`.

pipo.delta.digest: delta filter for estimating derivative and acceleration
pipo.delta.use_when: PiPo module (not a standalone box) that estimates the rate of change (derivative) of each column by linear regression over `@delta.size` frames. Use it by name, without the `pipo.` prefix, inside a PiPo host: `pipo` (lists), `pipo~` (live audio), `mubu.process` (MuBu tracks, offline) or `mubu.model`; chain modules with colons. Example based on the help files: `pipo delta @delta.size 9`. Attributes carry the module prefix: `@delta.size`, `@delta.normalize`, `@delta.absolute`.

pipo.descr.use_when: PiPo module (not a standalone box) that computes basic audio descriptors: f0, periodicity, loudness and spectral moments. Use it by name, without the `pipo.` prefix, inside a PiPo host: `pipo` (lists), `pipo~` (live audio), `mubu.process` (MuBu tracks, offline) or `mubu.model`; chain modules with colons. Example based on the help files: `mubu.process <mubu> audio descr:onseg @name descr @descr.moments 1`. Use it by name, without the `pipo.` prefix, inside a PiPo host: `pipo` (lists), `pipo~` (live audio), `mubu.process` (MuBu tracks, offline) or `mubu.model`; chain modules with colons.
