Attributes carry the module prefix: `@yin.minfreq`, `@yin.downsampling`, `@yin.threshold`, `@yin.old`, `@yin.qualitygate`.

pipo~.digest: Simple PiPo host receiving audio and outputting lists
pipo~.use_when: PiPo host for live audio: runs a chain of PiPo modules on the incoming signal and outputs analysis frames as lists (outlets: results, frame time, info). Args: optional audio input size, then the PiPo definition — module names without the `pipo.` prefix, joined with colons, e.g. `pipo~ slice:fft:moments`, `pipo~ loudness:chop @chop.size 242`, `pipo~ mel @mel.log 1`. Module attributes carry the module prefix (`@slice.size`, `@fft.mode`). Host attributes: `@outputbuffer`, `@active`. `reset` clears state. Offline counterpart on recorded tracks: `mubu.process`.

nls.ar~.use_when: Clickless exponential attack-release envelope triggered at audio rate: send a click~ or trigger signal to the left inlet; other inlets set duration (ms) and envelope shape; output is the envelope signal to multiply with a sound (*~). Also available as mc.nls.ar~ via the package's init mapping. Commonly driven by nls.cross_seq2~ / nls.cross_seq3~ triggers.

nls.cross_seq2~.use_when: Rhythm generator from two LFOs: every time the two LFO curves intersect, a trigger is produced. Outlet 1: audio trigger signal; outlet 2: a 4-channel MC cable with LFO 1, LFO 2, their normalized difference, and the master phasor. Messages set freq (master rate), per-LFO rate (rt1, rt2), waveform interpolation (w1, w2: 0 sine, 1 tri, 2 rect, 3 saw), phase (ph1, ph2), amount (am1, am2) and pulse width (pw1, pw2). Deterministic, not random: patterns morph as parameters change. A ready bpatcher is in the snippets.

nls.cross_seq3~.use_when: Rhythm generator from three LFOs: triggers fire at intersections 1-2, 1-3, 2-3 and 1-2-3. Outlets 1-4: triggers; 5-7: the three LFOs; 8-11: normalized differences between LFO pairs and total; 12: master phasor. Messages like nls.cross_seq2~ (freq, rt1-rt3, w1-w3, ph1-ph3, am1-am3). LFOs can map to pitch and differences to velocity. A ready bpatcher is in the snippets.

nls.trigger_logic~.use_when: Trigger-logic combinator for nls.* streams — boolean/conditional gating between sequencer outputs.

IOmap~.use_when: Route 8 audio channels to 8 outputs with click-free 100 ms fades, usually just before `dac~ 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8`, so a piece can be remapped to any venue's speaker numbering without repatching. It is `matrix~ 8 8 0 @ramp 100` inside, so the left inlet takes every `matrix~` message: `<in> <out> <gain>` triplet lists (numbered from 0), `connect`, `disconnect`, `clear`. It starts with nothing connected, so send a pass-through list on load (the help sends `0 0 1 1 1 1 2 2 1 ...`) or drive it from a `patchbay` bpatcher.

IOrouter8to2dd~.use_when: Fold an octophonic 'double diamond' mix (speaker 1 center-front, numbered clockwise) down to stereo, to check octophonic panning on headphones or two speakers. Connect the eight outlets of `octopan~`, `panpolardd~` or `surroundstereo~` to its eight inlets; it pans each channel by its left-right position and makes side and rear channels softer, darker (`lores~`) and a little reverberant. No arguments or messages. Needs Max 9, because it uses `abl.dsp.darkhall~` from the ableton-dsp package.

balancestereo~.digest: Adjust the balance of two signals
balancestereo~.use_when: Turn down one side of a stereo signal without moving either channel: inlets 1-2 take left and right audio, inlet 3 a float balance (0. = left only, 0.5 = no change, 1. = right only). The side being reduced fades by up to -60 dB and then to silence, over a 10 ms `line~` ramp. The balance is float only (no signal); an optional argument sets the starting balance (default 0.5). To move one channel toward the other instead, use `panstereo~`.

circularLRFBpan~.use_when: Spin a mono sound in a steady circle around four speakers (outlets left-front, right-front, left-rear, right-rear). Inlet 2 is the rotation rate in Hz, float or signal (negative = counterclockwise, 0 = pause); inlet 3 is a float azimuth 0.-1. (clockwise from front) to jump to. Inside, a `phasor~` drives two `cycle~` a quarter-cycle apart into `panLRFB~`. From the package's misc folder.

circularXYslider.digest: 2D slider constrained within a unit circle
circularXYslider.use_when: A 2D mouse pad that outputs x and y from -1. to 1., always kept inside the unit circle, for driving circular panners. Load it in a `bpatcher` sized 256x256 (or 256x302) with offset -128 -128; send an `x y` list to set it without the mouse; outlets are x and y floats. The help converts its output with `cartopol` to feed `panpolardd~`. Needs Max 9 (it draws with `v8` and `lcd`).

cubepan~.digest: Constant-intensity octophonic audio panning for a cuboid configuration, using xyz values
cubepan~.use_when: Pan a mono sound in 3D among eight speakers at the corners of a cube: outlets 1-4 are the lower ring (left-front, right-front, left-back, right-back), 5-8 the upper ring in the same order. Inlets 2-4 take left-to-right, front-to-back and down-to-up, each 0.-1., as float or signal; three arguments set the starting positions. It is `pan~` (down-up) feeding two `panLRFB~`, so it keeps constant intensity.

distance2D.digest: Calculate the distance between two points in 2D space
distance2D.use_when: Get the straight-line distance between two 2D points as a float, for distance-based gain or delay. Send x0, y0, x1, y1 to the four inlets (only the left inlet triggers output) or a four-item list to the left inlet. It is one `expr`; for continuously moving sources use `distance2D~`.

distance2D~.digest: Calculate the distance between two points expressed as MSP signals
distance2D~.use_when: Signal-rate distance between two moving 2D points: four signal inlets x0, y0, x1, y1 and one signal outlet. Use it to drive `dopplerd~` (travel delay) and a 1/distance gain (`!/~ 1.` then `*~`), as the package's `dopplerdemo` example does.

distance3D.digest: Calculate the distance between two points in 3D space
distance3D.use_when: Get the distance between two 3D points as a float: six inlets x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1 (left inlet triggers) or a six-item list in the left inlet. Built on `expr`; use `distance3D~` for moving sources.

distance3D~.digest: Calculate the distance between two points expressed as MSP signals
distance3D~.use_when: Signal-rate distance between two moving 3D points: six signal inlets x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, one signal outlet. Feed `dopplerd~` and a 1/distance gain for a moving virtual source in 3D.

dopplerd~.digest: Delay a sound based on its distance
dopplerd~.use_when: Delay a sound by the time it takes sound to travel a distance, so a moving source gets a natural Doppler pitch shift. Inlet 1 audio; inlet 2 distance in meters, float or signal (use a signal for motion). Inside it multiplies by 2.915452 ms per meter (343 m/s), converts to samples and drives `delay~`'s signal delay input, which interpolates. `@maxdelay <samples>` (default 48000) sizes the buffer: that is 343 m at 48 kHz but only about 171 m at 96 kHz, so raise it for long distances or high sample rates.

fourchanpan~.digest: Constant-intensity panning between four speakers placed in a linear array or an arc
fourchanpan~.use_when: Pan a mono sound across four speakers in a straight line or front arc (outlets left to right) with constant intensity. Inlet 2 is the position 0.-1. and must be a signal (use `sig~` or `line~` for set values): 0.-0.333 pans between speakers 1-2, then 2-3, then 3-4. Built from three `pan~` stages chosen by `gate~ 3`; two of them make `pan2x4~`.

gainsimple~.use_when: Set a mono signal's level in dB with no UI, like a one-channel `live.gain~` without the slider. Inlet 2 takes dB as a float or int (0 = unchanged, -70 or lower = silence), smoothed over 10 ms by `line~`; it does not accept a signal there, despite the refpage. Handy inside `poly~` voices or wherever many level stages would clutter the screen; use `live.gain~` when the operator needs to see and touch the level.

hexapan~.digest: Constant-intensity panning between six speakers placed in a hexagon
hexapan~.use_when: Pan a mono sound around six speakers in a hexagon with constant intensity. Inlet 2 azimuth 0.-1. clockwise from front (signal; wraps, negative goes counterclockwise); inlet 3 spread 0.-1. (0 = two nearest speakers, up to 0.5 = four, up to 1 = all six); inlet 4 int layout: 1 (default) puts speaker 1 at -30 degrees (front-left), 0 puts speaker 1 dead center. It can sit in a 128x128 `bpatcher` that shows the layout; clicking the diagram toggles it. Spread above 0 raises the total loudness.

kinky~.use_when: Demo phase-distortion synth voice (`kink~` bending a `phasor~` that reads a `cycle~`), built to run inside `poly~` or `mc.poly~` so each note can be panned separately with an mc Panning Tools panner. Inlets: MIDI pitch (triggers the note), velocity (loudness and brightness, default 127), duration ms (1000), attack ms (100), release ms (500); a bang retriggers and a list sets several at once. Total note length is duration plus release.

mc.cubepan~.digest: Constant-intensity octophonic audio panning for a cuboid configuration, using xyz values
mc.cubepan~.use_when: MC version of `cubepan~` for panning many voices in 3D at once: inlet 1 an MC signal of N sounds, inlets 2-4 left-right, front-back and down-up as MC signals (0.-1. per voice). Each outlet is an MC cord with one channel per voice, so mix each outlet to mono with `mc.mixdown~ 1` before `dac~`. Control inlets want MC signals with one channel per voice (build them with `mc.sig~ @chans N` plus `mc.target`, or `mc.list~`).

mc.distance2D~.digest: Calculate the distance between two points expressed as MSP signals
mc.distance2D~.use_when: MC version of `distance2D~`: four MC signal inlets (x0, y0, x1, y1), one channel per voice, and an MC outlet of per-voice distances. Use it before `mc.dopplerd~` and a per-voice 1/distance gain when many sources move independently.

mc.distance3D~.digest: Calculate the distance between two points expressed as MSP signals
mc.distance3D~.use_when: MC version of `distance3D~`: six MC signal inlets (x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1), one channel per voice, and an MC outlet of per-voice distances for per-voice Doppler delay and gain.

mc.dopplerd~.digest: Delay a sound based on its distance
mc.dopplerd~.use_when: MC version of `dopplerd~`: inlet 1 an MC signal of N sounds, inlet 2 an MC signal of distances in meters (one per voice); each voice gets its own travel delay through `mc.delay~`. The argument is meant to set the maximum delay in samples (default 48000), but the patch sends it as a `maxdelay` message, which `mc.delay~` does not document (its message is `maxsize`), so it may not resize the buffer; test before relying on long distances.

mc.fourchanpan~.digest: Constant-intensity panning between four speakers placed in a linear array or an arc
mc.fourchanpan~.use_when: MC version of `fourchanpan~` for many voices across four speakers in a line: inlet 1 an MC signal of N sounds, inlet 2 an MC signal of positions 0.-1. Each outlet is an MC cord with one channel per voice, so mix each outlet to mono with `mc.mixdown~ 1` before `dac~`.

mc.hexapan~.digest: Constant-intensity panning between six speakers placed in a hexagon
mc.hexapan~.use_when: MC version of `hexapan~`: inlet 1 an MC signal of N sounds, inlets 2-3 MC signals of azimuth and spread (one per voice), inlet 4 an int layout (1 = speaker 1 front-left, 0 = speaker 1 center). Each outlet is an MC cord with one channel per voice, so mix each outlet to mono with `mc.mixdown~ 1` before `dac~`.

mc.mixS~.digest: Combine two signals using sinusoidal gain curves
mc.mixS~.use_when: MC version of `mixS~`: S-curve crossfade between two MC signals channel by channel. Inlet 3 takes an MC signal of mix values (0.-1. per channel) or a float that sets every channel; an argument sets the starting mix.

mc.mix~.digest: Combine two signals with linear crossfade
mc.mix~.use_when: MC version of `mix~`: linear crossfade between two MC signals channel by channel. Inlet 3 takes an MC signal of balances (0.-1. per channel) or a float that sets every channel; an argument sets the starting balance.

mc.octopan~.digest: Constant-intensity panning between eight speakers placed as an octagon
mc.octopan~.use_when: MC version of `octopan~` for giving many voices their own place around eight speakers (speaker 1 center-front, clockwise): inlet 1 an MC signal of N sounds (for instance from `mc.poly~`), inlets 2-3 MC signals of azimuth and spread (0.-1. per voice). Each outlet is an MC cord with one channel per voice, so mix each outlet to mono with `mc.mixdown~ 1` before `dac~`. The `circularharmonics` example pans 32 voices this way.

mc.pan2x4~.digest: Constant-intensity octophonic audio panning using xy values
mc.pan2x4~.use_when: MC version of `pan2x4~` for many voices in a shoebox of four stereo pairs: inlet 1 an MC signal of N sounds, inlets 2-3 MC signals of left-right and front-back (0.-1. per voice). Each outlet is an MC cord with one channel per voice, so mix each outlet to mono with `mc.mixdown~ 1` before `dac~`.

mc.panLRFB~.digest: Constant-intensity quadraphonic audio panning using xy values
mc.panLRFB~.use_when: MC version of `panLRFB~` for many voices over four speakers in a rectangle: inlet 1 an MC signal of N sounds, inlets 2-3 MC signals of left-right and front-back (0.-1. per voice). Outlets are left-front, right-front, left-rear, right-rear, each an MC cord; mix each with `mc.mixdown~ 1`.

mc.panlinear~.use_when: MC version of `panlinear~`: linear stereo pan of each channel of an MC signal. Inlet 2 takes an MC signal of positions or a float that sets every channel. Each outlet is an MC cord with one channel per voice, so mix each outlet to mono with `mc.mixdown~ 1` before `dac~`. Mostly for comparing with `mc.pan~`.

mc.panpolardd~.digest: Constant-intensity panning among eight speakers in "double diamond" configuration
mc.panpolardd~.use_when: MC version of `panpolardd~`: each voice of an MC signal gets its own distance (inlet 2) and azimuth (inlet 3) as MC signals, panned over a double-diamond octagon. Each outlet is an MC cord with one channel per voice, so mix each outlet to mono with `mc.mixdown~ 1` before `dac~`.

mc.panstereo~.digest: Alter the panning of a stereo sound
mc.panstereo~.use_when: MC version of `panstereo~`: inlets 1-2 left and right MC signals, inlet 3 an MC signal of amounts -1. to 1. (0 = unchanged). Use it when many stereo voices each need their own width shift. Its refpage file names itself `panstereo~`.

mc.pan~.use_when: MC version of `pan~` for panning many voices independently: inlet 1 an N-channel MC signal (for instance from `mc.poly~`), inlet 2 an N-channel MC signal of positions 0.-1. (build it with `mc.sig~ @chans N` plus `mc.target`, or `mc.list~`). Outlet 1 carries every voice's left signal and outlet 2 every right signal; sum each with `mc.mixdown~ 1` before `dac~`. Max's own `mc.stereo~` pans and sums to one 2-channel MC cord in a single object.

mc.perturbxyz~.digest: Add a random offset to x, y, and z signals
mc.perturbxyz~.use_when: MC version of `perturbxyz~`: adds a slowly wandering random offset to x, y and z MC signals, voice by voice. Inlets 4-6 set the maximum offsets and inlet 7 the rate in Hz (MC signal or float for all channels); arguments set their starting values.

mc.perturbxy~.digest: Add a random offset to x and y signals
mc.perturbxy~.use_when: MC version of `perturbxy~`: adds a wandering random offset to x and y MC signals, voice by voice, for jittering many panning positions at once. Inlets 3-4 set the maximum offsets, inlet 5 the rate in Hz; arguments set the starting values.

mc.perturb~.digest: Add a random perturbation (offset) to a signal
mc.perturb~.use_when: MC version of `perturb~`: adds a wandering random offset (built on `mc.rand~`) to every channel of an MC signal. Inlet 2 sets the maximum offset and inlet 3 the rate in Hz, as MC signals or floats that set every channel; arguments set the starting values.

mc.quadpan~.digest: Constant-intensity quadraphonic audio panning using azimuth angle
mc.quadpan~.use_when: MC version of `quadpan~`: inlet 1 an MC signal of N sounds, inlet 2 an MC signal of azimuths (0.-1. clockwise from front, one per voice). Outlets are left-front, right-front, left-rear, right-rear, each an MC cord; mix each with `mc.mixdown~ 1`.

mc.surroundstereo~.digest: Distribute a stereo sound to 8 speakers in an octagon
mc.surroundstereo~.use_when: MC version of `surroundstereo~`: left and right MC signals (one channel per stereo voice) spread over eight speakers, with rotation, spread and separation as MC signals (inlets 3-5). Each outlet is an MC cord with one channel per voice, so mix each outlet to mono with `mc.mixdown~ 1` before `dac~`.

mixS~.digest: Combine two signals using sinusoidal gain curves
mixS~.use_when: Crossfade two signals with S-shaped (raised-cosine) gain curves, so changes are gentler near each end. Inlets 1-2 audio, inlet 3 mix 0.-1. (0 = first only, 0.5 = half each, 1 = second only), float or signal; an argument sets the starting mix. The two gains always add to 1, so, like `mix~`, two unrelated sounds dip about 3 dB at the midpoint; for an equal-loudness crossfade use the two outputs of `pan~` (fed `sig~ 1.`) as gains.

mix~.digest: Combine two signals with linear crossfade
mix~.use_when: Mix or crossfade two signals linearly, for instance as a dry/wet control: inlets 1-2 audio, inlet 3 balance 0.-1. (0 = first, 1 = second), float or signal; an argument sets the starting balance. It computes a + (b - a) x balance, one multiply instead of two. Smooth float changes (for instance `line~` over 10 ms) to avoid clicks.

noisebandstereo~.use_when: Demo band-limited noise synth voice with a stereo pan built in, for `poly~` or `mc.poly~`. The left inlet triggers a note on bang, a number (center frequency) or a seven-item list; the other inlets, or the messages `f`, `a`, `q`, `dur`, `att`, `rel`, `pan`, set amplitude, Q (higher = more pitched), duration, attack, release (ms) and pan 0.-1. Arguments give the defaults (440 1 10 500 1 499 0.5). Inside `poly~` the pan is fixed at each note's start, so overlapping notes keep separate places.

noiseband~.use_when: Demo band-limited noise synth voice (`rand~` noise ring-modulated by `cycle~`) for `poly~` or `mc.poly~`; pair with an mc panner to place each note. The left inlet triggers on bang, a number (center frequency) or a six-item list; the other inlets, or the messages `f`, `a`, `q`, `dur`, `att`, `rel`, set amplitude, Q, duration, attack and release (ms). Arguments give the defaults (440 1 10 500 1 499).

octonode~.digest: Panning among eight speakers based on the source's proximity to each speaker
octonode~.use_when: Pan a mono sound among eight speakers in a circle by dragging a point over a `nodes` display; each speaker's level depends on how close the point is to it. Load it in a `bpatcher` sized 256x256 with offset -128 -128. Inlet 2 takes an `x y` list (-1. to 1., 0 0 = center, all speakers equal); inlet 3 an `angle distance` list (0.-1.). Levels ramp over 25 ms through `matrix~`. Not constant-intensity: each speaker is about -9 dB when the point is at the center.

octopan2~.digest: Constant-intensity panning between eight speakers placed as an octagon
octopan2~.use_when: Same as `octopan~`, but for eight speakers with no center speaker: speaker 1 is 22.5 degrees left of front, numbered clockwise. Inlet 2 azimuth 0.-1. clockwise from front (0 = halfway between speakers 1 and 2), inlet 3 spread 0.-1.; use signals. Equivalent to adding 0.0625 to `octopan~`'s angle. From the misc folder.

octopan~.digest: Constant-intensity panning between eight speakers placed as an octagon
octopan~.use_when: The package's main octophonic panner: a mono sound around eight speakers in a circle with constant intensity, speaker 1 center-front, numbered clockwise ('double diamond'). Inlet 2 azimuth 0.-1. clockwise from front (0.0625 = halfway between speakers 1 and 2; wraps; negative goes counterclockwise); inlet 3 spread 0.-1. (0 = two nearest speakers, up to 0.333 = four, up to 0.666 = six, up to 1 = all eight). Use signals for both. It also has `in~`/`out~`, so it works as a `poly~` voice; spread above 0 raises total loudness.

octosampler~.use_when: A sound-file player whose output is panned to eight speakers by `octopan~`, built as a `poly~` or `mc.poly~` voice so overlapping sounds each keep their own place. The left inlet takes any `sfplay~` message (`preload`, a cue number to play, and so on); inlets 2-7 set amplitude, duration ms (0 = play to the end), attack, release, azimuth 0.-1. and spread 0.-1.

pan2x4~.digest: Constant-intensity octophonic audio panning using xy values
pan2x4~.use_when: Pan a mono sound in a 'shoebox' of eight speakers laid out as four left-right pairs from front to back (1-2 front, 3-4, 5-6, 7-8 back; odd = left). Inlet 2 left-to-right 0.-1.; inlet 3 front-to-back 0.-1., which must be a signal. Up to four speakers sound at once, with constant intensity. Built from `pan~` feeding two `fourchanpan~`.

panLRFB~.digest: Constant-intensity quadraphonic audio panning using xy values
panLRFB~.use_when: Pan a mono sound among four speakers in a rectangle using x and y: inlet 2 left-to-right, inlet 3 front-to-back, each 0.-1. (0.5 0.5 = center), float or signal; a two-item list in inlet 2 sets both. Outlets: left-front, right-front, left-rear, right-rear. Two arguments set the starting position. It is three `pan~` (one left-right, then each side front-back), so it keeps constant intensity and suits any x-y controller such as `pictslider`.

panlinear~.use_when: Stereo pan with a straight-line law: left gain = 1 - position, right gain = position. Inlet 2 position 0.-1., float or signal; an argument sets the start. Mainly for comparing panning laws: a centered sound is 3 dB quieter than at either side. Use `pan~` for normal panning.

panpolardd~.digest: Constant-intensity panning among eight speakers in "double diamond" configuration
panpolardd~.use_when: Pan a mono sound over eight speakers in a circle (speaker 1 center-front, clockwise) using polar controls: inlet 2 distance from center (0 = middle, 1 = circle edge; up to +/-1.414, negative flips to the opposite side), inlet 3 azimuth 0.-1. clockwise from front. Use signals. Unlike `octopan~` it can place a sound inside the circle, because it pans within two squares (two `panLRFB~`) turned 45 degrees apart. `circularXYslider` plus `cartopol` makes a ready controller.

panstereo~.digest: Alter the panning of a stereo sound
panstereo~.use_when: Move one side of a stereo sound toward the other: inlets 1-2 left and right audio, inlet 3 amount -1. to 1. (0 = unchanged; positive moves the left channel toward the right, negative moves the right toward the left), float or signal; an argument sets the start. It uses cosine gain curves and lowers the total by up to 3 dB as channels overlap, to avoid clipping. To simply turn one side down, use `balancestereo~`.

pan~.use_when: Pan a mono sound between two speakers with constant intensity (cosine/sine law, -3 dB each at center); the building block most other panners in the package use. Inlet 1 audio, inlet 2 position 0.-1. (0 = left, 0.5 = center, 1 = right) as float or signal; an argument sets the starting position. Use a signal (for instance `line~` over 10 ms) when moving it while sound plays, or it can click. Positions outside 0.-1. are not clipped and flip the polarity of a channel.

patchbay.use_when: An 8x8 on-screen grid (`matrixctrl`, one output per input by default) for choosing which channel goes to which speaker. Load it in a `bpatcher` and wire its outlet to the left inlet of `IOmap~` (or any 8x8 `matrix~`); an inner `pattr` saves the grid with the parent patch. It passes on any `matrixctrl` message, such as `one/column 0` to allow several outputs per input.

perturb.digest: Add a random perturbation (offset) to any number
perturb.use_when: Add a random offset up to +/- a maximum to each number, for small human-like variation (for instance pitch +/-1 semitone, level +/-10 dB, pan +/-0.1). The left inlet takes the number (int or float) and triggers output; the right inlet or the argument sets the maximum. Always outputs a float.

perturbxy.digest: Add a random perturbation (offset) to the coordinates of any xy point
perturbxy.use_when: Add random offsets to an x-y pair, for instance to scatter note locations around a panning path. Inlets: x (triggers), y, maximum x offset, maximum y offset; an `x y` list in the left inlet also works; two arguments set the maxima. Outputs x and y floats from two outlets.

perturbxyz.digest: Add a random perturbation (offset) to the coordinates of any xyz point
perturbxyz.use_when: Add random offsets to an x-y-z point, for scattering note locations in 3D (for instance before `cubepan~`). Inlets: x (triggers), y, z, then the three maxima; an `x y z` list in the left inlet also works; three arguments set the maxima. Three float outlets.

perturbxyz~.digest: Add a random offset to x, y, and z signals
perturbxyz~.use_when: Add slowly wandering random offsets to three signals, such as x, y and z panning controls. Inlets 1-3 the signals; inlets 4-6 the maximum offsets and inlet 7 the rate in Hz at which new offsets are chosen (signal or float; changes glide linearly). Four arguments set maxima and rate. Built on `rand~`.

perturbxy~.digest: Add a random offset to x and y signals
perturbxy~.use_when: Add slowly wandering random offsets to two signals, for instance to make a panned sound drift around its path. Inlets 1-2 the x and y signals; inlets 3-4 the maximum offsets and inlet 5 the rate in Hz (signal or float). Arguments set the two maxima and the rate. Built on `rand~`.

perturb~.digest: Add a random perturbation (offset) to a signal
perturb~.use_when: Add a slowly wandering random offset to a signal. Inlet 2 sets the maximum offset and inlet 3 the rate in Hz at which a new offset is chosen (signal or float; changes glide linearly); two arguments set their starting values. It is `rand~` scaled and added to the input.

polysimpleFM~.use_when: Demo two-operator FM voice (the MSP tutorial's simpleFM~ with `in~`/`out~` added) for `poly~` or `mc.poly~`. Three signal inlets: carrier frequency in Hz, harmonicity ratio, modulation index. It has no envelope, so shape the amplitude outside. Its help runs `mc.poly~ polysimpleFM~ 6` into `mc.pan~` and `mc.mixdown~ 1` for per-voice panning.

quadpan~.digest: Constant-intensity quadraphonic audio panning using azimuth angle
quadpan~.use_when: Pan a mono sound around four speakers in a square by angle alone: inlet 2 azimuth 0.-1. clockwise from front-center, float or signal (wraps; a `phasor~` gives a steady circle). Speakers sit at 45, 135, 225 and 315 degrees (outlets left-front, right-front, left-rear, right-rear). Only the two nearest speakers sound, with constant intensity, so it cannot move a sound through the middle of the room; use `panLRFB~` for that.

surroundstereosampler~.digest: Soundfile player with surround-stereo octophonic panning
surroundstereosampler~.use_when: A stereo sound-file player (`sfplay~ 2`) spread over eight speakers by `surroundstereo~`, built as a `poly~` or `mc.poly~` voice so each stereo cue gets its own rotation. The left inlet takes any `sfplay~` message; inlets 2-8 set amplitude, duration ms (0 = play to end), attack, release, rotation 0.-1., spread 0.-1. and separation -1. to 1.

surroundstereo~.digest: Distribute a stereo sound to 8 speakers in an octagon
surroundstereo~.use_when: Spread a stereo sound around eight speakers in a circle: two `octopan~` place the left and right channels either side of a rotation angle. Inlets: left audio, right audio, rotation 0.-1. clockwise from front, spread 0.-1. (applied at half strength per channel), separation -1. to 1. (0 = channels 45 degrees either side, 1 = 90 degrees; negative narrows but may clip); float or signal. Speaker 1 is center-front as in `octopan~`, whatever the refpage says.

JC_rev~.use_when: Reverb, not a physical model: John Chowning's JCRev (three series allpasses, four parallel combs, two decorrelation delays). Mono signal in, one signal out. Set decay with `T60 <seconds>` and balance with `mix <0-1>`. Cheap and somewhat metallic; compare `N_rev~` (denser) and `PRC_rev~` (lighter), or built-in `cverb~`.

N_rev~.use_when: Reverb, not a physical model: CCRMA NRev (six parallel combs, allpasses and a lowpass). Mono signal in, one signal out. `T60 <seconds>` sets decay, `mix <0-1>` sets dry/wet. The densest of PeRColate's three reverbs; see `JC_rev~`, `PRC_rev~`.

PRC_rev~.use_when: Reverb, not a physical model: Perry Cook's PRCRev (two series allpasses, two parallel combs). Mono signal in, one signal out. `T60 <seconds>` sets decay, `mix <0-1>` sets dry/wet. The lightest of PeRColate's three reverbs.

absmax~.digest: Compare two signals, output the absolute maximum
absmax~.use_when: Signal utility by R. Luke DuBois, not a physical model. Compares two signals (or a signal and a float) and outputs whichever has the larger absolute value, keeping its sign. Rarely needed: `maximum~` plus `abs~` covers most uses.

absmin~.digest: Compare two signals, output the absolute minimum
absmin~.use_when: Signal utility by R. Luke DuBois, not a physical model. Compares two signals (or a signal and a float) and outputs whichever has the smaller absolute value, keeping its sign. Rarely needed: `minimum~` plus `abs~` covers most uses.

agogo~.use_when: STK modal-synthesis agogo bell. Inlets (float/signal): stick hardness, stick position, amplitude, vibrato frequency, vibrato amount, frequency (Hz). Strike with a `noteon` message to the left inlet, damp with `noteoff`. Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first.

bamboo~.use_when: STK (PhISM) bamboo wind-chime model. Inlets: number of chimes, resonance, damping (0-1), maximum shake (energy), resonance spread (0-1), random resonance (0-1). Sound comes from shaking: change the energy / maximum-shake inlet repeatedly (a metro or noise into it). `metashaker~` covers this model and six others in one object.

bandedWG~.use_when: STK banded-waveguide model of bowed or struck bars, glass harmonica and Tibetan bowls. One inlet. Play it with `noteon <Hz> <amp 0-1>` and `noteoff <amp>`; shape it with `control <number> <value 0-128>`: 1 gain, 2 bow pressure, 4 bow motion, 11 vibrato frequency, 16 instrument (0 uniform bar, 1 tuned bar, 2 glass harmonica, 3 Tibetan bowl), 64 striking on/off, 128 bow velocity. Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first.

blotar~.use_when: Dan Trueman's hybrid of the STK flute and electric-guitar models. Twelve float/signal inlets: pluck amplitude, pluck position, body size, breath pressure, jet frequency, noise gain, vibrato frequency, vibrato amount, frequency (Hz), pre-feedback gain, pre-distortion gain, filter ratio. `mode 0` is the stabler classic algorithm, `mode 1` the less stable modern one; `mic <0-11>` picks a body perspective; `clear` resets delay lines. Superseded by `ublotar~`. Some settings get very loud; follow it with limi~ as the help file does.

blow_botl~.use_when: STK blown-bottle model (Helmholtz resonator with breath-noise jet). One inlet. Play it with `noteon <Hz> <amp 0-1>` and `noteoff <amp>`; shape it with `control <number> <value 0-128>`: 1 gain, 4 noise gain, 11 vibrato frequency, 128 volume. Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first.

blow_hole~.use_when: STK clarinet with a register hole and one tonehole. One inlet. Play it with `noteon <Hz> <amp 0-1>` and `noteoff <amp>`; shape it with `control <number> <value 0-128>`: 1 register hole state, 2 reed stiffness, 4 noise gain, 11 tonehole state, 128 breath pressure. The bore length is fixed, so its highest pitch is limited. Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first.

bowedbar~.use_when: STK bowed-bar model (Georg Essl's algorithm), like a bowed vibraphone. Each inlet takes a float or signal and the model sounds continuously from those values (no note messages): bow pressure, bow position, bow velocity, gain, integration, frequency (Hz). Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first.

bowed~.use_when: STK bowed-string model (violin-like). Each inlet takes a float or signal and the model sounds continuously from those values (no note messages): bow pressure, bow position, bow velocity, vibrato frequency, vibrato gain, frequency (Hz). Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first. Some settings get very loud; follow it with limi~ as the help file does.

brass~.use_when: STK brass model. Each inlet takes a float or signal and the model sounds continuously from those values (no note messages): lip tension, slide deviation, vibrato gain, maximum air pressure, vibrato frequency, slide length as frequency (Hz). Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first.

cabasa~.use_when: STK (PhISM) cabasa model. Inlets: number of beads, damping (0-1), energy, resonant frequency (Hz). Sound comes from shaking: change the energy / maximum-shake inlet repeatedly (a metro or noise into it). `metashaker~` covers this model and six others in one object.

casey~.digest: Output N greatest samples in a vector
casey~.use_when: Spectral utility by R. Luke DuBois, not a physical model. Keeps the N largest samples in each signal vector and zeroes the rest; argument or right inlet (int) sets N. Put it on FFT magnitudes to keep only the strongest bins: the help file runs `fft~` → `cartopol~` → `casey~ 10` → `poltocar~` → `ifft~`.

chase~.use_when: Signal utility by R. Luke DuBois, not a physical model. Three signal inlets: input 1, input 2, sync. Left outlet gets whichever input is nearer the sync signal, right outlet the farther one. Rarely needed.

clar~.use_when: STK clarinet model. Each inlet takes a float or signal and the model sounds continuously from those values (no note messages): reed stiffness, noise gain, vibrato gain, breath pressure, vibrato frequency, frequency (Hz). Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first. Some settings get very loud; follow it with limi~ as the help file does.

curvesmooth~.use_when: Control-signal smoother by Dan Trueman, not a physical model. Inlets: target signal, up time (ms), down time (ms), up curve coefficient, down curve coefficient (1 linear, >1 exponential, <1 logarithmic; 0.001-1000). Send `mode 1` (follow mode) for input outside -1 to 1. Like `rampsmooth~` but with curve shape and times in ms.

dcblock~.use_when: DC-blocking filter by Dan Trueman, not a physical model. One signal in, one out, no arguments or messages. Put it after feedback loops, waveshapers or physical models to remove DC offset and slow drift.

escal~.use_when: Signal rounder by R. Luke DuBois, not a physical model. Rounds a signal to integers; argument or right inlet picks -1 always down, 0 nearest, 1 always up. Its own help file says `round~` has more or less superseded it.

flapper~.use_when: Delay-line effect by Dan Trueman, not a physical model. Inlets: trigger (0/1 signal or float), audio input, playback speed. On a trigger it scrubs back and forth between the trigger point and the present; two signal outlets. Messages: `attack`, `decay`, `sustain`, `release` shape each flap; `length <ms>` (max 5000); `overlap <ms>`; `linear` / `poly` interpolation; `trigger_off` stops new triggers. The help file derives triggers with the `findtrigger~` patch.

flip~.use_when: Signal folder by R. Luke DuBois, not a physical model. Folds the carrier (left) back around the threshold (right signal) when its absolute value is larger. Its own help file says `pong~` has more or less superseded it.

flute~.use_when: STK flute model. Each inlet takes a float or signal and the model sounds continuously from those values (no note messages): breath pressure, jet delay (angle), noise gain, vibrato frequency, vibrato gain, frequency (Hz). Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first. Some settings get very loud; follow it with limi~ as the help file does.

gQ~.use_when: Stereo equalizer by Dan Trueman (MSP version of his gQ), not a physical model. Argument sets the number of bands in series. Inlets: left audio, right audio, center frequency (Hz), bandwidth (multiple of center frequency), boost, response-test frequency. Choose the band with `currentbank <n>`, its type with `peaknotch`, `lowshelf` or `highshelf`; `numbanks`, `clear`, `clearsettings`. Outlets: left, right, bank settings, response amplitude. Its three band parameters do not interact.

gen10.use_when: Wavetable generator ported from RTcmix, not a physical model. Send a list of harmonic amplitudes (fundamental first), then `bang`: it outputs index/amplitude pairs to write into a `buffer~` with `peek~`, for playback with `wave~`. Arguments: table size, size offset; also `size`, `offset`, `rescale 0/1` (default rescales to -1..1).

gen17.use_when: Chebyshev waveshaping-table generator ported from RTcmix, not a physical model. Send a list of harmonic amplitudes, then `bang`: outputs index/amplitude pairs for `peek~` into a `buffer~` read by `lookup~`, so a full-level sine through the table gains those harmonics. `size`, `offset`, `rescale 0/1`.

gen20.use_when: Random table generator ported from RTcmix, not a physical model. Send an int to pick a distribution (0 even, 1 low, 2 high, 3 triangle, 4 Gaussian, 5 Cauchy), then `bang`: outputs index/amplitude pairs for `peek~` into a `buffer~`. `size`, `offset`.

gen24.use_when: Breakpoint table generator ported from RTcmix, not a physical model. Send a list of time/amplitude pairs (times are rescaled to the table size), then `bang`: outputs index/amplitude pairs for `peek~` into a `buffer~` (for `lookup~` or `wave~`). `size`, `offset`, `rescale 0/1`. A `function` object plus `peek~` does the same visually.

gen25.use_when: Window table generator ported from RTcmix, not a physical model. Send 1 (Hanning) or 2 (Hamming), then `bang`: outputs index/amplitude pairs for `peek~` into a `buffer~`. `size`, `offset`. Built-in shortcut: send the `buffer~` `fill 1` then `apply hanning` or `apply hamming`.

gen5.use_when: Exponential breakpoint table generator ported from RTcmix, not a physical model. Send a list of amplitudes and distances, then `bang`: outputs index/amplitude pairs for `peek~` into a `buffer~`. The refpage warns never to use a target time of 0. `size`, `offset`, `rescale 0/1`.

gen7.use_when: Linear breakpoint table generator ported from RTcmix, not a physical model. Send a list of amplitudes and distances, then `bang`: outputs index/amplitude pairs for `peek~` into a `buffer~` (for `wave~` or `lookup~`). `size`, `offset`, `rescale 0/1`.

gen9.use_when: Wavetable generator ported from RTcmix, not a physical model. Send triplets of partial ratio, amplitude and phase (ratios need not be whole numbers), then `bang`: outputs index/amplitude pairs for `peek~` into a `buffer~`, played with `wave~`. `size`, `offset`, `rescale 0/1`.

guiro~.use_when: STK (PhISM) guiro model. Inlets: number of items (int), resonant frequency (MIDI value as float), damping (0-1), maximum shake (energy), second resonant frequency (MIDI value as float). Change the shake inlet repeatedly to scrape. `metashaker~` also has a guiro model. The init file's `mc.guiro` mapping is misspelled, so there is no MC version.

jitter~.use_when: Signal randomizer by R. Luke DuBois, not a physical model. Adds a random offset within ±range to the input signal. Arguments: range, manual flag; `range <n>` message; with `manual 1` a new offset is drawn only on bang. `noise~` scaled and added with `+~` is the built-in equivalent.

klutz~.use_when: Glitch utility by R. Luke DuBois, not a physical model. Reverses the sample order within each signal vector; one signal in, one out, no messages. The result depends on the vector size set in Audio Status.

mandolin~.use_when: STK plucked-mandolin model with body resonance. Inlets (float/signal): pluck amplitude, pluck position, string damping, detuning, body size, frequency (Hz). Send `bang` to the left inlet to pluck. `mic <0-11>` picks one of the NBody body/microphone perspectives. Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first. Some settings get very loud; follow it with limi~ as the help file does.

marimba~.use_when: STK modal-synthesis marimba. Inlets (float/signal): stick hardness, stick position, amplitude, vibrato frequency, vibrato amount, frequency (Hz). Strike with a `noteon` message to the left inlet, damp with `noteoff`. Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first.

mesh2d~.use_when: STK two-dimensional waveguide mesh (Julius Smith and Gary Scavone), for drum-head and plate sounds. Type it `mesh2d~ <x> <y>` (lowercase d), where the arguments are mesh size in samples. `strike 1` hits it at `position <x> <y>` (0-1, as in the help); `setDecay` sets loss gains; `setNX` / `setNY` resize; `clear` silences. It also accepts a signal as excitation. Large meshes cost a lot of CPU.

metashaker~.use_when: STK (PhISM) shaker bank in one object: choose the model with `bamboo`, `cabasa`, `guiro`, `maraca`, `sekere`, `sleigh` or `tambourine`; `off` silences. Eleven inlets: number of objects, damping (0-1), energy, resonant frequencies 1-5, scrape velocity, resonance spread, resonance randomness. Change the energy inlet repeatedly to shake. Prefer it to the single-instrument shaker objects.

munger~.use_when: Dan Trueman's live granulator and pitch shifter, not a physical model. Audio into the left inlet; float/signal inlets: grain rate, rate variation, grain length (ms), length variation, grain pitch (multiplier), pitch variation, pan spread. Stereo out. Argument is maximum delay in ms (max grain = 1/3 of it). Key messages: `voices`, `maxvoices` (max 100), `position <0-1>` (-1 random), `record 0` freezes the buffer, `ambidirectional -1/0/1`, `gain`, `rand_gain`, `minsize`, `ramptime`, `delaylength_ms`, `tempered` plus `scale <list>` for pitch sieves (`smooth` turns them off), `oneshot`, `note` for single grains, `clear`.

nbody~.use_when: Body-resonance filter from the NBody project (Perry Cook and Dan Trueman), not an STK model. Filters a signal (left inlet) through LPC filters measured from real instruments. Choose the instrument with `violin`, `hardanger`, `guitar1`, `guitar2`, `archtop` or `mandolin`, and the microphone perspective with an int 1-12 in the right inlet. Feed it a string model, noise or a pluck.

nscradle~.use_when: Newton's-cradle physics model that outputs an impulse signal on each collision; not an STK model. Argument is the number of balls; there is one signal outlet per neighbouring pair (`nscradle~ 3` has two). Start motion with `put <ball> <angle in radians>`, stop with `zero`. `mass`, `length`, `radius`, `damping` take `<ball> <value>`, with ball -1 meaning all; `which`, `push`. Use the impulses (e.g. through `edge~`) to trigger other sounds.

pit_shift~.use_when: STK delay-line pitch shifter, not a physical model. One signal in, one out. `shift <factor>` sets the transposition (1 = none). Low quality next to built-in `pitchshift~` or `abl.dsp.pitchshifter~`.

plucked~.use_when: STK basic Karplus-Strong plucked string. Two inlets: pluck amplitude (bang or float plucks) and frequency (Hz). No other controls; `stif_karp~` adds stiffness and pickup position. Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first.

pokef~.digest: Write sample values to buffers by index with interpolation
pokef~.use_when: Buffer writer by Dan Trueman, not a physical model. Argument names the `buffer~`. Signal inlets: value to write, index (samples), interpolation coefficient, channel. A -1 index signal stops writing. `set <buffer>` changes buffer. Built-in `poke~` does the same without the coefficient.

prc_chorus~.use_when: Perry Cook's STK chorus effect, not a physical model. One signal in, one out; argument is base delay. Messages: `depth`, `frequency`, `mix`. Basic; built-in `abl.dsp.chorus~` is fuller.

prc_fm~.use_when: Perry Cook's STK FM instruments, not a physical model. `type <1-7>` picks BeeThree, FMVoices, HevyMetl, PercFlut, Rhodey, TubeBell or Wurley. Play it with `noteon <Hz> <amp 0-1>` and `noteoff <amp>`; shape it with `control <number> <value 0-128>`: 1 LFO depth, 2 control one, 4 control two, 11 LFO speed, 128 ADSR targets. One inlet, one signal outlet. Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first.

random~.use_when: Audio-rate random-number generator by R. Luke DuBois, not a physical model. Outputs random values up to the limit set by its argument or `range <n>`. Built-in `noise~` or `rand~` usually does the job.

recordf~.digest: Copy a signal into a buffer
recordf~.use_when: Buffer recorder with feedback by Dan Trueman, not a physical model: like `record~`, but keeps part of the old contents while recording (overdub). Argument names the `buffer~`. Inlets: signal in plus 1/0 record on/off, feedback amount, loop start (ms), loop end (ms). Messages: `loop 0/1`, `append`, `goto <ms>`, `reset`, `set <buffer>`. Play the buffer with `play~` or `groove~`.

saxofony~.use_when: STK saxophone-like conical-bore reed model (the 'blowed string'). One inlet. Play it with `noteon <Hz> <amp 0-1>` and `noteoff <amp>`; shape it with `control <number> <value 0-128>`: 1 vibrato gain, 2 reed stiffness, 4 noise gain, 11 blow position, 26 reed aperture, 29 vibrato frequency, 128 breath pressure. Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first. Some settings get very loud; follow it with limi~ as the help file does. The init file misspells its MC mapping (`saxophony~`), so there is no MC version.

scrubf~.use_when: Delay-line scrubber with feedback by Dan Trueman, not a physical model. Inlets: signal in, scrub rate, feedback (0-1). Messages: `delay <ms>` (max 3000), `overlap <ms>`, `ramp <ms>`, `sync 1` feeds back the old input (default) and `sync 0` the old output, `trigger` resets record/playback points, `zero` clears.

scrub~.use_when: Delay-line scrubber by Dan Trueman, not a physical model. Audio in the left inlet, scrub rate (signal or float) in the right. Crossfades three buffers to avoid clicks. Messages: `delay <ms>` (max 3000), `overlap <ms>`, `ramp <ms>`, `zero`.

sekere~.use_when: STK (PhISM) sekere model. Inlets: number of beads, damping (0-1), shake energy, resonant frequency (Hz). Sound comes from shaking: change the energy / maximum-shake inlet repeatedly (a metro or noise into it). `metashaker~` covers this model and six others in one object.

shakers~.use_when: Dan Trueman's message-driven wrapper of the STK shaker instruments. One inlet. `play <instrument> <amp>` or `noteon <amp>` starts a sound; `energy`, `decay`, `numobjects`, `resfreq` take 0-128. The refpage does not list the instrument numbers. `metashaker~` is easier to control.

shaker~.use_when: STK (PhISM) maraca model. Inlets: number of beans, resonance, damping (0-1), shake speed, maximum shake. `envelope <attack> <decay> <release>` ratios. Sound comes from shaking: change the energy / maximum-shake inlet repeatedly (a metro or noise into it). `metashaker~` covers this model and six others in one object.

simple~.use_when: STK 'Simple' instrument: looped wavetable plus noise through a resonant filter with an ADSR. Not a physical model. One inlet. Play it with `noteon <Hz> <amp 0-1>` and `noteoff <amp>`; shape it with `control <number> <value 0-128>`: 1 gain, 2 filter pole position, 4 noise/pitch crossfade, 11 envelope rate. Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first. Easily built from built-in objects.

sitar~.use_when: STK Karplus-Strong sitar model. Play it with `noteon <Hz> <amp>` and `noteoff <amp>`; there are no other controls. One inlet, one signal outlet. Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first.

sleigh~.use_when: STK (PhISM) sleigh-bell model. Inlets: number of bells, resonance, damping, maximum shake (energy), resonant frequencies 1-4 (Hz). Sound comes from shaking: change the energy / maximum-shake inlet repeatedly (a metro or noise into it). `metashaker~` covers this model and six others in one object.

stif_karp~.use_when: STK plucked stiff-string model (Karplus-Strong with stiffness and pickup position). One inlet. Play it with `noteon <Hz> <amp 0-1>` and `noteoff <amp>`; shape it with `control <number> <value 0-128>`: 1 string stretch (stiffness), 4 pickup position, 11 string sustain. Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first.

tamb~.use_when: STK (PhISM) tambourine model. Inlets: number of cymbals, damping (0-1), maximum shake (energy), resonant frequencies 1-3 (Hz). Sound comes from shaking: change the energy / maximum-shake inlet repeatedly (a metro or noise into it). `metashaker~` covers this model and six others in one object.

terrain~.use_when: 2D wavetable oscillator by R. Luke DuBois, not a physical model. Arguments: `buffer~` name, frame size (samples), number of frames. Left signal inlet scans within a frame (e.g. `phasor~`), right signal inlet moves and interpolates between frames. Messages: `set <buffer>`, `size`, `frames`.

ublotar~.use_when: Dan Trueman's six-string/bore flute-guitar hybrid (successor to `blotar~`), based on STK models. Inlets: six string/bore frequencies (Hz), feedback/jet frequency, pre-distortion level, post-distortion level, breath pressure. `pluck <string 0-5> <amp> [squish]` plucks; `setsustain <string|-1> <0-1>`, `lowpasscross <string|-1> <0-1>` (1 flute-like, 0 guitar-like), `distortgain`, `feedgain`, `noise`, `limit`, `vibrato <freq> <gain>`. Some settings get very loud; follow it with limi~ as the help file does.

vcomb~.use_when: Spectral comb filter by Dan Trueman, not a physical model. Use inside `pfft~`: two FFT signal inputs plus per-bin delay time (samples) and feedback coefficient, usually read from two `buffer~` objects (see the help's `vcomb-pfft~`). Two FFT outputs. Feedback can blow up; the help puts `limi~` after it.

vcompand2~.use_when: Per-bin spectral compander by Dan Trueman, not a physical model. Use inside `pfft~` (see `vcompand2-pfft~`). Inlets: FFT signal, compression threshold, compression amount, expansion threshold, expansion amount, each per bin. For spectral noise reduction or frequency-dependent compression.

vcompand~.use_when: Spectral compander by Dan Trueman, not a physical model. Use inside `pfft~` on bin amplitudes. Messages: `compthresh`, `compratio`, `expthresh`, `expratio`, applied to every bin. A simple spectral noise gate or noise enhancer; `vcompand2~` sets them per bin.

vibraphone~.use_when: STK modal-synthesis vibraphone. Inlets (float/signal): stick hardness, stick position, amplitude, vibrato frequency, vibrato amount, frequency (Hz). Strike with `noteon`, damp with `noteoff`. Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first.

voice_form~.use_when: STK four-formant singing-voice synthesizer (not a waveguide model). One inlet. Play it with `noteon <Hz> <amp 0-1>` and `noteoff <amp>`; shape it with `control <number> <value 0-128>`: 1 vibrato gain, 2 voiced/unvoiced mix, 4 vowel/phoneme, 11 vibrato frequency, 128 loudness (spectral tilt). Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first.

vstretch~.digest: Stretch/compress frequency axis of FFT bins
vstretch~.use_when: Spectral stretcher by R. Luke DuBois, not a physical model. Use inside `pfft~` (see `vstretch-pfft`) to move FFT bins up or down in frequency, e.g. for transposition. `stretch <factor>`; interpolation `linear`, `poly` (3rd order) or `poly2` (4th order).

vwarp~.use_when: Per-bin spectral warper by Dan Trueman, not a physical model. Use inside `pfft~` (see `vwarp-pfft~`): reads a per-bin stretch amount from a `buffer~` (argument names it) and moves bins like `vstretch~`. `stretch` sets a global factor; interpolation `linear`, `poly`, `poly2`.

waffle~.use_when: Signal router by R. Luke DuBois, not a physical model. Inlets: input, crossover, sync (all signals). Input goes out the left outlet while sync is below crossover, otherwise out the right. `gate~` with a comparison does the same.

weave~.use_when: Zero-crossing effect by R. Luke DuBois, not a physical model. Counts zero crossings of the input and outputs a ±1 square wave that flips after the set number of low and high crossings, giving subharmonics (octave-divider fuzz). Arguments: low count, high count; the int inlets change them.

whistle~.use_when: STK hybrid physical/spectral police or referee whistle (Perry Cook). One inlet. Play it with `noteon <Hz> <amp 0-1>` and `noteoff <amp>`; shape it with `control <number> <value 0-128>`: 1 ripple modulation gain, 2 blow frequency modulation, 4 noise gain, 11 ripple modulation frequency, 128 breath pressure. Frequency is in Hz: convert MIDI note numbers with mtof first.

wuter~.use_when: STK (PhISM) water-droplet model. Inlets: number of droplets, resonant frequency (Hz), damping (0-1), maximum shake (energy). Two signal outlets. Sound comes from shaking: change the energy / maximum-shake inlet repeatedly (a metro or noise into it). `metashaker~` covers this model and six others in one object.

sbb.env.adsr.digest: A linear attack-decay-sustain-release envelope with built-in attenuator.
sbb.env.adsr.use_when: RNBO ADSR envelope (linear) with built-in attenuator. Stereo input, attack/decay/sustain/release in ms. Use in RNBO patches as the standard amp envelope; cleaner than building it from gen~ primitives.

sbb.env.adsr.stereo.digest: A stereo attack-decay-sustain-release envelope with built-in attenuator.
sbb.env.adsr.stereo.use_when: RNBO stereo ADSR envelope. Same as sbb.env.adsr but with stereo signal path.

sbb.env.analog.digest: An analog-style (exponential) attack-decay-sustain-release envelope with built-in attenuator.
sbb.env.analog.use_when: RNBO analog-style (exponential curves) ADSR envelope. Use when you want the characteristic non-linear curve of analog hardware envelopes.

sbb.env.follower.digest: number of samples to use in computing envelope
sbb.env.follower.use_when: RNBO envelope follower — track signal amplitude via RMS over a sliding window. `samples` arg sets window length.

sbb.env.lpg.use_when: A lowpass gate circuit emulation. RNBO synth building block — pre-built primitive for use inside RNBO patches.

sbb.env.slope.use_when: An analog-style ADSR envelope. RNBO synth building block — pre-built primitive for use inside RNBO patches.

sbb.util.xfade.use_when: Crossfade between the two sources, using the range of -50. to 50. RNBO synth building block — pre-built primitive for use inside RNBO patches.

16step-seq.digest: A 16-step sequencer which patterns can be created by random or by supplying a list (see below) - the pattern can be changed gradually by applied operations.
16step-seq.use_when: 16-step on/off sequencer. Argument and right inlet: tempo in BPM. Send a 16-element list of 0/1 to the middle inlet to set the pattern, and 1/0 to the left inlet to start/stop. Outlets: rhythm bangs on active steps, and a bang when the 16-step phrase ends. Patterns can be randomized or changed step by step from outside (see help). For pitch or velocity per step use `live.step`.

@.digest: Scales a standard slider (ranging from 0 to 127) between min and max. The type of the first argument specifies the output type.
@.use_when: Range-scaled slider — maps a 0–127 standard slider into an arbitrary range. Constructor args: `<min> <max>`; the type of the first argument (int vs float) determines the output type. Use as a one-line replacement for scale + slider chains.

BPM2ms.digest: Converts beats per minute (BPM) into milliseconds.
BPM2ms.use_when: Convert beats-per-minute to milliseconds (per beat). Use as the standard tempo→duration conversion for sequencers and metronomes.

DblBang.digest: Detects single or double bang (like single or double mouse clicks)
DblBang.use_when: Detect single vs double bang (like single/double-click). Constructor arg: `<threshold-ms>` (default 250). Use to extend a single trigger source into two distinct events for two different actions.

ED-rhythm.use_when: Rhythm generator that picks entry delays (ms) from a list. Argument: selection principle, 1 = alea, 2 = series, 3 = sequence (also settable on the middle inlet). Send the ED list to the right inlet, then a toggle (1/0) to the left inlet to start/stop. Outlets: rhythm bangs, chosen index, bang when the supply is exhausted, ED value.

ED-trans.digest: Generates a transition between two entry delays (ED) within a certain time span producing either a ritardando or an accelerando. A number (= time in ms) sent to the leftmost inlet starts the process.
ED-trans.use_when: Transition between two EDs over a time span — produces ritardando (ED rising) or accelerando (ED falling). Constructor args: `<start-ED> <end-ED>` (default 75, 300). Send time-in-ms to start. Use for tempo transitions over a defined duration.

ED2EP.digest: Converts ED (= entry delays) into EP (= entry points). Argument = offset (can be negative). NB: Only works with integers!
ED2EP.use_when: Convert entry delays to entry points (cumulative). Constructor arg: `<offset>` (default 0). Integer-only. Use for converting relative timing to absolute timing.

Labs.digest: Recompiled as Universal Binary for Intel and ARM processors by Jeremy Bernstein (May 2022)
Labs.use_when: List absolute value — apply `abs` element-wise to a stored list when triggered. Use as the list-domain absolute value.

Ladd.digest: Recompiled as Universal Binary for Intel and ARM processors by Jeremy Bernstein (May 2022)
Ladd.use_when: List add — store a list in the right inlet; int/float in left adds to all elements (or operate list+list element-wise). Constructor args: `<list>` (default 4 3 2). Use for element-wise list addition.

Ldiv.digest: List in right inlet is stored. Int or Float in right replaces all members of stored list. 0s in right are converted to 1s.
Ldiv.use_when: List divide — element-wise division; 0s in the divisor list are converted to 1s to avoid division-by-zero. Use as the list-domain `/`.

Lmult.digest: Recompiled as Universal Binary for Intel and ARM processors by Jeremy Bernstein (May 2022)
Lmult.use_when: List multiply — element-wise multiplication. Same usage pattern as Ladd. Use as the list-domain `*`.

Lpow.digest: Note: 0^0 and( negative number)^(a fraction) are not defined. If that happens, the left value is passed through.
Lpow.use_when: List power — element-wise exponentiation. Constructor args: `<list>` (default 1 2 3 4.). Note: 0^0 and (negative)^(fraction) are passed through unchanged. Use as the list-domain `pow`.

Lrem.digest: List in right inlet is stored. Int or Float in right replaces all members of stored list. 0s in right will always return 0.
Lrem.use_when: List modulo — element-wise modulo; 0s in the divisor list always return 0 (avoids divide-by-zero crash). Use as the list-domain `%`.

Lround.digest: Recompiled as Universal Binary for Intel and ARM processors by Jeremy Bernstein (May 2022)
Lround.use_when: List round — round each list element to a grid. Constructor arg: `<grid>` (default -1 = round to integer). Use as the list-domain version of native `round`.

Lsub.digest: Recompiled as Universal Binary for Intel and ARM processors by Jeremy Bernstein (May 2022)
Lsub.use_when: List subtract — element-wise subtraction. Same usage pattern as Ladd. Use as the list-domain `-`.

Lsum.digest: Recompiled as Universal Binary for Intel and ARM processors by Jeremy Bernstein (May 2022)
Lsum.use_when: Sum of list elements. Use as a one-shot list-summation utility (avoids zl + iter chains).

MSP-iovs~.digest: Sets the I/O vector size of MSP. Watch the DSP Status window!
MSP-iovs~.use_when: Set MSP I/O Vector Size. Constructor arg: `<size>` (default 256). Use for runtime IO-vector reconfiguration; watch DSP Status window.

MSP-sigvs~.digest: Sets the signal vector size of MSP. Watch the DSP Status window!
MSP-sigvs~.use_when: Set MSP Signal Vector Size. Constructor arg: `<size>` (default 64). Use for runtime sig-vector reconfiguration.

MSP-sr~.digest: Sets the sampling rate of MSP. Watch the DSP Status window!
MSP-sr~.use_when: Set MSP sample rate. Constructor arg: `<sr>` (default 44100). Use for runtime sample-rate reconfiguration.

MSP-takeover~.digest: 1 sent to the inlet (or set as the argument) puts the scheduler in audio interrupt. 0 turns it off. Watch the DSP Status window!
MSP-takeover~.use_when: Set scheduler-in-audio-interrupt mode. Constructor arg: `<flag>` (default 0). Use to programmatically engage takeover timing.

QT-PercPlayer.digest: Plays the General MIDI Percussion sounds directly from Quicktime. The 1st inlet specifies the instrument to be played (75 = Claves, 37 = SideStick), the 2nd inlet defines the velocity (0-127).
QT-PercPlayer.use_when: Play General MIDI percussion sounds via QuickTime. 1st inlet = instrument number (75=Claves, 37=SideStick), 2nd inlet = velocity. macOS-only (legacy). Use only on systems with QuickTime General MIDI available.

QT-SndPlayer.digest: Plays the General MIDI instruments directly from Quicktime. The 1st argument specifies the instrument to be played (1 = GrandPiano, 175 = WoodBlock), the 2nd the duration (in ms).
QT-SndPlayer.use_when: Play General MIDI instrument sounds via QuickTime. Constructor args: `<instrument> <duration-ms>` (default 1=GrandPiano, 500). macOS-only (legacy). Use only on systems with QuickTime General MIDI available.

RTC-seed.digest: Seeds the different random generators of MAX. Sends out a global message called "RTC-rs" to all RTC's random based objects.
RTC-seed.use_when: Seed all RTC random generators by sending the global `RTC-rs` message. Use at session start to seed reproducible random behaviour across the whole patch.

RandomSeeder.digest: Seeds the different random generators of MAX. Sends out a global message called "RTC-rs" to all RTC's random based objects.
RandomSeeder.use_when: Abstraction (loads as `RandomSeeder`) that builds a seed number from the current `date` and time when banged and outputs it. It does not seed anything by itself: send its output to `RTC-seed`, which broadcasts `RTC-rs` to all seedable RTC-lib random objects.

VolAmb.digest: Controlling the ambitus between minimum and maximum dynamic with a single controller.
VolAmb.use_when: Single-controller dynamic-ambit control — map one CC to a min-max dynamic range. Use for performance-friendly velocity/dynamics control via a single fader.

add%.digest: Adding a certain percentage <int, float> to values <int, float> in left inlet.
add%.use_when: Add a configurable percentage to incoming values. Constructor arg: `<percent>` (default 20). Use to apply percentage-based offsets without scale + + chains.

alea.digest: A bang in the left inlet makes a random selection of a supply sent to right inlet before. Note that there is no repetition check of chosen elements.
alea.use_when: Random selection from a supply (sent to right inlet) with NO repetition check. Bang in left inlet draws. Use as the basic Koenig ALEA selection principle — drawn elements may repeat in close succession.

alea-rhythm.digest: Sends out rhythm bangs at random times from a geometrical time row defined by a a min. and max. entry delay (ED) and a certain number of ED-values.
alea-rhythm.use_when: Random rhythm (ALEA principle) with gaps chosen from a geometric scale of entry delays. Arguments: `<min-ED> <max-ED> <steps>`. Toggle the left inlet to start. Outlets: rhythm bangs, chosen ED (ms), row index. Limits can change on the other inlets.

anti-bis.digest: Filters out immediate repetitions of integers. Right output sends a bang whenever this occurs.
anti-bis.use_when: Repetition filter — suppress immediate (bis) repetitions of integers. Right output bangs when a repetition is filtered. Use to enforce no-direct-repeat constraints.

anti-bis&osc.digest: Filters out direct repetitions and when a number has occured the penultimate time, right output sends a bang when this occurs.
anti-bis&osc.use_when: Filter both immediate repetitions and oscillations (a-b-a) — suppresses returns to penultimate values. Use for stricter no-repetition than anti-bis.

anti-interval.digest: Filters out a certain interval (which is the argument of this function) of a stream of notes and outputs a bang from right outlet whenever this interval would have occured.
anti-interval.use_when: Filter a specific interval. Constructor arg: `<interval>` (default -1 = no filter). Right outlet flashes when filtered. Use to forbid a specific melodic interval.

anti-octave.digest: Filters out octaves between two consecutive notes and outputs a bang from right outlet whenever an octave has occured.
anti-octave.use_when: Octave filter — suppress octaves between consecutive notes. Right outlet flashes. Use in counterpoint to avoid parallel octaves.

anti-octave&prime.digest: Filters out octaves and primes (i.e. tone repetitions) between two consecutive notes and outputs a bang from right outlet whenever this would have occured.
anti-octave&prime.use_when: Filter octaves AND primes (unison repetitions) between consecutive notes. Use for counterpoint where both unison and octave parallels must be suppressed.

anti-osc.digest: Filters out an integer which has occured the penultimate time. Right output sends a bang when this occurs. Does not filter out immediate repetition as it is done by"anti-bis".
anti-osc.use_when: Oscillation filter — suppress returns to penultimate values (a-b-a patterns). Right outlet flashes. Use to break trill-like oscillations.

banger.digest: Recompiled as Universal Binary for Intel and ARM processors by Jeremy Bernstein (May 2022)
banger.use_when: Peter Elsea external that bangs its outlets one at a time, in order: each bang fires the next outlet. An int bangs that one outlet; `set <n>` chooses the next outlet without output. Argument sets the number of outlets (default 16). Use to step through N actions on successive bangs. It is not a fan-out: for one bang to many outlets at once use `bangbang`.

between.digest: Bang (or any input) in left inlet outputs a random number between min <int, float> and max <int, float> excluding max.
between.use_when: Output a random number between min and max (max excluded). Constructor args: `<min> <max>` (default 1, 12). Bang or any input triggers. Use as the standard bounded uniform random.

between-lin.digest: Bang (or any input) in left inlet outputs a random number <float> of a linear scale between min <int, float> and max <int, float> with a certain number of elements.
between-lin.use_when: Random number on a linear scale between min and max with a fixed number of elements. Constructor args: `<min> <max> <num-elements>` (default 1, 2, 5). Use for quantised-linear random within a range.

between-lin-urn.use_when: Like between-lin but with no-repetition (urn-style). Constructor args: `<min> <max> <num-elements>`. Use when you want quantised-linear random without immediate repetition.

between-log.digest: Bang (or any input) in left inlet outputs a random number <float> of a logarithmic scale between min <int, float> and max <int, float> with a certain number of elements.
between-log.use_when: Random number on a logarithmic scale between min and max with a fixed number of elements. Constructor args: `<min> <max> <num-elements>` (default 1, 2, 13). Use for log-scale random — e.g. frequencies / durations where perceptual spacing is logarithmic.

between-log-urn.use_when: Like between-log with no-repetition. Constructor args: `<min> <max> <num-elements>`. Use for log-scale random without repetition.

block-bang.digest: Filters out bangs that arrive before a certain time span ("blocking time") is over.
block-bang.use_when: Filter out bangs arriving within a 'blocking time' after a previous bang. Constructor arg: `<blocking-ms>` (default 2000). Use to enforce a minimum interval between events.

brown-melody.use_when: Brownian melody generator. Constructor args: `<min-pitch> <max-pitch> <step>` (default 24, 108, 0.1). Use for stepwise random melodic generation.

brown-rhythm.use_when: Brownian rhythm — Brownian walk on the ED scale. Constructor args: `<min-ED> <max-ED> <num-EDs> <step>` (default 100, 1000, 12, 0.2). Use for smoothly evolving ED streams.

brownian.use_when: Random walk between a min and max (max excluded). Arguments: `<min> <max> <variation>`; variation 0–1 sets the jump size as a share of the range (1 = plain random, 0 = always the same value). Bang to output a float. Built on `drunk`; used by brown-melody and brown-rhythm.

butfirst.digest: Outputs the input list without its first element.
butfirst.use_when: Output the input list without its first element (cdr-like). Use for list head/tail processing.

butlast.digest: Outputs the input list without its last element.
butlast.use_when: Output the input list without its last element. Use for list tail-removal in compositional algorithms.

check-octaves.digest: Checks whether an interval list sums up to an octave and outputs the list only when it does not contain any hidden octaves..
check-octaves.use_when: Test whether an interval list sums to an octave; output the list only if it does NOT contain hidden octaves. Use for hidden-octave avoidance in counterpoint.

check-row.digest: Outputs the input row if it is a proper twelve-tone row; otherwise a bang is sent out of the right outlet.
check-row.use_when: Validate a 12-tone row — output if it's a proper twelve-tone row (all pitch classes 0–11 used exactly once); bang on right outlet otherwise. Use for verifying generated or input rows.

choice-rhythm.use_when: Random rhythm with chosen number of distinct EDs. Constructor args: `<min-ED> <max-ED> <num-EDs> <choice-count>` (default 100, 1000, 12, 6). Use for rhythms restricted to a subset of available EDs.

choose.digest: An int n sent to the left inlet outputs n randomly chosen elements from a given supply. Contains a repetition check.
choose.use_when: Choose n elements at random from a supply with repetition check. `<n>` in left inlet sets count; supply on right. Use for distinct-sample drawing — e.g. pick 5 unique notes from a 12-tone supply.

choose-intervals.digest: flashes when the sum of the chosen intervals would have been an octave
choose-intervals.use_when: Choose intervals at random with octave-flash detection. Constructor arg: `<count>`. Right outlet flashes when chosen interval sums would have made an octave. Use in 12-tone composition contexts where octave avoidance matters.

collect.digest: Collects numbers (ints or floats) and symbols sent to the left inlet into a list. A bang in the right inlet clears the list.
collect.use_when: Collect numbers/symbols sent to the left inlet into a list. Bang in right inlet clears. Use as a list builder when accumulating values over time.

contrario.digest: A number <int, float> in left inlet outputs a complimentary number. The axis number <float, int> has to be sent to the right inlet or given as an argument to the function.
contrario.use_when: Output the complement of a number around an axis — `2*axis - x`. Constructor or right-inlet arg: `<axis>`. Use for melodic inversion: transform a melodic line into its inversion around a pivot.

cos-slider.digest: Transforms a linear slider into a cosine function.
cos-slider.use_when: Transform a linear slider into a cosine-mapped slider. Use for non-linear slider mapping (e.g. for parameters where sensitivity should bunch at the extremes).

count-bang.digest: Counts the number of received bangs.
count-bang.use_when: Count received bangs. Use as a bang counter — sums total bangs since last clear.

countdown.digest: An int sent to the inlet causes the object to start a countdown (in seconds).
countdown.use_when: Start a countdown in seconds (int sent to inlet). Use for timed event scheduling.

cp-pan~.use_when: Constant-power panner (Chris Dobrian). Constructor arg: `<initial-pan>` (default 0.4). Use for stereo panning that maintains perceived loudness across the field.

cresc-decresc.use_when: Generate a velocity transition over a duration. Constructor args: `<start-vel> <end-vel> <duration-ms>` (default 1, 127, 5000). Up = cresc, down = decresc. Use for programmable dynamic transitions.

crossfade~.digest: Crossfades two input signals according to a sine function which guarantees that loudness of the result is constant.
crossfade~.use_when: Crossfades two signals (left and middle inlets) with a sine-shaped, constant-loudness curve. Right inlet: crossfader position 0–127, smoothed with `line~`. Output is one signal.

dB2lin.use_when: Convert dB to linear amplitude. Use as the inverse of lin2dB; chain with native math objects when you need both representations.

del-fb~.use_when: Delay with feedback. Constructor args: `<delay-ms> <feedback-dB>` (default 8000, -12). Use for self-running delay textures with built-in feedback gain.

display-row.digest: Displays a numerical 12-tone-row in musical notation.
display-row.use_when: Display a numerical 12-tone row in musical notation. Use for visualising rows during composition.

divmod.digest: divmod is the same as / and % for positive left operands. For negative left operands divmod sticks to modulo arithmetic wheras / and % do something else. divmod does not allow right operands below 1 (they become 1). Only works with integers.
divmod.use_when: Combined divide + modulo with consistent negative-number behaviour. Constructor arg: `<divisor>`. divmod sticks to modulo arithmetic for negative left operands (where native `/` and `%` do something else). Use when arithmetic with negative dividends must wrap consistently — pitch math, cyclic indexing into negative ranges.

dur-from-ED.digest: Calculates note durations from entry delays (ED) and a duration factor. dur-factor = 1: legato; dur-factor < 1: portato, staccato; dur-factor > 1: pedal effect
dur-from-ED.use_when: Calculate note durations from EDs and a duration factor. Factor 1=legato, <1=portato/staccato, >1=pedal. Constructor arg: `<duration-factor>` (default 1). Use to derive note durations from rhythmic EDs.

first.digest: Outputs the first element of a list.
first.use_when: Output the first element of a list (car). Use for list head extraction.

first-bang.digest: Outputs only the first bang of a stream of bangs (e.g. rhythm) until the right inlet receives a (reset) bang.
first-bang.use_when: Output only the first bang in a stream until a reset bang arrives on the right inlet. Use for rising-edge detection on bang streams.

first-shot.digest: Outputs only the first message of a stream of messages (bangs, ints, floats, symbols, lists) until the right inlet receives a (reset) bang.
first-shot.use_when: Output only the first message of any type until reset. Use as the message-typed version of first-bang.

frq2note.digest: Converts frequency into a note (= MIDI key number).
frq2note.use_when: Convert frequency (Hz) to MIDI note number. Use as the standard ftom for control-rate values.

geom.digest: Int in right inlet outputs the nth member of a geometrical row. The other parameters are reference value <int, float> and the proportional factor q <float>.
geom.use_when: Nth element of a geometric row with reference value and proportion factor q. Constructor args: `<reference> <q>` (default 20, 1.25). Use for geometric scaling of values.

grid-rhythm.use_when: Rhythm made of multiples of a time grid. Arguments: `<grid-ms> <deviation-%> <selection-principle>` (help uses 125 10 3; principle 1 alea, 2 series, 3 sequence). Send a list of multiples (e.g. `1 2 4`) to the right inlet first, then toggle the left inlet. Outlets: rhythm bangs and the chosen ED in ms. Deviation adds random timing variation.

groove-rhythm.digest: Generates a rhythm based on a time grid and a list of multiples, from which elements are picked according to the chosen selection principle.
groove-rhythm.use_when: Rhythm based on a time grid and a list of multiples chosen by selection principle. Constructor arg: `<grid-ms>` (default 125). Use for groove-style patterns derived from grid-multiples.

group.digest: 1992 by James McCartney; rewritten as an abstraction 2006 by Karlheinz Essl
group.use_when: Group numbers into sublists of size n. Constructor arg: `<group-size>` (default 4). Use to chunk a stream into fixed-size groups (e.g. for chord building from a melodic stream).

group-rhythm.use_when: Grouped-rhythm generator. Constructor args: `<min-ED> <max-ED> <num-EDs> <group-prob>` (default 100, 1000, 12, 0.5). Use for rhythmic streams with chord-/grace-note-style groupings.

group-rhythm2.use_when: Variant of group-rhythm with different grouping behaviour. Use as the alternate group-rhythm flavour when the grouping logic of the original isn't quite right.

groups.digest: 1993-98 by Karlheinz Essl after Gottfried Michael Koenig, vs. 2.1
groups.use_when: Koenig-style group selection. A bang picks one element from the supply list (middle inlet) and one group size from the group list (right inlet), both by the series principle (no repeats until used up), then repeats that element group-size times on following bangs. Outlets: chosen element, chosen index, chosen group size. Use for material that comes in clusters of repeated values.

inc-dec.digest: Functional implementation of the graphical user interface object IncDec.
inc-dec.use_when: Functional implementation of the GUI IncDec object. Use as a programmable inc/decrement source without the GUI footprint.

infinity-row.digest: Discovered by Per Nørgård (1959), further variants by Peter Richter (1996). NB: The fourth, sixteenth, sixtyfourth etc. note of the row is identical!
infinity-row.use_when: Per Nørgård's infinity row (1959 / Peter Richter 1996 variants) — every 4th, 16th, 64th... element of the row equals the first. Constructor args define starting parameters. Use for infinity-row-based generative composition.

insert.use_when: Insert an element into a list at a position. Index 0 places at the start; bigger-than-list-size appends at the end. Use for ordered list construction.

integ.digest: Accumulates input values <int, float> until a bang (or any input) is sent to the right inlet.
integ.use_when: Integrate (accumulate) input values until a bang in the right inlet resets. Use as a running-sum integrator with explicit reset.

intv2ratio.digest: Converts an interval (int = tempered or float = any micro-interval) into a ratio.
intv2ratio.use_when: Convert an interval (semitones, int = tempered or float = microtonal) to a frequency ratio. Use for working with just-intonation analysis from semitone deviations.

inv.digest: Calculates the inversion of a number.
inv.use_when: Outputs the reciprocal of the input (`expr 1/$f1`), always as a float. Use for 1/x, e.g. converting a period to a frequency. For mirroring a value around an axis use `contrario` instead.

key-bang.digest: Sends out a bang whenever a certain key is pressed. The argument is the ASCII-number of that key.
key-bang.use_when: Send a bang when a specific key is pressed. Constructor arg: `<ASCII-code>` (default 13 = return). Use for keyboard-triggered events without rolling key + select chains.

last.digest: Outputs the last element of a list.
last.use_when: Output the last element of a list. Use for list tail-element extraction.

lin2dB.use_when: Convert linear amplitude to dB. Use whenever you need the dB form of an amplitude value (display, threshold comparison).

listlen.digest: Outputs the length of a list or anything arriving at its inlet. Bang in left inlet retriggers output of length of previous list. List or anything in inlet sends length of list out the outlet.
listlen.use_when: Output the length of an incoming list (or anything). Bang re-emits previous length. Use to query list size for downstream sizing logic.
