listreg.digest: 1992 by James McCartney; rewritten as an abstraction 2006 by Karlheinz Essl
listreg.use_when: List register — store and retrieve a list. Use as a one-list memory cell.

loop-buff~.digest: Loops a buffer and changes the transposition resp. speed. A negative transposition factor plays the buffer backwards.
loop-buff~.use_when: Buffer-based stereo looper with transposition control. Constructor args: `<buffer-name> <pitch>` (default snd, 0.73). Negative pitch plays backwards. Use for buffer-based loop playback with pitch / speed control.

loop-sf~.digest: Loops a selected mono sndfile and changes the transposition resp. speed. A negative factor plays the file backwards.
loop-sf~.use_when: Soundfile-based stereo looper with transposition. Negative factor plays backwards. Use for direct-from-file looped playback (no buffer pre-load needed).

make-ED-scale.digest: Generates a geometrical scale of entry delays (ED) between a min. ED and a max. ED with a certain number of elements.
make-ED-scale.use_when: Geometric scale of entry delays between min and max ED with N elements. Constructor args: `<min-ED> <max-ED> <count>` (default 250., 1000., 6). Use to build the ED scale that drives most RTC rhythm objects.

make-choice-list.digest: max. list element (must be larger than min. list element)
make-choice-list.use_when: Generates a random integer list whose length and values fall between set limits. Arguments: `<min-length> <max-length> <min-value> <max-value>` (max value must exceed min value). Bang to generate a new list. Use to make choice lists for the RTC-lib selection principles (alea, series, etc.).

make-scale.digest: Generates an integer list with a certain number of ints starting from a given value.
make-scale.use_when: Generate an integer scale of n elements starting from a value. Constructor arg: `<count>` (default 1). Use for arithmetic scale generation.

make-trans-scale.use_when: Generate a transition scale between start and end values with n elements. Constructor args: `<start> <end> <count>` (default 2., 1., 13). The transition type (linear, exp, log) is configurable. Use for parametric scale interpolation.

markov.digest: Creates a matrix where transitions are only possible between adjacent elements. Result similar to "sneak" random!
markov.use_when: Front end for Max's `prob` (first-order Markov chain). Send the transition table in `prob` format to the right inlet and the start element (int, also the argument) to the middle inlet; each bang on the left inlet outputs the next element. A second outlet bangs ('I am stuck') when the current element has no transitions. Use when you want `prob` with a start value and a stuck warning.

markov-harmony.digest: Flashes when there are no transitions possible ("I am stuck!")
markov-harmony.use_when: Markov harmonic transitions with stuck-state flash on dead ends. Use for Markov-modelled chord-progression generation with explicit feedback when transitions are impossible.

markov-rhythm.use_when: Rhythm whose entry delays follow a Markov chain. Inlets, left to right: toggle on/off, start index (0-n), Markov table in `prob` format, list of EDs in ms. Argument: start index. Outlets: rhythm bangs, chosen index, chosen ED. Built on the RTC-lib `markov` abstraction.

matrix12.digest: 1994-2006 by Charles Baker and R. Albert Falesch, vs. 2.0
matrix12.use_when: Charles Baker's serial matrix external. Send a twelve-tone row (0–11) as a list; then select a row of the 12×12 matrix by index and choose prime, inversion or retrograde form; bang outputs the selected row as a list. Matrix origin is 0. Pair with `random-row` and `display-row`.

max-cursor.digest: 1 or 0 send to the inlet (or given as the argument) shows or hides the mouse cursor.
max-cursor.use_when: Show/hide mouse cursor (1=show, 0=hide). Use for kiosk / fullscreen patches that need to hide the cursor programmatically.

max-menubar.digest: 1 or 0 send to the inlet (or given as the argument) turns Max's menubar mode on or off.
max-menubar.use_when: Toggle Max's menubar mode (1/0). Constructor arg: `<initial>` (default 1). Use for fullscreen presentation patches.

max-overdrive.digest: 1 or 0 send to the inlet (or given as the argument) turns Max's Overdrive mode on or off.
max-overdrive.use_when: Turns Max's Overdrive mode on (1) or off (0) by sending `;max preempt 1/0`. The argument is also sent when the patch loads, so it can switch Overdrive off unexpectedly. Same as a message box `;max preempt $1`. For Scheduler in Audio Interrupt use `MSP-takeover~`.

max-quit.use_when: Immediately quit Max. Use only with great care — typically for scripted exits, kiosk shutdown.

member.digest: The number  list at the right inlet is searched for occurences of the ints that arrive at the left inlet. The output is a one if the list includes the int and zero if it doesn't.
member.use_when: Test whether each int in the left-inlet stream occurs in the right-inlet list. Output 1 (member) or 0 (not). Use as a membership predicate for list filtering.

metro-dev%.digest: Introduces irregularities to an equal pulsation by deviating from a given pulsation speed ("inégalité", "rubato", "human feeling)."
metro-dev%.use_when: Metronome with percentage deviation from base pulsation — adds 'inégalité' / rubato / human-feel. Constructor args: `<base-ms> <deviation-percent>` (default 250., 15.). Use for humanised metro-style timing.

ms2sec.digest: Converts milliseconds into seconds. The argument sets the number of decimal places.
ms2sec.use_when: Convert milliseconds to seconds. Constructor arg: `<decimal-places>` (default 2). Use whenever a millisecond value should be displayed as seconds with controlled precision.

multiple.use_when: Repeats each element of a supply list (left inlet) as many times as the matching number in a multiples list (right inlet); a 0 removes that element. Both lists must be the same length, otherwise it posts an error. Use to build weighted supplies for the selection-principle objects (e.g. `3 1 2` makes the first element three times as likely).

neutral-harmony.digest: Building an interval row by alternating a given interval (e.g. 3) with its compliment (e.g. 8). Outputs pitch classes (i.e. notes without any register informations).
neutral-harmony.use_when: Build an interval row by alternating an interval with its complement (e.g. 3 alternating with 8). Constructor arg: `<interval>` (default 6). Output is pitch classes. Use for symmetric-interval harmonic structures.

normalize-row.digest: Normalization of a twelve-tone row - the pitch classes are transposed in a way that the new row always starts with 0 (i.e. pitch class c).
normalize-row.use_when: Normalise a 12-tone row so it starts with pitch class 0 (transposes the row down). Use for canonical-form storage of rows.

note2cents.digest: Shows how many cents a microtonal note <float> is deviating from a tempered one.
note2cents.use_when: Show how many cents a microtonal note (float) deviates from the nearest tempered semitone. Use when working with microtonal tunings — exposes the deviation explicitly for display or quantisation.

note2frq.digest: Converts a note (= MIDI key number or MIDI cents) into frequency.
note2frq.use_when: Convert a MIDI note number (or MIDI cents float) to frequency in Hz. Use as the standard mtof — accepts microtonal floats too.

note2pitch.digest: Outputs the pitch class <integer> (i.e. a note without register information) of a note (i.e. MIDI note number) <int>.
note2pitch.use_when: Extract the pitch class (0–11) from a MIDI note number — essentially `% 12`. Use for octave-equivalent comparisons (chord recognition, pitch-class set theory).

note2st.digest: Outputs the intervals of an incoming stream of notes. The argument resp. the number sent to the right inlet determines the reference note.
note2st.use_when: Output intervals (in semitones) between consecutive notes of a stream. Constructor arg: `<reference-note>` (default 60). Use to convert an absolute note stream into a relative interval stream.

nth.digest: 1993 by Serge Lemouton/IRCAM, rewritten as an abstraction 2010 by Karlheinz Essl
nth.use_when: Output the nth element of a list (0-indexed). Use as a list indexer.

panning.digest: Equal power panning based on John Chowning's paper "Simulation of Moving Sound Sources".
panning.use_when: Turns one controller value 0–127 into left and right channel values 0–127 using an equal-power curve (stored tables, after Chowning). Control-rate only: scale the outputs and apply them to audio gains yourself. Use for MIDI-driven stereo placement.

pass.digest: vs. 1.1: seedable by sending an int via the "RTC-rs" message
pass.use_when: Probability gate — let a configurable percentage of inputs through. Constructor arg: `<percent>` (default 50). Seedable via `RTC-rs <int>`. Use for stochastic event filtering.

pass-bang.digest: Let every nth bang (= argument resp. int sent to the right inlet) pass.
pass-bang.use_when: Let every nth bang pass through. Constructor or right-inlet arg: `<n>` (default 15). Use as a beat divider — fire on every Nth bang.

per2pass.digest: Converts a periodicity factor <float between 0 and 1> into a percentage value <int between 0 and 100> for the pass-object.
per2pass.use_when: Convert a periodicity factor (0.–1. float) to a percentage value (0–100 int) for the pass object. Use to translate musical 'periodicity' (1.=fully periodic) into pass-object probabilities.

periodic.use_when: Random integer generator with controllable repetition. Arguments: `<max>` (range 0 to max-1) and `<periodicity>` 0–1. Periodicity 1 repeats one value forever, 0 never repeats (series-like); values between set the chance of repeating. Bang left inlet to output; range and periodicity can be changed on the other inlets. Built from `xrandom` and `pass`.

permutate.digest: The permutation mechanism prevents direct repetitions of notes!
permutate.use_when: Permutation with no direct repetitions. Use as the no-immediate-repetition permutation variant.

permutate-row.digest: Permutates a given row using its own structure as a permutation program. NB: The given row must be a twelve-note-row which smallest index is 0.
permutate-row.use_when: Permutate a 12-tone row using its own structure as the permutation program — input must be a row whose smallest index is 0. Use for structural permutation in serial composition.

pianoteq6-player.digest: Controls how fast this energy is transferred: the higher the inertia, the longer it takes to be transferred.
pianoteq6-player.use_when: Plays notes on a Pianoteq 6 plug-in inside `vst~`, with `makenote`-style velocity and duration handling plus sliders for Pianoteq sound settings (hammer noise, resonances, overtone energy transfer). Needs a licensed Pianoteq 6 installed; the plug-in name is fixed, so newer Pianoteq versions need the patcher edited.

pianoteq7-player.digest: Controls how fast this energy is transferred: the higher the inertia, the longer it takes to be transferred.
pianoteq7-player.use_when: Plays notes on a Pianoteq 7 plug-in inside `vst~`, with `makenote`-style velocity and duration handling plus sliders for Pianoteq sound settings (hammer noise, resonances, overtone energy transfer). Needs a licensed Pianoteq 7 installed; the plug-in name is fixed, so newer Pianoteq versions need the patcher edited.

piece.digest: Outputs the elements between a start.index ("from") and an end.index ("to") from a numerical list send to the leftmost inlet before.
piece.use_when: Output the elements between a start and end index from a numerical list. Use to extract a sublist range.

pitch-from-intervals.use_when: Generates pitch classes (0–11) by choosing intervals from a supply. Argument and middle inlet: selection principle 1–3 (alea, series, sequence). Send the interval list to the right inlet; each rhythm bang on the left inlet outputs a pitch class, and the right outlet the chosen interval.

pitch-from-row-mod.digest: flashes when the next transposition starts
pitch-from-row-mod.use_when: Modular extraction of pitches from a 12-tone row, with transposition flash on outlet. Use for row-based generative pitch streams with phase tracking.

pitch2note.digest: Combines pitch class and register into a note (i.e. MIDI note number).
pitch2note.use_when: Combine a pitch class (0–11) and a register (octave number) into a MIDI note number. Constructor arg: `<register>` (default 4 = middle). Use as the inverse of note2pitch.

play.use_when: General-purpose play trigger. Constructor args: `<velocity> <duration-ms> <channel>` (default 127, 1000, 1). Use as a one-stop note-emit object.

play-samp~.use_when: Stereo sample player. Use as the standard sample-playback voice in RTC-lib audio chains.

position.digest: Sorts a list in the left inlet using the index numbers in the right inlet.
position.use_when: Sort a list using indices supplied in the right inlet. Use as a custom-order sorter — supply a permutation in the right inlet to apply it to the left list.

random-env.digest: RTC implementation of Sonology's Random Envelope Generator as it was defined by Gottfried Michael Koenig et al. Thanks to Kees Tazelaar for the inspiration!
random-env.use_when: RTC-lib version of Koenig's Sonology Random Envelope Generator: random ramps separated by random waits. Four int arguments set the ramp-time and wait-time limits in ms (help: `random-env 100 1000 500 1000`). Two outlets; the help drives a gain from them.

random-norep.digest: Outputs random numbers <int> without direct (= immediate) repetitions.
random-norep.use_when: Random integers with no immediate repetition. Constructor arg: `<max>` (default 3). Use for cleaner random-walk-style streams where consecutive identical values must be avoided.

random-pan~.use_when: Turns a mono signal into pseudo-stereo by giving left and right slowly and randomly varying short delays (built on `tapin~`/`tapout~`). Argument and right inlet: strength 0–1; 0 switches the effect off, higher values add audible pitch wobble (Doppler). Outlets: left and right signal. It does not pan the sound between speakers.

random-ramp.digest: A simple musical example for using the random-ramp object:
random-ramp.use_when: Random envelope generator for MIDI velocity. Arguments: `<min-velocity> <max-velocity> <number-of-values> <min-ramp-ms> <max-ramp-ms> <number-of-ramp-times>` (values on a linear scale, times on a log scale). Each rhythm bang on the left inlet outputs the current velocity along a ramp to a new random target; `stop` ends it. Outlets: velocity, target velocity, ramp time.

random-ramp-urn.use_when: Like random-ramp but with no-repetition (urn-style value selection). Same args. Use for ramp generation that explores all values before repeating.

random-rampf.use_when: Float version of random-ramp. Arguments: `<min-value> <max-value> <number-of-values> <min-ramp-ms> <max-ramp-ms> <number-of-ramp-times>`. Each rhythm bang on the left inlet outputs the current value on a ramp to a random target; `stop` ends it. Outlets: value, target value, ramp time.

random-rampf-urn.use_when: Float, no-repetition version of random-ramp. Same args. Use for the float, urn-style variant of random ramps.

random-row.digest: Generates a twelve-tone row by random. The elements of the row range from 0 to 11.
random-row.use_when: Generate a random twelve-tone row (random permutation of 0–11). Use as the standard 12-tone row generator for serial composition.

ratio.digest: Chooses elements from a supply <int list> which are repeated according to a multiple list <int list> by using the "series" selection principle. - NB: The supply must be a list of numbers!
ratio.use_when: Choose elements from a supply repeating each according to a multiple list, using the SERIES selection principle. Right outlet flashes when supply is exhausted. Use for proportional repetition patterns — e.g. element A occurs 3x, B occurs 2x, C occurs 1x in a structured sequence.

ratio2intv.digest: Converts a ratio into an interval (int = tempered or float = any micro- interval).
ratio2intv.use_when: Inverse of intv2ratio — convert a frequency ratio to an interval in semitones. Use for converting just-intonation ratios back to a familiar interval representation.

reanimate.use_when: Send a bang on right outlet if no input bang has arrived for x ms. Constructor arg: `<reanimation-ms>` (default 3000). Use as a 'wake-up' or watchdog timer.

remove.digest: Removes the nth element of a list. When the position (= index) <int> is bigger than the the list size, the last element will be truncated.
remove.use_when: Remove the nth element from a list (truncates the last if n > size). Use for list-element deletion by index.

remove-dc~.digest: Removes the DC offset of an audio signal.
remove-dc~.use_when: DC-offset removal filter. Use as a single-object DC blocker on signal chains where DC accumulation is possible (long convolution, chained nonlinearities).

repchord-rhythm.digest: Generates a rhythm which repetition rate and chord size are depending on the index of the chosen ED. The following parameters allow you to model a lot of different musical situations:
repchord-rhythm.use_when: Rhythm where the chord size and chance of repetition depend on which entry delay is chosen. Arguments: `<min-ED> <max-ED> <ED-steps> <max-chord-size> <periodicity-min-ED> <periodicity-max-ED>` (help uses 100 1000 12 6 0.8 0.2); periodicity 0 = never repeat, 1 = always repeat. Toggle the left inlet to start. Outlets include rhythm bangs, chord bangs, chord size and ED.

repeat-ED.digest: Int in left inlet sends out a certain number of rhythm bangs with an entry delay (ED) given in right inlet.
repeat-ED.use_when: Send n bangs at a given ED. Int in left = bang count, ED in right. Constructor arg: `<ED-ms>` (default 300). Use for n-bang bursts at fixed timing.

replace.use_when: Replace an element in a list at a given position. Out-of-range positions are clamped. Use for in-place list updates.

reverse.digest: 1992 by James McCartney; rewritten as an abstraction 2006 by Karlheinz Essl
reverse.use_when: Reverse a list. Use as the list-domain reverse — bang re-emits last reversed list.

rit-acc.digest: Generates a ritardando or an accelerando, depending on the slope parameter. If it is < 1, the tempo becomes faster, when it is > 1, the speed slows down.
rit-acc.use_when: Generate a ritardando or accelerando via a slope parameter. Constructor args: `<initial-ED> <slope>` (default 75, 1.1). Slope <1 = accel, >1 = rit. Use for tempo-curve transitions.

rota.digest: A bang in the left inlet starts cycling through the supply sent to the middle inlet before. A bang sent to the rightmost inlet resets the cycling mechanism.
rota.use_when: Cyclic with bang-driven offset. Bang in left inlet starts cycling through the supply; bang in right inlet resets. Use as Koenig's ROTA — cyclic with explicit reset semantics.

rotate.digest: Cyclically rotate a list. Bang in left inlet retriggers output. List in left inlet gets rotated. Int in right inlet sets rotation.
rotate.use_when: Cyclically rotate a list. Constructor arg: `<rotation>` (default 2). Bang in left re-triggers; int in right resets rotation amount. Use for rotation-based variation of list patterns.

roundto.digest: A number sent to right inlet is rounded onto a certain "grid" <int, float> sent to right inlet.
roundto.use_when: Round to an arbitrary grid (int or float). Right inlet sets the grid value (default 0.5). Use for snap-to-grid behaviour with non-integer grids — e.g. quantize to 0.25 (16th-note grid) or 0.5 (eighth grid).

samp10~.digest: Allows a polyphony of up to 10 voices at the same time.
samp10~.use_when: 10-voice polyphonic stereo sample player. Use for moderate-polyphony sample playback.

samp20~.digest: Allows a polyphony of up to 20 voices at the same time.
samp20~.use_when: 20-voice polyphonic stereo sample player. Use for higher-polyphony sample playback when samp10~ runs out of voices.

scale-changer.digest: open to construct a specific start scale
scale-changer.use_when: Changes one pitch class of a scale at random on each bang (left inlet). The start scale goes to the right inlet as 12 values of 0/1 (1 = pitch class in use). Outlets include the changed list and a list of active positions. Use for slowly drifting harmony.

schweller.use_when: Crescendo-decrescendo (swell) generator. Constructor args define velocity range and timing (default 15, 127, 3000, 0.25). Use for automatic swell shapes (German 'Schweller' = swelling).

scramble.digest: Scrambles the order of a list of numbers. Bang in left inlet retriggers output. List in inlet gets scrambled and sent out the outlet.
scramble.use_when: Random shuffle of a list. Bang re-triggers (re-shuffles). Use as the standard list scrambler.

sect.digest: 1992 by James McCartney; rewritten as an abstraction 2006 by Karlheinz Essl
sect.use_when: List intersection — output the elements common to two input lists. Use for set-intersection on numerical lists.

sel-princ.digest: Changes between the selection principles ALEA, SERIES and SEQUENCE (as defined by G. M. Koenig) and ROTA according to the number sent to the middle inlet.
sel-princ.use_when: Selection-principle switcher — toggle between ALEA, SERIES, SEQUENCE, ROTA based on a number sent to the middle inlet. Constructor arg: `<initial-mode>` (default 3). Use to expose Koenig's selection-principle choice as a runtime control parameter.

sequence.digest: A bang in the left inlet outputs the next element of a supply <any list> sent to right inlet before. When the list is exhausted it is looped.
sequence.use_when: Cyclic supply iterator — bang outputs the next element; supply on right inlet. Loops when exhausted; right outlet bangs on the last element. Use as the Koenig SEQUENCE selection principle — strict cyclic ordering.

serial-rhythm.digest: Serial permutation (i.e. with repetition check) of entry delays (ED) from a geometrical row defined by a min. ED, a max. ED and a certain number of ED-values.
serial-rhythm.use_when: Serial permutation of EDs from a geometric row with repetition check. Constructor args: `<min-ED> <max-ED> <num-EDs>` (default 100, 1000, 12). Use as the SERIES-principle rhythmic stream.

series.digest: Outputs a bang when the supply is exhausted - i.e. when the last element of the supply has been chosen and the supply has to be refreshed again.
series.use_when: Random with repetition check — like alea but each element is used exactly once before any repeats (urn-style). Right outlet bangs when the supply is exhausted (at which point it refreshes). Use as Koenig's SERIES selection principle.

show.digest: Displays a list in a message box.
show.use_when: Display a list in a message box. Use as an inline display widget for list values.

show-pitchclass.digest: Shows the pitch class of a MIDI note number.
show-pitchclass.use_when: Display the pitch class of a MIDI note number with note-name labelling (C, C#, etc.). Use as a debugging / display widget for note streams.

slice.digest: Splits up a list in two. Argument determines the number of elements of list to send out the left outlet. The rest goes out the right outlet.
slice.use_when: Split a list into two — left outlet gets the first `<count>` elements, right outlet gets the rest. Constructor arg: `<count>` (default 4). Use to head/tail-split a list.

smooth-line.digest: Interpolates smoothly between consecutive input values.
smooth-line.use_when: Smooth interpolation between consecutive input values. Constructor arg: `<smoothing-ms>` (default 1000). Use as a click-free value smoother for parameter streams.

sneak.use_when: Markov-style random where transitions are only between adjacent elements — like a constrained random walk. Use for melodic contours that move stepwise rather than jumping.

sneak-random.digest: Outputs random number between 0 and n-1 whereas two adjacent numbers are always direct neighbours. 2nd argument: start value.
sneak-random.use_when: Random integer 0..(n-1) where consecutive outputs are always adjacent. Constructor args: `<n> <start-value>`. Use for constrained-step random walks (smoother contours than full random).

sneak-rhythm.digest: Generates a rhythm which "sneaks" between neigboured ED of a scale - this will result in a sort of continuous ritardando/accelerando/rubato etc.
sneak-rhythm.use_when: Rhythm that 'sneaks' between neighbouring EDs of a scale, producing continuous ritardando/accelerando/rubato. Constructor args: `<min-ED> <max-ED> <num-EDs>` (default 100, 1000, 12). Use for organic tempo fluctuation.

sort.digest: 1992 by James McCartney; rewritten as an abstraction 2006 by Karlheinz Essl
sort.use_when: Sorts a numerical list (wraps `zl sort`). Default order is ascending; a negative argument (e.g. `sort -1`) sorts descending. If any element is a float, all output is float. Bang re-outputs the last sorted list.

sqrt-pan~.use_when: Square-root-law stereo panner: mono signal in the left inlet, pan index 0–1 in the right inlet, left and right signals out. The square-root law also keeps total power constant, like cp-pan~, with a different curve shape.

st2pitch.digest: Accumulates incoming intervals and outputs pitch classes (i.e. notes without register information) at the left outlet resp. notes (= MIDI note numbers) at the right outlet.
st2pitch.use_when: Inverse of note2st — accumulate semitone intervals starting from a reference, output pitch classes (left) and notes (right). Constructor arg: `<reference>` (default 60). Use to convert interval streams back to note streams.

sum.use_when: Sum of input list elements. Use as a one-shot summation utility.

super-rhythm.digest: select a given supply of ED's
super-rhythm.use_when: Composite rhythm model — combines an ED supply, a selection principle, and probabilistic periodicity. Constructor args define supply and behaviour (default 3, 10, 1, 4, 0.7). Use as RTC-lib's most complete rhythm-generation primitive.

trans.use_when: Nth member of a transition row between two values in n steps. Constructor args: `<start> <end> <count> <type>` (default 500, 2000, 12, 0). Use for indexed-access to interpolated transition values.

trans-exp.digest: 1993-2010 by Karlheinz Essl, Frank Barknecht and R. Albert Falesch
trans-exp.use_when: Nth member of an exponential transition row. Constructor args: `<start> <end> <count>` (default 500, 2000, 12). Use for exponential interpolation curves.

trans-lin.digest: nth member of a linear transition row
trans-lin.use_when: Nth member of a linear transition row. Same args as trans-exp. Use for linear interpolation curves.

trans-log.digest: nth member of a logarithmic transition row
trans-log.use_when: Nth member of a logarithmic transition row. Same args as trans-exp. Use for log interpolation curves.

transp-pitch.digest: Transposes pitch classes by a certain interval.
transp-pitch.use_when: Transpose pitch classes by an interval (mod 12). Use for pitch-class set transposition without leaving the 0–11 space.

transpose-row.use_when: Transpose a 12-tone row by a given interval. Use for systematic row transposition in serial composition.

union.digest: Outputs a list which combines the atoms of  both input lists without duplicates
union.use_when: List union — output the combined elements of two lists with duplicates removed. Use for set-union on numerical lists.

unique.digest: Outputs a list comprised of those items in the left input list that are not contained in the right input list.
unique.use_when: List difference — output elements in the left list that are NOT in the right list. Use for set-difference / list filtering by exclusion.

xrandom.digest: maximum range of random numbers (must be larger than 1)
xrandom.use_when: Random with completion notification — outputs all numbers in range, then bangs when exhausted. Constructor arg: `<max>` (must be > 1). Use as a self-resetting urn that signals when a full cycle completes.

rtt.8sequence~.use_when: Eight rtt.sequence~ step sequencers in one object, driven by one counter or clock signal. Attributes come in nine sets: unnumbered ones (such as stepsize) are global and affect all eight sequences; numbered ones control a single sequence. Made with RNBO; a matching UI module is in the package's patchers/modules.

rtt.clockin~.digest: Convert a trigger-based clock signal into a phasor-based one
rtt.clockin~.use_when: Convert a trigger-based clock signal into a phasor-based one.

rtt.clock~.digest: Generate ramp signals in beats per minute.
rtt.clock~.use_when: Generate ramp signals in beats per minute.

rtt.counter~.digest: Count and resequence impulses and steps
rtt.counter~.use_when: Count and resequence impulses and steps.

rtt.euclidean~.digest: Generate patterns using the euclidean algorithm
rtt.euclidean~.use_when: Generate patterns using the euclidean algorithm.

rtt.feel~.digest: Modulate a phasor ramp for loose timing.
rtt.feel~.use_when: Modulate a phasor ramp for loose timing.

rtt.loop~.digest: Convert a phasor signal into a step counter
rtt.loop~.use_when: Convert a phasor signal into a step counter.

rtt.makecc~.digest: Convert signals to MIDI control change
rtt.makecc~.use_when: Convert signals to MIDI control change.

rtt.notes~.digest: Store and playback a sequence of notes.
rtt.notes~.use_when: Store and playback a sequence of notes.

rtt.resync~.digest: Reset the phase of a ramp signal.
rtt.resync~.use_when: Reset the phase of a ramp signal.

rtt.scala~.digest: Map MIDI note values to any scale
rtt.scala~.use_when: Map MIDI note values to any scale.

rtt.sequence~.digest: Store and play back lists of values
rtt.sequence~.use_when: Store and play back lists of values.

rtt.swing~.digest: Create variations in a ramp's slope for shuffle.
rtt.swing~.use_when: Create variations in a ramp's slope for shuffle.

rtt.upright~.digest: Convert any signal to a phasor-style clock.
rtt.upright~.use_when: Convert any signal to a phasor-style clock.

sadam.dom.digest: A Document Object Model (DOM) interface for Max.
sadam.dom.use_when: Java (mxj) class, not a native external: create it as `mxj sadam.dom` (help file); needs Java support in Max. Reads, creates, edits and writes XML as a W3C DOM tree using Java's DOM parser. Elements get an Element Index for addressing. Messages include `read`, `readagain`, `load`, `createDocument`, `getElement`, `getElementsByTagName`, `getChildNodes`, `getAttribute`, `getText`, `appendChild`, `insertBefore`, `appendText`, `print`, `clear`; attributes `@redundant`, `@symbolOutput`. For the same job without Java, use sadam.rapidXML.

sadam.envelopeGenerator.digest: Expr-based envelope generator for function objects
sadam.envelopeGenerator.use_when: Expr-based envelope generator for function objects.

sadam.fromBytes.digest: Convert a sequence of bytes into numbers
sadam.fromBytes.use_when: Convert a sequence of bytes into numbers.

sadam.gcd.digest: Compute the Greatest Common Divisor of two integers
sadam.gcd.use_when: Compute the Greatest Common Divisor of two integers.

sadam.lcm.digest: Compute the Least Common Multiple of two integers
sadam.lcm.use_when: Compute the Least Common Multiple of two integers.

sadam.limits.digest: Get minimum and maximum finite values of Max data types
sadam.limits.use_when: Get minimum and maximum finite values of Max data types.

sadam.lzo.digest: Lossless data compression and decompression using the LZO library
sadam.lzo.use_when: Lossless data compression and decompression using the LZO library.

sadam.normalize~.digest: An object that sets the gain of a source to the level of a reference signal
sadam.normalize~.use_when: An object that sets the gain of a source to the level of a reference signal.

sadam.phasor~.digest: Phasor object with maximal resting state
sadam.phasor~.use_when: Phasor object with maximal resting state.

sadam.prime.digest: Compute the closest prime numbers and the prime factorization of a positive integer
sadam.prime.use_when: Compute the closest prime numbers and the prime factorization of a positive integer.

sadam.sax.digest: A Simple API for XML (SAX) interface for Max.
sadam.sax.use_when: Java (mxj) class, not a native external: create it as `mxj sadam.sax` (help file); needs Java support in Max. Parses an XML document with SAX and outputs each element in turn, right to left: element index, tree depth, tag name, attributes, text content. The leftmost outlet reports -1 on a parse error or 0 when done. Messages `read`, `readagain`, `parse`, `clear`; attributes `@redundant`, `@symbolOutput`. Use to stream a large XML file into Max without building a tree.

sadam.sortLists.digest: Sort a set of lists simultaneously
sadam.sortLists.use_when: Sort a set of lists simultaneously.

sadam.standardMap~.digest: A chaotic oscillator based on Chirikov's Standard Map
sadam.standardMap~.use_when: A chaotic oscillator based on Chirikov's Standard Map.

sadam.stat.digest: Get mean and standard deviation of a number sequence
sadam.stat.use_when: Get mean and standard deviation of a number sequence.

sadam.tcpReceiver.digest: Receive data from the network using the TCP protocol
sadam.tcpReceiver.use_when: Receive data from the network using the TCP protocol.

sadam.tcpSender.digest: Send data through the network using the TCP protocol
sadam.tcpSender.use_when: Send data through the network using the TCP protocol.

sadam.toBytes.digest: Convert numbers into a sequence of bytes
sadam.toBytes.use_when: Convert numbers into a sequence of bytes.

sadam.udpClient.digest: UDP Sender/Receiver object with fixed source port
sadam.udpClient.use_when: UDP Sender/Receiver object with fixed source port.

sadam.udpReceiver.digest: Receive data from the network using the UDP protocol
sadam.udpReceiver.use_when: Receive data from the network using the UDP protocol.

sadam.udpSender.digest: Send data through the network using the UDP protocol
sadam.udpSender.use_when: Send data through the network using the UDP protocol.

samplor2.kg.use_when: Key-group voice allocator for samplor3~ (by Serge Lemouton): maps incoming MIDI pitch (int, or float for microtuning), velocity and channel to key groups and outputs control messages for samplor3~. Key groups can be created by message (bang builds them), imported from MOTU MachFive XML presets (import), and exported (export, exportastext, exportasxml); clear empties them. Mac only.

sdt.bouncing~.digest: [solids, control] Control algorithm to render bouncing sounds.
sdt.bouncing~.use_when: Control algorithm that schedules a series of impacts with realistic timing decay (a ball bouncing). Drives sdt.impact~ via the standard SDT control→interactor signal connection. Configure with `@height` (initial drop height), `@restitution` (bounce energy retention 0–1), `@irregularity` (timing jitter). Send `bang` to start a bouncing sequence. Use as the trigger source for bouncing-object sounds; pair with sdt.impact~ + sdt.modal/inertial for the resonating body.

sdt.breaking~.digest: [solids, control] Control algorithm to render breaking sounds.
sdt.breaking~.use_when: Control algorithm emitting a burst of impact events for breaking/shattering. Drives sdt.impact~. `@crushingEnergy` and `@storedEnergy` control overall power, `@fragmentation` controls how many pieces, `@granularity` controls fragment size. Send `bang` to fire one breaking event. Use for glass / ceramic / wood breaking; pair with sdt.impact~ + sdt.modal for the body.

sdt.bubble~.use_when: Liquid model — single bubble pop. `@radius` sets bubble size (drives pitch); `@riseFactor` controls the chirp glide as the bubble surfaces. Send `bang` to emit one bubble. Use directly as a bubble source; layer many sdt.bubble~ instances for boiling, fizzing, underwater textures.

sdt.crumpling~.digest: [solids, control] Control algorithm to render a granular, crumpling/crushing sound.
sdt.crumpling~.use_when: Granular impact stream for crushing/crumpling textures (paper, leaves, gravel). Same parameter shape as sdt.breaking~ — `@crushingEnergy`, `@fragmentation`, `@granularity` — but emits a continuous stream rather than one event. Drives sdt.impact~. Use for prolonged crushing/crumpling rather than single break events.

sdt.dcmotor~.use_when: Self-contained electric motor synthesis (no interactor needed). Optional `Buffer-size:int` argument tunes internal buffer length. Tunable timbre via `@coils` (number of brush sparks per revolution), `@harshness`, `@reson` (resonance), and per-source gains: `@airGain`, `@brushGain`, `@gearGain`, `@rotorGain`, `@gearRatio`. Drive RPM via signal input. Use as a robotic / mechanical source without rolling a noise+filter chain.

sdt.demix~.use_when: Three-component source separation: splits input audio into transient, tonal, and residual signals. Optional `window-size` and `smoothing-kernel-radius` constructor args set FFT window and median-filter radius. `@tonalThreshold` and `@noiseThreshold` gate the tonal/residual decision; `@overlap` controls FFT overlap. Use as a component-aware processor — apply different effects to each component in parallel and recombine.

sdt.envelope~.digest: Envelope follower with settable attack and release times.
sdt.envelope~.use_when: Envelope follower with separately tunable `@attack` (rise time, ms) and `@release` (fall time, ms). Compare to native `average~ + rampsmooth~` (close behaviour but coarser control). Use sdt.envelope~ when you need clean attack/release control as one object — particularly when attack and release should differ significantly (e.g. fast attack, slow release for amplitude tracking).

sdt.explosion~.use_when: Supersonic explosion synthesis. Optional constructor args set internal `scatter-size` and `propagation-size` buffers. `@blastTime`, `@scatterTime` shape the explosion envelope; `@distance` simulates listener distance (delays + filtering); `@dispersion`, `@waveSpeed`, `@windSpeed` model atmospheric propagation. Send `bang` to fire. Use for film/game explosion sources — much more realistic than noise+envelope.

sdt.fluidflow~.digest: [liquids] Sound of water dripping, waterfalls, burbling streams, etc.
sdt.fluidflow~.use_when: Liquid flow synthesis — drips, waterfalls, burbling streams. Optional `polyphony:int` argument caps simultaneous bubbles. `@avgRate` controls drip rate; `@minRadius`/`@maxRadius`/`@expRadius` shape bubble size distribution; `@minDepth`/`@maxDepth`/`@expDepth` shape depth (cavity resonance) distribution; `@riseCutoff` filters the rise chirp. Use for continuous water sources where a single sdt.bubble~ wouldn't suffice.

sdt.friction~.digest: [solids, interactor] Friction interaction between two solid objects.
sdt.friction~.use_when: Friction interactor between two solid bodies (singing glass, squeaky hinges, bowed or rubbed surfaces). Arguments required: <object0 name> <object1 name> <max outlets> - the Unique_IDs of an sdt.inertial or sdt.modal pair and the total number of pickups to output. Six signal inlets: external force on object0, velocity of object0 (puts the objects in contact), fragment size of object0, and the same three for object1. Outlets are displacement signals at each pickup (the sound). Contact via @kStatic / @kDynamic (friction coefficients), @breakAway, @stribeck, @viscosity, @noisiness, @stiffness, @dissipation, @force, @contact0 / @contact1 (pickup index of each contact point). Drive with sdt.scraping~ for surface textures.

sdt.impact~.digest: [solids, interactor] Impact interaction between two solid objects.
sdt.impact~.use_when: Impact interactor between two solid bodies (hammer on bell, ball on plate). Arguments required: <object0 name> <object1 name> <max outlets> - the Unique_IDs of an sdt.inertial (usually object0) and an sdt.modal, and the total pickup count to output. Six signal inlets: external force on object0, velocity of object0 (puts objects in contact), fragment size of object0, then the same for object1. Outlets are displacement signals at each pickup - the sound. Tune @stiffness, @dissipation, @shape (1.5 for spherical), @contact0 / @contact1. Feed the velocity inlet from sdt.bouncing~ or sdt.breaking~, or the force inlet from sdt.rolling~ / sdt.scraping~.

sdt.inertial.use_when: Point-mass body — non-resonating object that responds to forces. Constructor arg required: `Unique_ID:symbol`. `@mass` sets the inertial mass; `@fragmentSize` sets break-fragment scale. Drive with `strike <displacement> <velocity>` messages or via interactor coupling. Use as the 'striker' end of an interaction (e.g. the hammer in impact, the slider in friction) — for the resonating end use sdt.modal.

sdt.modal.use_when: Modal resonator — multi-mode resonating body. Constructor args: `<Unique_ID> <Modes> <Pickup-points>` (e.g. `mybell 32 2` for a 32-mode bell with 2 pickup positions). `@activeModes` caps how many modes are computed (CPU control). Define mode bank via `@freqs` (list of mode frequencies in Hz), `@decays` (per-mode decay times), `@pickup` (per-pickup mode amplitudes). `@fragmentSize` controls break-fragment behaviour. Use as the resonating object in physical models — bells, plates, bars, drums; configure mode lists per material.

sdt.motor~.use_when: Combustion engine synthesis. Optional `Buffer-size:int` constructor arg. Many tunable params: `@cycle` (2 or 4 stroke), `@cylinderSize`, `@compressionRatio`, `@asymmetry`, `@backfire`, `@expansion`, `@exhaustSize`, `@extractorSize`, plus throttle/RPM via signal input. Use for car/motorcycle/generator sources with realistic engine character.

sdt.myo~.use_when: Detect myoelastic vocal sounds - non-voiced vibrations such as vocal fry, palate grind and bilabial trills - in a voice signal. Four outlets: slow myoelastic amount, slow average frequency (Hz), fast amount, fast average frequency (Hz). Attributes @threshold (input gate), @lowFrequency / @highFrequency (envelope tracking cutoffs), @dcFrequency. For best results feed it the percussive output of sdt.demix~. Not a general voice activity detector.

sdt.pitchshift~.use_when: Frequency-domain pitch shifter. Optional `window-size:int` constructor arg. `@ratio` sets pitch shift (1.0 = no shift, 2.0 = octave up); `@overlap` controls FFT overlap (higher = better quality, more CPU). Use for pitch shifting without time-stretching. Compare to fftz.pvharm~ (FFTease) — both phase-vocoder-based; sdt.pitchshift~ is self-contained while pvharm~ is part of FFTease's broader spectral toolkit.

sdt.pitch~.use_when: Fundamental-frequency estimator based on the Normalized Square Difference Function. Optional window-size argument (default 4096). Outlets: pitch in Hz and pitch clarity 0-1. @overlap sets analysis overlap; @tolerance sets the detection tolerance. Compare with Max's fzero~; use sdt.pitch~ when you also want the clarity value or are already in the SDT ecosystem.

sdt.reverb~.digest: A computationally efficient yet maximally diffusive reverb.
sdt.reverb~.use_when: Computationally efficient feedback-delay-network reverb, meant to add turbulence and scattering texture to SDT models. Optional argument: maximum delay-line length in samples (default 44100). @xSize / @ySize / @zSize set room size in metres, @randomness the shape deviation from a rectangular room (0-1), @time the global reverberation time (s) and @time1k the time at 1 kHz. Choose it for low CPU; for a lush musical reverb, bp.Gigaverb (BEAP) is the usual built-in choice.

sdt.rolling~.digest: [solids, control] Control algorithm to render rolling sounds.
sdt.rolling~.use_when: Control layer for rolling sounds (wheel, marble). Input: a signal representing the rolling surface profile (e.g. noise). Output: a force signal to send to the force inlet of sdt.impact~, which strikes sdt.inertial against sdt.modal as a dense series of micro-impacts. @mass (use the same value as sdt.inertial's mass), @velocity (m/s), @depth (size of surface bumps), @grain (density of micro-impacts). Needs the sdt.inertial / sdt.impact~ / sdt.modal structure.

sdt.scraping~.digest: [solids, control] Control algorithm to render scraping/sliding/rubbing sound textures.
sdt.scraping~.use_when: Control algorithm for scraping/sliding/rubbing textures. `@force` sets contact pressure; `@velocity` sets sliding speed; `@grain` sets surface roughness. Drives sdt.friction~ to render the actual scraping sound. Use for sandpaper-on-wood, knife-on-stone, brake-pad-style textures.

sdt.spectralfeats~.digest: Spectral analyzer extracting several audio descriptors.
sdt.spectralfeats~.use_when: Bundled multi-descriptor spectral analyser — outputs centroid, spread, skewness, kurtosis, flatness, etc. all in one object. Optional `window-size:int` constructor arg. `@minFreq` / `@maxFreq` define the analysis band; `@overlap` controls FFT overlap. Use when you want several spectral features at once cheaper than chaining individual zsa.* objects (which each run their own FFT).

sdt.windcavity~.digest: [gases] Sound of airflows passing through cavities, such as tunnels, pipes, valves, etc.
sdt.windcavity~.use_when: Wind through a cavity model — tunnels, pipes, valves. Optional `Buffer-length:long` constructor arg. `@length` sets cavity length (drives resonance pitch); `@diameter` sets bore (drives timbre). Drive turbulence via signal input. Use for whistling pipes, organ-flue tones, howling chimneys.

sdt.windflow~.use_when: Plain wind noise: white noise through a non-resonant lowpass (about 800 Hz) whose amplitude follows the input wind-speed signal (0-1). No attributes. Use as a wind bed; for whistling or howling use sdt.windkarman~ (thin obstacles) or sdt.windcavity~ (pipes, tunnels).

sdt.windkarman~.use_when: Karman-vortex wind — howling/whistling wind around an obstacle. `@diameter` sets obstacle diameter (drives whistle pitch). Drive turbulence via signal input. Use for high-wind dramatic effects, whistling-around-corners textures.

sdt.zerox~.use_when: Zero-crossing detector and counter. Optional `Analysis-window-length:int` constructor arg. `@overlap` controls window overlap. Outputs zero-crossing rate per analysis window. Use as a cheap monophonic pitch estimator, transient detector, or noise/tone classifier (high zerox rate = noise-like, low = tonal) — much cheaper than full spectral analysis when one descriptor suffices.

jit.gl.syphonclient.use_when: Receive a Syphon texture stream from another macOS application. Drop into a Jitter GL chain to consume textures published by any Syphon-enabled app. `@servername` selects which publisher to read; supports alpha. Use for cross-app live video routing without round-tripping through pixel buffers.

jit.gl.syphonserver.use_when: Publish a Jitter GL texture as a Syphon stream consumable by other apps. Drop into a Jitter GL chain to make its output available systemwide. `@servername` sets the published name.

ts.4to1Switch.digest: Switch between four input signals and output one of them
ts.4to1Switch.use_when: Steps through four input signals, switching after a set number of gates. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.4to1Switch.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Utility. Inlets: 0 gate to change; 1 (unlabeled); 2 (unlabeled); 3 (unlabeled); 4 (unlabeled); 5 Steps to change. Outlets: 0 (unlabeled). Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: selector~ — picks an input by number, not by counting gates. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.CV.digest: Create signal sequences with different directions
ts.CV.use_when: Sequences stepped control signals in several playback directions. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.CV.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Sequencers. Inlets: 0 clock in; 1 multiplication mod; 2 length mod; 3 reset gate; 4 mod direction. Outlets: 0 outCV; 1 outSmoothCV. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.DrumSeq.use_when: Sequences six drum gate channels with a chance per step. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.DrumSeq.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Sequencers. Inlets: 0 clock in; 1 multiplication mod; 2 length mod; 3 reset gate; 4 mod direction. Outlets: 0 outGate; 1 outGate; 2 outGate; 3 outGate; 4 outGate; 5 outGate. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: bp.Drum Sequencer — BEAP drum sequencer sending MIDI. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.aKastle.use_when: Generates FM tones from two voices with six routing algorithms. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.aKastle.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > OSCs. Inlets: 0 v/oct A; 1 v/oct B; 2 Mul1; 3 Mul2; 4 Mul3; 5 Mul4; 6 Lev1; 7 Lev2; 8 Lev3; 9 Lev4; 10 Algorithm. Outlets: 0 outA; 1 outB. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.ad.digest: Set the curve for the exponential envelope segments
ts.ad.use_when: Generates an attack/decay envelope with adjustable curves from a gate. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.ad.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Functions. Inlets: 0 gate; 1 mod attack; 2 mod decay; 3 mod attackCurve; 4 mod decayCurve. Outlets: 0 out ad. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: bp.AD — BEAP attack/decay envelope. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.adsr.use_when: Generates an ADSR envelope signal from a gate. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.adsr.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Functions. Inlets: 0 gate; 1 attack mod; 2 decay mod; 3 sustain mod; 4 release mod; 5 mod log/exp. Outlets: 0 outAdsr; 1 outGate. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: adsr~ — ADSR envelope generator. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.attenuverter.digest: Multiplication of incoming signal. If multiplied by negative value - signal is inverted.
ts.attenuverter.use_when: Scales a signal down or flips its polarity. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.attenuverter.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Utility. Inlets: 0 L in~; 1 mod crossfade. Outlets: 0 out~. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: bp.Gain and Bias — BEAP gain and offset module. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.beatrepeat.digest: clock division if synced to external clock
ts.beatrepeat.use_when: Loops a slice of incoming audio in time with a clock, with pitch change. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.beatrepeat.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > FX. Inlets: 0 inL; 1 inR; 2 record start/stop; 3 pitch; 4 clock in~. Outlets: 0 outL; 1 outR. Loop time syncs to Max's global tempo, or divides an external clock. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.biToUni.digest: Convert bipolar signals to unipolar output
ts.biToUni.use_when: Converts a -1 to 1 signal into a 0 to 1 signal. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.biToUni.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Utility. Inlets: 0 sample. Outlets: 0 out. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.biquad.use_when: Filters a mono signal with a selectable biquad filter. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.biquad.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Filters. Inlets: 0 inSig; 1 modfreq; 2 modQ. Outlets: 0 out. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: filtercoeff~ — feeds biquad~ with modulatable coefficients. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.chorus.use_when: Adds a stereo delay-based chorus. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.chorus.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > FX. Inlets: 0 inL; 1 inR; 2 timeL; 3 timeR; 4 freq; 5 mod; 6 feedback. Outlets: 0 outL; 1 outR. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: abl.dsp.chorus~ — chorus. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.clave.use_when: Synthesizes a clave hit modeled on the Roland CR-8000. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.clave.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Drums_Sample. Inlets: 0 trig; 1 freq; 2 decay. Outlets: 0 (unlabeled). Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.clockMini.digest: A clock generator with clock multiplication, phase change and synchronization to external clocks.
ts.clockMini.use_when: Generates clock gates with multiplication, phase, width and external sync. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.clockMini.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Clock. Inlets: 0 clock in~; 1 modClock1; 2 width; 3 Phase. Outlets: 0 gate 1. The help file is named ts.clock, but the module file is ts.clockMini.maxpat. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.clockdiv.digest: A clock divider which divides an input clock by 2, 4, 6, or 8.
ts.clockdiv.use_when: Divides an incoming clock into slower clocks. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.clockdiv.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Clock. Inlets: 0 in clock. Outlets: 0 div by 2; 1 div by 4; 2 div by 8; 3 div by 16. The help file is named ts.clockDiv; the module file is ts.clockdiv.maxpat. Help text says divide by 2, 4, 6, 8, but the outlets are labeled 2, 4, 8, 16. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.clockmult.digest: A clock multiplier which multiplies an input clock by 2, 4, 6, or 8
ts.clockmult.use_when: Multiplies an incoming clock into faster clocks. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.clockmult.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Clock. Inlets: 0 in clock. Outlets: 0 mult by 2; 1 mult by 4; 2 mult by 8; 3 mult by 16. The help file is named ts.clockMult; the module file is ts.clockmult.maxpat. Outlets are labeled ×2, 4, 8, 16. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.complexOsc.digest: A complex oscillator which generates timbres by means of  internal modulation between 2 oscillators.
ts.complexOsc.use_when: Generates rich tones from two cross-modulating oscillators with wavefolding. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.complexOsc.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > OSCs. Inlets: 0 1v/oct A; 1 1v/oct B; 2 "LinFM B"; 3 "LinFM A"; 4 Fold Mod; 5 Fold. Outlets: 0 out~. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.crazyClock.digest: A clock with Hz frequency that can have a random spread for its frequency.
ts.crazyClock.use_when: Generates clock gates at a Hz rate with random spread. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.crazyClock.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Clock. Inlets: 0 freq; 1 freq. Outlets: 0 gate out. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: abl.dsp.pulsate~ — random pulse emitter. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.crossfade.digest: Crossfade signal output between two input signals
ts.crossfade.use_when: Crossfades between two signals. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.crossfade.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Utility. Inlets: 0 inL; 1 inR; 2 mod crossfade. Outlets: 0 out~. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: bp.Xfade — BEAP crossfader. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.cymbal.use_when: Synthesizes cymbal sounds from FM and noise. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.cymbal.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Drums_Sample. Inlets: 0 gate; 1 freq; 2 FM amount; 3 highpass; 4 impactDecay; 5 adsrDecay; 6 log/exp; 7 overdrive. Outlets: 0 (unlabeled). Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.dadsr.digest: An Attack/Decay/Sustain/Release envelope generator with input gate delay
ts.dadsr.use_when: Generates an ADSR envelope after a delay from the gate. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.dadsr.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Functions. Inlets: 0 gate; 1 attack mod; 2 decay mod; 3 sustain mod; 4 release mod; 5 mod log/exp. Outlets: 0 outDadsr; 1 outGate. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: bp.DADSR — BEAP delayed ADSR. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.delayUnit.digest: An eight-tap delay with individual volume control for every tap and pitchshift in feedback which outputs even/odd taps from different outputs
ts.delayUnit.use_when: Delays audio through eight taps with per-tap volume and feedback pitch shift. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.delayUnit.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > FX. Inlets: 0 sigIn~; 1 delayMod; 2 feedbackMod; 3 pitchshiftMod; 4 clockIn. Outlets: 0 manualMixOut; 1 oddManualMixOut; 2 evenManualMixOut; 3 oddMixOut; 4 evenMixOut. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.drumModule.digest: Universal drum module with an internal sampler
ts.drumModule.use_when: Plays drum hits from an oscillator, noise and a loaded sample. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.drumModule.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Drums_Sample. Inlets: 0 trig; 1 velocity; 2 mod Freq; 3 mod Amount; 4 cutoff freq; 5 main freq. Outlets: 0 (unlabeled). Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.euclideanSeq.use_when: Sequences gates with evenly spread (Euclidean) hits and rotation. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.euclideanSeq.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Sequencers. Inlets: 0 clock in; 1 multiplication mod; 2 reset gate; 3 mod steps; 4 mod hits; 5 mod rotation. Outlets: 0 gate out; 1 bang out. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: abl.dsp.euclid~ — Euclidean rhythm ramp generator. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.euscale.digest: Creates scales for quantization using a Euclidean distribution
ts.euscale.use_when: Builds scales by Euclidean distribution and quantizes up to four melodies to them. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.euscale.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Quantizers. Inlets: 0 quantize; 1 quantize; 2 quantize; 3 quantize; 4 notes; 5 diapason; 6 inversion; 7 base note. Outlets: 0 (unlabeled); 1 (unlabeled); 2 (unlabeled); 3 (unlabeled). Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.feedback.digest: Make feedback connections for modules - The smaller the signal vector size, the tighter the feedback
ts.feedback.use_when: Lets you patch a module's output back into an earlier module. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.feedback.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Utility. Inlets: 0 L in~; 1 feedback attenuation. Outlets: 0 out~. The smaller the signal vector size, the tighter the feedback. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: bp.Feedback — BEAP feedback module. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.fmPerc.digest: !!! When modulated externally !!! every modulation value is changed only when the module is gated
ts.fmPerc.use_when: Synthesizes percussive FM sounds with two envelopes and feedback. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.fmPerc.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Drums_Sample. Inlets: 0 gate; 1 freq Start; 2 freq End; 3 FM; 4 feedback FM; 5 Attack 1; 6 Decay 1; 7 Curve 1; 8 Attack 2; 9 Decay 2; 10 Curve 2; 11 overdrive. Outlets: 0 (unlabeled). When modulated externally, every modulation value changes only when the module is gated. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.scaler.use_when: Quantizes pitch signals or MIDI notes to a custom scale. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.scaler.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Quantizers. Inlets: 0 v/oct; 1 inMidi. Outlets: 0 cv~; 1 midi. The help file is named ts.scale; the module file is ts.scaler.maxpat. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Built-in alternative: bp.Quantizer — BEAP pitch quantizer. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.simpleDelay.use_when: Delays stereo audio with separate left and right times and feedback. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.simpleDelay.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > FX. Inlets: 0 inL; 1 inR; 2 timeL; 3 timeR; 4 feedback. Outlets: 0 outL; 1 outR. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: bp.Feedback Delay — BEAP delay module. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.simpleFM.digest: "simpleFM~" Max abstraction-based synthesizer with internal AD envelope for overall amplitude and Modulation Index.
ts.simpleFM.use_when: Plays a two-operator FM voice with an AD envelope. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.simpleFM.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Drums_Sample. Inlets: 0 gate; 1 1v/oct; 2 Harm Ratio; 3 Env Mod Index; 4 Attack; 5 Decay; 6 Curve. Outlets: 0 out. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: bp.FM — BEAP FM oscillator. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.simpleLFOs.use_when: Generates six synced LFO shapes at once. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.simpleLFOs.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > LFOs. Inlets: 0 mod Freq; 1 mod Duty Cycle; 2 mod Pulse Width. Outlets: 0 outSin; 1 outTri; 2 outSquare; 3 outRampUp; 4 outRampDown; 5 outRandom. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: bp.LFO — BEAP LFO module. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.sine.digest: Simple sine oscillator with FM input
ts.sine.use_when: Generates a sine wave with FM input. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.sine.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > OSCs. Inlets: 0 1v/oct; 1 FM in; 2 FM amount. Outlets: 0 outSig. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: cycle~ — sine oscillator. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.sineLFO.use_when: Generates a slow sine control signal. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.sineLFO.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > LFOs. Inlets: 0 mod Freq. Outlets: 0 out. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: cycle~ — sine oscillator. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.snare.digest: Snare synthesis module inspired by "Sound on Sound" article for snare synthesis. Nearly all parameters are modulatable.
ts.snare.use_when: Synthesizes snare drums from tone and noise. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.snare.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Drums_Sample. Inlets: 0 trigger; 1 freq mult; 2 fm in; 3 modIndex; 4 mod tone decay; 5 mod toneCurve; 6 mod noise decay; 7 bandstop freq; 8 filter to; 9 Overdrive. Outlets: 0 (unlabeled). Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.spectralResonator.digest: Spectral resonator based on Mutable Instrument's resonating filter code. 7 resonating filters spreaded from main frequency in some ratio.
ts.spectralResonator.use_when: Resonates audio through seven tuned filters spread from one pitch. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.spectralResonator.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > FX. Inlets: 0 inL; 1 inR; 2 Pitch; 3 spread; 4 inharmonicity; 5 Q; 6 randFreq. Outlets: 0 (unlabeled); 1 (unlabeled); 2 Envelope follower. Made with Volker Böhm; based on Mutable Instruments' resonating filter code. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: abl.device.spectralresonator~ — spectral resonator. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.stereoBiquad.use_when: Filters a stereo signal with a selectable biquad filter. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.stereoBiquad.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Filters. Inlets: 0 inL; 1 inR; 2 modfreq; 3 modQ. Outlets: 0 outL; 1 outR. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: filtercoeff~ — feeds biquad~ with modulatable coefficients. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.stereoRecorder.digest: Lets you to record stereo WAV files.
ts.stereoRecorder.use_when: Records stereo WAV files from the patch. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.stereoRecorder.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Save + Rec. Inlets: 0 Lrec; 1 Rrec. Outlets: none. Receives recorder channel 1 from ts.outDAC by the global names Lrec1 / Rrec1; no cords needed. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Built-in alternative: sfrecord~ — record to audio file on disk. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.strangeVerb.digest: Improvised random algorithm for reverberation made from large numbers of delays
ts.strangeVerb.use_when: Makes an unusual reverb from many randomly timed delays. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.strangeVerb.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > FX. Inlets: 0 inL; 1 inR; 2 (unlabeled); 3 feedback; 4 reflections. Outlets: 0 outR; 1 outR. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.tanhOsc.digest: balance between two functions before their transformation with mathematical operations
ts.tanhOsc.use_when: Generates tones by combining two oscillators through math functions. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.tanhOsc.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > OSCs. Inlets: 0 Freq A; 1 Freq B; 2 Amp A; 3 Amp B; 4 Balance; 5 fold. Outlets: 0 out. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.toBEAP.digest: Conversion signals from TS.Modular to BEAP package for super-integration :)
ts.toBEAP.use_when: Converts TS.Modular's -1 to 1 signals to BEAP's -5 to 5 range. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.toBEAP.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular. Inlets: 0 (unlabeled). Outlets: 0 (unlabeled). Scales -1..1 up to BEAP's -5..5. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.triangle.digest: Simple antialiased triangular oscillator with FM input
ts.triangle.use_when: Generates an antialiased triangle wave with FM and sync. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.triangle.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > OSCs. Inlets: 0 1v/oct; 1 FM in; 2 FM amount; 3 duty Cycle; 4 sync. Outlets: 0 (unlabeled). Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: tri~ — antialiased triangle oscillator. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.uniToBi.digest: Convert unipolar (0. - 1.0) positive signals to bipolar (-1.0 - 1.0) output
ts.uniToBi.use_when: Converts a 0 to 1 signal into a -1 to 1 signal. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.uniToBi.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Utility. Inlets: 0 sample. Outlets: 0 out. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.vca.digest: Unipolar CV is good for enveloping input signal. Bipolar CV is good for amplitude modulation.
ts.vca.use_when: Controls a signal's level from a control signal. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.vca.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Utility. Inlets: 0 inSig; 1 CV; 2 mod log/exp. Outlets: 0 outSig. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: bp.VCA — BEAP amplifier module. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.vertecho.digest: Assymetric time stereo delay with a filter in the feedback loop
ts.vertecho.use_when: Delays stereo audio with uneven left/right times and a feedback filter. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.vertecho.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > FX. Inlets: 0 inL; 1 inR; 2 Ext mod; 3 Mod amount; 4 Freq Filtercut; 5 Delay Time; 6 Feedback; 7 trig~ change. Outlets: 0 OutL; 1 OutR. The help file is named ts.vertEcho; the module file is ts.vertecho.maxpat. Delay time 5000 = equal in both channels; below, left faster; above, left longer. Feedback filter 0–99 lowpass, 100 off, 101–200 highpass. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.wavefolder.use_when: Folds a signal back on itself for bright harmonics. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.wavefolder.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > FX. Inlets: 0 in; 1 fold. Outlets: 0 out. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: bp.Wavefolder — BEAP wavefolder. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.waveshaper.digest: Waveshaper module based on the Max/MSP tutorials
ts.waveshaper.use_when: Reshapes audio through a hand-drawn transfer table. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.waveshaper.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > FX. Inlets: 0 (unlabeled); 1 InAmp. Outlets: 0 (unlabeled). Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. Built-in alternative: bp.Waveshaper — BEAP waveshaper. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.wavetableRandomLFO.digest: random frequency spread for the LFO
ts.wavetableRandomLFO.use_when: Generates a random control signal read from a wavetable. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.wavetableRandomLFO.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > LFOs. Inlets: 0 freq; 1 freq; 2 morph. Outlets: 0 (unlabeled). Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). Its modulation inputs use TS.Modular's Normalization subpatcher: the module's own dial sets the parameter until a signal cord is plugged into that inlet. TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

ts.xyz.digest: Toggle turns performance sequencing mode (sequencer start to use only toggled steps). To go out of this mode just press "out" button.
ts.xyz.use_when: Sequences notes along snake-shaped paths through a grid. Place it as a bpatcher of ts.xyz.maxpat: right-click > Paste From > TS.Modular > Sequencers. Inlets: 0 clock in; 1 multiplication mod; 2 length mod; 3 reset gate; 4 mod direction; 5 step modulation; 6 add note. Outlets: 0 outGate; 1 outBang; 2 outNote. The help file is named ts.XYZ; the module file is ts.xyz.maxpat. A toggle enters performance mode (only toggled steps play); the out button leaves it. Modules talk by signal cords in the MSP -1 to 1 range; use ts.toBEAP / ts.fromBEAP to connect BEAP modules (-5 to 5). TS.Modular by Tim Shatnyy.

och.hset.digest: generates a series of microqiskit h gate instructions to help speed up circuit construction.
och.hset.use_when: generates a series of microqiskit h gate instructions to help speed up circuit construction.

och.int2qc.digest: converts decimal number to a series of microqiskit x gate instructions to compose the corresponding qubit encoding.
och.int2qc.use_when: converts decimal number to a series of microqiskit x gate instructions to compose the corresponding qubit encoding.

och.mset.digest: generates a series of microqiskit measure gate instructions to help speed up circuit construction.
och.mset.use_when: generates a series of microqiskit measure gate instructions to help speed up circuit construction.

och.mtos.digest: Convert MIDI note numbers to note names
och.mtos.use_when: Convert MIDI note numbers to note names.

och.qubits2states.digest: calculates the number of states that X qubits can represent.
och.qubits2states.use_when: calculates the number of states that X qubits can represent.

och.states2qubits.digest: calculates the required number of qubits to represent X many different states.
och.states2qubits.use_when: calculates the required number of qubits to represent X many different states.

och.topcount.digest: returns the top result output by och.microqiskit get_counts.
och.topcount.use_when: returns the top result output by och.microqiskit get_counts.

och.xset.digest: generates a series of microqiskit x gate instructions to help speed up circuit construction.
och.xset.use_when: generates a series of microqiskit x gate instructions to help speed up circuit construction.

upshot_16chanpanner.use_when: Pans stereo audio around 16 speakers in a circle with one control. Two audio inlets (L, R) plus a 0–127 position inlet; the position is an endless rotary around the ring. Outlets: 16 speaker signals. Place as a bpatcher from the us.16chanpanner clipping (Upshot/clippings/ROUTING). Upshot controls take and output 0–127 floats; hover over inlets to read their roles. By Benjamin Van Esser.

upshot_1bitprobability.use_when: Outputs 0 or 1 on each bang, with a set chance of 1. Left inlet: bang to draw a result. Right inlet: probability (0–127) of getting 1. Outlet: 0 or 1.
