Control messages (to the leftmost inlet, as listed in its help file): enable [boolean] sync_lock [0 - 3] angle [0. - 360.] sync_invert [boolean] time [0 - 10] speed [-10. - 10.] freq [0. - 1000.] [0. - 10000.] fm [-1. - 1.] [-5. - 5.] bias [0. - 100.] bm [-0.5 - 0.5] phase [0. - 1.] pm [-1. - 1.] [-5. - 5.] shape [0. - 1.] curve [boolean]. Angle rotates the pattern; pow toggle changes the curve (v1.7). Vsynth by Kevin Kripper.

vs_wfg_av.digest: Low-Res and unsynced video oscillator. It implements an internal FM operator.
vs_wfg_av.use_when: Generates a low-resolution video oscillator that also outputs audio, with FM. Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu, `Vsynth/menu/vs_menu.maxpat`); passes OpenGL textures and needs exactly one `vs_render` running in the patch. Inlets: Control In. Outlets: Texture Out; Audio Out. Control messages (to the leftmost inlet, as listed in its help file): enable [boolean] waveform [0 - 3] freq [0. - 3400] pw [0. - 1.] ratio [-1. 1.] depth [-60. - 60.] gain [0. - 1.]. Not synced to the render timer. Vsynth by Kevin Kripper.

vs_wfg_bipolar.use_when: Generates waveform patterns centered on the screen, for symmetrical images. Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu, `Vsynth/menu/vs_menu.maxpat`); passes OpenGL textures and needs exactly one `vs_render` running in the patch. Inlets: FM In / Control In; Phase Modulation In; Bias Modulation In. Outlets: Texture Out; Inverted Texture Out. Control messages (to the leftmost inlet, as listed in its help file): enable [boolean] sync_lock [0 - 3] angle [0. -360.] sync_invert [boolean] time [0 - 10] speed [-10. - 10.] freq [0. - 1024.] [0. - 10000.] fm [-1. - 1.] [-5. - 5.] bias [0. - 100.] bm [-0.5 - 0.5] phase [0. - 1.] pm [-1. - 1.] [-5.-5.] shape [0. -1.] polarity [boolean]. Like vs_wfg_3 but in the -1 to 1 range. Vsynth by Kevin Kripper.

vs_wfg_polarizer.digest: Mix between Bipolar and Radial WFG. It implements Phase and Bias texture modulation inputs.
vs_wfg_polarizer.use_when: Morphs between straight stripe and polar waveform patterns. Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu, `Vsynth/menu/vs_menu.maxpat`); passes OpenGL textures and needs exactly one `vs_render` running in the patch. Inlets: PM In / Control In; BM In. Outlets: Texture Out; Inverted Texture Out. Control messages (to the leftmost inlet, as listed in its help file): enable [boolean] center [-1. 1.] sync_lock [0 - 3] angle [0. - 360.] sync_invert [boolean] time [0 - 10] speed [-10. - 10.] freq [0. - 1000.] [0. - 10000.] bias [0. - 100.] bm [-0.5 - 0.5] phase [0. - 1.] pm [-1. - 1.] [-5. - 5.] shape [0. - 1.] polarizer [0. - 1.] morph [0. - 1.]. Mix of vs_wfg_bipolar and vs_wfg_rad. Vsynth by Kevin Kripper.

vs_wfg_rad.digest: Generates different polar patterns with standard waveshapes. It implements Phase and PW texture modulation inputs.
vs_wfg_rad.use_when: Generates radial and spiral patterns from standard waveforms. Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu, `Vsynth/menu/vs_menu.maxpat`); passes OpenGL textures and needs exactly one `vs_render` running in the patch. Inlets: PM In / Control In; PWM. Outlets: waveform_from_selector; inverted waveform_switch. Control messages (to the leftmost inlet, as listed in its help file): enable [boolean] phase [0. - 1.] center [-1. 1.] time [0 - 10] sync_invert [boolean] shape [0 - 2] waveform [0 - 5] freq [0. - 1000.] [0. - 10000.] freq_lock [boolean] pm [-1. - 1.] [-5. - 5.] pw [0. - 100.] pwm [-0.5 - 0.5]. Freq_lock snaps frequency to multiples of 60 for clean spirals. Vsynth by Kevin Kripper.

vs_wfg_s.digest: Creates vertical scrolling lines with different waveshapes. It implements phase and pulse-width modulation inputs.
vs_wfg_s.use_when: Generates simple vertical scrolling line patterns with phase and pulse-width modulation. Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu, `Vsynth/menu/vs_menu.maxpat`); passes OpenGL textures and needs exactly one `vs_render` running in the patch. Inlets: Phase Modulation In / Control In; PWM In. Outlets: Texture Out; Inverted Texture Out. Control messages (to the leftmost inlet, as listed in its help file): enable [boolean] sync_lock [0 - 3] sync_invert [boolean] time [0 - 10] waveform [0 - 5] freq [0. - 1000.] [0. - 10000.] fm [0. - 1.] [0. - 60.] pw [0. - 100.] pwm [-0.5 - 0.5] phase [0. - 1.] pm [-3. - 3.]. The basic oscillator; vs_wfg_2 adds frequency modulation. Vsynth by Kevin Kripper.

vs_wfg_shapes.digest: Generates different shapes with standard waveforms. It implements Phase and PW texture modulation inputs.
vs_wfg_shapes.use_when: Generates circles, polygons and other shapes from standard waveforms. Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu, `Vsynth/menu/vs_menu.maxpat`); passes OpenGL textures and needs exactly one `vs_render` running in the patch. Inlets: PM Texture In / Control In; PWM Texture In. Outlets: Texture Out; Inverted Texture Out. Control messages (to the leftmost inlet, as listed in its help file): enable [boolean] time [0 - 10] sync_invert [boolean] shape [0 - 5] waveform [0 - 5] freq [0. - 1000.] [0. - 10000.] pm [-1. - 1.] [-5 - 5.] pw [0. - 100.] pwm [-0.5 - 0.5] center [-1. 1.] vertex [3.-12.]. Vertex sets polygon sides. Vsynth by Kevin Kripper.

vs_wfg_tri_core.digest: Triangle/Ramp generator with variable peak phase and curve.
vs_wfg_tri_core.use_when: Generates triangle-to-ramp patterns with adjustable peak and curve. Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu, `Vsynth/menu/vs_menu.maxpat`); passes OpenGL textures and needs exactly one `vs_render` running in the patch. Inlets: Freq Modulation In / Control In; Phase Modulation In; Peak Phase Modulation In. Outlets: Texture Out; Inverted Texture Out. Control messages (to the leftmost inlet, as listed in its help file): enable [boolean] sync_lock [0 - 3] angle [0. - 360.] sync_invert [boolean] time [0 - 10] speed [-10. - 10.] freq [0. - 1000.] [0. - 10000.] fm [-1. - 1.] [-5. - 5.] peak_phase [0. - 1.] ppm [-0.5 - 0.5] phase [0. - 1.] pm [-1. - 1.] [-5. - 5.] curve [-1. - 1.] ppm_mode [boolean]. Added in v1.7. Vsynth by Kevin Kripper.

vs_xyz_disp.digest: Try directly in the Render's window!
vs_xyz_disp.use_when: Wraps a texture onto a 3D mesh and displaces it by brightness. Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu, `Vsynth/menu/vs_menu.maxpat`); passes OpenGL textures and needs exactly one `vs_render` running in the patch. Inlets: Texture In / Control In; Displacement & Brightness In. Outlets: Texture Out. Control messages (to the leftmost inlet, as listed in its help file): enable [boolean] aspect_rect [boolean] xdisp / ydisp / zdisp [-1. - 1.] brightness [toggle] draw_mode [0 - 6] shape [0 - 1] width [0. - 10.] // line and points rotatexyz $1 $2 $3 position $1 $2 $3 axes [boolean] // rgb axes bang / reset. Seven draw modes; position and rotation save with presets. Try it directly in the render window. Vsynth by Kevin Kripper.

vsc_angle_encoder.digest: These extra modules are meant to facilitate some controls and work with several modules. Here are just a few examples.
vsc_angle_encoder.use_when: Endless knob for setting angle or hue on Vsynth modules. Vsynth control helper (a bpatcher, pasted from the Vsynth clippings/menu) that sends control data, not textures. Inlets: none. Outlets: Angle / Hue Out. Outputs numbers to a module's control inlet. Vsynth by Kevin Kripper.

vsc_center_ctrl.digest: These extra modules are meant to facilitate some controls and work with several modules. Here are just a few examples.
vsc_center_ctrl.use_when: X/Y pad for setting the center point of Vsynth modules. Vsynth control helper (a bpatcher, pasted from the Vsynth clippings/menu) that sends control data, not textures. Inlets: Center In. Outlets: Center Out. Double-click resets. Used with vs_wfg_rad and vs_wfg_shapes. Vsynth by Kevin Kripper.

vsc_color_picker.digest: These extra modules are meant to facilitate some controls and work with several modules. Here are just a few examples.
vsc_color_picker.use_when: Color picker that sends colors to Vsynth modules. Vsynth control helper (a bpatcher, pasted from the Vsynth clippings/menu) that sends control data, not textures. Inlets: none. Outlets: Color Out. Vsynth by Kevin Kripper.

vsc_data_scope.digest: These extra modules are meant to facilitate some controls and work with several modules. Here are just a few examples.
vsc_data_scope.use_when: Plots control numbers over time, like a small data oscilloscope. Vsynth control helper (a bpatcher, pasted from the Vsynth clippings/menu) that sends control data, not textures. Inlets: Data In. Outlets: Data Out. Data passes through. Vsynth by Kevin Kripper.

vsc_freq_encoder.digest: These extra modules are meant to facilitate some controls and work with several modules. Here are just a few examples.
vsc_freq_encoder.use_when: Endless knob for setting frequency on Vsynth waveform generators. Vsynth control helper (a bpatcher, pasted from the Vsynth clippings/menu) that sends control data, not textures. Inlets: none. Outlets: Freq Out. Vsynth by Kevin Kripper.

vsc_presets.digest: 5) To force to read a specific file and preset at the beginning of a patch plug to the [preset] module a [loadbang] and a messege configured in this way.
vsc_presets.use_when: Stores, recalls and morphs Vsynth module settings as presets. Vsynth control helper (a bpatcher, pasted from the Vsynth clippings/menu) that sends control data, not textures. Inlets: unlabelled. Outlets: dumpout. Paste From > Vsynth/vs_presets.maxpat. Shift-click stores; write and read save a .json file. Excludes vs_render, vs_sources_main and vector_sosci. Can morph between presets. Vsynth by Kevin Kripper.

vsc_spacebang.digest: These extra modules are meant to facilitate some controls and work with several modules. Here are just a few examples.
vsc_spacebang.use_when: Sends bangs and 0/1 changes when the spacebar is pressed and released. Vsynth control helper (a bpatcher, pasted from the Vsynth clippings/menu) that sends control data, not textures. Inlets: Bang. Outlets: Bang; Zero->One; One->Zero. Vsynth by Kevin Kripper.

xray.diagonalize.digest: create a diagonal matrix from a row vector
xray.diagonalize.use_when: Turn a row-vector matrix into a square diagonal matrix: the input is made square using its width, and every cell off the diagonal is zeroed. A js script by Wesley Smith (XRAY), typed as `js xray.diagonalize.js`; 1 inlet (jit_matrix), 1 outlet. Use to rebuild the sigma vector from `xray.jit.svd` as a matrix before `jit.la.mult`. Note: XRAY keeps it in its jsextensions folder, and Max for the Visual Arts ships a different file with the same name.

xray.dynamicexpr.digest: jit.expr-like message extended to accept message substitutions
xray.dynamicexpr.use_when: Build `jit.expr` expressions with Max-style substitutions. First send `expr` followed by the plane expressions (quoted per plane, same rules as jit.expr's `expr` message, commas escaped); then send a list, and each `$1`, `$2`… (numbers or symbols) is filled in and output as an `expr …` message. Wire its outlet into `jit.expr`. A js script by Wesley Smith (XRAY), typed as `js xray.dynamicexpr.js`. Max for the Visual Arts ships a different file with the same name.

xray.jit.3dbuffer.digest: note: argument 6 is for giving the 3dbuffer a unique name so that more than one 3dbuffer object can be used without conflict.
xray.jit.3dbuffer.use_when: Circular multi-frame buffer: writes each incoming 2D matrix into successive slices of a named 3D `jit.matrix`, so recent frames can be read back as a time-delay stack. Arguments: planes, type, width, height, number of frames, buffer name (give each instance a unique name). Outlet reports the last written slice (the 3rd-dimension position) as a sync value. Read the stack with `xray.jit.timecube`, or pull one slice with `jit.matrix` using `usesrcdim`, `srcdimstart` and `srcdimend`. Abstraction by Wesley Smith (XRAY), based on a patch by Jeremy Bernstein.

xray.jit.cellcoords.digest: gives the coordinates corresponding to logical 1 of a 2D matrix. Useful when working with CV data as well.
xray.jit.cellcoords.use_when: Output the coordinates of every 'logical 1' cell of a 2D matrix (255 for char, 1 for long, 1. for float). Attributes: `plane` (which plane to look in), `out_mode` (0 long, 1 float32 output). Use after thresholding a camera image (`jit.op @op >`) to get point lists for drawing or tracking; pairs with `xray.jit.keepcell`. External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xray.jit.cellminmax.digest: scans a matrix bidirectionally and reports coordinates of first non-zero cell
xray.jit.cellminmax.use_when: Scan a 1-plane 2D matrix from both ends of each row (or column) and report the coordinates of the first non-zero cell from each side. Attribute `mode`: 0 horizontal scan (default), 1 vertical. Use to find silhouette edges of a thresholded image. External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xray.jit.cellvalue.digest: xray.jit.cellvalue is a support object for xray.jit.contourmap. It was createed to get the value of a cell that a contour line passes through.
xray.jit.cellvalue.use_when: Read the values of a matrix at an arbitrary list of cell coordinates. Left inlet: any 2D matrix; right inlet: 2-plane float32 matrix of coordinates. Output has the type and planecount of the left input and the dimensions of the coordinate list. Support object for `xray.jit.contourmap` (gets the value where a contour line passes). External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xray.jit.colormap.digest: xray.jit.colormap takes a standard video matrix and generates a colormap for use with jit.charmap for coloring grayscale images. In mode 0, all of the values of the incoming matrix a binned according to luminance accumulatively and then averaged to derive the colormap. In mode 1, only the first color value of a particular luminance is binned. In both modes, if there isn't a particular color value associated with a luminance bin, the map value is interpolated from the nearest existing values.
xray.jit.colormap.use_when: Build a 1D colour map, sorted by luminance, from a 4-plane char video matrix, for colouring grayscale images with `jit.charmap`. Attribute `mode`: 0 averages all colours in each luminance bin (default), 1 keeps the first colour found; empty bins are interpolated. External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xray.jit.contourmap.digest: 0: set isolevels based on levels attribute with each level equally spaced between the min and max of the surface
xray.jit.contourmap.use_when: Calculate the isolines (contour lines) of a 3D surface given as a 3-plane float32 matrix; draw the output with `jit.gl.mesh @draw_mode lines`. Attributes: `mode` 0 = `levels` evenly spaced isolevels between the surface min and max, 1 = use the `isolevel` list (up to 10 z values). External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xray.jit.crossproduct.digest: xray.jit.crossproduct can be replaced with a jit.gen patch
xray.jit.crossproduct.use_when: Cross product of two matrices of 3D vectors (3-plane float32 or float64), one in each inlet. Attribute `normalize` takes two values, each 0 or 1. The XRAY help itself says a `jit.gen` patch can replace it. External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xray.jit.cumsum.digest: accumulation of matrix values across a dimension
xray.jit.cumsum.use_when: Cumulative sum of float32/float64 matrix values along one dimension. Attribute `dimmode` picks the dimension to accumulate across. External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xray.jit.distance.digest: Takes 1-plane char and long matrices of any dimension
xray.jit.distance.use_when: Distance transform of a 1-plane char or long matrix: each cell gets its city-block (L1) distance to the nearest 'on' cell. Attribute `mode`: 0 horizontal passes only, 1 vertical only, 2 both (default, four passes). Threshold the image first (e.g. `jit.op @op < @val 127`). Use for glows, outlines and distance-based effects. External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xray.jit.grid2tri.digest: xray.jit.grid2tri can process both 3- and 2-plane matrices. This is so that texture coordinates can be mapped correctly to the surface after it undergoes the transformation into explicit triangles.
xray.jit.grid2tri.use_when: Convert a grid-shaped vertex matrix (2 or 3 planes) into an explicit triangle list so the triangulation order is known; render with `jit.gl.mesh @draw_mode triangles`. Use instead of `quad_grid`/`tri_grid` draw modes when you need control over how vertices are joined (e.g. for texture coordinates). External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xray.jit.invertrepos.digest: Since most repos maps aren't 1 to 1, some information is lost, which becomes evident after the inversion process.
xray.jit.invertrepos.use_when: Invert a `jit.repos` map in absolute mode, so a warp can be approximately undone. Input: 2-plane long repos map. Because most repos maps are not one-to-one, the inverse loses information. External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xray.jit.keepcell.digest: keeps only those pixels specified by the second inlet matrix
xray.jit.keepcell.use_when: Keep only the cells of the left-inlet matrix whose coordinates are listed in the right-inlet coordinate matrix; everything else is zeroed. Pairs with `xray.jit.cellcoords`. External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xray.jit.kmeans.digest: Vectors belonging to the same cluster have the same color with white spheres representing the centroid of the clusters.
xray.jit.kmeans.use_when: Cluster a 1-plane matrix of vectors with the k-means algorithm. Attributes: `clusters` (k, must be chosen in advance), `dimmode` (0 vectors are columns, 1 vectors are rows). 1 inlet, 4 outlets; the help draws clusters in colour with white spheres at the centroids. External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xray.jit.line2quad.digest: xray.jit.line2quad has 2 modes that calculate the quads differently. In mode 0, the calculation is done purely in 2 dimensions. This can give odd results for lines that don't exist in a single z-plane but is much faster than the 3D calculation. If each individual line is contained in a single z-plane, then this mode will give the exact same results as mode 1
xray.jit.line2quad.use_when: Convert a matrix of line segments into quads, so lines can be drawn with width via `jit.gl.mesh @draw_mode quads`. Attributes: `mode` 0 (2D, faster; exact if each line lies in one z-plane) or 1 (3D, homogeneous coordinates), `scale` (quad width and height), `normalize` (two values; makes all quads the same size regardless of line length — only the first applies in mode 1). External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xray.jit.mean.digest: takes 2D matrices of any type and outputs a 1xn or nx1 float32 or float64 matrix
xray.jit.mean.use_when: Mean (or sum) of each row or column of a 2D matrix of any type, output as a 1×n or n×1 float32 matrix (float64 for float64 input). Attributes: `meandim` (0 across dim 0, 1 across dim 1), `mean` (1 mean, default; 0 sum). External by Wesley Smith (XRAY). For a whole-matrix mean per plane use built-in `jit.3m`.

xray.jit.pinv.digest: The pseudo inverse of a matrix can be calculated from the Singular Value Decomposition of a matrix where svd(A) = U∑V^T. The pseudo inverse of A is then pinv(A)=V∑^-1U^T.
xray.jit.pinv.use_when: Pseudo-inverse of a matrix from its singular value decomposition: pinv(A) = V∑⁻¹Uᵀ. Three inlets take the U, ∑ and V outputs of `xray.jit.svd` (it does not compute the SVD itself); 1 outlet. Real 1- or 2-D float matrices. Abstraction by Wesley Smith (XRAY) built from `jit.la.mult`, `jit.op`, `jit.transpose`.

xray.jit.quicksort.digest: specifies the inital location to divide the data to be sorted. Negative values return to the default, values larger than the dimsize-1 are clipped. (default is (dimsize-1)/2)
xray.jit.quicksort.use_when: Sort a matrix of any type, dimension and planecount along rows or columns with quicksort. Attributes: `dimmode` (0 horizontal, 1 vertical), `planemode` (plane to sort by), `summode` (1 = sort by sum of planes), `splitpoint` (initial pivot), `iterations` and `recursions` (-1 = unlimited; lower values stop early for glitchy partial sorts). External by Wesley Smith (XRAY). Built-in `jit.bsort` is a bubble sort.

xray.jit.sift.digest: matrix must have at least the same width with siftdim 0 or same height with diftdim 1 as the input matrix, otherwise, the dimension can be arbitrary
xray.jit.sift.use_when: Keep only the rows or columns of the left-inlet matrix that are marked 'logic 1' in the right-inlet matrix (255 char, 1 long, 1. float). Attributes: `siftdim` (0 check the top row of the marker matrix → keep columns; 1 check the left column → keep rows), `siftplane` (marker plane to read). External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xray.jit.svd.digest: xray.jit.svd always outputs the matrices U, ∑, and V with the largest eignevalue and corresponding eigenvector in the left-most position and the rest in descending order.
xray.jit.svd.use_when: Singular value decomposition of a 1-plane 2D matrix of any type. For an m×n input it outputs U (n×m), ∑ as an n×1 vector of eigenvalues, and V (n×n), float32 or float64, largest value first. Use `xray.diagonalize` to turn ∑ into a matrix and `xray.jit.pinv` for the pseudo-inverse. External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xray.jit.timecube.digest: The left input can be a 3D matrix of any type and any planecoount. The right input matrix can be either 1-plane char or long (similar to jit.repos, but in time).
xray.jit.timecube.use_when: Read a 3D frame buffer (from `xray.jit.3dbuffer`) through time. Left inlet: 3D matrix of any type/planecount; right inlet (mode 2): 1-plane char or long map. Attribute `mode`: 0 vertical slices (Vasulka-style slit scan, default), 1 horizontal, 2 map mode (each map value picks the frame per pixel, like `jit.repos` in time; values beyond the `sync` range wrap). External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xray.jit.water.digest: xray.jit.water implements a finite element simulation of a water surface. The algorithm used was modified from:
xray.jit.water.use_when: Finite-difference simulation of a water surface in a float32 matrix. Requires feedback: use the same named `jit.matrix` at input and output. Right inlet: float or matrix of per-cell wave speed (shallow water = faster). Attributes: `damping`, `timestep`, `spacestep`. Make ripples by poking cells (`setcell x y val 0.5`) on the named matrix. Grids below about 100×100 are unstable. External by Wesley Smith (XRAY).

xy.attractors~.use_when: Generate chaotic x, y, z motion from strange attractors. Load one of seven gen~ codes: gen~ @gen xyz.lorenz, xyz.chen, xyz.dadras, xyz.fourwing, xyz.halvorsen, xyz.sprott or xyz.thomas; send x, y, z starting values and a speed. These are not typeable object names: the package ships gen~ code in code/*.gendsp and a matching clipping; the name here is its help file. All outputs are signals in the 0-1 range, suited to panning and MC patching.

xy.fm~.digest: xy.fm generates xy coordinates through the principles of fm synthesis
xy.fm~.use_when: Generate x/y coordinates using FM synthesis math (carrier frequency, modulator frequency, FM ratio). Load as gen~ @gen xy.fm; a decoding message sets the mode. These are not typeable object names: the package ships gen~ code in code/*.gendsp and a matching clipping; the name here is its help file. All outputs are signals in the 0-1 range, suited to panning and MC patching.

xy.galaxy~.digest: xy.galaxy distributes a specified number of voices in a circular space for use in MC-based patching
xy.galaxy~.use_when: Distribute many voices on rotating rings for multichannel spatialization, with rotation, distance, phase and spread controls, sample-and-hold and reverse-direction options. Load as mc.gen~ @gen xy.galaxy @chans <voices>; changing chans needs an audio restart. These are not typeable object names: the package ships gen~ code in code/*.gendsp and a matching clipping; the name here is its help file. All outputs are signals in the 0-1 range, suited to panning and MC patching.

xy.grains~.digest: set how much time will pass before a grain is re-triggered.  Every time a voice is triggered, its wait-time is picked randomly from the range selected
xy.grains~.use_when: Pseudo-random, self-retriggering grain positions: each voice waits a random time, then emits a windowed burst of x/y position with random length. Load as mc.gen~ @gen xy.grain @chans <voices>; set wait-time and length ranges, window shape, distance and rotation ratios. These are not typeable object names: the package ships gen~ code in code/*.gendsp and a matching clipping; the name here is its help file. All outputs are signals in the 0-1 range, suited to panning and MC patching.

xy.manual~.digest: xy.manual allows to controll manually the 2D distribution of each channel / optimised for MC implementation
xy.manual~.use_when: Set each channel's 2D position by hand, in cartesian or polar mode (phase and spread work in polar mode only). Load as mc.gen~ @gen xy.manual; the help drives it from a pictslider. These are not typeable object names: the package ships gen~ code in code/*.gendsp and a matching clipping; the name here is its help file. All outputs are signals in the 0-1 range, suited to panning and MC patching.

xy.mass~.digest: xy.mass generates xy coordinates using Forces and Newton’s Laws of Motion
xy.mass~.use_when: Generate 2D motion from mass, gravity and wind forces (Newton's laws). Load as gen~ @gen xy.mass. These are not typeable object names: the package ships gen~ code in code/*.gendsp and a matching clipping; the name here is its help file. All outputs are signals in the 0-1 range, suited to panning and MC patching.

xy.multi~.digest: xy.multi distributes a specified number of voices in a circular space for use in MC-based patching
xy.multi~.use_when: Distribute voices around a rotating circle for MC spatialization, with rotation, distance, phase, spread and deviate (random start position) controls. Load as mc.gen~ @gen xy.multi @chans <voices>; changing chans needs an audio restart. These are not typeable object names: the package ships gen~ code in code/*.gendsp and a matching clipping; the name here is its help file. All outputs are signals in the 0-1 range, suited to panning and MC patching.

xy.random~.use_when: Generate random x/y positions with an interpolation time in ms between them. Load as gen~ @gen xy.random; start with a toggle or trigger. These are not typeable object names: the package ships gen~ code in code/*.gendsp and a matching clipping; the name here is its help file. All outputs are signals in the 0-1 range, suited to panning and MC patching.

xy.sequencer~.digest: xy.sequencer generates xy coordinates for each step in sequence
xy.sequencer~.use_when: Step through stored x/y positions, one per step, with rate, step count, mode and interpolation controls. Load as gen~ @gen xy.sequencer4 (4 steps) or xy.sequencer8 (8 steps). These are not typeable object names: the package ships gen~ code in code/*.gendsp and a matching clipping; the name here is its help file. All outputs are signals in the 0-1 range, suited to panning and MC patching.

xy.wave~.digest: xy.wave uses a combination of waveforms to describe complex hamonic 2D motion
xy.wave~.use_when: Describe 2D motion by combining waveforms on x and y, each with its own frequency, amplitude and phase. Load as gen~ @gen xy.wave. These are not typeable object names: the package ships gen~ code in code/*.gendsp and a matching clipping; the name here is its help file. All outputs are signals in the 0-1 range, suited to panning and MC patching.

abc.2plf.ui.use_when: A two-line breakpoint editor with coloured points (three degrees of freedom); type `abc.2plf.ui` (bpatcher). `play <ms>` outputs lists shaped for `line`; `init` clears the points. Double-click adds a point on the thick line, option-double-click on the thin line. Three outlets. Works with `pattrstorage`.

abc.adcinput~.use_when: Mono microphone input with optional DC filter and gain; type `abc.adcinput~` and Max substitutes a bpatcher. Bpatcher arguments `@channel <n>`, `@gain <dB>`, `@dc-filter 0|1`; send 1 or 0 to switch it on or off.

abc.audiotester~.use_when: Check a speaker array by sending pink noise to each speaker in turn: `abc.audiotester~` into `mc.dac~ 1 2 … n`. Right-inlet messages: `nls <n>` (number of speakers, 1-64), `freq <Hz>` (how fast it steps), `gain <dB>`.

abc.cartopol~.use_when: Convert a 2-channel mc cartesian pair (x, y) into the polar pair abclib uses (angle in radians): `abc.cartopol~`, no arguments or control inlet. Typical use: `abc.map.ui` cartesian output, turned into signals, then `abc.cartopol~` into the right inlet of `mc.combine~ 2` ahead of `abc.hoa.map~`.

abc.delaychain~.digest: Abclib's sequential double overlapped delays without reinjection
abc.delaychain~.use_when: Chain 2-16 delay lines in series, each feeding the next, for rhythmic echo cascades: `abc.delaychain~ <n>`, output an n-channel mc cord (one tap per stage). Right-inlet messages: `dur<i>` in note values, `gain<i> <dB>`, `fdbk` (global loop), `tempo <bpm>`, `updatefreq <Hz>`.

abc.drops~.use_when: Synthesise rain drops: a periodic exciter into a resonant filter whose frequency wanders randomly. `abc.drops~`, no input. Right-inlet messages: `dropperiod <ms>`, `attackdur <ms>`, `avgfreq <Hz>`, `dropthinness`, `qf`, `gain <dB>`, `limiter 0|1`.

abc.dtd.ui.use_when: Draw per-harmonic delay and gain for `abc.hoa.decorrelation~ @mode man`; type `abc.dtd.ui` (bpatcher). Messages: `functiontype 0-22`, `factor 0.-1.`, `delay <samples>`, `channels <n>` (segments, one per circular harmonic). Its outputs feed `gain<i>`/`delay<i>` lists to the decorrelator. Works with `pattrstorage`.

abc.env.generator~.use_when: Internal helper — a refpage with no patcher or help file behind it; it duplicates `abc.env.noise~`'s description. Use `abc.env.noise~` instead.

abc.env.noise~.use_when: Enveloped noise grains with random dropouts; type `abc.env.noise~` and Max substitutes a bpatcher. Set initial values as bpatcher arguments: `@grainsize <ms>`, `@rarefaction 0.-1.`, `@gain <dB>`. Mono signal outlet.

abc.envfollower~.use_when: Follow the amplitude envelope of a signal at signal rate: `abc.envfollower~`, signal into the left inlet, `attack <s>` and `release <s>` into the right inlet.

abc.gaincontrol.use_when: A dB slider that outputs `gain <dB>` (-127 to 18) for abclib objects such as `abc.mc.gain~` and `abc.hoa.decoder~`; type `abc.gaincontrol` and Max substitutes a bpatcher. Initial value as bpatcher argument `@gain <dB>`. Connect to the target's rightmost inlet.

abc.generatorinterface~.digest: Abclib's GUI for simple multi-source generator
abc.generatorinterface~.use_when: A front panel for `abc.generator~` with on/off, frequency and pulse controls plus a meter; type `abc.generatorinterface~` and Max substitutes a bpatcher. One signal outlet.

abc.generator~.use_when: Pulsed test tones: sine, phasor and low-passed noise, each switchable and pulsed at its own rate. `abc.generator~`, no input. Right-inlet messages: `sinuson`, `phasoron`, `noiseon` (0|1), `sinusfreq`, `phasorfreq`, `noisecutoff` (Hz), `sinuspulserate`, `phasorpulserate`, `noisepulserate` (Hz), `sinuspulseratio`, `phasorpulseratio`, `noisepulseratio`, `gain <dB>`.

abc.gotoevent.use_when: Jump to event N of a mixed-music piece during rehearsal: type `abc.gotoevent` (bpatcher). Send the target event number to the left inlet and bang the right inlet; it switches DSP off, counts through events 0 to N, then restores the DSP state.

abc.hoa.binaural~.digest: Abclib's High Order Ambisonics (HOA) Binaural Decoder based on the code of P.Lecomte
abc.hoa.binaural~.use_when: Decode an ambisonic stream to headphones: `abc.hoa.binaural~ <order> @dimensions 2|3`, fed by any abc.hoa encoder/map/process at the same order. Uses P. Lecomte's decoder built on Neumann KU100 HRIRs. Right-inlet message: `gain <dB>`. Output is a 2-channel mc cord for `mc.live.gain~` or `mc.dac~`. Reach for it whenever the piece must be checked away from the speaker array; for plain stereo speakers use `abc.hoa.stereodecoder~`.

abc.hoa.decoder~.use_when: Decode an ambisonic mc stream to a loudspeaker ring or sphere: `abc.hoa.decoder~ <order> @speakers <n> @dimensions 2|3`. Default speaker count is 2N+2 (2D) or (N+1)^2 (3D); 2D takes 3-16 speakers, 3D 4-16. Input is one mc cord from an abc.hoa encoder/map/process at the same order; output is one mc cord of n channels for `mc.dac~`. Right-inlet messages: `gain <dB>` (-127 to 18), `a<i> <deg>` speaker angles (plus `e<i>` in 3D, as the help patch does), `angularoffset <deg>`, `directangles 0|1` (1 = anticlockwise, the ambisonic norm), `stereo 0|1` to fold the decoded field down to stereo, for checking a piece without the speaker array.

abc.hoa.decorrelation~.use_when: Spread or diffuse a field by delaying ambisonic components by different amounts: `abc.hoa.decorrelation~ <order> @mode fx|syn|man @dimensions 2|3`. fx processes an existing stream; syn builds a decorrelated stream from one mono input; man takes per-harmonic `gain<i>` and `delay<i>` lists from `abc.dtd.ui`. Right-inlet messages: `factor 0.-1.`, `delay <samples>` (max window), `fdbk`, `functiontype 0-21` (distribution curve), `distributionmode 0-2` (3D).

abc.hoa.delay~.use_when: Delay each ambisonic component by a different time: `abc.hoa.delay~ <order> @mode fx|syn`. Right-inlet messages: `deltime <ms>` or `deltime<i>`, `window <ms>` (maximum delay; used in the help patches though missing from the refpage), `feedback`, `factor 0.-1.`. syn mode spreads a mono input into delayed spatial components.

abc.hoa.encoder~.use_when: Encode 1-8 mono sources into an ambisonic stream: `abc.hoa.encoder~ <order> @sources <n> @dimensions 2|3`. With @sources 1 the input is a plain mono signal; with more sources feed one mc cord of n channels (e.g. `mc.combine~ 3`). Position each source by message to the right inlet: `a<i>` azimuth in degrees, `e<i>` elevation (3D), `s<i>` rotation speed in turns/s (2D), `sa<i>`/`se<i>` azimuth/elevation speeds (3D), `returntime` ms to glide back when speed returns to 0. Output is one mc cord of 2N+1 channels (2D) or (N+1)^2 (3D); send it to `abc.hoa.decoder~`, `abc.hoa.binaural~` or `abc.hoa.stereodecoder~` at the same order.

abc.hoa.grain~.use_when: Granulate ambisonic components separately: `abc.hoa.grain~ <order> @mode fx|syn`. Right-inlet messages: `grainsize <ms>`, `deltime <ms>`, `feedback 0.-1.`, `rarefaction 0.-1.` (1 = no grains). syn mode turns a mono input into a granular spatial field.

abc.hoa.map~.use_when: Encode sources that move in distance as well as angle: `abc.hoa.map~ <order> @sources <n>` (1-8). It has one inlet per source and no control inlet. Each inlet takes a 3-channel mc cord: the mono source plus a 2-channel polar position pair, built as `mc.combine~ 2` with the source in the left inlet and `abc.trajectories~`, `abc.pict2map` or `abc.cartopol~` in the right. Output is a 2N+1-channel stream for any abc.hoa decoder.

abc.hoa.mirror~.use_when: Mirror a 2D ambisonic field left/right: `abc.hoa.mirror~ <order>`, then `factor 1|0|-1` into the right inlet. The help and overview patches read 1 as the original field, 0 as original plus mirror, and -1 as the mirror alone.

abc.hoa.optim~.use_when: Apply a decoding optimisation before the decoder: `abc.hoa.optim~ <order> @dimensions 2|3`, then `optimtype 0|1|2` into the right inlet: 0 basic (no change), 1 maxRe for listeners near the centre, 2 inPhase for an audience spread across the whole circle. Insert it between encoder/map and decoder.

abc.hoa.ringmod~.digest: Abclib's High Order Ambisonics (HOA) Ring Modulation
abc.hoa.ringmod~.use_when: Ring-modulate ambisonic components at different frequencies for a spatialised modulation effect: `abc.hoa.ringmod~ <order> @mode fx|syn @dimensions 2|3`. Right-inlet messages: `f0 <Hz>` (maximum frequency), `factor 0.-1.`, `functiontype 0-21`, `distributionmode 0-2` (3D). fx processes a stream; syn builds one from a mono input.

abc.hoa.rotate~.use_when: Rotate a whole 2D ambisonic field: `abc.hoa.rotate~ <order>`. Right-inlet messages: `speed <turns/s>` for continuous rotation, `angle <deg>` for a fixed rotation when speed is 0, `returntime <ms>` to glide between the two. Input and output are the same 2N+1-channel stream.

abc.hoa.scope~.use_when: Visualise a 2D ambisonic stream: `abc.hoa.scope~ <order>` fed by the stream, output connected to an `abc.scopeembedded` (in-patch) or `abc.scope` (floating window) bpatcher. Right-inlet messages: `refresh <ms>`, `normalize 0|1`.

abc.hoa.stereodecoder~.digest: Abclib's 2D High Order Ambisonics (HOA) Stereo Decoder
abc.hoa.stereodecoder~.use_when: Decode a 2D ambisonic stream to two speakers: `abc.hoa.stereodecoder~ <order>`. Input is the mc stream at that order; output is a 2-channel mc cord for `mc.dac~`. Right-inlet messages: `gain <dB>`, `directangles 0|1`. Use it for a stereo mix of an ambisonic scene; use `abc.hoa.binaural~` for headphones and `abc.hoa.decoder~ @stereo 1` when the same decoder must switch between array and stereo.

abc.hoa.stereoencoder~.digest: Abclib's 2D High Order Ambisonics (HOA) Stereo Encoder
abc.hoa.stereoencoder~.use_when: Place a stereo source in a 2D ambisonic field as two encoded points: `abc.hoa.stereoencoder~ <order>`, input a 2-channel mc cord (e.g. `mc.combine~ 2`). Set the opening angle between the two points with `angle <deg>` into the right inlet (the help patch loads 60). Output is the 2N+1-channel ambisonic stream.

abc.hoa.wider~.use_when: Blur a localised ambisonic source outward: `abc.hoa.wider~ <order> @dimensions 2|3`, then `width 0.-1.` into the right inlet (0 point-like, 1 spread). Insert between encoder and decoder.

abc.jupiterbank~.digest: Abclib's synthesizer inspired by Manoury's Jupiter bank of oscillators
abc.jupiterbank~.use_when: A bank of 14 oscillators and 14 matching resonant filters, after Manoury's Jupiter: `abc.jupiterbank~` or `abc.jupiterbank~ @mode 2` (adds per-oscillator amplitude control `fa`). Right-inlet messages: `f0 <Hz>`, `k` (1 = harmonic, non-integers inharmonic), `osc2filter 0.-1.` (oscillators to filters, the filters ringing on the signal input), `resg`, `resq`, `gain <dB>`. Output is a 14-channel mc cord, one partial per channel.

abc.linedrive~.use_when: Map a 0-127 signal onto 0-outputmax along an exponential curve: `abc.linedrive~`, with `outputmax` and `expcurve` messages into the right inlet.

abc.map.ui.use_when: A jsui map of circles whose position, radius and opacity control processes; type `abc.map.ui` (bpatcher). Messages: `add <n>`, `del` or `del <indices>`, `mode cartesian|polar`, `precision`, `flip_axis`, `set_xy <i> <x> <y>`, `set_ad <i> <azim> <dist>`. The help patches read per-circle `/circle/<n>/pol` messages from outlet 0 and a flat list (x y radius opacity per circle) from outlet 1. Works with `pattrstorage`.

abc.mc.addsynth~.use_when: Additive synthesis with n partials, each a pair of detunable oscillators: `abc.mc.addsynth~ <n>` (1-16), no signal input, n-channel mc output. Right-inlet messages: `f0 <Hz>`, `gain <dB>`, `fmult<i>` (partial ratio), `amp<i> <dB>`, `fbeat<i> <Hz>` (beating offset of the second oscillator). Follow with `abc.mc.randenv~` and `abc.mc.chopan~` as the help patches do.

abc.mc.busmult~.use_when: Multiply two n-channel mc buses channel by channel (e.g. ring modulation or envelopes): `abc.mc.busmult~ <n>`, left bus into inlet 0, right bus into inlet 1. No control inlet.

abc.mc.busplus~.use_when: Add two n-channel mc buses channel by channel: `abc.mc.busplus~ <n>`, left bus into inlet 0, right bus into inlet 1. No control inlet.

abc.mc.busselect~.digest: Abclib's crossfaded selector of two buses
abc.mc.busselect~.use_when: Crossfade between two n-channel mc buses: `abc.mc.busselect~ <n> @ramp <ms>`. Left bus into inlet 0, right bus into inlet 1, and `leftOrRight 0|1` plus `ramp <ms>` into inlet 2.

abc.mc.chopan~.use_when: Spread N inputs across a stereo pair with Chowning's constant-energy panning: `abc.mc.chopan~ <n>` (1-16), input an n-channel mc cord, output a 2-channel mc cord. First input goes left, last right, others evenly between. Right-inlet messages: `phi0 <deg>` (stereo opening), `gain <dB>`, `incAngle <deg>` (only for `abc.mc.chopan~ 1`).

abc.mc.delay~.use_when: Run n parallel, click-free delay lines with feedback, timed in musical units: `abc.mc.delay~ <n>` (1-16), n-channel mc in and out. Right-inlet messages: `tempo <bpm>`, `dur<i>` (1 = quarter note, 0.5 = eighth), `gain<i> <dB>`, `fdbk<i>`, `updatefreq <Hz>` (how often durations may change without clicks). A semicolon message box such as `;dels dur0 0.5;dels fdbk0 0.4` into `[r dels]` sets many lines at once.

abc.mc.flanger~.use_when: Flange n channels with a sine LFO: `abc.mc.flanger~ <n>` (1-16). Right-inlet messages: `rate <Hz>`, `depth <ms>`, `offset <ms>`, `fdbk 0.-1.`, `spread 0.-1.` (0 all channels identical, 1 maximum spatial split).

abc.mc.freqshift~.use_when: Shift the frequency of n channels independently: `abc.mc.freqshift~ <n>` (1-16). Right-inlet messages: `fr<i> <Hz>` (positive or negative), `gain<i> <dB>`.

abc.mc.gain~.use_when: Set the level of every channel of an mc cord at once: `abc.mc.gain~ <n>` (1-16), then `gain <dB>` (-127 to 18) into the right inlet, typically from an `abc.gaincontrol` bpatcher.

abc.mc.grain~.use_when: Run n parallel delay-based granulators: `abc.mc.grain~ <n>` (1-16). Right-inlet messages: `gs<i> <ms>` grain size, `dt<i> <ms>` maximum delay, `fdbk<i>`, `rrf<i>` rarefaction (0 none, 1 silent).

abc.mc.harmo~.use_when: Pitch-shift n channels independently: `abc.mc.harmo~ <n>` (1-16). Right-inlet messages: `trans<i>` in midicents (100 = semitone up, -400 = major third down), `gain<i> <dB>`, `winsize<i>`.

abc.mc.matrix~.use_when: Mix n inputs to n outputs with gain coefficients from -1 to 1: `abc.mc.matrix~ <n>` (2-16), input and output one n-channel mc cord. Set a cell with `m<i> <coef>`, where the help patch builds the index as first*n + second; `ramp <ms>` sets the crossfade time for every change.

abc.mc.multinoise~.use_when: Produce n decorrelated white-noise channels: `abc.mc.multinoise~ <n>` (1-16), no input. Typical source for `abc.mc.substractsynth~` or for testing a speaker array.

abc.mc.pulsedenv2synth~.use_when: Make n channels of pulsed sine bursts: `abc.mc.pulsedenv2synth~ <n>`. Right-inlet messages: `carrierFreq <Hz>`, `envFreq <Hz>` (burst rate), `ratio` (silence to sound), `spread 0.-1.` (decorrelates envelopes across channels), `fc <Hz>` low-pass, `gain <dB>`.

abc.mc.randenv~.use_when: Apply random on/off envelopes to each channel of an mc cord: `abc.mc.randenv~ <n> @mode cosinus|linear` (1-16; `cos`, `lin`, `line` also accepted). Right-inlet messages: `freq <Hz>`, `rarefaction 0.-1.` (share of muted envelopes), `spread 0.-1.` (phase offset between channels). The standard way in abclib to make a static multichannel texture flicker.

abc.mc.substractsynth~.use_when: Subtractive synthesis with n band-pass filters on n noise inputs: `abc.mc.substractsynth~ <n>` (1-16), fed by e.g. `abc.mc.multinoise~ <n>`. Right-inlet messages: `f0 <Hz>`, `gain <dB>`, `filterQ`, `filterG`, `fmult<i>`, `amp<i> <dB>`.

abc.mult2pi~.use_when: Multiply a signal by 2*pi, e.g. to turn a `phasor~` ramp into an angle in radians for abclib position pairs. No arguments or control inlet.

abc.musdur.use_when: Pick a delay duration as a note value from a menu (whole, half, quarter, eighth, sixteenth, 32nd, triplet); type `abc.musdur` and Max substitutes a bpatcher, with the initial menu index as argument. Connect its outlet to a `dur<i> $1` message for `abc.mc.delay~` or `abc.delaychain~`.

abc.peakamp~.use_when: Output the peak absolute amplitude over a window as a signal: `abc.peakamp~ @period <ms>` (or `period` message into the right inlet).

abc.phasor2pi~.use_when: A ramp from 0 to 2*pi instead of 0 to 1, for driving angles in radians: `abc.phasor2pi~`, then `freq <Hz>` into the right inlet.

abc.pict2map.digest: Abclib's Graphic 2D control of a source position
abc.pict2map.use_when: Drag a point on a 2D pad to position one source for `abc.hoa.map~`; type `abc.pict2map` (bpatcher). Outputs a 2-channel mc polar pair; connect it to the right inlet of `mc.combine~ 2` with the source on the left. Floats into the left/right inlets set x/y; `reset` returns to the centre.

abc.poltocar~.use_when: Convert abclib's 2-channel mc polar pair back to cartesian x, y: `abc.poltocar~`, no arguments or control inlet. The help patches use it to draw a trajectory on an X-Y `scope~` after `mc.unpack~ 2`.

abc.puckettespaf~.use_when: Puckette's phase-aligned formant synthesis for vowel-like tones: `abc.puckettespaf~` or `abc.puckettespaf~ @mode 2` (adds inharmonic phase variation `ifreq`, `iamp`). Right-inlet messages: `f0 <Hz>`, `cf <Hz>` centre frequency, `bw <Hz>` bandwidth, `wf 0|1` (Gaussian or Cauchy shaping), `a` (Gaussian shape), `sigma` (Cauchy shape), `gain <dB>`.

abc.quadriout~.use_when: Four-channel output stage with gain and meters; type `abc.quadriout~` and Max substitutes a bpatcher. Bpatcher arguments: four output channel numbers then `@gain <dB>`, e.g. `1 2 3 4 @gain 0`. Input is one 4-channel mc cord.

abc.rev4~.use_when: A simple feedback-delay reverb in stereo or quad: `abc.rev4~` (stereo) or `abc.rev4~ @mode quadri`. Right-inlet messages: `revDur 0-127` (127 near-infinite), `revGain 0-127`. Input and output are mc cords of 2 or 4 channels.

abc.rissetsbell~.use_when: Risset's bell model on 11 oscillator/envelope layers: `abc.rissetsbell~ @dur <ms>`. Trigger with `gate 1` then `gate 0` into the right inlet. Other messages: `freq <Hz>`, `gain <dB>`, `osc2filter 0.-1.` (crossfade to band-pass filters on the signal input), `resg`, `resq`, and detune (`pfreq2` in the help patch and inside the external, `pfreq` in the refpage). Output is 11 channels.

abc.scope.digest: Abclib's Visualization of X-Y signals using Jitter
abc.scope.use_when: Draw X-Y signals from `abc.hoa.scope~` in a floating Jitter OpenGL window; type `abc.scope` (bpatcher). Inspector arguments: `@drawing-type`, `@size`, `@display 0|1`. Colour messages: `color-bg`, `color-pos`, `color-neg`, `color-circ` (r g b a), `reset-color`.

abc.scopeembedded.digest: Abclib's Visualization of X-Y signals using Jitter
abc.scopeembedded.use_when: Same display as `abc.scope` but drawn inside the bpatcher with a `jit.pwindow`; type `abc.scopeembedded`. Feed it from `abc.hoa.scope~`. Colour messages: `color-bg`, `color-pos`, `color-neg`, `color-circ`, `reset-color`.

abc.simplefmburst~.digest: Abclib's simple and short (110 ms) FM Synthesis
abc.simplefmburst~.use_when: A 110 ms FM burst (440 Hz carrier, 220 Hz modulator, index 5) triggered by bang; type `abc.simplefmburst~` and Max substitutes a bpatcher. Test source for delays and detectors.

abc.soundcoat~.use_when: A slowly changing noise texture from 16 band-pass filters whose gains drift randomly: `abc.soundcoat~`, no input. Right-inlet messages: `gain <dB>`, `randwin <ms>` (length of one randomisation cycle). Used throughout the abclib help patches as a test source.

abc.sounddetector~.use_when: Detect note attacks and releases in live sound: `abc.sounddetector~`, signal in. Output is a 3-channel mc cord: on/off envelope, attack pulses, release pulses (split with `mc.unpack~ 3`). Right-inlet messages: `noteOn <dB>` threshold, `noiseFloor <dB>`, `offset <dB>`, `noteDur`, `offDur`, `attack 0|1`, `tSlide`.

abc.soundgrain~.digest: Abclib's granulator on a rainstick sound
abc.soundgrain~.use_when: A ready-made granular texture on a looped rainstick recording: `abc.soundgrain~`. Messages into its inlet: `freqmult` (loop speed), `gain <dB>`. Mainly a test source in the help patches.

abc.stereoout~.use_when: Two-channel output stage: an mc cord in, a dB gain, meters and an `ezdac~` on/off button; type `abc.stereoout~` and Max substitutes a bpatcher. Initial gain as `@gain <dB>`.

abc.trajectories~.use_when: Generate a moving source position for `abc.hoa.map~`: `abc.trajectories~ @mode random|square|Z|squareZ|circular`. Output is a 2-channel mc polar pair; join it with the source using `mc.combine~ 2` (source left). Messages: `freq`, `size` (all but circular), `crossfade` (squareZ: 0 square, 1 Z), and for circular `ampRho`, `ampTheta`, `freqRho`, `freqTheta`, `rotSpeed`. Pass through `abc.poltocar~` only to draw the path on a `scope~`.

abc.vbap~.digest: Abclib's circular VBAP spatialization with irregular angles
abc.vbap~.use_when: Pan a mono source over a ring of 2-16 speakers at irregular angles with Pulkki's VBAP: `abc.vbap~ <speakers>`. Right-inlet messages: `a<i> <deg>` for each speaker angle, `theta <deg>` for the source angle. Output is one mc cord with a channel per speaker. Choose it over ambisonics for irregular layouts and a single source, where sharp speaker-to-speaker panning is wanted.

abc.vector~.digest: Abclib's Energy and Velocity Vectors computation
abc.vector~.use_when: Evaluate how well a speaker layout localises: `abc.vector~ <speakers> @dimensions 2|3` (4-16), fed by the decoder's speaker signals, with `a<i>` (and `e<i>` in 3D) speaker angles into the right inlet. Output is an mc cord of Gerzon velocity and energy vector coordinates (4 channels in 2D, 6 in 3D).

av.sync~.digest: Synchronize sound and visual recording in post production
av.sync~.use_when: Synchronize sound and visual recording in post production. av-toolbox audio/visual utility.

av.testpattern.use_when: Display a testpattern. av-toolbox audio/visual utility.

av.texture.digest: Initialize a jit.gl.texture with preset attributes
av.texture.use_when: Initialize a jit.gl.texture with preset attributes. av-toolbox audio/visual utility.

av.texturefolder.digest: Load a folder of images into named textures
av.texturefolder.use_when: Load a folder of images into named textures. av-toolbox audio/visual utility.

av.timepoint.digest: Bang at a specific time in min:sec:ms
av.timepoint.use_when: Bang at a specific time in min:sec:ms. av-toolbox audio/visual utility.

av.timetoticks.digest: Convert minutes, seconds, milliseconds to ticks
av.timetoticks.use_when: Convert minutes, seconds, milliseconds to ticks. av-toolbox audio/visual utility.

av.timetrigger~.use_when: Output a bang every min:sec:ms. av-toolbox audio/visual utility.

av.trigger~.digest: Output a bang when envelope crosses threshold
av.trigger~.use_when: Output a bang when envelope crosses threshold. av-toolbox audio/visual utility.

av.videogrid.digest: Place a videoplane on a segment of a grid
av.videogrid.use_when: Place a videoplane on a segment of a grid. av-toolbox audio/visual utility.

av.videoplane.digest: Initialize a jit.gl.videoplane with preset attributes
av.videoplane.use_when: Initialize a jit.gl.videoplane with preset attributes. av-toolbox audio/visual utility.

av.when.digest: Report current Transport time in min:sec:ms
av.when.use_when: Report current Transport time in min:sec:ms. av-toolbox audio/visual utility.

av.world.digest: Initialize a jit.world with preset attributes
av.world.use_when: Initialize a jit.world with preset attributes. av-toolbox audio/visual utility.

bach.+.use_when: llll addition — element-wise + with broadcasting. Constructor takes the right operand; left-inlet llll is the left operand. The bach version of `+` for nested data.

bach.abs.use_when: Element-wise absolute value of an llll.

bach.adj.digest: Compute the adjugate of a matrix
bach.adj.use_when: Adjugate of a matrix (matrix of cofactors transposed). For non-singular A, adj(A)/det(A) = inv(A). Right outlet bangs on non-square/ill-conditioned input.

bach.append.use_when: Deprecated: its help file says to use bach.join instead, which behaves the same. Joins lllls arriving at separate inlets into one llll; the argument sets the inlet count, @triggers picks the hot inlets, @inwrap and @outwrap add bracket levels.

bach.approx.digest: Snap pitches or MIDIcents to microtonal grid
bach.approx.use_when: Snap pitches or midicents to the nearest step of a microtonal grid. The right inlet or the argument sets the tone division (2 = semitones, 4 = quarter tones, 8 = eighth tones). Use bach.mcapprox when the data is midicents only.

bach.args.use_when: Subpatcher argument parser for bach. Parses positional args and `@key value` attribute pairs from the parent's `#1 #2 …` and emits them through dedicated outlets. `@attrs <list>` declares known attribute names. The bach analogue of `patcherargs`. Use at the top of every bach abstraction that takes args.

bach.arithmser.use_when: Generate an arithmetic series. Inlets (or arguments) are start, end, step and maximum number of items; bang or a number in the left inlet outputs the series. Use for index lists, evenly spaced onsets or pitch ramps.

bach.autoscale.use_when: Linearly rescale an llll automatically so its min and max become the supplied targets. Output min/max are constructor args. If all input values are equal, returns the mean of the targets to avoid divide-by-zero. Use for normalization where you don't yet know the input range.

bach.bachtree2omtree.digest: Convert a bach rhythmic tree into an OpenMusic rhythmic tree
bach.bachtree2omtree.use_when: Convert a bach rhythmic tree to OpenMusic rhythmic tree format. Use for bach↔OM interop.

bach.beatbox.digest: Box voice-wise parameters into measure-wise information
bach.beatbox.use_when: Box plain voice-wise data into measure-wise structure — adds the measure paren level required by bach.score. Constructor `separate` flag for the separate-syntax form. Use after building a long flat sequence and you want it metrically parsed.

bach.beatunbox.digest: Flatten measure-wise parameters into plain voice-wise information
bach.beatunbox.use_when: Inverse of bach.beatbox — flatten measure-structured data back to plain voice-wise. `@merge 1` rejoins tied notes. Use after dumping a bach.score and you want to operate on the flat representation.

bach.belong.digest: Tell if some elements belong to a llll
bach.belong.use_when: Test whether all elements received in the left inlet occur in the llll stored in the middle inlet (or the argument). Outputs a single 1 or 0, not a per-element mask. For a custom equality test, set up a lambda loop on the two rightmost outlets and the right inlet.

bach.bin.use_when: Binomial coefficient `C(n, k)` — `bin 5 2 = 10`. Use for probability work, combinatorial counting, or Pascal-triangle generation.

bach.bitdecode.use_when: Decode which bits are on in an integer: send an int, get the list of active bit indices. Use for unpacking flag values such as the bitfield from bach.contains.

bach.cartesianprod.use_when: Cartesian product of N input lllls — generates every combination. Use for parameter-sweep generation, search-space enumeration. Caution: output size grows multiplicatively.

bach.cartopol.digest: Cartesian to polar coordinate conversion for lllls
bach.cartopol.use_when: Convert Cartesian to polar coordinates on whole lllls: x (real) values in the left inlet, y (imaginary) values in the right inlet. Left outlet gives amplitudes (radii), right outlet phases in radians. Pairs with bach.fft output.

bach.change.digest: Filter out repetitions of an llll
bach.change.use_when: Filter out repetitions — only emit the input llll if it differs from the previous. Like Max's `change` for nested data. Use upstream of expensive operations to avoid recomputation when nothing changed.

bach.chordrev.digest: Reverse the non-rest elements of an llll
bach.chordrev.use_when: Reverse the non-rest elements of an llll, preserving rest positions. Use for retrograde transformations that ignore rests.

bach.chordrot.digest: Rotate the non-rest elements of an llll
bach.chordrot.use_when: Rotate the non-rest elements (preserves rest positions). Companion to bach.chordrev.

bach.circle.use_when: Clock-diagram visualization — display a pc-set as points on a circle (octave divided by `@modulo`, default 12). Selection at outlets emits the highlighted subset. Use for pedagogy and interactive set-class exploration.

bach.classify.use_when: Group the elements of an llll into classes of equal items; output is an llll of sublists. Equality defaults to exact match (@matchtype decides whether 1.5 and 3/2 count as equal). For a custom test, use the lambda loop or the @lambda attribute with a bell expression.

bach.clip.digest: Limit elements of lllls within a certain range
bach.clip.use_when: Clip elements to a [min, max] range. Right inlet (or args) sets bounds. Vectorized over nested structure.

bach.collect.use_when: Build lllls from streamed data: send elements to the middle inlet, then bang the left inlet to output. The right inlet manages structure with messages such as clear, clearall, back, top, size and collection. The argument sets the number of parallel collectors. Standard partner of bach.iter for iterate-and-rebuild patterns.

bach.comb.use_when: Combinations — all `C(n, k)` k-element subsets of an llll. Use for combinatorial enumeration in voice-leading or set-theory.

bach.combinevoices.digest: Combine voices into a new bach.roll or bach.score
bach.combinevoices.use_when: Combine multiple voices into a single bach.roll/bach.score. Use to assemble a multi-voice piece from independently-generated parts.

bach.compl.digest: Find complement of a pitch-class set
bach.compl.use_when: Pitch-class set complement — given a set, returns the pc-set containing all pitch-classes not in it. `@modulo` (default 12) sets the universe size for microtonal work.

bach.constraints.use_when: Constraint satisfaction problem solver. Variables, domains, and constraints expressed declaratively; lambda inlet supplies per-constraint test. `@solutions` caps result count; `@maxtime` limits CPU; `@parallel` enables concurrent search; `@minscore`/`@maxscore`/`@goalscore` for soft constraints. Use for voice-leading puzzles, twelve-tone row generation, harmonic completion problems — anything where a solution must satisfy multiple criteria simultaneously.

bach.contains.use_when: Report which data types an llll contains (numbers, rationals, symbols, sublists and so on): left outlet a bitfield, right outlet type names. Not a membership test; use bach.find or bach.belong for that. @mindepth and @maxdepth limit the depth range.

bach.convertbase.use_when: Convert numbers from one base to another, such as decimal to binary. Set bases with @startbase and @endbase (or the two arguments). Left outlet gives the number, right outlet its digits; @maxdecimals limits fractional digits.

bach.coprime.use_when: Coprimality test — boolean. `coprime 4 9 = 1`. Use upstream of bach.coprimeser for filtering, or in twelve-tone work where coprime-to-modulus matters.

bach.coprimeser.use_when: List all numbers M smaller than N that are coprime with N (share no divisor with it). Send N as an int. For N = 12 this gives the pitch-class multipliers 1 5 7 11.

bach.counter.use_when: Multi-index counter, like a multi-digit odometer: each index counts between its own minimum and maximum. Argument sets the number of indices. Bang or inc/dec to step; inlets 2 to 4 set direction, minima and maxima. Outlets give the current indices, underflow, overflow, local carry and global carry. @strictly forces strictly increasing or decreasing indices.

bach.cross.digest: Compute the cross product of two lllls
bach.cross.use_when: Vector cross product — 3-element vectors only. Returns a vector perpendicular to both inputs. Use for spatial control patches and 3D geometric algebra.

bach.defer.digest: Put an llll at the front of the low-priority queue
bach.defer.use_when: Defer-scheduled message passing — like Max's `defer` but for lllls. Use to break high-priority recursion in lambda chains (rare; usually you don't want this in a lambda — see package_concepts.md).

bach.deferlow.digest: Put an llll at the tail of the low-priority queue
bach.deferlow.use_when: Low-priority deferred message passing — schedule a Max message at low priority. Useful at the top of patcher init to avoid blocking the audio thread.

bach.delace.use_when: Inverse of bach.lace — split an interleaved llll into N separate streams.

bach.depth.use_when: Maximum nesting depth of an llll. `0` = empty `()`; `1` = flat list; `2+` = nested. Use to branch logic on whether an input is flat or nested.

bach.derive.use_when: Numerical derivative of an llll (treated as a sampled function). Useful for slope/velocity extraction from envelope data.

bach.det.digest: Compute the determinant of a matrix
bach.det.use_when: Matrix determinant. Use to test invertibility (det = 0 → singular) before bach.inv, or to compute volume scaling under a linear map.

bach.diag.use_when: Build a square matrix llll with the incoming llll on its diagonal and zeros elsewhere. @shift moves the diagonal above or below the main one.

bach.dict2llll.digest: Convert a dictionary into an llll
bach.dict2llll.use_when: Convert a Max dict to an llll. Use to bridge dict-based JSON workflows into bach's nested-list world.

bach.diff.use_when: Set difference: output the elements of the left-inlet llll that are not in the middle-inlet llll. For elements in either but not both use bach.symdiff; for differences between neighbors use bach.x2dx. Custom equality via the lambda loop or @lambda.

bach.divisors.use_when: All divisors of N as an llll — `divisors 12 = (1 2 3 4 6 12)`. Use for tuplet-decomposition or rhythmic-grid alternatives.

bach.dl2curve.digest: Convert a duration line into pitch and velocity curve~ messages
bach.dl2curve.use_when: Turn a note's duration line (the pitch glissando drawn in bach.roll or bach.score) into messages for two curve~ objects, one for pitch and one for velocity. Inlets take base pitch in midicents, base velocity, duration in ms and pitch breakpoints; usually fed from bach.playkeys or bach.unpacknote output.

bach.dl2line.digest: Convert a duration line into pitch and velocity line~ messages
bach.dl2line.use_when: Turn a note's duration line (the pitch glissando drawn in bach.roll or bach.score) into messages for two line~ objects, pitch and velocity. Same inlets as bach.dl2curve but segment curvature is ignored.

bach.drip.digest: Automatically step through lllls with delays
bach.drip.use_when: Output the elements of an llll one at a time on a timer: send the llll to the left inlet, set the interval in ms in the right inlet or argument. Outlets give each element, its address, and a bang when done. stop halts it; @circular loops; @maxdepth and @unwrap control nesting. For bang-driven stepping use bach.step.

bach.dsort.use_when: Sort numbers by their distance from a reference number, nearest first. Reference comes in the right inlet or argument; right outlet gives the sorted indices. Useful for picking the closest pitches to a target.

bach.dx2x.use_when: Convert a delta-list to absolute values — `(0.5 0.25 0.25) → (0.5 0.75 1.0)`. Common rhythm-domain operation: durations to onsets.

bach.eig.use_when: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a matrix. Use for spectral analysis of correlation matrices, modal-analysis applications.

bach.enharm.use_when: Respell pitches enharmonically. Right inlet or argument is a number of diatonic steps to shift the spelling, or the symbol auto for automatic respelling. Works on bach pitch lllls such as those from bach.mc2p.

bach.eq.use_when: Compare two whole lllls for equality: output 1 if identical, else 0. It is not element-wise. The argument sets a default comparison llll for the right inlet. @matchtype 1 makes 1.5 and 3/2 count as different. Also typed as bach.==.

bach.eval.use_when: Evaluator for the **bell** scripting language — Lisp-flavoured embedded language with variables, conditionals, loops, user-defined functions, and lambdas. Code in via the inlet, message box, or `@file <path.bell>`; outputs on `directouts`/`extraoutlets` configured at construction. Use when a chain of bach objects gets long enough that maintaining cords is harder than maintaining a script. See package_concepts.md for the bell language overview.

bach.expr.use_when: Evaluate a math expression element by element over lllls, like vexpr for nested data. Type the expression as the argument with numbered variables: $i1 integers, $f1 floats, $r1 rationals, $p1 pitches, $x1 any type, $s1 symbols; each variable number adds an inlet (@maxvars forces the count). Division of integers gives exact rationals. The expr message changes the expression. @scalarmode 1 lets a single number apply to every element of the other lllls.

bach.extractbasis.use_when: Extract a basis (linearly independent subset) from a set of vectors.

bach.ezmidiplay.use_when: Easy MIDI playback — connect a bach.roll/bach.score directly to a MIDI port for quick monitoring. Lighter than bach.playkeys when you just want to hear what you've written.

bach.f2mc.use_when: Frequency (Hz) → midicents. Use for analysis output where you have spectral peaks in Hz and need to plug them into bach's pitch domain.

bach.fact.use_when: Compute the factorial of an integer N. The right outlet bangs if the result overflows.

bach.factorize.use_when: Prime factorization — `12 → (2 2 3)`. Useful for tuplet-decomposition logic.

bach.fft.use_when: FFT over an llll of samples. `@inv 1` for inverse. Use for spectral analysis of any numeric llll, not just audio buffers.

bach.filter.digest: Only let specified data types through
bach.filter.use_when: Route data by type: anything whose type is in the accepted list goes out the left outlet, the rest goes out the right. Set the accepted types in the right inlet or argument. Useful in lambda loops that must treat numbers and sublists differently.

bach.filternull.use_when: Drop null/empty lllls — lets through every non-empty input. Use to scrub `()` from a stream.

bach.find.use_when: Search an llll for elements or sequences: compare against the llll in the middle inlet (or argument), or decide with a lambda loop on the rightmost outlet and inlet. Outlets give the matches and their addresses. @op selects a comparison operator; @maxcount limits results; @mindepth, @maxdepth, @minidx, @maxidx and @recursive limit the search. Set @out t to send readable text to ordinary Max objects.

bach.flat.digest: Decrease the depth of an llll
bach.flat.use_when: Remove bracket levels from an llll. The argument gives how many levels to remove; @minlevel and @maxlevel pick which levels. Use before sending nested data to objects that expect flat lists. Set @out t to send readable text to ordinary Max objects.

bach.float2rat.digest: Approximate a floating point number with a rational number
bach.float2rat.use_when: Approximate decimal numbers with fractions, for recovering exact rhythmic values. @maxden sets the largest denominator, @tolerance the allowed error, @algorithm the method. Right outlet gives the errors.

bach.fromc&r.use_when: Reassemble an llll from the chord (non-rest) elements, the rest elements and the rest positions produced by bach.toc&r. The name means chords and rests, not Lisp car/cdr.

bach.funnel.use_when: Index the elements of one llll: each element becomes a sublist starting with an increasing number. @offset sets the first index (default 1) and @step the increment. The llll version of listfunnel.

bach.gausselim.use_when: Gaussian elimination — row-reduce a matrix to row-echelon form. Use for solving linear systems by hand or for educational visualization.

bach.gcd.use_when: Greatest common divisor — element-wise across an llll. Use for finding the unit cell of a rhythmic pattern.

bach.geomser.use_when: Generate a geometric series — multiplicative analogue of bach.arithmser. Use for log-spaced grids, equal-tempered tunings (frequencies in geometric progression).

bach.geq.digest: Compare two lllls for greater than or equal condition
bach.geq.use_when: Test whether the left llll is greater than or equal to the right llll. It compares two whole lllls and outputs one 1 or 0; it is not element-wise. lllls compare lexicographically: elements are compared in parallel and the first difference decides; numbers compare by value, symbols alphabetically, numbers < symbols < sublists, and a longer llll wins a tie. The argument sets a default comparison llll for the right inlet. Also typed as bach.>=.

bach.getcol.digest: Get a column of a matrix
bach.getcol.use_when: Extract column j from a 2D matrix-shaped llll. Right inlet sets the column index.

bach.getrow.digest: Get a row of a matrix
bach.getrow.use_when: Extract row i from a 2D matrix-shaped llll. Right inlet sets the row index. Companion to bach.getcol.

bach.graph.use_when: Plot mathematical expressions as a graph: set the formula with expr (exprx, expry and exprr also exist for other graph types, see @graphtype), send parameters to the right inlet, bang to draw. Axes range via @minx, @maxx, @miny, @maxy; @numpoints sets resolution. Left outlet dumps x y pairs. It plots functions, not lllls.

bach.group.use_when: Split an llll into consecutive sublists of regular size. @count (or argument) sets the size or a repeating size pattern; @overlap sets how many elements neighboring groups share.

bach.gt.digest: Compare two lllls for greater than condition
bach.gt.use_when: Test whether the left llll is greater than the right llll. It compares two whole lllls and outputs one 1 or 0; it is not element-wise. lllls compare lexicographically: elements are compared in parallel and the first difference decides; numbers compare by value, symbols alphabetically, numbers < symbols < sublists, and a longer llll wins a tie. The argument sets a default comparison llll for the right inlet. Also typed as bach.>.

bach.histo.use_when: Count how often each value occurs in an llll. Inlets 2 and 3 (or arguments) set the minimum and maximum integer values to count, or auto. Left outlet gives the counts, right outlet the matching values.

bach.hypercomment.use_when: A comment box whose linked words can be clicked. @linkstart sets the character that marks a link (dropped from output with @drop), @sendto sends clicked links to a receive name, @hyperlinkcolor and @underline style them. Use for clickable navigation in help or teaching patches.

bach.idmatrix.use_when: Identity matrix of size N — N x N matrix with 1s on the diagonal and 0s elsewhere. Use as the multiplicative identity in linear-algebra chains.

bach.idvector.use_when: Identity vector — basis vector e_i (1 in position i, 0 elsewhere).

bach.ifunc.digest: Compute interval function of two pitch-class sets
bach.ifunc.use_when: Compute the interval function of two pitch-class sets: for each interval k, how many pairs (a from set A, b from set B) are k steps apart. Set A left, set B middle, modulo right (default 12).

bach.im.digest: Find the image of a matrix
bach.im.use_when: Image (column space) of a matrix — basis for the span of A's columns. Use for linear-algebra dimensionality analysis.

bach.insert.use_when: Insert elements at specific addresses without overwriting — like bach.subs but additive. `@multi` enables multiple insertions per call. Use when you need to splice into an existing structure; use bach.subs for replace-in-place.

bach.integrate.use_when: Numerical integral (cumulative sum) of an llll. The inverse of bach.derive on smooth signals.

bach.interp.use_when: Generate a series of lllls stepping from a starting llll to an ending llll. Inlets: number of interpolation points, interpolation exponent (1 = linear), starting llll, ending llll. Output is one llll containing all steps.

bach.intersection.use_when: Intersection of two lllls / two pc-sets.

bach.inv.digest: Find the inverse of a matrix
bach.inv.use_when: Matrix inverse — A^-1. Right outlet bangs on singular input (use bach.det first to check). Companion to bach.adj for educational visualization of the formula adj(A)/det(A).

bach.is.use_when: Type-check an element — outputs class name (int, float, sym, llll, rational, pitch). Use as a dispatch lookahead in bach.eval/bach.expr chains where you need to branch on element type.

bach.istruct.digest: Get the interval structure pitch-class set
bach.istruct.use_when: Report the interval structure of a pitch-class set: the distances between consecutive pitch classes around the circle. Right inlet or argument sets the modulo; @autosort sorts the set first.

bach.iter.use_when: Iterate through an llll depth-first, one element at a time: left outlet element, middle outlet address, right outlet depth changes. Argument sets how many lllls iterate in parallel. @maxdepth limits depth, @unwrap removes brackets, @iterationmode handles unequal lengths, @scalarmode lets a single value pair with every element. With @lambda 1, sublists are proposed on the right outlet and entered only if 1 comes back in the right inlet; stop halts. Pair with bach.collect to rebuild.

bach.ivec.digest: Compute the interval vector of a pitch-class set
bach.ivec.use_when: Compute the interval vector of a pitch-class set (how many of each interval class it contains); set the subsets cardinality (argument or @subsetscardinality) for a multi-interval vector (k-deck). Right inlet or @modulo sets the modulo; @group and @mode choose the prime-form rules.

bach.join.use_when: Join lllls arriving at several inlets into one llll, in inlet order. Argument sets the number of inlets. @triggers chooses the hot inlets (-1 = all), @inwrap and @outwrap add bracket levels. Replaces the deprecated bach.append. Set @out t to send readable text to ordinary Max objects.

bach.ker.digest: Find the kernel of a matrix
bach.ker.use_when: Kernel (null space) of a matrix — basis for vectors x with Ax = 0. Use for solving homogeneous systems.

bach.keychain.use_when: Organize the elements of an llll under keys: each element is sent out the lambda outlet, you return a key in the lambda inlet, and the output groups elements by key. Pairs with bach.keys for reading the result.

bach.keys.digest: Route an llll according to specific keys
bach.keys.use_when: Route keyed sublists (sublists whose first element is a key) to outlets: type the keys as arguments, one outlet each plus a final outlet that bangs when nothing matches. @keep 1 keeps the key in the output; @nullmode 1 outputs null for missing keys. The standard way to pull named sections out of a bach.roll or bach.score dump. Port count depends on the arguments.

bach.kurtosis.digest: Find the kurtosis of the numbers in an llll
bach.kurtosis.use_when: Statistical kurtosis — fourth central moment, normalised. Use for tail-heaviness analysis (peakedness vs uniformity).

bach.lace.use_when: Interleave several lllls element by element, round-robin. The argument sets the number of inlets. @iterationmode decides what happens with unequal lengths (stop at shortest, longest, or pad).

bach.lcm.use_when: Least common multiple — element-wise across an llll. Use for finding common rhythmic periods (durations that align cyclically).

bach.length.use_when: Count the elements at the root level of an llll; sublists count as one element each. No attributes. Pair with bach.depth for nesting.

bach.leq.digest: Compare two lllls for less than or equal condition
bach.leq.use_when: Test whether the left llll is less than or equal to the right llll. It compares two whole lllls and outputs one 1 or 0; it is not element-wise. lllls compare lexicographically: elements are compared in parallel and the first difference decides; numbers compare by value, symbols alphabetically, numbers < symbols < sublists, and a longer llll wins a tie. The argument sets a default comparison llll for the right inlet. Also typed as bach.<=.

bach.linearsolve.digest: Solve a linear system of equations
bach.linearsolve.use_when: Solve the linear system Ax = b: matrix A in the left inlet, column vector b in the right. Left outlet gives x when a unique solution exists; right outlet reports the number of solutions.

bach.llll2dict.digest: Convert an llll into a dictionary
bach.llll2dict.use_when: Convert an llll to a Max dict. Use to export bach data into dict consumers (jit.cellblock-via-dict, JSON output, web APIs).

bach.locate.use_when: Return the address of the first occurrence of an element or sequence: llll to find in the left inlet, llll to search in the right inlet (or argument). @mindepth, @maxdepth, @minidx and @maxidx limit the search. For all matches use bach.find.

bach.lookup.digest: Return specific elements of an llll (inlets reversed)
bach.lookup.use_when: Retrieve elements by address like bach.nth, but with inlets swapped: address in the left (hot) inlet, source llll in the right inlet or argument. Use it as a lookup table driven by incoming indices. @unwrap and @nils as in bach.nth.

bach.lt.digest: Compare two lllls for less than condition
bach.lt.use_when: Test whether the left llll is less than the right llll. It compares two whole lllls and outputs one 1 or 0; it is not element-wise. lllls compare lexicographically: elements are compared in parallel and the first difference decides; numbers compare by value, symbols alphabetically, numbers < symbols < sublists, and a longer llll wins a tie. The argument sets a default comparison llll for the right inlet. Also typed as bach.<.

bach.m2jitcellblock.digest: Display the content of an llll matrix in a jit.cellblock
bach.m2jitcellblock.use_when: Bach matrix → jit.cellblock conversion. Use to display matrix-shaped lllls in a cellblock UI.

bach.m2matrixctrl.digest: Format an llll matrix to be used with matrixctrl or matrix~
bach.m2matrixctrl.use_when: Bach matrix → matrixctrl conversion. Use for matrix-style UI control rendering.

bach.mapchord.use_when: Apply a function (lambda) per chord in a score-shaped llll. Lambda outlet emits one chord at a time. Score-aware analogue of bach.mapelem.

bach.mapelem.use_when: Map a transformation across every element of an llll — bach's `map`. Send the llll to the left inlet; each element exits the lambda outlet, your wired chain transforms it, and the modified value comes back at the lambda inlet. Final transformed llll exits the left outlet. `@unwrap 1` strips/restores the outermost paren level so each lambda iteration sees a flat list (often what you want). `@maxdepth` limits recursion. The lambda chain must be synchronous — no `pipe`/`delay`/`defer`. Use this whenever you'd reach for `map(fn, list)` in a real language.

bach.matrixctrl2m.digest: Convert a matrixctrl object into an llll matrix
bach.matrixctrl2m.use_when: Inverse — read matrixctrl state back into a bach matrix llll.

bach.maximum.use_when: Compare two lllls element by element and keep the larger value at each position. Right operand from the right inlet or argument. It does not find the largest element of one llll; use bach.minmax for that.

bach.mc2f.use_when: Midicents → frequency (Hz). Use to drive oscillators/sample players from bach pitch data.

bach.mc2n.use_when: Convert midicents into note names such as C4 or Do4. @notenamesstyle picks Anglo-Saxon or Latin names, @octave adds the octave number, @tonedivision sets microtonal accuracy, @accidentalspreferences picks sharps or flats. Inverse of bach.n2mc; for bach pitch values use bach.mc2p.

bach.mc2p.use_when: Convert midicents → pitch llll. Snaps to the current microtonal grid (`@tonedivision`) for symbolic display. Use after pitch-domain arithmetic to get back human-readable pitch names. Lossy if the value isn't on the grid.

bach.mc2pc.use_when: Midicents → pitch-class — modulo the octave. Strips octave information.

bach.mc2r.use_when: Midicents → pitch ratio. Inverse of bach.r2mc.

bach.mcapprox.use_when: Snap midicents to the nearest step of a microtonal grid across the full range; tone division in the right inlet (2 = semitones, 4 = quarter tones). Use bach.approx when the data may be pitches.

bach.mean.digest: Find the mean of the numbers in an llll
