cv.jit.covariance.use_when: Covariance matrix of a vector. n-element input → n×n covariance matrix output. Use for statistical pattern analysis or feeding shape descriptors into ML pipelines.

cv.jit.dilate.digest: Switch between binary and greyscale mode using grayscale attribute. Works also with "greyscale" spelling!
cv.jit.dilate.use_when: Morphological dilation. `@grayscale 0/1` (also accepts 'greyscale' spelling) switches between binary and greyscale modes. Use to grow ON regions / fill small gaps / make foreground objects larger.

cv.jit.direction.digest: cv.jit.direction: calculate main axis of image
cv.jit.direction.use_when: Calculate the main-axis direction of an image (or blob). `flip` attribute toggles whether the axis points toward the lighter side (like a pointing hand) or the heavier side (like a tail). Use for whole-image directional analysis; for per-blob use cv.jit.blobs.direction.

cv.jit.elongation.digest: cv.jit.elongation receives moments of inertia calculated by cv.jit.moments and computes the elongation of the shape. Elongation quantifies how thin a shape is. High values correspond to thin shapes, like lines, where pixels are grouped close to the main axis (as cv.jit.orientation calculates). On the other hand, the closer elongation is to 0, the more the shape is spread out, like a circle.
cv.jit.elongation.use_when: Whole-image elongation from cv.jit.moments output. Quantifies how thin a shape is. Use to characterise overall image shape with one number; for per-blob use cv.jit.blobs.elongation.

cv.jit.erode.digest: Switch between binary and greyscale mode using grayscale attribute. Works also with "greyscale" spelling!
cv.jit.erode.use_when: Morphological erosion. `@grayscale 0/1` (also accepts 'greyscale') switches modes. Use to shrink ON regions / remove small noise pixels / detach touching objects.

cv.jit.extrema.digest: cv.jit.extrema object is utilized by the cv.jit.hough2lines abstraction
cv.jit.extrema.use_when: Find local extrema in a matrix. Used internally by cv.jit.hough2lines. Use for general peak detection in 2D data — feature points, blob centres, line votes in Hough space.

cv.jit.face.landmarks.digest: The output matrix has 1 row for each face in the image. Each row has 68 columns, with each cell holding the coordinates of the 68 facial landmarks.
cv.jit.face.landmarks.use_when: 68-point facial landmark detector. Output matrix has 1 row per face × 68 columns per landmark (x, y coords). `@normalize` (default 1) scales coords to [0, 1]. Use after cv.jit.faces (or independently if you have face crops) to get detailed face geometry; feed to cv.jit.face.parts for per-feature subsets.

cv.jit.face.parts.digest: This should be connected to the output of cv.jit.face.landmarks.
cv.jit.face.parts.use_when: Slices cv.jit.face.landmarks output into 9 per-feature outlets (eyes, brows, nose, mouth, jawline, etc.). Use to extract just the parts you need — e.g. only lips for lip-sync, only eyes for gaze tracking.

cv.jit.face.rigidpoints.digest: This abstraction filters the data of cv.jit.face.landmarks to only return a few useful "rigid" points. That is, points that should not move regardless of the facial expression.
cv.jit.face.rigidpoints.use_when: Filter cv.jit.face.landmarks down to the 'rigid' points that don't move with expression (typically nose bridge, eye corners, jaw points). Output format matches cv.jit.keypoints. Use for stable face-tracking when you don't want expression to perturb the tracked points.

cv.jit.faces.digest:
cv.jit.faces scans through a greyscale image and tries to find regions that resemble frontal views of human faces. Because the algorithm is rather computationally intensive, it works best on small matrices. Ideally, the smallest face to be detected should be about 20 pixels wide.

While it can be used alone for face tracking, a more efficient use of resources would be to use cv.jit.faces in tandem with a proper tracking object, such as cv.jit.track, only performing face detection when necessary.
cv.jit.faces.use_when: Face detection — scans a greyscale image for frontal-face regions. Outputs (left, top, right, bottom) bounds per face on outlet 0; query face count via `getnfaces` (NOT bare `nfaces` — info-outlet pattern). `model` attr selects detection model (4 built-in models); `read <file>` loads a custom model. Greyscale input only (use jit.rgb2luma upstream). Use for the standard face-detect pipeline; pair with cv.jit.face.landmarks for detailed geometry.

cv.jit.features.digest: cv.jit.features: find features in an image
cv.jit.features.use_when: Find feature points in an image (corners / interest points). `precision 1` enables sub-pixel accuracy at higher CPU cost. Use as a feature detector for tracking or matching; pair with cv.jit.track for optical-flow tracking from these features.

cv.jit.features2track.use_when: Find sticky / trackable features for cv.jit.track — selects high-contrast areas (corners, edges) that survive optical-flow tracking better than smooth regions. 2 inlets (image, params) / 1 outlet. Use as the prep stage before cv.jit.track; produces a feature-points matrix that tracks more reliably than uniform sampling.

cv.jit.findchessboardcorners.digest: The output image blinks when chessboard corners coordinates are taken into account.
cv.jit.findchessboardcorners.use_when: Detect chessboard pattern corners for camera calibration. Output blinks when corners are accepted. 1 inlet / 3 outlets. Pair with cv.jit.calibration to build a calibration. Use as the standard pattern-based camera-calibration step.

cv.jit.findcontours.use_when: Trace contours from a binary raster image — outputs ordered point sequences per closed contour. Use to convert a binary mask into vector-style outlines for shape analysis, polygon approximation, or visual rendering.

cv.jit.findhomography.digest: This external is like cv.jit.getperspective except it needs 1-plane n x 2 matrix input instead of 2-plabe n x 1 due to an OpenCV issue
cv.jit.findhomography.use_when: Find a 3×3 homography matrix from corresponding point pairs — like cv.jit.getperspective but accepts 1-plane n×2 matrix input (vs 2-plane n×1) due to OpenCV API constraints. Use for perspective alignment / image rectification when you have ≥4 corresponding feature points.

cv.jit.floodfill.use_when: Connected-components flood fill. `@seed` attr sets the seed point. Use to label one connected region from a seed — useful for region-grow segmentation or region-of-interest extraction from a click point.

cv.jit.framesub.digest: cv.jit.framesub returns the absolute difference between consecutive frames.
cv.jit.framesub.use_when: Absolute difference between consecutive frames — frame subtraction. Use as the simplest motion detector; threshold the output to get a binary motion mask.

cv.jit.getperspective.digest: This external calculates a matrix of perspective transforms form 4 couples of corresponding points. Useful for tracking calibration.
cv.jit.getperspective.use_when: Compute a 3×3 perspective transform from exactly 4 corresponding point pairs. Inputs: source and destination points, each a 2-plane float32 matrix of 4 cells (plane 0 x, plane 1 y); output: 1-plane float32 3×3 matrix. Apply it to point coordinates with `cv.jit.perspective`; for 4 or more points in 1-plane n×2 format use `cv.jit.findhomography`. By Antoine Villeret.

cv.jit.hough.digest:
cv.jit.hough computes the Hough space from a binary image. For every ON pixel in the input, every line passing through that point is represented in the output by its distance and angle from the origin. The result is that for every point a sinusoid is created.
Places where many sinusoids intersect correspond to likely lines in the image. See cv.jit.extrema to extract this data.
The resolution of the Hough space representation is regulated bby the two parameter "rho" and "theta" which affect the accuracy of the distance and angle measurement respectively. The actual output matrix dimensions are computed as follows:width = ((input width + input height)*2 + 1) / rhoheight = PI / theta
cv.jit.hough.use_when: Compute the Hough space from a binary edge image. For every ON pixel, every line through that point votes in the Hough space. Use as the analysis stage of line detection; pair with cv.jit.hough2lines (which uses cv.jit.extrema on the Hough output) to extract actual line parameters.

cv.jit.hough2lines.digest: cv.jit.hough2Lines: find lines in Hough space
cv.jit.hough2lines.use_when: Find lines in a Hough space (output of cv.jit.hough). Internally uses cv.jit.extrema. Use as the second stage of explicit Hough-based line detection. For one-shot line detection prefer cv.jit.lines.

cv.jit.iter.digest: This works a lot like jit.iter but instead outputs one row or one column of the input matrix at a time.
cv.jit.iter.use_when: Output a 2D matrix one row or one column at a time (like `jit.iter`, but whole rows/columns). Argument `rows` or `cols`; any type and planecount. Left outlet: the row or column matrix; right outlet: its index.

cv.jit.kalman.use_when: Kalman filter optimised for 2D tracking (factors in velocity and acceleration). 1 inlet / 1 outlet. Use to smooth and predict tracked-point positions — much more stable than raw cv.jit.track output, especially through brief occlusions.

cv.jit.keypoints.digest: Adjust the threshold to change the number of features detected. Be careful, very small threshold values will return a verly large number of features. Usually between 0.05 and 0.3.
cv.jit.keypoints.use_when: Detect keypoints (interest points) for image matching. `threshold` adjusts feature density (smaller = more features); `@normalize 1` rescales coords to [0, 1] for cross-resolution matching. 1 inlet / 3 outlets. Use as the modern feature detector for image matching pipelines (vs older cv.jit.features); pair with cv.jit.keypoints.match.

cv.jit.keypoints.match.digest: Use cv.jit.unproject to find the position relative to the camera.
cv.jit.keypoints.match.use_when: Match keypoints between two images for finding correspondences. 4 inlets (two image keypoint sets + their descriptors) / 3 outlets. Use cv.jit.unproject to convert matches to camera-relative positions. Use for image-stitching, object recognition, structure-from-motion-style applications.

cv.jit.label.use_when: Connected-components labelling — assigns a unique label to each connected ON region in a binary image. `@charmode 0/1` and `@mode` control labelling behaviour. Use as the prerequisite for any cv.jit.blobs.* analysis (those operate on labelled images).

cv.jit.learn.digest:
cv.jit.learn is a tool for pattern recognition similar, though more elaborated, to cv.jit.undergrad. The user trains the object by feeding lists in its right inlet. These lists are assumed to desribe the state of something to be recognized. Normally, this will be moments of inertia or Hu invariants, as calculated by cv.jit.moments, but could be anything. If the size of the list is not 7, you need to specify it as an argument to the object.
Care should be taken during the training phase, as the quality of the training data will affect the accuracy of the recognition stage.
Once a model has been trained it can be saved using the "write" message. Saved models can be loaded with the "read" message.
When lists are sent to the left inlet, the statistical distance between the current state and the model is computed and output. By setting an appropriate threshold, the user can determine if the candidate list matches the training data.
Models created by cv.jit.learn can also be used by cv.jit.blobs.recon.
cv.jit.learn.use_when: Pattern-recognition trainer (more capable than cv.jit.undergrad). Train by feeding lists into the right inlet (training mode); switch to comparison mode to classify new lists. The training/comparison toggle is configurable via attribute. Use to build classifiers from feature lists (e.g. cv.jit.moments output) — pair with cv.jit.blobs.recon for shape recognition.

cv.jit.lines.digest: cv.jit.lines uses the Hough space to find straight lines in a greyscale image. First, the Canny algorithm is used to find image edges. The edge image is then transformed into a Hough representation, from which line candidate features are extracted. The output of cv.jit.lines is a 4-plane matrix of long type. The number of cells in the matrix corresponds to the number of lines found in the image. The four planes describe the position of the line segments in the following manner:Plane 1: Left-most x coordinatePlane 2: Top-most y coordinatePlane 3: Right-most x coordinatePlane 4: Bottom-most y coordinateA utility abstraction, cv.jit.lines.draw, is provided to easily draw the output of cv.jit.lines onto an image.
cv.jit.lines.use_when: One-shot straight-line detection — runs Canny then Hough internally. `gap` attr = max gap in a broken line; `length` attr = min line length. Use for direct line detection on greyscale images without manual Canny/Hough plumbing.

cv.jit.lowpass.digest: Use the mouse position as a source. Try moving the mouse very quickly back and forth.
cv.jit.lowpass.use_when: First-order low-pass filter for floats or lists of floats (not matrices): smooths rapid changes, like `slide` but for lists and with a cutoff in Hz. Attribute `cutoff` (Hz); messages `reset` or `clear` restart the filter. Subtract its output from the input for a simple high-pass. Use to smooth tracked coordinates; `cv.jit.kalman` also predicts motion.

cv.jit.mass.use_when: Sum of all pixel values in a matrix (total 'mass'). 1 inlet / 2 outlets (mass, pass-through). Use for one-number activity detection or as the denominator in centroid/normalisation calculations.

cv.jit.mean.digest: Calculates the mean matrix value over time.Note that cv.jit.mean now accurately calculates char matrices, so there is no need to convert to float for accuracy.
cv.jit.mean.use_when: Time-domain pixel-wise mean — running average of a matrix stream. Now char-accurate (no float conversion needed). Use to model a static background for background-subtraction-style motion detection.

cv.jit.module.presence.digest: Raise the lo slider to tune out background activity so that you get a clean 0 on the ouput. Lower the hi slider to define a condition of maximum activitiy or presence near the camera.
cv.jit.module.presence.use_when: Max for Live presence-detection module — outputs CC1 in M4L MIDI Effect context. Lo slider tunes background; hi slider sets max-activity reference. Use as a drop-in M4L device for camera-based presence sensing in Live sets.

cv.jit.moments.digest: cv.jit.moments is the basic object for shape analysis. It computes a list of seven moments, or shape descriptors. Refer to the documentation for a more detailed explanation of these descriptors.Those descriptors are said to be "central normalized" moments. That means that for the same shape, the values remain constant regardless of size or position.cv.jit.moments also computes a list of seven invariant shape descriptors. Like moments, they remain constant despite translation and scale. However, unlike moments, they are also invariant to rotation.See cv.jit.orientation, cv.jit.direction, cv.jit.elongation and cv.jit.learn for uses of moments.
cv.jit.moments.use_when: Shape analysis of a single-plane matrix (any type), e.g. a thresholded blob. Outputs (5 outlets): a 7-element list of central normalized moments, a 7-element list of Hu invariants, a 2-element centroid list, and the mass. Feed the moments to `cv.jit.orientation`, `cv.jit.direction`, `cv.jit.elongation`, or the lists to `cv.jit.learn`/`cv.jit.undergrad` for recognition. For many blobs use `cv.jit.blobs.moments` after `cv.jit.label`.

cv.jit.noise.digest: Every dimension can have different parameters. Here, the first two dimensions are used as coordinates and the third as the hue.
cv.jit.noise.use_when: Output pseudo-random floating-point values (not image noise). Bang for new values. Arguments: number of values (dimensions), then min and max (uniform distribution) or mean and standard deviation (`@mode 1` or `@mode normal`). `seed <n>` makes sequences repeatable. Used in the `cv.jit.kalman` help to simulate a noisy sensor. Built-in `random` covers uniform values.

cv.jit.notempty.digest: This matrix only has one cell. It is empty if this cell's value is 0.
cv.jit.notempty.use_when: Gate that passes a matrix only if it is not 'empty' — a single-cell matrix whose value is 0, as `cv.jit.faces` outputs when it finds no face. Left outlet: the matrix if not empty; right outlet: 1 or 0. Any type, planecount and dims.

cv.jit.open.use_when: Morphological open (erode then dilate). Removes ON-pixel noise (specks). Use as a binary-image cleanup step — opens small gaps between objects and removes tiny isolated bright pixels.

cv.jit.opticalflow.digest: Double-click these patchers to read more about each algorithm and see what kind of parameters you can adjust.
cv.jit.opticalflow.use_when: Unified optical-flow front-end with multiple algorithm choices (Horn-Schunck, Lucas-Kanade, etc. — double-click the help patchers for details). `@unique 1` recommended (sending the same matrix twice yields zero flow). Use as the convenience wrapper instead of choosing between cv.jit.hsflow / cv.jit.lkflow directly.

cv.jit.orientation.digest: cv.jit.orientation calculates the orientation of a shape's main axis. You need to compute moments of inertia beforehand.The orientation is calculated in radians, with 0 and Pi radians corresponding to a horizontal line. Pi/2 radians is vertical. Note that cv.jit.orientation only returns values between 0. and Pi.
cv.jit.orientation.use_when: Whole-image principal-axis orientation in radians (requires upstream cv.jit.moments). Use for whole-image rotation tracking; for per-blob use cv.jit.blobs.orientation.

cv.jit.perimeter.digest: cv.jit.perimeter counts the number of edge pixels in a binary image, that is, the number of ON pixels that have at least one OFF neighbour.
cv.jit.perimeter.use_when: Count edge pixels (ON pixels with at least one OFF neighbour) — perimeter length of a binary shape. Use to compute shape complexity or as the denominator in cv.jit.circularity-style ratios.

cv.jit.perspective.digest: there are 3 points for this example but you can put as many as you like
cv.jit.perspective.use_when: Apply a 3×3 perspective transform to a matrix of point coordinates (not to an image). Left inlet: 2-plane float32 n×1 matrix of points (plane 0 x, plane 1 y); right inlet: 1-plane float32 3×3 matrix from `cv.jit.getperspective` or `cv.jit.findhomography`. Output: transformed points. Use to map tracked camera coordinates onto a projection surface; to warp an image on screen use `jit.gl.cornerpin`. By Antoine Villeret.

cv.jit.poltocar.digest: Thesse abstractions work just like the regular Max objects cartopol and poltocar on matrix data.
cv.jit.poltocar.use_when: Polar → Cartesian conversion for matrix data. Inverse of cv.jit.cartopol. Use to undo polar transforms or generate radial patterns in (r, θ) and convert to (x, y) for display.

cv.jit.ravg.digest: cv.jit.ravg: calculate the running average over time
cv.jit.ravg.use_when: Running average over time (smoothing). `@alpha` sets the smoothing weight. Similar to cv.jit.mean but with explicit alpha control rather than uniform averaging. Use as a cheap temporal smoother for matrix streams.

cv.jit.resize.digest: cv.jit.resize output is anti-aliased compared to jit.matrix.
cv.jit.resize.use_when: Anti-aliased matrix resize — better quality than jit.matrix's interp resize. `@size <w> <h>` sets target dimensions. Use whenever you need quality resampling (e.g. resizing tracked image regions for analysis).

cv.jit.shift.use_when: Track an image area via continuously adaptive mean shift. Click-and-drag on the input pwindow to set the search window's starting position. 1 inlet / 4 outlets (position, size, etc.). Use for object tracking initialised by user selection — e.g. select a face once, track it as it moves.

cv.jit.stddev.digest: cv.jit.stddev computes the standard deviation over time for every pixel of the incoming matrices. The standard deviation is a statistical measure of how spread out from the mean the data is. For a normal distribution, about 68% of samples are within 1 standard deviations of the mean, 95% within 2 and 99.7% within 3 standard deviations.The standard deviation can be useful for filtering and recognition tasks like background subtraction: in the background analysis stage, the standard deviation is computed. In the comparison stage, pixels are compared to the standard deviation, if they are more than, for instance, 2 * the standard deviation, they can be considered foreground.
cv.jit.stddev.use_when: Pixel-wise standard deviation over time. Use to detect unusual variation per pixel — useful for change detection more sensitive than simple frame difference.

cv.jit.sum.use_when: Total pixel sum across a matrix. 1 inlet / 2 outlets. Use for whole-frame activity measurement or as a normalisation denominator.

cv.jit.threshold.use_when: Adaptive thresholding (local, not global). `@mode` selects algorithm, `@radius` sets neighbourhood size, `@threshold` sets bias. Use when global thresholding fails (uneven lighting) — adaptive threshold compares each pixel to its local neighbourhood.

cv.jit.touches.digest: A series of lists containing the same information as the first outlet but for LOST objects. The coordinates are the last valid values.
cv.jit.touches.use_when: Track several bright regions of similar size and give each a persistent ID, using MeanShift (built on `cv.jit.shift`). Originally for finger tracking on touch surfaces. Input: 1-plane char binary image, objects bright on black (e.g. `jit.chromakey` → `jit.rgb2luma`). Attribute `radius` sets object size; `reset` restarts ID numbering. Three outlets, each a series of `id x y radius` lists: NEW objects, EXISTING objects, LOST objects (last valid coordinates). `cv.jit.touches.draw` overlays them.

cv.jit.track.use_when: Track chosen points from frame to frame with pyramidal Lucas-Kanade optical flow (Bouguet's method). Input: 1-plane greyscale char matrix. Attribute `npoints` sets how many points; `set <index> <x> <y>` places a point. Output: 3-plane float32 matrix, one cell per point (x, y, status = still tracked). Seed good points with `cv.jit.features2track`; `cv.jit.track.draw` overlays frame-to-frame motion (right inlet image, `frgb` colour).

cv.jit.undergrad.digest: cv.jit.undergrad performs very simple pattern analysis and recognition on an input list. Usually, this list will be the output of cv.jit.moments.The user must first train the object by sending lists that correspond to "positives" in its right inlet. The mean value and standard deviation of each list element is computed. When a list is sent to its left inlet, it is compared with the mean vector computed in the training phase. The object then counts the number of elements that are within 2.5 standard deviations of the mean and outputs the result. For instance, if using the output of cv.jit.moments, input lists have 7 elements. An output of 7 from cv.jit.undergrad would mean that every element is within bounds of the training data, thus almost certainly a positive hit.
cv.jit.undergrad.use_when: Simpler pattern recognition than cv.jit.learn. Use to test classification ideas with minimal setup. The number of list elements within 2.5 standard deviations of the mean is reported as the match. For production use cv.jit.learn.

cv.jit.unproject.digest: Here we paint each point with the value of its index. This simulates the effect of cv.jit.label, while also ensuring that each blob's label doesn't change as the shape is rotated.
cv.jit.unproject.use_when: Convert 2D image coordinates to 3D camera-relative coordinates using calibration data. 2 inlets / 3 outlets. Use after cv.jit.calibration to convert tracked image points into a 3D camera frame — necessary for AR / spatial-projection workflows.

cv.jit.variance.digest: cv.jit.variance computes the standard deviation over time for every pixel of the incoming matrices. The variance is a statistical measure of how spread out from the mean the data is. See cv.jit.stddev for a related, easier to use, measurement.
cv.jit.variance.use_when: Pixel-wise variance over time (square of cv.jit.stddev). Use as the variance form of stddev when downstream math expects variance rather than standard deviation.

dada.analysis.centroid.use_when: Feature module for dada.segment: outputs the average pitch (centroid) of a score's gathered syntax. Wire it inside dada.segment's lambda loop, or use it alone on any roll or score dump. Requires bach.

dada.analysis.chroma.use_when: Feature module for dada.segment: outputs the chroma vector of a score's gathered syntax; modulo in the right inlet or argument. Requires bach.

dada.analysis.count.use_when: Feature module for dada.segment: counts the items of a score; the argument chooses the item type to count. Requires bach.

dada.analysis.duration.use_when: Feature module for dada.segment: outputs a score's duration in milliseconds. Requires bach.

dada.analysis.energy.use_when: Feature module for dada.segment: outputs a score's average velocity as its energy. Requires bach.

dada.analysis.minmax.digest: Minimum and maximum of a parameter
dada.analysis.minmax.use_when: Feature module for dada.segment: outputs the minimum and maximum of one note parameter, named by the argument. Requires bach.

dada.analysis.rhythmdistrib.use_when: Feature module for dada.segment: outputs how rhythmic energy is spread over @numdiv regions of a score, plus the onsets. Requires bach.

dada.analysis.spread.use_when: Feature module for dada.segment: outputs how widely pitches spread around the centroid. Requires bach.

dada.base.use_when: SQLite database that stores lllls (including whole scores) and ordinary Max values. The argument or @name names the database; addtable creates tables, addentry adds rows, query runs SQL and outputs results, appendfromfile imports CSV, read and write load and save. adddistancetable and adddistanceentry store distances for dada.distances. @llllastext stores lllls as text for SQL UPDATE queries. Browse data with dada.cartesian or dada.distances. Requires bach.

dada.bodies.use_when: Interactive gravity model: planets orbit fixed stars, and each star plays its notes when a planet passes. Add bodies with addstars and addplanets, play and stop to run; outlets give dump, notifications, hit data and playout. @g sets gravity strength, @hidewhileplaying improves timing. Requires bach.

dada.boids.use_when: Interactive flocking (boids) simulation: define swarms and rules such as center, avoid, align, wind and barriers, each with a gain; play and stop to run. The third outlet outputs sequencing data. Requires bach; the help file lists all rules and parameters.

dada.bounce.use_when: Interactive 2D room of edges with balls bouncing at constant speed; each edge hit triggers the note or score stored on that edge. addball adds balls, play and stop run it; outlets give dump, notifications, bounce info and playout. Scores stored on edges are saved with the patch. Requires bach.

dada.cartesian.use_when: Browse a dada.base table as a 2D scatter plot: @database and @table pick the data, @xfield and @yfield the axes, @colorfield and @sizefield the look, @contentfield what is output when a point is hovered or clicked. knn queries nearest points; turtle messages walk through grains; @beatsync plays grains on the beat. The symbolic CataRT-style corpus explorer, usually fed by dada.segment. Requires bach and dada.base.

dada.catart.use_when: Old name mapped to dada.cartesian (dada-objectmappings.txt); type dada.cartesian instead. Browses a dada.base table as a 2D scatter plot for symbolic concatenative playback.

dada.distances.use_when: Place the items of a dada.base table in 2D so that screen distance follows a stored distance table (multidimensional scaling). @database, @table and @distancetable pick the data; @contentfield sets hover output. turtle and turtlemarkov walk between neighboring points. Requires bach and dada.base.

dada.graph.use_when: Draw and edit a network of nodes and edges, with automatic layout (autocoord, @autocoordalgo). Send a graph llll to set it; nodes can hold values output on hover or click. turtle and turtlemarkov walk the graph as a Markov chain. Requires bach.

dada.kaleido.use_when: Kaleidoscope interface: shapes in a mirror chamber move and rotate; sampling points play notes or scores when shapes pass over them. shake, move, rotate and scale animate shapes; setsample assigns content; @count sets the number of mirror chambers. Outputs hits and playout. Requires bach.

dada.life.use_when: Interactive 2D cellular automaton with sound: bang to evolve, random to fill, rule or @born and @stayalive to set Conway-style rules, @customrule for your own. Living cells can be played as notes (@minpitch, @maxpitch, @play). getnumliving and getcellsum query state. For a matrix-only version use jit.conway. Requires bach.

dada.life.info.use_when: Analyze a pattern dumped from dada.life: outputs its period, period shift, annihilation time, trimmed pattern and orbit. Set the same rule attributes (@born, @stayalive, @lattice, @neighborhood) as the dada.life that produced it; @maxiter limits the search. Requires bach.

dada.machines.use_when: Draw a network of machines that transform scores or other data; data entering the network passes through each connected machine. Custom machines are defined as prototypes and implemented in a lambda loop. Prepend data to feed non-score data. Requires bach; see the help file for machine syntax.

dada.multibrot.use_when: Display the Mandelbrot set or its generalizations (@exp sets the exponent, 2 = Mandelbrot) and report whether a point belongs to the set and how fast it diverges, via getinfo or mouse clicks. @maxiter sets the iteration limit. Requires bach.

dada.music~.use_when: Browse a timeline that in principle contains every possible short digital sound, ordered by length; click or set cursor to pick one and play it. @bitdepth sets sample resolution. A thought experiment more than a tool. Mac only: no Windows external ships. Requires bach.

dada.nodes.use_when: Place pitch nodes in a 2D plane and move a knob among them: the knob outputs a pitch and velocity interpolated from nearby nodes. addnode and deletenode edit, interp queries a position, @p sets the inverse-distance weighting exponent, @minpitch and @maxpitch the range. Like Max's nodes but outputs pitches. Requires bach.

dada.peanos~.use_when: Browse a space of static timbres and hear them: the three inlets set amplitude, frequency-shift and noisiness configurations. @fzero sets the fundamental, @numpartials the number of partials. Outputs audio and coordinates. No help file ships. Requires bach.

dada.platform.use_when: Scriptable platform-game interface whose events (coins, blocks, characters) can trigger music. add, addsprite and addprototype build levels; play, stop and restart run them; fix saves a state to restart from. @gravity and friction attributes tune physics. Saving is tricky because playing changes the level; read the help file. Requires bach.

dada.segment.use_when: Cut a bach.roll or bach.score into segments and compute features for each. Set segment size with @segmentsize (or argument) and overlap with @hopsize; @voicewise segments each voice. Built-in features are switched on with attributes whose names start with ft, such as @ftduration, @ftonset and @fttempo; custom features run in the lambda loop, often with the dada.analysis modules. Store the results in dada.base and browse with dada.cartesian. Requires bach.

dada.stage.use_when: Display movable cards (icon, name and value) on a 2D stage, like a mixer view. addcards and deletecards edit; values are set by dragging; @minimum, @maximum and @slope set the value range and fader curve. Outputs positions and values only; it does no audio processing. Requires bach.

dada.terrain.ellipse~.use_when: Signal path generator for dada.terrain~: a phase signal (0 to 1) in, x and y signals out tracing an ellipse. @a and @b set the axes, @center the center, @rot the rotation; @polar outputs radius and angle instead. Drive it with a 0 to 1 ramp such as phasor~. Built on gen~.

dada.terrain.rect~.use_when: Signal path generator for dada.terrain~: a phase signal (0 to 1) in, x and y signals out tracing a rectangle. @x, @y, @w and @h set position and size; @polar outputs radius and angle. Drive it with a 0 to 1 ramp such as phasor~. Built on gen~.

dada.terrain.segment~.use_when: Signal path generator for dada.terrain~: a phase signal (0 to 1) in, x and y signals out along a straight line from @start to @end (or @polarstart to @polarend). @polar outputs radius and angle. Drive it with a 0 to 1 ramp such as phasor~. Built on gen~.

dada.terrain.spiral~.use_when: Signal path generator for dada.terrain~: a phase signal (0 to 1) in, x and y signals out along an Archimedean spiral. @a and @b set turn and distance, @n the number of turns, @center the center; @polar outputs radius and angle. Drive it with a 0 to 1 ramp such as phasor~. Built on gen~.

dada.terrain~.use_when: Wave-terrain synthesizer: reads a 2D terrain along x and y signal paths (from the dada.terrain path abstractions) to make audio. The terrain is either a formula written as C code compiled on the fly (see @staticfunction; changeable only with DSP off) or a wheel of radially arranged buffers (@buffers, @eqp for equal-power interpolation). Requires bach.

ears.!-~.digest: Subtract buffer samples with reversed inlets
ears.!-~.use_when: Subtract buffer samples with reversed inlets. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.!/~.digest: Divide buffer samples with reversed inlets
ears.!/~.use_when: Divide buffer samples with reversed inlets. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.!=~.use_when: Compare two buffers: outputs 1 if they differ, 0 if identical. Type it as `ears.!=~`. Second buffer name in the right inlet, first in the left (which triggers). Requires bach.

ears.*~.use_when: Multiply buffer samples. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.+~.use_when: Sum buffer samples. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.-~.use_when: Subtract buffer samples. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears./~.use_when: Divide buffer samples. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.==~.use_when: Compare two buffers: outputs 1 if they coincide in all properties and samples, 0 otherwise. Type it as `ears.==~`. Second buffer name in the right inlet, first in the left (which triggers). Not an equalizer. Requires bach.

ears.assemble~.use_when: Mix buffers one by one. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.biquad~.use_when: Two-pole two-zero filter for buffers. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.channel~.use_when: Get buffer channels. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.clicks~.use_when: Put clicks at time points. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.clip~.use_when: Buffer hard clipping. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.collect~.use_when: Collect buffer samples. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.cqt~.use_when: Constant-Q Transform. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.crop~.use_when: Crop a buffer. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.dcfilter~.use_when: Filter DC offset. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.delace~.use_when: De-interleave buffer channels. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.dynamics~.use_when: Dynamics processing. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.envelope~.digest: Fill a buffer with an envelope or a number
ears.envelope~.use_when: Fill a buffer with an envelope or a number. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.essentia~.digest: Extract buffer features via the Essentia library
ears.essentia~.use_when: Extract audio descriptors from buffers with the Essentia library. Arguments name the features, optionally with their own attributes in brackets, e.g. `ears.essentia~ [onsets @silenceThreshold 0.1]`, `ears.essentia~ chordsdetection @out m`. Frame analysis via `@framesize`, `@hopsize`, `@overlap`, `@wintype`; `@summary` reduces time series to single values; units via `@timeunit`, `@antimeunit`, `@frequnit`. Results come out as lllls; `@out` sets their format. Requires bach.

ears.expr~.use_when: Evaluate mathematical expressions on buffers. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.fade~.use_when: Apply fades. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.fft~.use_when: Fast Fourier Transforms. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.filterempty~.use_when: Passes on only the buffer names whose buffers are not empty. `@ampthresh` sets the level below which a buffer counts as empty (default 0), `@ampunit` linear or dB. Requires bach.

ears.format~.use_when: Modify buffers properties. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.freeverb~.use_when: Freeverb reverberation. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.fromdiffs~.digest: Reconstruct signal from sample or frame differences
ears.fromdiffs~.use_when: Reconstruct signal from sample or frame differences. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.fromsamps~.digest: Create a buffer from an llll
ears.fromsamps~.use_when: Create a buffer from an llll. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.fromvector~.digest: Convert synchronously a signal vector into a list
ears.fromvector~.use_when: Inside a patch loaded by ears.process~, turns each signal vector into a list so ordinary Max objects can work on it; convert back with ears.tovector~. Requires bach.

ears.gain~.use_when: Change buffer gain. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.griffinlim~.use_when: Reconstruct signal from magnitude spectrum. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.hoa.decode~.use_when: Decode higher-order ambisonic buffers. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.hoa.encode~.use_when: Encode 2D or 3D higher-order ambisonic buffers. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.hoa.mirror~.use_when: Mirror higher-order ambisonic buffers. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.hoa.rotate~.use_when: Rotate higher-order ambisonic buffers. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.in.digest: Message input for a patch loaded by ears.process~
ears.in.use_when: Message inlet inside a patch loaded by ears.process~: receives data sent to ears.process~'s message inlets. Argument: which message inlet(s), counted from 1 (default 1). With `@direct 0` (default) lllls are iterated in step with the buffers processed; `@direct 1` passes them on immediately. `@unwrap` removes the outer parentheses. Requires bach.

ears.info~.use_when: Report information about buffers. Arguments are the properties wanted, output in order: `min`, `max`, `maxabs`, `rms`, `length` (or `duration`), `numchannels`, `sr`, `numsamples`, plus spectral ones such as `spectral`, `audiosr`, `binsize` (e.g. `ears.info~ sr`). Send a buffer name to query. `@ampunit`, `@timeunit`. Requires bach.

ears.interp~.use_when: Buffer linear interpolation. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.in~.digest: Signal input for a patch loaded by ears.process~
ears.in~.use_when: Signal inlet inside a patch loaded by ears.process~: plays the samples of an input buffer into the patch. Argument: an llll with the ears.process~ inlet number and a sublist of channel numbers. Requires bach.

ears.istft~.use_when: Inverse Short-Time Fourier Transform. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.iter~.use_when: Outputs a buffer's samples one frame at a time as lists (one value per channel), then a bang when done. Argument sets how many buffers to iterate in parallel (which adds inlets and outlets); `@iterationmode` decides what happens when lengths differ. Pair with ears.collect~ to rebuild buffers. Requires bach.

ears.join~.use_when: Concatenate buffers. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.lace~.use_when: Interleave buffer channels. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.mc.in~.digest: Signal input for a patch loaded by ears.process~
ears.mc.in~.use_when: Multichannel signal inlet inside a patch loaded by ears.process~. Arguments / attributes: `inlet` (which ears.process~ buffer inlet, from 1), `firstchannel`, `chans` (0 = all channels). Requires bach.

ears.mc.out~.digest: Signal output for a patch loaded by ears.process~
ears.mc.out~.use_when: Multichannel signal outlet inside a patch loaded by ears.process~, writing to an output buffer. Arguments / attributes: `outlet` (from 1), `firstchannel`, `chans` (0 = all incoming channels). Requires bach.

ears.mixdown~.use_when: Reduce number of channels. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.mix~.use_when: Mix buffers. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.model.sine.analysis~.use_when: Sinusoidal analysis model. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.model.sine.synthesis~.use_when: Sinusoidal synthesis model. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.model.sps.analysis~.use_when: Sinusoidal-plus-stochastic analysis model. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.model.sps.synthesis~.use_when: Sinusoidal-plus-stochastic synthesis model. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.model.stochastic.analysis~.use_when: Stochastic analysis model. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.model.stochastic.synthesis~.use_when: Stochastic synthesis model. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.normalize~.use_when: Normalize buffers. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.offset~.use_when: Temporally offset a buffer. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.onepole~.digest: Single pole lowpass or highpass filter for buffers
ears.onepole~.use_when: Single pole lowpass or highpass filter for buffers. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.out.digest: Message output for a patch loaded by ears.process~
ears.out.use_when: Message outlet inside a patch loaded by ears.process~: whatever it receives comes out of the corresponding ears.process~ message outlet. Argument: which outlet(s), counted from 1. With `@direct 0` (default) data from all iterations is collected and output at the end; `@outwrap 1` wraps each iteration as a sublist. Requires bach.

ears.out~.digest: Signal output for a patch loaded by ears.process~
ears.out~.use_when: Signal outlet inside a patch loaded by ears.process~: records its input into the buffer output by ears.process~. Argument: an llll with the ears.process~ outlet number and a sublist of channel numbers; more channels give it more signal inlets. Requires bach.

ears.overdrive~.use_when: Buffer soft clipping. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.pack~.use_when: Pack buffer channels. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.pan~.use_when: 1D buffer panning. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.paulfreeze~.use_when: Paulstretch freeze. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.paulstretch~.use_when: Paulstretch timestretching. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.peaks~.use_when: Find peaks of a spectrogram. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.phaseunwrap~.use_when: Unwrap phase. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.phasewrap~.use_when: Get principal phases. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.playmp3~.use_when: Plays portions of mp3 files directly. `play <file> [start ms] [end ms]`; argument sets 1 or 2 output channels; `@loop 1`, `@fadeinsamps`. Not in ears' object registry and has no help file of its own (legacy). For general playback prefer playlist~. Requires bach.

ears.processinfo~.digest: Report information about the process running
ears.processinfo~.use_when: Reports the state of the offline process inside a patch loaded by ears.process~. Outlets: position as signal (ms), position as float (ms), running flag, sample rate, vector size, input buffer durations, and messages for objects supporting setclock. `stop` ends the process. Requires bach.

ears.process~.digest: Offline host for patches operating on buffers
ears.process~.use_when: Offline host that runs an ordinary MSP patch on buffers faster than realtime, like a DAW's offline render. Argument: the patch name (as with poly~), optionally preceded by output buffer names. Inside the patch, ears.in~ / ears.mc.in~ read the input buffers, ears.out~ / ears.mc.out~ write outputs, ears.in / ears.out pass messages, ears.processinfo~ reports progress. Send buffer names (or `bang`) to the left inlet to run. `@tail <ms>` extends rendering for decays; `@duration` sets the length policy; `@vs` vector size (default 128); `@sr` for generator patches; `@reload`. Timed objects (metro, delay…) follow audio time; objects that turn signals into messages may mistime; a local `startwindow` elsewhere blocks it. Experimental. Requires bach.

ears.read~.use_when: Read an audio file into a named buffer. The standard ears entry point — equivalent to `buffer~ <name>` + `read` but returns when complete and integrates with the ears workflow.

ears.reg~.use_when: Store or clone buffers. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.repeat~.use_when: Repeat buffer. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.resample~.use_when: Resample buffer. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.rev~.use_when: Reverse buffer. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.roll.sampling~.use_when: Bounce a bach.roll whose notes carry sound-file or buffer names into one mixed buffer. Send the roll's gathered syntax. `@audioslot` (or `@fileslot`) names the slot holding files; `@gainslot`, `@panslot`, `@offsetslot` read per-note settings; `@numchannels`, `@panlaw`, `@velmode`, `@usedurations`, `@fadein` / `@fadeout`, `@normalize`, `@assemble`. Requires bach.

ears.roll.synthesis~.use_when: Bounce a bach.roll into a buffer, playing each note as an oscillator. Send the roll's gathered syntax. `@waveform` / `@wavetable` choose the sound; `@gainslot`, `@panslot`, `@numchannels`, `@velmode`, `@fadein` / `@fadeout`, `@normalize`. Requires bach.

ears.roll.toreaper~.use_when: Export a bach.roll as a Reaper project containing a montage of audio samples. Slots map per-note file, gain, pan, offset, colour, fade, time-stretch and transposition (`@fileslot`, `@gainslot`, `@panslot`, `@offsetslot`, `@transpositionslot`, `@timestretchslot`…); `@copymedia` / `@mediafolder` handle audio files. Requires bach.

ears.rot~.use_when: Circular rotation of a buffer. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.rubberband~.digest: Rubber Band pitch and time processing
ears.rubberband~.use_when: Rubber Band pitch and time processing. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.slice~.use_when: Slice a buffer into two. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.soundtouch~.use_when: SoundTouch pitch and time processing. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.specshow~.use_when: Display a spectrogram stored in a buffer (one channel per bin, one sample per window), such as the output of ears.stft~, ears.cqt~ or ears.tempogram~. Send the buffer name, or set `@buffername`. `@autoscale` or `@minvalue` / `@maxvalue` with `@mincolor` / `@maxcolor` and `@colorcurve` set the colour map; `@timegrid`, `@freqgrid`, `@maxnumbins` set grids and detail. Display only: no output. Requires bach.

ears.split~.digest: Split a buffer into multiple buffers
ears.split~.use_when: Split a buffer into multiple buffers. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.stft~.use_when: Compute spectrograms. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.tempogram~.use_when: Compute tempograms. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.timesquash~.use_when: Content-aware time abridgement. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.todiffs~.use_when: Get sample or frame differences. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.tosamps~.use_when: Outputs all the samples of a buffer as a bach llll, one sublist per channel. Send the buffer name; `@out` sets the llll output format. Inverse of ears.fromsamps~. Requires bach.

ears.tovector~.digest: Convert synchronously a list of numbers into a signal vector
ears.tovector~.use_when: Inside a patch loaded by ears.process~, collects numbers into a signal vector. All values for one vector must arrive in one event synchronised with the offline audio vector (respond to ears.fromvector~ or ears.processinfo~'s position outlet). Messages: int, float, list, `set <index>`, `clear`; `@autoclear 1` (default) zeroes each new vector. Requires bach.

ears.trans~.digest: Transpose a buffer considered as a matrix
ears.trans~.use_when: Transpose a buffer considered as a matrix. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.trim~.use_when: Trim silence from a buffer. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.unpack~.use_when: Unpack buffer channels. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.vamp~.use_when: Extract audio features from buffers using installed Vamp plug-ins. Arguments: plug-in identifiers as `libraryid:pluginid[:output]`; `getlist` lists installed plug-ins. Frame settings `@framesize`, `@hopsize`, `@overlap` or `@auto 1`; `@summary` summarises frames. One outlet per feature plus notifications. Requires bach and Vamp plug-ins.

ears.waveset.average~.use_when: Waveset averaging. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.waveset.decimate~.use_when: Waveset repetition. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.waveset.interp~.use_when: Waveset interpolation. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.waveset.repeat~.use_when: Waveset repetition. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.waveset.shuffle~.use_when: Waveset shuffling. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.waveset.split~.use_when: Waveset splitting. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.waveset.subs~.use_when: Waveset substitution. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.window~.use_when: Apply an analysis window. Buffer-domain operation — non-realtime, writes a named output buffer. See package_concepts.md ears section.

ears.write~.use_when: Write a named buffer out to an audio file. Use for offline render output.

ease.digest: Generate or apply an easing function
ease.use_when: Generate or apply an easing function.

ease.xfade.digest: Use an easing function to interpolate between successive lists
ease.xfade.use_when: Use an easing function to interpolate between successive lists.

ease.xfade~.digest: Use an easing function to interpolate between two sample values
ease.xfade~.use_when: Use an easing function to interpolate between two sample values.

ease~.digest: Generate or apply an easing function
ease~.use_when: Generate or apply an easing function.

jit.ease.digest: Generate or apply an easing function
jit.ease.use_when: Generate or apply an easing function.

list.ease.digest: Generate or apply an easing function
list.ease.use_when: Generate or apply an easing function.

ej.4m.digest: output the min, median, mean, maximum on a int/float stream
ej.4m.use_when: Minimum, median, mean and maximum over a sliding window of incoming numbers (JS). Typed as `js ej.4m.js <window>`; optional 2nd arg `verbose`. Messages: `window <n>`, `getwindow`, `reset` (alias `clear`), `verbose $1`; outlets for min, median, mean and max. The ejies readme marks it obsolete — `mxj ej.mmmm` is the faster replacement; in Max 9 the `array.min/median/mean/max` objects also cover it.

ej.buffer2l.digest: look at this patch in presentation in Mira
ej.buffer2l.use_when: Pick representative ('meaningful') samples of a `buffer~` as a list, for drawing waveforms in list-based displays. Attributes: `@buf_name <buffer>`, `@grain <n>` (points), `@channel`; message `zoom <start> <end>` then `bang` to output a zoomed region. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.buffer2l`, not `ej.buffer2l`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

ej.cc.digest: arg (optional): recursive mode (0 disable, 1 enable - default)
ej.cc.use_when: Change the colours of objects in a patch by scripting name (JS). Typed as `js ej.cc.js`; optional argument 0 disables searching subpatchers (default 1 = recursive). Messages: `[object name] [color index]`, `defaults` (the author's favourite colours), `resetall`, `global $1`. Written for older Max; its colour handling predates Max 7 styles, so prefer Format palette / styles in current Max.

ej.cn.digest: change name of a named (via the Object>Name... command) object
ej.cn.use_when: Change the scripting name of a named object from inside the patch (JS). Typed as `js ej.cn.js <name>`; send `<old name> <new name>` to rename. Useful when a patch retargets named objects by scripting.

ej.cycle.digest: cycle send only the message to the outlet, the arguments are dispatched over the others outlets.
ej.cycle.use_when: Send each incoming message — whole, with its arguments — to the next outlet in turn (JS). Typed as `js ej.cycle.js <outlets>`; `set <n>` chooses the next outlet. Unlike built-in `cycle`, which splits list items across outlets, it keeps messages intact.

ej.dialog.digest: Open a dialog box for text entry
ej.dialog.use_when: Floating dialog window for typing a line of text. Abstraction; arguments are the prompt text. A bang in the inlet opens it; the typed text leaves the left outlet as a symbol; the right outlet bangs when the user cancels or presses Escape. Built-in `dialog` does the same job.

ej.dn.digest: argument (optional): 1 search a named object which contains the string
ej.dn.use_when: Open (display) the patcher window that contains a named object (JS). Typed as `js ej.dn.js`; send the object's scripting name. Argument 1 matches partial names. Place it at the top level of the main patch so it can search everything below.

ej.dx2x.use_when: Turn a list of intervals into a list of running totals, starting from an origin (argument, e.g. `60.`); inverse of `ej.x2dx`. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.dx2x`, not `ej.dx2x`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

ej.fplay.digest: ej.fplay uses the same messages as the standart function object:
ej.fplay.use_when: Non-graphical multi-breakpoint function store and player using the same messages as `function`, for several functions at once (argument = number of functions). Can sync with the `ej.function` jsui (`sync`, `synccurrent`), output a function as a Jitter matrix (`dumpmatrix`), and reads the ej.function file format. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.fplay`, not `ej.fplay`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

ej.ftom.digest: args:- float tuning (default: 440 Hz)- int MIDI pitch reference (default: 69)
ej.ftom.use_when: Convert frequencies (numbers or lists) to MIDI note numbers with custom tuning. Args/attributes: `@tuning` (default 440 Hz), pitch reference (default 69), `@mode` float, int, round, quarter or n (nearest 1/n tone). Built-in `ftom` also accepts lists and has a `base` attribute. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.ftom`, not `ej.ftom`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

ej.function.digest: ej.function uses the same messages as the standart function object:
ej.function.use_when: Graphical editor for several breakpoint functions in one display (jsui, `ej.function.js`); create it from the ejies object prototypes or snippets. Same messages as `function` plus curve mode (alt-drag), `movemode` (normal, clip, shift, shift-clip, shift-extend, shift-zoom, auto-zoom), zoom, grid and `dumpmatrix`. Pair with `mxj ej.fplay` for headless playback (needs Java). Use when one `function` per envelope is not enough.

ej.jit.preview.digest: Jitter Patcher Window (with slowing down feature)
ej.jit.preview.use_when: Small Jitter matrix preview with an adjustable refresh interval (argument, ms), to monitor a pipeline without spending CPU on every frame. A bpatcher: create it from the bpatcher prototypes (`ej.jit.preview`). Built on `jit.pwindow`; built-in `jit.pwindow` alone is usually enough.

ej.l2buffer.use_when: Write a list of numbers into a `buffer~` channel. Args: `<buffer name> <channel>`; messages `set <buffer> <channel>` (change destination) and `buftime <ms>`. Max 9's `array.tobuffer` does the same with arrays. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.l2buffer`, not `ej.l2buffer`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

ej.lchange.digest: You can define the mode attribute with an integer or a symbol:- "mode 0" is equivalent to "mode thru" (default)- "mode 1" is equivalent to "mode bang"- "mode 2" is equivalent to "mode int".
ej.lchange.use_when: Output only when an incoming list (numbers or symbols, any length) differs from the previous one. Attribute `@mode`: `thru`/0 passes the new list (default), `bang`/1 bangs, `int`/2 outputs 1 on change and 0 when unchanged. Message `set <list>` stores without output. Built-in `zl.change` covers the thru case. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.lchange`, not `ej.lchange`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

ej.lclip.digest: Constrains a list within a certain range
ej.lclip.use_when: Constrain every number in a list between a minimum and maximum (args, e.g. `20 80`). `@outputmode` can send the result to the outlet, to a buffer~ (`@buf_name`), or both. Built-in `clip` also accepts lists. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.lclip`, not `ej.lclip`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

ej.ldrunk.digest: args:- min (optional, 0 if not present)- max- random step: ± (step / 2)- % of random's probability
ej.ldrunk.use_when: Random walk applied to every element of a list. Args: min, max, random step (± step/2), percentage probability of change. Attributes: `@interval` (ms; >0 outputs continuously), `ignore` (leave zeros untouched), `autoreset` (always walk from the original list), `@outputmode`/`@buf_name` to write into a buffer~. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.ldrunk`, not `ej.ldrunk`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

ej.led.digest: Fun "meter" effects can be achieved by clever setting of the led "flash time" in the Get Info… dialog.
ej.led.use_when: Alternative LED / button indicator (jsui, `ej.led.js`), created from the ejies prototypes or snippets. Messages: `bang` (flash), `1`/`0`, `toggle` (button vs toggle behaviour), `pict <N>` (change colour). Flash time is set in the inspector. Built-in `led` does the basic job.

ej.line.digest: Note:there is some timing problem (it's getting shorter while the number of segment is getting higher). You can attenuate that problem while using a smaller grain size.
ej.line.use_when: Control-rate multi-segment ramp. Abstraction; args: initial value (also sets int or float output) and time grain in ms. Send `target time` pairs, e.g. `0, 100 1000` or a multi-segment list; right inlet sets the grain (default 20 ms); right outlet bangs when the ramp ends. The help notes timing drift with many segments (smaller grain helps). Built-in `line` already handles multi-segment lists.

ej.linterp.digest: with autotrigger on, each input trigger the interpolation
ej.linterp.use_when: Interpolate between up to eight stored lists (A–H), by position or by a list of weights (`weight` mode, e.g. `mxj ej.linterp weight 8`). `@autotrigger 1` makes each input update the output; `@outputmode`/`@buf_name` can write into a buffer~. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.linterp`, not `ej.linterp`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

ej.lock.digest: Note that polling doesn't always work since Max 5 because, the patcher might have multiple views with different lock states.
ej.lock.use_when: Get or set the patcher's locked state (JS). Typed as `js ej.lock.js`; optional argument = polling interval in ms (default 0). Messages: `lock 0`/`lock 1`, `getlock`, `poll <ms>`, `nopoll`. Polling is unreliable since Max 5 because a patcher can have several views with different lock states.

ej.lop.digest: sin: sinecos: cosinetan: tangentasin: arcsineacos: arccosineatan: arctangentatan2: arctangent(binary)
ej.lop.use_when: Math on every element of (long) lists. Args: operator then value(s), e.g. `mxj ej.lop @op * @val 2`; attributes `@op`, `@val`, `@scalarmode`, `@autotrigger`. Operators include + - !- * / !/ // % min max avg abs absdiff, comparisons (> < >= <= == != and 'pass' variants such as >p), exp ln log2 log10 pow sqrt ceil floor round trunc, sin cos tan asin acos atan atan2, atodb dbtoa. Built-in `vexpr` covers many cases. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.lop`, not `ej.lop`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

ej.lquant.digest: Quantize a stream of number or a list (sort of multiple rounding process)
ej.lquant.use_when: Quantize numbers or lists to the nearest multiple of a step (argument; several steps allowed, e.g. `0.25 0.7`). `@outputmode`/`@buf_name` can write into a buffer~. Built-in `round` also accepts lists. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.lquant`, not `ej.lquant`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

ej.lscale.digest: arg1 is input low value (default 0.)arg2 is input high value(default 127.)arg3 is output low value (default 0.)arg4 is output high value (default 1.)arg5 is exponent value (default 1. = linear)
ej.lscale.use_when: Map every number of a list from one range to another with an optional exponent. Args: in low (0.), in high (127.), out low (0.), out high (1.), exponent (1. = linear); `@clip 1` keeps output in range; `@outputmode`/`@buf_name` write into a buffer~. Built-in `scale` also accepts lists. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.lscale`, not `ej.lscale`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

ej.lslide.digest: When interval attribute is set to a value greater than 0, it outputs lists continuously.
ej.lslide.use_when: Smooth changes in every element of a list with y(n) = y(n-1) + (x(n) - y(n-1))/slide. Args or attributes: slide up, slide down; `@interval` (ms; >0 outputs continuously); `reset` if values explode; `@outputmode`/`@buf_name` write into a buffer~. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.lslide`, not `ej.lslide`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

ej.lui.digest: ej.lui is a self-destructive object. It kills itself after creating a jsui objet. This allows you to quickly create jsui objects with custom javascript file.
ej.lui.use_when: Shortcut that creates a jsui object from a script and then deletes itself (JS): type `js ej.lui.js <file.js>` in an object box (e.g. `js ej.lui.js ej.numbox.js`). A convenience from older Max versions; creating `jsui` directly works too.

ej.mmmm.digest: output the min, median, mean, maximum on a int/float stream
ej.mmmm.use_when: Minimum, median, mean and maximum over a sliding window of incoming numbers (argument = window size). `@mode list` outputs all four as one list. Faster replacement for `js ej.4m.js`; Max 9's `array.min/median/mean/max` cover the same statistics. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.mmmm`, not `ej.mmmm`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

ej.mout~.digest: offset 0 turns off the automatic offset (where the spatialization is centered between the first and second speaker)
ej.mout~.use_when: Pan a mono signal around 2–16 loudspeakers arranged in a circle. Abstraction; argument = number of outputs (2–16; unused outlets are disabled). Left inlet: signal; right inlet: position signal 0.–1. around the circle. `@offset 1` (default) centres position 0 between the first two speakers; `@offset 0` puts it on the first speaker. Uses a stored gain curve; no distance or elevation.

ej.mtof.digest: args:- float tuning (default: 440 Hz)- int MIDI pitch reference (default: 69)
ej.mtof.use_when: Convert MIDI note numbers (numbers or lists) to frequency with custom tuning. Args/attributes: `@tuning` (default 440 Hz), pitch reference (default 69). Built-in `mtof` also accepts lists and has a `base` attribute. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.mtof`, not `ej.mtof`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

ej.nthru.digest: it does nothing... just pass the input to the output
ej.nthru.use_when: Pass-through placeholder with any number of inlets and outlets (JS). Typed as `js ej.nthru.js <inlets> <outlets>`; input passes unchanged. Only useful to keep wiring in place while a patch is under construction.

ej.numbox.digest: you can use the tabulation key to pass to the next number box...
ej.numbox.use_when: Alternative number box (jsui, `ej.numbox.js`) created from the ejies prototypes or snippets. Features: Tab moves focus to the next ej.numbox, `select` gives it focus, keyboard entry while locked, rounding and leading-zero options, endless scrolling, idle reporting, pattr and `jit.getparam` compatible. Built-in `number`/`flonum`/`live.numbox` cover most uses.

ej.op.digest: argument (optional): 1 search a named object which contains the string
ej.op.use_when: Open a subpatcher window by its scripting name (JS). Typed as `js ej.op.js`; send the name. Argument 1: partial-name search; second argument 1: case-insensitive. Messages `searchmode $1`, `casemode $1`.

ej.route.use_when: Route incoming data to outlets by type — bang, int, float, list, symbol, signal (JS). Typed as `js ej.route.js`. Built-in `typeroute~` also routes by data type.

ej.sliders-overview.digest: 3 sizes (big, small, tiny)2 colors (Aqua, Graphite)2 backgrounds (Aqua, Metal)2 orientations (vertical, horizontal)
ej.sliders-overview.use_when: Reference patch showing the ejies Aqua-style `pictslider` designs (3 sizes, 2 colours, 2 backgrounds, horizontal/vertical), available as object prototypes (`ej.blue-…`, `ej.graph-…`). Not an object: open it to copy a slider style. The look dates from old macOS.

ej.urn.digest: takes two optional arguments: first sets maximum (default 1), second sets random number seed (default 0)
ej.urn.use_when: Random integers without repeats until all values have been drawn. Args: maximum (default 1), seed (0 = time-based). Right inlet sets a new maximum; right outlet bangs when all numbers are used; messages `clear`, `seed`; `@autoclear 1` refills automatically. Its reason to exist is range: built-in `urn` is limited to 4096 values. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.urn`, not `ej.urn`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

ej.vdb-sig~.digest: Variable delay without clicks or transposition
ej.vdb-sig~.use_when: Variable delay without clicks or pitch change, with the delay time given as a signal. Abstraction; connect a `tapin~` to its left inlet; middle inlet = window size (int, ms; argument sets the default); right inlet = delay time (signal, ms). Two windowed taps crossfade and change time only at window zeros. Signal-controlled version of `ej.vdb~`.

ej.vdb~.digest: Variable delay without clicks or transposition
ej.vdb~.use_when: Variable delay without clicks or pitch change (optimized version of Benjamin Thigpen's vdb~). Abstraction; connect a `tapin~` to its left inlet (inlet 1); inlet 2 = window size (int, ms); inlet 3 = delay time (float, ms). Args: window size, delay time. Two windowed taps crossfade, changing delay time only when a window is at zero. Built-in `delay~` has a `ramp` message for smooth delay changes.

ej.x2dx.digest: get the interval between successive values of a list
ej.x2dx.use_when: Output the differences between successive values of a list (e.g. note onsets → inter-onset intervals); inverse of `ej.dx2x`. Java class from ejies (Emmanuel Jourdan): type it as `mxj ej.x2dx`, not `ej.x2dx`. Needs a Java runtime (JDK) installed; without one the box does not load (no JDK was found on the curating machine).

jit.fullscreen.digest: If there is a second monitor, the window will be displayed on it. Press Escape key to toggle the fullscreen mode.
jit.fullscreen.use_when: Open a `jit.window` on a second monitor (if present) and toggle fullscreen with Escape. Abstraction from ejies (not a built-in Jitter object despite the name). Args: `<x dim> <y dim> <jit.window attributes>` (e.g. `640 480 @interp 1 @pos 700 40`); message `fullscreen $1`; right outlet is a dumpout (e.g. mouse position). For new work use `jit.world` (`fullscreen`, `esc_fullscreen` attributes).

jit.getparam.digest: arg: name of the receive connected to the jitter object
jit.getparam.use_when: Getter/setter panel for any Jitter (obex) object's attributes: fills a menu with the object's parameters, then lets you get and set them. Abstraction from ejies (not a built-in). Argument = name of a `receive` wired into the target object; special message `defaults` (does not work on every object). Built-in `attrui` and `getattr` do this per attribute.

kaf.use_when: Kill and relaunch the macOS Finder from Max. Abstraction; messages `kill`, `open`, `activate` (bang kills). Mac only; requires the third-party `shell` external — on the curating machine it came from the Samplor package as an Intel-only binary, so it does not load in native Apple Silicon Max.

kd&u.digest: Output is 1 when the desired key is down, 0 when it's going up…
kd&u.use_when: Report a chosen key going down (1) and up (0). Abstraction; args: key number (default 32 = space bar), modifier number (default 0 on Mac, 128 on Windows); 3 outlets. Double-click it to see key and modifier numbers. Built-in `key` + `keyup` do the same.

ptt.digest: first: maximum slider value second : minimum value when you're talking
ptt.use_when: Push-to-talk level control for an audio signal: while alt+cmd is held, the level drops to the 'talking' value; ctrl+cmd changes the maximum. Abstraction; args: maximum slider value (default 127), level while talking (default 90). Signal in left inlet, controlled signal out. Mac modifier keys.

splay~.use_when: Sound-file player with a small window and keyboard shortcuts, built on `sfplay~`. Abstraction; argument = number of channels. Messages `wopen`/`wclose` show or hide its window; shortcuts use the numeric keypad (shift + / start/stop, shift + - pause, shift + * loop, shift + = open file). Accepts files by drag and drop. For new work use `playlist~`.

stout~.digest: Since Max 5, in order to use the shortcuts, you need to press the ctrl key, then the shortcut letter.
stout~.use_when: Stereo output stage replacing `ezdac~`/`dac~`: faders, meters, input switch and DSP shortcuts. Abstraction; 2 signal inlets; optional args select the output channels (e.g. `stout~ 2 6`). Float input sets gain in dB; messages `wopen`/`wclose` show its window. Shortcuts need ctrl since Max 5 (ctrl+space start/stop DSP, ctrl+0 / ctrl+1 faders to -inf / 0 dB). For new work use `live.gain~` + `ezdac~`.

filter.butterworth.digest: Nth-order Butterworth filterThis object is intended mainly for plotting
filter.butterworth.use_when: Nth-order Butterworth filterThis object is intended mainly for plotting.

filter.chebyshev1.digest: Nth-order Chebyshev Type-I filterThis object is intended mainly for plotting
filter.chebyshev1.use_when: Nth-order Chebyshev Type-I filterThis object is intended mainly for plotting.

filter.chebyshev2.digest: Nth-order Chebyshev Type-II filterThis object is intended mainly for plotting
filter.chebyshev2.use_when: Nth-order Chebyshev Type-II filterThis object is intended mainly for plotting.

filter.elliptic.digest: Nth-order elliptic filterThis object is intended mainly for plotting
filter.elliptic.use_when: Nth-order elliptic filterThis object is intended mainly for plotting.

filter.legendre.digest: Nth-order Legendre filterThis object is intended mainly for plotting
filter.legendre.use_when: Nth-order Legendre filterThis object is intended mainly for plotting.

grainflow.freeze~.digest: Freeze moments in time with granulation
grainflow.freeze~.use_when: Freeze moments in time with granulation.

grainflow.function2D.digest: An easy way to pan grains generated with grainflow.
grainflow.function2D.use_when: XY pad sequencer (jsui) that moves one or more trackers between points with linear interpolation. Tracker position 0–1 goes in; x/y positions come out. Edit points with `addPoint`, `insertPoint`, `movePoint`, `removePoint`, `swapPoint`, `setPoints` (x/y pairs), `clear`, `getPoints`; change them with `scramble`, `randomize`, `jitter`; `trackers` sets how many trackers run; appearance messages `bgColor`, `color`, `dotSize`, `lineThickness`, `trackerColor`. Use to draw a path and scan it with a phasor to modulate two grain parameters (the help file drives a granulator with it).

grainflow.live~.digest: the live granulation object for grainflow
grainflow.live~.use_when: Live-input version of grainflow~: it records incoming audio into its own internal buffer and keeps the granulator in sync. Arguments per help: `<buffer length> <max grains>` (refpage also allows a buffer name and envelope buffer). Recording and playback are separate: `@rec` starts/stops recording, `@play` playback, `@freeze` keeps recording but freezes the playhead, `@overdub` mixes old and new content, `@buffer_name` names the internal buffer. Takes the same grain attributes and messages as grainflow~ (`@delay`, `@delayRandom`, `@transpose`, `@ngrains`, `g`, `deviate`, ...); grain clock and modulation inputs work the same way; each grain is its own mc channel, so pan after it. Use for live granular delays, harmonizers, sustain and freeze effects (the help file shows all three).
