grainflow.scrubSynth~.digest: Create a noise synthesizer through granular synthesis.  The scrubSynth uses integer multiples of frequency and traversal to generate a wavelet synthesis-like approach using granulation.
grainflow.scrubSynth~.use_when: Create a noise synthesizer through granular synthesis.  The scrubSynth uses integer multiples of frequency and traversal to generate a wavelet synthesis-like approach using granulation.

grainflow.spat.3dspread.digest: Spreads grains from a center point
grainflow.spat.3dspread.use_when: Spreads grains from a center point.

grainflow.spat.format.digest: Formats grain position messages for other systems such as Spat Gris or the IEM Suite
grainflow.spat.format.use_when: Formats grain position messages for other systems such as Spat Gris or the IEM Suite.

grainflow.spat.phys.digest: A simple physics engine that allows for manipulation of position, velocity, and acceleration manipulations.
grainflow.spat.phys.use_when: A simple physics engine that allows for manipulation of position, velocity, and acceleration manipulations.

grainflow.spat.phys.add.digest: Adds values to physics fields using the lambda outlet for custom updates.
grainflow.spat.phys.add.use_when: Adds values to physics fields using the lambda outlet for custom updates.

grainflow.spat.phys.drag.digest: Applies drag to a grainflow physics matrix
grainflow.spat.phys.drag.use_when: Applies drag to a grainflow physics matrix.

grainflow.spat.phys.magnets.digest: Calculates distanced between grains and magnets then applies physics
grainflow.spat.phys.magnets.use_when: Calculates distanced between grains and magnets then applies physics.

grainflow.spat.phys.transform.digest: Applies transformations to a selected physics field
grainflow.spat.phys.transform.use_when: Applies transformations to a selected physics field.

grainflow.spat.speakers.digest: Allows for easy access to speaker presets and loading of speaker files
grainflow.spat.speakers.use_when: Allows for easy access to speaker presets and loading of speaker files.

grainflow.spat.spirograph.digest: Samples signals to spatialize grains with grainflow.spat.pan~
grainflow.spat.spirograph.use_when: Samples signals to spatialize grains with grainflow.spat.pan~.

grainflow.spat.split.digest: Splits grain posiiton messages based on their IDs
grainflow.spat.split.use_when: Splits grain posiiton messages based on their IDs.

grainflow.spat.transform.use_when: Transforms grain positions for grainflow.spat.pan~: `translate x y z`, `scale`, `rotate` (normalized values), each with a `...Random` variant applied per new grain. Input: xyz position messages from another grainflow.spat.* object. Without a bang, only newly created grains are transformed; `bang` updates all stored points (use for animated transforms). Outlets: positions, and data for grainflow.spatview~.

grainflow.spat.transformOverLife.use_when: Moves each grain's position over the grain's lifetime for grainflow.spat.pan~: `translate`, `scale` (ratio of the original) and `rotate` (normalized) define where a grain ends up, each with a `...Random` variant per grain. Input: xyz position messages from another grainflow.spat.* object. Outlets: positions, and data for grainflow.spatview~.

grainflow.streams~.digest: Create multiple streams of grains without channel loss.
grainflow.streams~.use_when: Create multiple streams of grains without channel loss.

grainflow.sustain~.use_when: Stereo granular hold effect: continuously overdubs a short (about 250 ms) buffer based on input amplitude and plays it back with random grain positions, so a sound keeps sounding after it stops. Argument: grain count. Messages: `decay` (how long the sound is held), `grainSize` (choose to suit the material), `pitchshift`, `randomPan` (mix between random panning and the original stereo image), plus grainflow~ messages. Accepts mono or stereo input; outputs stereo.

grainflow.util.3dspread.digest: An easy way to pan grains generated with grainflow.
grainflow.util.3dspread.use_when: Older helper that generates 3D positions for grains around a center, meant for the deprecated grainflow.util.vbap3d. Messages: `spread` (optionally per axis), `center`. Input: grains as mc channels; output: x y z positions. For new patches use grainflow.spat.3dspread with grainflow.spat.pan~.

grainflow.util.bphasor~.digest: An easy to adust phasor for granulation
grainflow.util.bphasor~.use_when: Phasor whose speed is based on a buffer's playback rate (help file). Left inlet: playback rate; right inlet: phase offset 0–1; `reset` jumps to the phase offset; `set` changes the buffer; the help file changes buffers from grainflow~'s data outlet.

grainflow.util.grainRecord~.digest: Record grains of an incoming signal to a buffer.
grainflow.util.grainRecord~.use_when: Record grains of an incoming signal to a buffer.

grainflow.util.list~.digest: Selects from a list based on an audio value from 0-1.
grainflow.util.list~.use_when: Selects from a list based on an audio value from 0-1.

grainflow.util.multiPan~.digest: An easy way to pan grains generated with grainflow
grainflow.util.multiPan~.use_when: Compiled equal-power circular panner for grainflow grains over any number of outputs. Argument: number of output channels. Input: grains as mc channels (one per grain). Attributes: `@panCenter` (central channel) and `@panSpread` (random spread per new grain). Help also shows quantizing to discrete outputs. Use to spread grains around a speaker ring.

grainflow.util.phasor~.digest: An easy to adust phasor for granulation
grainflow.util.phasor~.use_when: An easy to adust phasor for granulation.

grainflow.util.randomRangeList.digest: Generates a random list of n elements between two numbers.
grainflow.util.randomRangeList.use_when: Generates a random list of n elements between two numbers.

grainflow.util.rateSizePhasor~.digest: A utility that translates grain rate and grain size to the phasor overlap model used in grain flow for grain scheduling.
grainflow.util.rateSizePhasor~.use_when: A utility that translates grain rate and grain size to the phasor overlap model used in grain flow for grain scheduling.

grainflow.util.record~.digest: A simple buffer recorder intended to be used with grainflow
grainflow.util.record~.use_when: A simple buffer recorder intended to be used with grainflow.

grainflow.util.sahRandom~.digest: Generates random numbers in a range whenver a grain turns off.
grainflow.util.sahRandom~.use_when: Generates random numbers in a range whenver a grain turns off.

grainflow.util.stereoPan~.digest: An easy way to pan grains generated with grainflow
grainflow.util.stereoPan~.use_when: Compiled stereo panner for grainflow grains: each new grain gets a random equal-power stereo position. Input: grains as mc channels. Attributes: `@panCenter` and `@panSpread` (randomness around the center). Use as the simplest way to turn grainflow~'s one-channel-per-grain output into stereo.

grainflow.util.vbap3d.digest: An easy way to pan grains generated with grainflow.
grainflow.util.vbap3d.use_when: **Deprecated** (help file: use grainflow.spat.pan~). Control-rate 3D vector-based panner for grains with a single position. Messages: `position`, `speakers` (xyz coordinates); falloff distance and curve settings. Kept only for old patches.

grainflow.waveform~.digest: Visualize Grainflow granulation on a waveform display
grainflow.waveform~.use_when: Visualize Grainflow granulation on a waveform display.

grainflow~.use_when: Christopher Poovey's multichannel buffer granulator, scheduled sample-accurately on the audio thread. Arguments: `<buffer~ name> <max grains> [envelope buffer]`. Inlets per help: grain clock (a phasor signal; its frequency sets grain rate and size), traversal (0–1 position in the buffer), FM in semitones, AM. Any inlet can take an mc signal, one channel per grain. Each grain comes out as its own mc channel, so follow it with a panner (grainflow.util.stereoPan~, grainflow.util.multiPan~, grainflow.spat.pan~); other outlets carry grain windows, buffer channel and grain data for grainflow.waveform~. Key attributes: `@transpose`, `@rate`, `@delay`, `@window`, `@space`, `@density`, `@direction`, `@glisson`, `@amp`, `@ngrains`, `@loopMode` (with `@startPoint` / `@stopPoint`), `@bufChans`, `@chanMode`; most have `...Offset` (per grain index) and `...Random` variants. Messages: int turns it on; `buf` / `env` / `env2D` set buffers; `g <grain> <message>` addresses one grain; `deviate`, `spread`, `randomrange` spread a parameter over grains; `streamSet`, `stream`, `nstreams` group grains; `windowMode` / `rateMode` / `delayMode` / `glissonMode` 1 or 2 read per-grain values from buffers. The trigger message was removed in 2.0. Use grainflow.util.rateSizePhasor~ to build the clock from rate and size.

gtm.markov.digest: An external for generating second-order Markov chains.
gtm.markov.use_when: An external for generating second-order Markov chains.

gtm.markov~.digest: An external for generating second-order Markov chains.
gtm.markov~.use_when: An external for generating second-order Markov chains.

..digest: (dot) - the fastest bang in the west
..use_when: Typed as `.` (file dot.mxo). Turns any message into a bang. Built-in alternative: `bangbang` (`b`).

180wrap.use_when: Wraps an angle in degrees into −180…+180 (e.g. 270 → −90). One number in, one out. Use to keep headings continuous. Built-in alternative: `pong` in wrap mode.

3Dcartopol.use_when: Converts a 3D point `x y z` (list) into `distance elevation azimuth` in degrees. Left-handed coordinate system; rotation order yaw (y-axis) then pitch (x-axis). Pairs with 3Dpoltocar.

3Dmatrix.use_when: Loads as `3Dmatrix`. Applies transforms to 3D points given as `x y z` lists: `translate x y z`, `scale x y z`, `rotate x y z`, `skew` (6 values). `order` sets the sequence using the letters t, s, r, k (e.g. `order s r k t`); order changes the result. Also `mode` (which transforms apply), `anglemode`, `reset`, `dump`, `report`. Works on plain numbers, no Jitter needed.

3Dpoltocar.digest: convert polar to cartesian coords - 1 argument (optional) : <int 0/1> mode
3Dpoltocar.use_when: Converts `distance elevation azimuth` (list, degrees) into a 3D point `x y z`. Optional argument: mode 0/1. Left-handed coordinate system. Pairs with 3Dcartopol.

_.digest: • new: prefix can be changed with set message: what is the set of set of set?
_.use_when: Typed as `_` (file underscore.mxo). Shorthand prepend: puts its argument (default `set`) in front of any message. `set <word>` changes the prefix. E.g. `_ salt 1 2 3`. Built-in alternative: `prepend`.

__.use_when: Typed as `__` (file underscoremulti.mxo). Multiple prepend: one inlet per argument, and a message arriving at an inlet leaves with that inlet's argument in front (e.g. `__ myint[0] myint[1]`). Handy with `pattrstorage`/`route` naming. Inlet count follows the number of arguments.

a2db~.digest: convert linear amplitude to decibels - float output also works w/ dsp off
a2db~.use_when: Converts linear amplitude to decibels. Signal in gives signal out; float in gives float out, even with audio off. Built-in alternatives: `atodb~`, `atodb`.

bartime.digest: display time in bar:beats:etc - Arguments 4 (optional): timesig <int><int> t/beat <int> beat div <int>
bartime.use_when: Converts a running count of time units into bar, beat and tick numbers. Arguments: time signature (two ints), time units per beat, beat division (e.g. `bartime 4 4 1000 8`). Feed a counter; outlets give bar, beat and ticks. Built-in `transport` reports bars/beats directly.

bcf2000.digest: creating a namespace with the MIDI-channel allows you to use the presets on the bcf2000, by programming each preset to a different MIDI channel
bcf2000.use_when: Parses NRPN messages from a raw MIDI stream (from `midiin`) into controller number and high-resolution value, as sent by a Behringer BCF2000. Arguments and messages `rez1`, `rez2`, `rezsplit` set the resolution of two controller ranges; `report` posts state. Built-in alternative: `nrpnin`.

bezier.digest: draw a bezier curve from control points - 1 argument (optional): dimensions 0 - 2D, 1 - 3D
bezier.use_when: Computes a Bézier curve from control points given as one list (2D: x y pairs, 3D: x y z triples). Argument: 0 = 2D, 1 = 3D. `steps` sets curve resolution; a float 0–1 or `last` reads positions; `report` posts state. Outputs points as lists for drawing or parameter paths.

bitlist.digest: pad: pad list with zeros up to pad-amount, if the list is longer the highest occurence of a 1 will determine the list-length up to the length defined by the bitwidth attribute
bitlist.use_when: Converts an int into a list of bits, or a bit list back into an int. Arguments: mode (0 lowest bit first, 1 highest first) and pad length. Messages `mode`, `pad`; attribute `bitwidth` sets 8–64-bit signed/unsigned widths. Bang repeats the last output. Values above 52 bits behave oddly.

bits2int.use_when: Converts a list of 32 bits into an integer. For more widths and modes use bitlist.

bspline.use_when: Computes a B-spline curve through a list of control points; a float 0–1 selects the position along the curve. Output is a point list, e.g. to draw a curve or fill a `table`.

bytecount.digest: returns the size of a file in bytes
bytecount.use_when: Reports the size of a file in bytes. Send `open <file>` (name in the search path or absolute path); outputs −1 if not found.

ccext.digest: it measures the deltas betweeen successive numbers, filtering any repeating numbers
ccext.use_when: Merges two 7-bit MIDI controller values (high and low byte) into one 14-bit int. `mode`: 0 defluttered (default), 1 change, 2 unfiltered, 3 deflutter only (jitter filter on single ints, replaces Eric Singer's deflutter). Built-in alternative: `xctlin`.

ceil.digest: next higher integer from float, (also in the negative range)
ceil.use_when: Rounds a float up to the next integer, also for negative numbers. Built-in alternative: `expr ceil($f1)`.

centlist.digest: value at center of gravity (interpolated between the two adjacent values)
centlist.use_when: Computes the center of gravity of a list of numbers. Outlets: the position in the list (fractional index) and the value there, interpolated between neighbours.

changelist.digest: filter out repeated lists (int/float/list/anything) - arguments (optional): set item(s) to compare with
changelist.use_when: Passes any message (int, float, symbol, list) only when it differs from the previous one. Argument, `set` or right inlet: item to compare with; `lock 1` freezes the comparison item. Built-in alternative: `zl.change`.

checklist.digest: compare int, float, list, symbol, anything - arguments (optional) item(s) to compare against:
checklist.use_when: Compares each input (any type) with a stored item and outputs 1 on match, 0 otherwise. Argument, `set` or right inlet stores the item. `mode 1` outputs only when the match state changes. Built-in alternative: `zl.compare`.

compare.digest: compare 2 elements - argument (optional): sets comparison buffer
compare.use_when: Compares two elements (a list `a b`, or input vs. the stored item from the argument or `set`). Outputs 0 if a < b, 1 if equal, 2 if a > b, −1 for a number/symbol mismatch. Built-in alternative: `zl.compare` (equality only).

comport.digest: Danger: you can open every file in your system and if suid is root damage the system.
comport.use_when: Serial port object ported from Pure Data (IEM, Winfried Ritsch). Arguments: port number and baud rate. Messages: `open <n>`, `devicename <path>`, `close`, `baud`, `bits`, `stopbit`, `parity`, `rtscts`, `xonxoff`, `dtr`, `rts`, `pollintervall`, `devices`, `info`, `verbose`, `help`. Sends and receives single bytes 0–255. Built-in alternative: `serial`.

copysign.digest: copy the sign from sign-value to value
copysign.use_when: Outputs a value carrying the sign of a second value (sign-value). Two inlets, one outlet.

createfolder.digest: NOTE: on Windows there is no creation of intermediate nested folders and creating a folder where it already exists throws an error
createfolder.use_when: Creates a folder from a path symbol, including missing parent folders on Mac. On Windows nested folders are not created and an existing folder gives an error. Pair with getpaths for base paths.

d2r.digest: degree to radians - arguments (optional): offset in degrees, mode: wrap/no wrap
d2r.use_when: Converts degrees to radians. Arguments and messages: `offset` (in degrees) and `mode` (wrap or no wrap). Built-in alternative: `expr`.

datatype.use_when: Reports the type of any input (int, float, symbol, list, anything). Two outlets report the type (as a name and as an index). Use to branch on message type.

db*~.digest: multiply signal by dB values with slide interpolation - arguments: factor, midi splitpoint, slidevalue
db*~.use_when: Typed as `db*~` (file dbmult~.mxo). Multiplies a signal by a gain given in dB, with smooth interpolation. Int ≥ 0 is read as a MIDI fader value (with a split point for 0 dB), int < 0 as dB. Arguments: factor, MIDI split point, slide. Messages `slide`, `split`, `report`. Built-in alternative: `live.gain~`.

db2a~.digest: convert decibels to linear amplitude - arguments (optional): unity MIDI-value (0 dB), ramptime
db2a~.use_when: Converts decibels to linear amplitude. Signal in gives signal out; float in gives float out, even with audio off. Integers are read as MIDI values mapped from +12 dB down to −96 dB. Arguments: MIDI value for 0 dB (default 84) and ramp time (sent as second list element for `line~`); message `ramptime`. Built-in alternatives: `dbtoa~`, `dbtoa`.

dcblocker~.use_when: Removes DC offset from a signal with a one-pole/one-zero filter (y(n) = x(n) − x(n−1) + R·y(n−1)). `coef` sets the cutoff (default 63 ≈ −3 dB at 10 Hz). Built-in alternative: `biquad~` with DC-blocking coefficients.

deltalist.digest: subtract one list from another, member by member, right list determines length - argument <int> (optional): mode
deltalist.use_when: Subtracts one list from another element by element; the right (stored) list sets the output length. Argument and `mode` choose which list is subtracted from which. Built-in alternative: `vexpr`.

detox.digest: extract value and content from xml-tag-structures - argument (optional): <int> 0/1 mode
detox.use_when: Parses one line of XML at a time: outputs tag type, tag content, attribute value(s) and the current tag tree. `mode 0/1` switches attribute parsing (one value or all name:value pairs); `reset` clears the tag tree. Pair with toxine (file reading) and intox (writing).

dist~.digest: distance gain: logarithmic - argument (optional): dB drop per distance unit
dist~.use_when: Converts distance (signal or `dist` message) into a gain signal that drops logarithmically. Argument and `db_unit`: dB drop per distance unit. Use for distance attenuation.

duplist.digest: works in the full 32-bit integer range
duplist.use_when: Removes duplicate numbers from a list of ints (full 32-bit range). Built-in alternative: `zl.thin`.

dynroute.digest: based on jhno's xroute / dynamic selector, passthrough switchable
dynroute.use_when: Route with a changeable selector: attributes `@selector` (what to match), `@position` (which list element to test, default 1) and `@mode` (1 passes the matched element through). Match goes left, misses right. Based on jhno's xroute. Built-in alternative: `route`.

euler_constant.digest: outputs the euler constant and it's reciprocal
euler_constant.use_when: Also typed as `e`. Multiplies the input (default 1) by e and by 1/e; two outlets. Built-in alternative: `expr`.

exp.digest: e^n (euler constant raised to nth power)
exp.use_when: Outputs e raised to the input power. Built-in alternative: `expr exp($f1)`.

exp2.use_when: Outputs 2 raised to the input power. Built-in alternative: `pow`.

filemanager.digest: deep contents: iterate through folder in depth
filemanager.use_when: Mac-only file system external. Messages: `copy <src> <dst>`, `move <src> <dst>`, `rename <file> <newname>`, `replace <file> <new>`, `delete <path>` (cannot be undone), `mkdir <path>`, `contents <folder>`, `deepcontents <folder>`, `getpaths all` / `getpaths patcherpath`. Results can go to a `dict`; another outlet reports success 0/1.

floor.digest: next lower integer from float (also in the negative range)
floor.use_when: Rounds a float down to the next integer, also for negative numbers. Built-in alternative: `expr floor($f1)`.

fromascii.use_when: Converts ASCII character codes back into symbols and numbers. Pairs with toascii. Built-in alternative: `itoa`.

gaze.use_when: Perspective projection of 3D points to 2D screen coordinates plus depth. Set the camera with `eye x y z` and `poi x y z` (point of interest), `fov`, `roll`, `yaw`, `pitch`, `size`, `range`, `mode`; `reset`, `report`, `dump`. Input a point `x y z`; outputs projected x/y and z depth.

getenv.digest: get system paths (on Mac OS wraps shell commands)
getenv.use_when: Reads a system environment variable by name (e.g. `USERPROFILE`, `APPDATA`, `PATH`). On Windows it is an external; on Mac there is no external and it loads patchers/getenv.maxpat, which uses shell commands. For Mac system folders see getpaths.

getpaths.digest: get various paths from the operating system (Mac OS only, for Windows see getenv)
getpaths.use_when: Mac-only external that outputs system paths such as `home`, `desktop` and `user_library` as `<name> <path>` messages (bang or `dump`). Route by name and pass through `conformpath` if needed. Pairs with createfolder.

goldensection.digest: calculates the golden section and it's reciprocal
goldensection.use_when: Multiplies the input (default 1) by the golden ratio and by its reciprocal; two outlets. Built-in alternative: `expr`.

groupid.digest: generates group id numbers for instance managment - keeps internal map of assigned numbers and reassigns freed ones- arguments (optional): <int> group - default 0, <int> active - 0/1- default 1
groupid.use_when: Gives each instance a unique ID number within a group and reuses freed numbers. Arguments: group (default 0) and active 0/1 (default 1). Messages: `getID`, `setgroup <n>`, `getinfo`, `getgroup`, `getcount`, `getlength`, `getmap`. Use to number copies of an abstraction.

heading.digest: HEADING - The direction in which a vessel's bow points at any given time.
heading.use_when: Converts joystick or tablet x/y tilt into heading (degrees) and absolute tilt. Arguments: tilt scale factor, then x and y offset (e.g. `heading 1 -64 -64` for 0–127 controllers); message `offset x y`. Built-in alternative: `cartopol`.

hexlist.digest: convert ascii coded 8 digit hexlist to integer
hexlist.use_when: Converts a list of eight ASCII codes of hex digits into one integer (e.g. for the DIN66019II display protocol). Built-in alternatives: `itoa` then `fromsymbol`.

hsv2rgb.digest: convert hsv to rgb and vice versa - arguments: <int> mode 0/1
hsv2rgb.use_when: Converts a color between HSV and RGB; all values 0–1 as a 3-element list. Argument/`mode`: 0 HSV→RGB, 1 RGB→HSV. Scale up for 0–255 drawing colors.

hypot.digest: The longest leg of a right triangle (which is the side opposite the right angle). The word derives from the Greek hypo- ("under") and teinein "(to stretch)."
hypot.use_when: Computes the hypotenuse sqrt(a²+b²) from two sides (two inlets); e.g. a point's distance from the center. Built-in alternative: `expr sqrt($f1*$f1+$f2*$f2)`.

idx.digest: lock throughput once the upper limit of the range is reached, set lock to 0 or hit reset or set new min value to unlock, set new max value to extend limit and keep going
idx.use_when: Extended counter that prefixes an index to any message (or outputs the count on bang). Arguments: min, max, step, lock (default 0 255 1 1). Messages: `min`, `max`, `step`, `lock`, `offset`, `goto`, `set`, `reset`, `clear`, `dump`, `report`. With lock on it stops at max until reset or a new max.

insertlist.digest: insert items into a list - arguments (optional) item(s) to insert into
insertlist.use_when: Inserts items into a stored list at a position. Argument or `set` / right inlet: the list to insert into; `position <n>` sets where; the incoming list is the new items. Built-in alternative: `array.insert` (on array objects).

interpol.digest: send 2 lists (not necessesarily floats, can be mixed ) the shorter one determines the length of the output-list
interpol.use_when: Interpolates between two lists (shorter list sets the length). Send the two lists; a float 0–1 gives an in-between list (values beyond extrapolate), a bang steps from the first to the second list in `steps` steps. Arguments: steps, mode, then optional initial lists; do not mix @ attributes with plain arguments. `mode` sets float direction; `report`.

intox.use_when: Indents one XML line (symbol) according to tag nesting, for writing formatted XML files with toxine. Pairs with detox.

ldexp.use_when: Outputs value × 2^exponent (value left, exponent right or argument). Built-in alternative: `expr`.

log.use_when: Natural logarithm of the input. Built-in alternative: `expr ln($f1)`.

log10.use_when: Base-10 logarithm of the input. Built-in alternative: `expr log10($f1)`.

log2.use_when: Base-2 logarithm of the input. Built-in alternative: `expr`.

logb.use_when: Outputs the binary exponent (logb) of the input. Built-in alternative: `expr`.

mathlist.digest: basic math-operations on lists - arguments: op (symbol), (float/int) operand
mathlist.use_when: Applies one operation to every element of a list. Arguments: operator symbol then operand (e.g. `mathlist >> 8`). Operators: add sub mult div + - * / >> << !- !/ == != >= <= > < ~ ^ & | && || pow exp sqrt. Built-in alternative: `vexpr`.

memchr.digest: The memchr() function locates the first occurrence of c (converted to an unsigned char) in the initial n bytes (each interpreted as unsigned char) of the object pointed to by s.
memchr.use_when: C-string search: finds the position of a character (argument, default `:`) within the first n characters of a symbol. Arguments: character, n, mode (0 search input, 1 swap roles); message `mode`. Built-in alternative: `string.indexof`.

memcmp.digest: compare characters in string of n characters - arguments: string 2 (symbol), n (int) default 1, mode (int 0/1) default 0
memcmp.use_when: C-string compare of the first n characters of two symbols; outputs match 1/0 and a status. Arguments: second string, n, mode. Built-in alternative: `string.compare`.

memcpy.digest: The memcpy() function copies n bytes from the object pointed to by s2 into the object pointed to by s1. If copying takes place between objects that overlap, the behaviour is undefined.
memcpy.use_when: C-string copy of n characters from string 2 into string 1. Arguments: string 2, n, mode (swap direction). Built-in alternative: `string.replace`.

memmove.digest: copy n characters from src to dst by position - arguments: string 2 (symbol), n (int) default 1, src_pos (int) default 1, dst_pos (int) default 1, mode (int 0/1) default 0
memmove.use_when: C-string copy of n characters between two symbols at set positions. Arguments: string 2, n, src_pos, dst_pos, mode; messages `src_pos`, `dst_pos`, `mode`. Built-in alternative: `string.replace`.

memset.digest: The memset() function copies c (converted to an unsigned char) into each of the first n bytes of the object pointed to by s.
memset.use_when: Overwrites n characters of a symbol with one character (argument, default `/`), at the front (mode 0) or back (mode 1). Built-in alternative: `string.replace`.

mmmlist.digest: minimum, maximum and mean on a list - arguments: mode 0/1
mmmlist.use_when: Outputs the minimum, maximum and mean of a list of numbers. `mode` chooses one list output or separate outlets. Feed from streamlist for running statistics. Built-in alternatives: `array.min`, `array.max`, `array.mean`.

mtx.digest: mutually exclusive switching, global scope, switching by groups, dynamic group binding
mtx.use_when: Mutually exclusive switch: all `mtx` objects in the same group act like one radio group: switching one on switches the others off. Group set by argument, `@group` attribute, or `set <group>`; groups are global across all loaded patches. Wire toggles in and out. Built-in alternative: `radiogroup`.

multisplit.digest: split a stream of values into different ranges - arguments (int, float): at least 3 arguments, defining ranges (max 256)
multisplit.use_when: Sorts numbers into ranges. Arguments: at least 3 split points (max 256); outlets depend on the number of split points, and ranges include the lower point but not the upper. With no arguments it outputs the range index (−1 out of range). A list sets new split points. Outlet count follows the arguments.

n!.use_when: Outputs the factorial of an integer. Built-in alternative: `expr`.

nn2bits.use_when: Converts an integer into a list of 32 bits. For more widths and modes use bitlist.

p4mat.use_when: Formats `<name> <values>` messages into the form `pattrforward` expects, so one stream can address several named objects. Place before `pattrforward`.

panner~.use_when: Abstraction: constant-power stereo panner built on `matrix~`. Left inlet mono signal, right inlet pan position (argument sets the start, e.g. `panner~ 0.5`); outlets left and right signal.

peakfollow~.digest: follows signals straight up, decays exponentially - argument: (in/float, optional): decay time (default 1000)
peakfollow~.use_when: Envelope follower: rises instantly to peaks, then decays exponentially. Argument and `decay`: time in ms to fall to half (default 1000). Outlets: envelope signal and a 0/1 signal for falling/rising. Built-in alternatives: `slide~`, `peakamp~`.

peaklist.digest: reads list from front to back, if two identical high values are present, the one occuring later in the list is output
peaklist.use_when: Finds the highest value in a list (or lowest, set by the `mode` argument/message) and its zero-based index. If the top value occurs twice, the later one is reported. Built-in alternative: `array.max`.

pi_constant.use_when: Also typed as `pi`. Multiplies the input (default 1) by pi and by 1/pi; two outlets. Built-in alternative: `expr`.

piwrap.use_when: Wraps an angle in radians into −pi…+pi. Built-in alternative: `pong` in wrap mode.

pop.digest: positive counter: multiple bangs / negative counter: filtered bangs
pop.use_when: Bang counter. Argument/right inlet: count. A positive count repeats each input as that many bangs; a negative count passes only every nth input. Built-in alternatives: `uzi`, `counter`.

posit.digest: output attributes for each named object: class, scripting-name, box-coordinates, patcher name
posit.use_when: Patcher inspection by scripting name. Messages: `getinfo`, `getname`, `setname <name>`, `query <name>`, `names`, `objects`, `class <class>`, `rename <old> <new>`, plus `.global` versions (`names.global`, `objects.global`, `class.global`, `query.global`, `rename.global`) for all loaded patchers, and `colls` / `buffers` to list all coll and buffer~ names. Outputs class, scripting name, box coordinates and patcher name; right outlet found 0/1. Built-in alternatives: `thispatcher`, `v8`.

processes.digest: send commands to porcesses: experimental (mac OS only)
processes.use_when: Experimental Mac-only external that controls other applications: `set_process <app name>`, then `activate`, `showhide`, `kill`; `activateself` brings Max to the front. The help warns that unfinished functions crash Max. Use with care.

r2d.digest: radians to degrees - arguments (optional) offset in degrees, mode wrap/no wrap
r2d.use_when: Converts radians to degrees. Arguments and messages: `offset` (degrees, for coordinate correction) and `mode` (wrap to −180…180 or not). Built-in alternative: `expr`.

replacelist.digest: replace items in one list by new item(s) at specific position - arguments (optional) item(s) to replace into
replacelist.use_when: Replaces items in a stored list starting at a position. Argument or `set` / right inlet: the list to replace into; `position <n>`; the incoming items are the replacements. Built-in alternative: `array.replace` (on array objects).

rgb2yuv.use_when: Converts a 3-value color list from RGB to YUV (mode 0) or YUV to RGB (mode 1). Arguments: mode, YUV offset (default 16); message `yuvoffset`. For matrices use `jit.colorspace`.

rotatexyz.digest: quaternion rotation angle axis from xyz angles - argument (optional): prefix 1/0 (default 1)
rotatexyz.use_when: Converts x, y, z rotation angles (list) into an angle-axis rotation `angle x y z`, prefixed with `rotate` when `prefix` is 1 (default), ready for OpenGL objects such as `jit.gl.sketch`. Built-in alternatives: `jit.euler2quat` then `jit.quat2axis`.

slicelist.digest: slice list into sublists - arguments (mandatory): outlets, slicesize
slicelist.use_when: Cuts a list into sublists of a set size, one per outlet. Arguments: number of outlets, slice size, optional start position (with outlets ≤ 2 it runs single-slice mode). Messages `size`, `pos`, `mode`. Outlet count follows the first argument. Built-in alternative: `zl.iter`.

slidelist.digest: slide lowpass filter for lists, ints & floats - argument (optional): slide <float> default 1
slidelist.use_when: Slide (one-pole lowpass) filter applied element-wise to lists, ints and floats: y(n) = y(n−1) + (x(n) − y(n−1))/slide. Argument and `slide`: smoothing amount (default 1 = none); `clear`, `set`. Built-in alternative: `slide` (single numbers).

statlist.use_when: Statistics on a list of numbers. Outputs mean, average deviation, standard deviation, variance, skewness, kurtosis, min and max. Built-in alternatives: `array.mean`, `array.stddev`.

str2ul.digest: convert case of alphabetic characters - arguments: mode (int 0/1) default 0
str2ul.use_when: Converts the letters of a symbol to upper case (mode 0) or lower case (mode 1). Argument/`mode`. Built-in alternatives: `string.toupper`, `string.tolower`.

strcat.use_when: Joins two symbols: string 2 (argument or right inlet) is appended to string 1; `mode 1` swaps the order. Built-in alternatives: `string.concat`, `combine`.

strchr.digest: The strchr() function shall locate the first occurrence of c (converted to a char) in the string pointed to by s. The terminating null byte is considered to be part of the string.
strchr.use_when: Finds the position of the first occurrence of a character in a symbol. Argument/right inlet: the other string; `mode` swaps roles. Built-in alternative: `string.indexof`.

strcmp.use_when: Compares two symbols (strcmp): outputs the comparison result and match 1/0. Argument/right inlet: string 2; `mode` swaps order. Built-in alternative: `string.compare`.

strcoll.digest: The strcoll() function shall compare the string pointed to by s1 to the string pointed to by s2, both interpreted as appropriate to the LC_COLLATE category of the current locale.
strcoll.use_when: Compares two symbols using the system locale's sort order: result < 0, 0 or > 0, plus match 1/0. Argument/right inlet: string 2; `mode`. Built-in alternative: `string.compare`.

strcpy.digest: string copying (somewhat useless in this context) - arguments: string 2 (symbol) default <none>, mode (0/1) default 0
strcpy.use_when: C strcpy: copies string 2 over string 1; `mode` swaps direction. The help calls it somewhat useless in Max.

strcspn.digest: The strcspn() function shall compute the length (in bytes) of the maximum initial segment of the string pointed to by s1 which consists entirely of bytes not from the string pointed to by s2.
strcspn.use_when: Counts the characters of a symbol before the first character that appears in a second string (full length if none). Argument/right inlet: string 2; `mode`. Built-in alternative: `regexp`.

strcut.digest: terminate string at position - arguments: position (int) default 0, mode (0/1) default 0
strcut.use_when: Cuts a symbol at a position into two parts. Argument/right inlet: position; `mode` sets output order. Pair with strrchr to split file paths at the last slash. Built-in alternative: `string.slice`.

streamlist.digest: be careful when connecting this to "normal" max-objects, the 256 limit on lists can make them bomb when fed a larger list !
streamlist.use_when: Shift register: collects incoming floats, ints, lists or symbols into a rolling list of the most recent items. Argument/`length`: size (max 1024, default 1024); `reset`, `clear`. Long lists can break objects with small list limits. Built-in alternative: `zl.stream`.

strfilt.digest: several filters can be applied at the same time (up to all 12 of them)
strfilt.use_when: Keeps only the characters of chosen types. Argument or `mode` with up to 12 C ctype names, e.g. `isalpha`, `isdigit`, `ispunct`, `isblank`, `islower`, `isupper`; outputs the filtered symbol and its length. Built-in alternative: `regexp`.

stricmp.digest: compare two strings case insensitive - arguments: string 2 (symbol), mode (0/1)
stricmp.use_when: Compares two symbols ignoring case; outputs result and match 1/0. Argument/right inlet: string 2; `mode`. Built-in alternative: `string.compare`.

strlen.use_when: Outputs the number of characters in a symbol. Built-in alternative: `string.length`.

strncat.digest: string concate n chars - arguments: string 2 (symbol), number of chracters (int >= 1), mode (0/1)
strncat.use_when: Appends the first n characters of string 2 to string 1. Arguments: string 2, n (≥ 1), mode. Built-in alternative: `string.concat`.

strncmp.digest: compare two strings for n chars - arguments: string 2 (symbol), num chars (int, < 4096), mode (0/1) default 0
strncmp.use_when: Compares the first n characters of two symbols; outputs result and match 1/0. Arguments: string 2, n (< 4096), mode; an int sets n. Built-in alternative: `string.compare`.

strncpy.digest: string n character copy - arguments: string 2 (symbol) default <none>, mode (0/1) default 0
strncpy.use_when: Copies the first n characters of one symbol into another. Arguments: string 2, mode; an int sets n. Built-in alternative: `string.substring`.

strpbrk.digest: The strpbrk() function shall locate the first occurrence in the string pointed to by s1 of any byte from the string pointed to by s2.
strpbrk.use_when: Finds characters from a set in a symbol, e.g. `strpbrk "1234567890." 1` pulls the number out of `120.5bpm-lowBD`. Arguments: character set, mode (0 sequential, 1 grouped output). Built-in alternative: `regexp`.

strrchr.digest: The strrchr() function shall locate the last occurrence of c (converted to a char) in the string pointed to by s. The terminating null byte is considered to be part of the string.
strrchr.use_when: Finds the position of the last occurrence of a character in a symbol (e.g. `strrchr /`). Pair with strcut to split a file path. Built-in alternative: `string.indexof`.

strrcut.digest: remove stringsection before position - arguments: position (int) default 0, mode (0/1) default 0
strrcut.use_when: Removes the part of a symbol before a position and outputs both parts. Argument/right inlet: position; `mode` sets output order. Built-in alternative: `string.slice`.

strspn.digest: The strspn() function shall compute the length (in bytes) of the maximum initial segment of the string pointed to by s1 which consists entirely of bytes from the string pointed to by s2.
strspn.use_when: Counts the leading characters of a symbol that all belong to a character set. Argument/right inlet: the set; `mode`. Built-in alternative: `regexp`.

strstr.digest: The strstr() function shall locate the first occurrence in the string pointed to by s1 of the sequence of bytes (excluding the terminating null byte) in the string pointed to by s2.
strstr.use_when: Finds the position of string 2 inside string 1 (C strstr). Argument/right inlet: string 2; `mode` swaps roles. Its help file demonstrates strspn instead, and inlet/outlet counts are unconfirmed. Built-in alternative: `string.indexof`.

strtok.digest: slice string into tokens at delimiter - arguments: string 2 (symbol), mode (0/1)
strtok.use_when: Splits a symbol into tokens at a delimiter character (argument or right inlet, e.g. `strtok /`); `mode` swaps roles. Use to split file paths. Built-in alternatives: `fromsymbol @separator`, `string.split`.

sumlist.digest: calculate the sum of a list
sumlist.use_when: Adds up all numbers in a list. Built-in alternative: `zl.sum`.

timestamp.use_when: Outputs the system date and time with milliseconds as a list (year month day hour minute second ms). Messages `date`, `ms`, `ticks`, `mode`. Built-in alternatives: `date`, `cpuclock`.

timex.digest: convert time to ms and vice-versa, outputs as float, list or symbol - argument (int, optional): display mode, default 0: set <symbol>
timex.use_when: Converts between milliseconds and `hours:min:sec:ms` text. An int is read as ms, a float as seconds, a symbol or text in many shorthand forms (any non-number character is a delimiter, e.g. `2..` or `..4.`). Argument/`mode`: output as list, float or `set <symbol>` for display. Floats lose precision above about 18 hours.

toascii.use_when: Converts symbols and numbers into lists of ASCII character codes. Pairs with fromascii. Built-in alternative: `atoi`.

toxine.digest: read and write file from/to disk by lines
toxine.use_when: Reads and writes text files line by line. Writing: `write <filename>`, then `line <symbol>` for each line, then `close` (or bang). Reading: `read` outputs each line; flags report read/write state and line count. Pairs with detox and intox for XML. Built-in alternative: `text`.

xframe~.digest: xframe~ generates a list of the amplitude in all the FFT-bins below Nyquist & statistics on spectrum - arguments: <int> FFT-size
xframe~.use_when: Takes FFT frames from `fft~` (argument: FFT size, e.g. `xframe~ 1024`) and outputs a list of bin amplitudes below Nyquist, plus spectrum statistics: max, mean, average and standard deviation, variance, skew, kurtosis, max bin index. Based on frame~ by j.jester.

xorlist.digest: calculate the accumulated xor vales of a list from one member to the next - minimum length 2 elements, ints only
xorlist.use_when: Computes the running XOR of a list of integers from one element to the next (minimum 2 elements), e.g. a serial-protocol checksum.

jk.lpx.digest: Lightshow randomizes the lights on your Launchpad X in different ways.
jk.lpx.use_when: Link one pad or button of a Novation Launchpad X to a live.text or live.menu. Use one jk.lpx per pad, together with one jk.lpxcore in the patch. Attributes: @pad (0-63 from lower left) or @button (lowercase button name, e.g. sessionmixer, scene1), @oncolor / @offcolor (k, w, r, m, o, y, g, c, p, b, plus d-suffixed dimmed versions), @texton / @textoff, @mode t (toggle), b (button) or r (radio), @radio <group>, @menu <item count>, @liveexclude. Inlets: from the output of live.menu and live.text; outlets: polypressure, to live.menu, pad number and velocity, to live.text.

jk.lpxcore.digest: Lightshow randomizes the lights on your Launchpad X in different ways.
jk.lpxcore.use_when: The one-per-patch part of jk.lpx for a Novation Launchpad X: MIDI input/output port menus (connect umenus as its comments describe), reset/initialize, all-pads-black, color theme 1-3, and a random light show (toggle on/off, speed in ms). Place it once alongside any number of jk.lpx pad objects.

karma~.use_when: Varispeed live looper on a named buffer~ (by Rodrigo Constanzo). Arguments: buffer~ name (required), channel count 1, 2 or 4 (sets the number of audio inlets and outlets). Inlets: audio (one per channel), then speed (signal or float; 1 normal, 0.5 half speed, 2 double). Outlets: audio, an optional audio-rate sync phase 0-1 when @syncout 1, and a list with position, play state, record state, start/end (ms), window size. Messages: record (first press starts a loop, while playing starts overdub), play, stop (also closes the first loop), append, overdub <amplitude>, jump <0-1>, position, window, setloop, resetloop, set <buffer> to switch buffers. Attributes: interp, ramp, snramp, snrcurv, report. Use for live looping beyond what groove~ plus record~ give easily.

mat.oocall.use_when: Call a piece of patch code that lives in one place (a `mat.oomethod` with the same name) from anywhere, and get its answer out of this box's outlet, like calling a function. The argument is the method name (`mat.oocall tonalize`). Inlet 1: the message or bang to send (starts the call); inlet 2: a symbol that switches to another method name; inlet 3 or `@parent <symbol>`: a 'this' name delivered to the method's right outlet just before the call. The answer only comes back if the method replies at once in the same message chain: no `delay`, `pipe` or `deferlow` inside the method.

mat.oomethod.use_when: Hold the shared code that `mat.oocall <name>` boxes call. Argument: the method name. Left outlet: whatever the caller sent into its left inlet; right outlet: the caller's parent name, if set (sent first). Send the result into the inlet and it returns only to the caller that asked. Inside an abstraction name methods `#1.<name>`, so `plasticCup joesCup` answers `mat.oocall joesCup.color`; wiring outlet to a `v` and back into the inlet makes a property (a bang reads, anything else writes).

jit.ml.lzw.digest: Lemper-Ziv-Welch string based compression for Jitter matrices.
jit.ml.lzw.use_when: Lemper-Ziv-Welch string based compression for Jitter matrices.

ml.art.digest: Fuzzy Adaptive Resonance Theory Neural Network
ml.art.use_when: Fuzzy Adaptive Resonance Theory Neural Network.

ml.kdtree.digest: k-d tree: organize "k" dimensioned data into a binary-tree for improved, and nearest neighbor searching.
ml.kdtree.use_when: k-d tree: organize "k" dimensioned data into a binary-tree for improved, and nearest neighbor searching.

ml.scale.digest: Uses distribution of elements to scale lists to -1./1
ml.scale.use_when: Uses distribution of elements to scale lists to -1./1.

ml.vmm.bin.digest: Binary CTW Variable order Markov Model Predictor
ml.vmm.bin.use_when: Binary CTW Variable order Markov Model Predictor.

ml.vmm.ppm.digest: Prediction by Partial Matchh Markov Model
ml.vmm.ppm.use_when: Prediction by Partial Matchh Markov Model.

mo.adc~.digest: Output audio signals from hardware input devices, and control gain.
mo.adc~.use_when: Multi-channel audio-input abstraction with built-in gain control. Wraps native adc~ with voice-aware gain UI. Use as a hardware-input stage when you want a uniform mo.* look across an installation patch.

mo.arrow.digest: Use keyboard's arrows to trigger events.
mo.arrow.use_when: Trigger events with the keyboard arrow keys. Outputs per-direction triggers. Use as a no-MIDI keyboard control surface for navigation, transport, or selection in performance patches.

mo.average.digest: Adjust mode (normal, absolute) and sensitivity to input data.
mo.average.use_when: Averages the values of an incoming list: sums the list and divides by its length, then outputs one number clipped to -1..1. `sensitivity <0.–1.>` shapes the result with a power curve; `mode 1` takes the absolute value of the result. Use in modulo chains to reduce several control channels (for example several sensor axes) to one overall value.

mo.calibrate.digest: Calibrate minimum and maximum input over an adjustable time window (s).
mo.calibrate.use_when: Auto-calibrate min/max input over an adjustable time window (seconds). Use for auto-ranging incoming sensor data — start the window, wave the sensor through its full range, get a normalised output afterward.

mo.click.use_when: Multi-mode click behaviour — single, double, hold, etc. Use to expand mouse-click input into multiple events (different actions for different click types) without writing the timing logic.

mo.cpu.digest: Keep track of your CPU utilization.
mo.cpu.use_when: CPU-utilisation tracker. `rate` selects polling interval (0=100ms, 1=500, 2=1000, 3=2000, 4=5000ms). Use to display Max's own CPU load in a performance UI.

mo.crosspatch.use_when: Visual cable-patching UI for routing a list of data inputs to outputs. Click a cable + Backspace to delete. Use for performer-friendly visual routing — drag cables to reroute control streams during performance.

mo.crosspatch~.digest: A multichannel audio signal routing object.
mo.crosspatch~.use_when: Audio version of mo.crosspatch — multichannel signal routing via visual cables. Click + Backspace to delete a connection. Use for ad-hoc multichannel audio routing UI in performance patches.

mo.ctlout.digest: Send continuous MIDI control change values to a MIDI device.
mo.ctlout.use_when: Single-voice MIDI continuous-controller output. Wraps native ctlout with mo.* UI. Use as the standard MIDI CC output in modulo patches.

mo.ctlouts.digest: Send continuous control change values to a MIDI device.
mo.ctlouts.use_when: Multi-voice MIDI CC output — sends a list of CC values to multiple controllers in one object. Use when you need to output many CCs from a list in one place rather than N parallel ctlouts.

mo.cue.digest: Set numbered cues and trigger events.
mo.cue.use_when: Numbered cue trigger system — set cues, recall by number to fire events. Use as a cueing engine for theatrical or installation patches where multiple events need to be recalled by index.

mo.dac~.digest: Send multichannel audio signals to hardware devices.
mo.dac~.use_when: Multi-channel audio-output abstraction with voice-aware gain. Use as the standard hardware-output stage in mo.* patches.

mo.date.digest: Keep track of today's time and date.
mo.date.use_when: Output today's date and time. Use as a clock source for time-stamped logs, scheduled events, or display in installation UIs.

mo.debounce.digest: Useful to filter out jittery values like buttons coming from Arduino.
mo.debounce.use_when: Debounce filter — suppresses rapid value changes shorter than a configurable interval (try 500 ms). Filters jitter from buttons (Arduino, MIDI controllers, mechanical switches). Use whenever a digital sensor produces noisy edges that fire native edge detectors multiple times per real event.

mo.dial.digest: Map this object to a MIDI controller.
mo.dial.use_when: Multi-voice rotary dial array — map to MIDI controller for instant tactile control. Use as a uniform dial UI when you have a knob-style controller and want to drive multiple parameters from one object.

mo.encoder.digest: Map this object to a MIDI controller. Can be controlled by any value (standard is 63-65).
mo.encoder.use_when: Multi-voice incremental encoder UI. Default uses 63/65 increment values (standard relative-encoder convention) but configurable. Map to a MIDI encoder controller. Use for endless-rotation encoder support without abs-position assumptions.

mo.fm~.use_when: FM synthesizer abstraction. Drive with a list of normalised values (0–1) or specific messages. Parameters: carrier, harmonicity, modulation index, etc. Use as a self-contained FM voice — quicker than rolling cycle~ + cycle~ + arithmetic per voice.

mo.gain~.digest: Hold SHIFT+Drag to control all channels simultaneusly.
mo.gain~.use_when: Multi-channel gain UI. SHIFT+drag controls all channels simultaneously. Use as the standard gain stage in mo.* signal chains.

mo.ggate.digest: The number of voices divides the right value equally.
mo.ggate.use_when: Multi-voice gate — divides a value range equally between N voices. Use for distributing a single control value across multiple gated channels (e.g. one CC controls panning across N speakers).

mo.granulator~.digest: A eight-phase shifted stereo granular synthesizer.
mo.granulator~.use_when: Eight-phase shifted stereo granular synthesizer. Drive with normalised list (0–1) or specific messages: (playstop), (mode), playback rate, grain size, etc. Use as a self-contained stereo granular voice without rolling phasor~ + tapout~ chains.

mo.grid.use_when: Step-grid sequencer with constraint and direction controls. Set step count, value constraints, and direction (forward/backward/random). Use for grid-based sequencing where step values fill a 2D pattern.

mo.gridmeter~.digest: Display multichannel signals level as brightness.
mo.gridmeter~.use_when: Multichannel signal-level grid display — channels as brightness-modulated cells. Click to mute/unmute per channel. Use for compact level monitoring of large channel counts (16+).

mo.hi.digest: Provides input from human-interface device interfaces (Trackpad, Gamepad, etc.)
mo.hi.use_when: Generic Human-Interface Device input — trackpads, gamepads, etc. Wraps native hi with voice-aware UI. Use for HID device input without configuring native hi manually.

mo.hrslider.use_when: Horizontal range slider (low-high pair). Constructor args set the (0., 1.) min/max range. Use to define a numerical range graphically (e.g. min/max for randomisation).

mo.hslider.digest: Map this object to a MIDI controller.
mo.hslider.use_when: Horizontal slider — map to MIDI controller. Use as the standard horizontal-slider UI in mo.* patches.

mo.htab.digest: Set the number of tabs and each item's name.
mo.htab.use_when: Horizontal tab UI with named items. Set tab count and item names. Use as a discrete-state selector with friendly labels (cleaner than radiogroup for named states).

mo.if.digest: Use conditional statements to process input data.
mo.if.use_when: Conditional comparison object. `condition` selects operator (1==, 2!=, 3>, 4>=, 5<, 6<=). Use for cleaner inline conditionals than native if statement object — UI exposes the operator choice.

mo.joystick.digest: Output data when passing a certain higher and lower threshold.
mo.joystick.use_when: Joystick input with per-axis dual-threshold output (high and low). Set origin and sensitivity. Use for joystick-driven event triggering — fires events when an axis crosses a threshold rather than continuously streaming.

mo.key.digest: Use spacebar, esc and return keys to trigger events.
mo.key.use_when: Keyboard event trigger. `key` ASCII code (32=space default, 27=esc, 13=return). Use for keyboard-shortcut event triggers without rolling key + select chains.

mo.keyboard.digest: Output numbers from an onscreen keyboard.
mo.keyboard.use_when: On-screen keyboard with mode select: 1=monophonic, 2=polyphonic, 3=touchscreen. Use as a built-in keyboard UI for note input in performance patches.

mo.latch.digest: Output greater/lower value from a list of data.
mo.latch.use_when: Outputs the greatest or the lowest value of an incoming list, chosen by `mode` (its mode inlet or argument); repeated identical results are filtered out. Use to follow the strongest (or weakest) of several parallel modulo control channels.

mo.launch.digest: Input, or drag and drop anything. Follow with a bang to launch.
mo.launch.use_when: Drag-and-drop launcher. Drag any file/folder into the UI; click to search disk; bang to launch. Use as a simple file-picker / launcher in installation UIs.

mo.led.use_when: Multi-state LED indicator. `outline mode` toggles active/inactive boundary look. Use for compact multi-state display in performance UIs.

mo.lfo~.digest: Output audio signal from the left outlet, data from the right.
mo.lfo~.use_when: LFO with both signal and data outputs. Configurable jitter, smoothing, offset, and depth. Left outlet = signal, right = control data. Use as a one-stop LFO when you need both signal-rate (for audio modulation) and event-rate (for parameter modulation) streams.

mo.line.digest: Ramp a list of data within a specific amount of time.
mo.line.use_when: Ramp a list of values over time — list-domain line~. Useful for filtering and smoothing parameter streams. Use to crossfade multi-channel parameters synchronously.

mo.makenote.use_when: Multi-voice makenote with optional probability per note. Inputs: pitch, velocity, duration, probability. Use for generative MIDI sequencing where some notes should be probabilistically suppressed.

mo.map.use_when: Universal MIDI/keyboard parameter mapper. Use a controller or computer keyboard to map any parameters in the patch; ESC to exit mapping mode. Use for runtime-configurable controller mapping without writing a separate map-saving system.

mo.matrix.use_when: Click-to-enable matrix routing for list data. Allows multi-input/multi-output connections; auto-loads on patch load. Use for fixed routing matrices (vs mo.crosspatch's cable-style UI) in installation patches.

mo.matrix~.digest: A multichannel audio signal matrix object.
mo.matrix~.use_when: Multichannel audio matrix routing — click cells to enable/disable connections. Use for fixed multichannel audio routing matrices.

mo.meter~.digest: The module will adapt to the number of signals.
mo.meter~.use_when: Multichannel meter that auto-adapts to incoming signal count. Use as a uniform meter object across channel counts without specifying voice count manually.

mo.midiin.digest: Choose your MIDI device from the pup-up menu.
mo.midiin.use_when: MIDI input from a chosen device. `high resolution mode` 1=Off (0–127), 2=Float (-1 to 1), 3=14-bit Fixed (-8192 to 8191). Use for general-purpose MIDI input with mode-controlled output range.

mo.midiout.digest: Choose your MIDI device from the pup-up menu.
mo.midiout.use_when: MIDI output to a chosen device. Same `high resolution mode` options as mo.midiin. Use as the universal MIDI-output companion to mo.midiin.

mo.minmax.digest: Calibrate minimum and maximum looking at highest and lowest values.
mo.minmax.use_when: Adaptive min/max calibration — tracks highest and lowest seen values continuously. Use for auto-ranging that updates throughout a session (vs mo.calibrate's fixed-window approach).

mo.monitor.use_when: Message-stream monitor — keeps a running display of incoming messages. Use for inline patch debugging without sending to the Max console.

mo.mouse.digest: set the 0,0 point from which to measure the mouse location
mo.mouse.use_when: Mouse-position tracker with configurable origin. `0,0 point` settable per-instance; reset to default. Use to track mouse offset from an arbitrary origin (e.g. distance from a fixed UI point).

mo.nodes.use_when: Graphical node-based interpolator — interpolate data by drawing weighted nodes. Use for visual control of multi-parameter blends (similar to native nodes but with mo.* UI consistency).

mo.noteout.digest: Choose the output MIDI port from the pup-up menu.
mo.noteout.use_when: Single-voice MIDI note output to a chosen port. Use as the standard MIDI note output in mo.* patches.

mo.noteouts.digest: Send a list of MIDI note messages to a specified port.
mo.noteouts.use_when: Multi-voice MIDI note output — accepts a list of notes and sends each. Use when sending chords or multi-voice MIDI from a single object.

mo.notepad.digest: Text is stored in a <dict> object.
mo.notepad.use_when: Text-storage UI; data stored in a `dict` object. `;toggle 1` + Return saves text. Use for in-patch text storage (notes, presets-as-text) without external file I/O.

mo.number.digest: Numbers can be int, float, or MIDI.
mo.number.use_when: Single-value number display — int, float, or MIDI mode. Use as the standard mo.* number-display widget.

mo.numbers.digest: Display and output a list of numbers.
mo.numbers.use_when: Multi-voice number display — auto-adapts to list length. Use for displaying parallel value streams without specifying voice count.

mo.pad.digest: Map this object to a MIDI controller.
mo.pad.use_when: Multi-voice pad UI — map to MIDI pads. Use for pad-controller-style trigger UIs.

mo.pads.digest: Set the mode for each pad (trigger or bang).
mo.pads.use_when: Multi-pad with per-pad mode (trigger or bang). Use when different pads in a grid should fire different message types.

mo.pipe.digest: Delay time will be restored to 0 once output is done.
mo.pipe.use_when: Delay with auto-reset of delay time after each output (returns to 0). Use for one-shot delayed events where the delay should not persist on subsequent inputs.

mo.playlist~.digest: Playback, loop and select section of sound files.
mo.playlist~.use_when: Soundfile playback with looping and section selection. Play/stop by index (0 stops). Use as a mo.* playlist~ wrapper with consistent UI.

mo.poll.digest: Output a list of data at a specific rate (in ms).
mo.poll.use_when: List-data resampler — output at a specific rate (ms). Useful for resampling an incoming list stream. Use to throttle a rapid value stream to a fixed rate (vs native speedlim's max-rate behaviour).

mo.prepend.digest: A "target" message followed by the voice number and message can be used.
mo.prepend.use_when: List prepend with multi-voice routing. `target <voice>` followed by message addresses one voice. Use for voice-addressed message construction.

mo.preset.digest: The module is connected to a pattrstorage and preset object.
mo.preset.use_when: Preset UI connected to pattrstorage and preset object. Use as the mo.* drop-in for a uniform preset-management UI.

mo.rand.digest: set step size (size of random steps)
mo.rand.use_when: Random walker with `step size` configurable. Use for bounded random walks (drunk-style) with explicit step control.

mo.receive.digest: Grab from a send or forward object sharing the same device name.
mo.receive.use_when: Cordless receive — paired with mo.send sharing the same device name. Use for clean inter-patcher connections without cluttering with patchcords.

mo.receives.digest: Receive a list of message from specified receive objects without patching cords.
mo.receives.use_when: Multi-stream receive — list of named receives in one object. Type `value-1`, `value-2`, etc. to set names. Use to consolidate many cordless receives into one object.

mo.receive~.digest: Grab audio signals from an mc.send~ object sharing the same device name.
mo.receive~.use_when: Audio receive companion to mc.send~ sharing the same device name. Use for cordless multichannel audio routing.

mo.record.use_when: Data recorder/playback with looping. Use for recording control streams to replay later — e.g. capture a gesture, replay it as automation.

mo.record~.use_when: Multichannel audio recorder. Specify length in seconds upfront; recording is cropped if shorter. Use for fixed-length multichannel capture without manual buffer~ management.

mo.rms~.use_when: Multichannel RMS computation. Use for level analysis on multichannel signals (DSP must restart on channel-count changes).

mo.route.digest: A "target" message followed by the voice number and message can be used.
mo.route.use_when: Multi-voice route. `target <voice>` addresses one voice. Use for voice-aware message routing.

mo.rsliders.digest: Set a minimum and a maximum range for each rslider (a list of two numbers).
mo.rsliders.use_when: Multi-voice range sliders — each slider is a (min, max) pair. Use to set per-voice ranges in a single multi-slider UI.

mo.scale.digest: Values can be changed globally, or individually for each voice.
mo.scale.use_when: Multi-voice scale (range remap). Values can be set globally or per-voice. Use as the multi-voice equivalent of native scale.

mo.schmitt.digest: Threshold can be set globally, or individually for each voice.
mo.schmitt.use_when: Schmitt trigger (hysteresis) — threshold settable globally or per-voice. Use for de-bounced threshold detection where you need different on/off thresholds.

mo.scope.digest: Output data can either be unipolar (0. - 1.) or bipolar (-1. - 1.).
mo.scope.use_when: Data oscilloscope — display data over time. Output unipolar (0–1) or bipolar (-1 to 1). Use for visualising control streams the same way scope~ visualises audio.

mo.scope~.digest: Display multichannel signals level through an oscilloscope.
mo.scope~.use_when: Multichannel signal oscilloscope. Auto-adapts to signal count. Use for multichannel audio visualisation in mo.* patches.

mo.select.digest: It matches floating points using "fuzzy" mode.
mo.select.use_when: Select with fuzzy float matching — matches floats within a tolerance rather than requiring exact equality. Use when native select fails on float comparisons due to precision.

mo.send.digest: Send to a receive object sharing the same device name.
mo.send.use_when: Cordless send — paired with mo.receive on the same device name. Use as the send half of mo.* cordless connections.

mo.sends.digest: The upper message box, if set, will target receive objects sharing the same name.
mo.sends.use_when: Multi-stream send — list of named sends; the upper message box can target receives sharing the name. Use as the multi-target counterpart of mo.send.

mo.send~.digest: Send multichannel audio signals without patch cords.
mo.send~.use_when: Multichannel audio send to mc.receive~ sharing the device name. Note: DSP restarts on channel-count changes. Use for cordless multichannel audio routing.

mo.serial.digest: Provides input and output through serial communication (Arduino, Teensy, etc.)
mo.serial.use_when: Serial communication for Arduino, Teensy, etc. Configurable blink/poll metro. Use as the mo.* wrapper around serial with uniform UI.

mo.shake.digest: Adjust mode (normal, absolute) and sensitivity to input data.
mo.shake.use_when: Motion-amount detector for one control stream (for example an accelerometer axis): measures how fast the value changes, smooths it with separate `up` and `down` amounts, and outputs 0–1. Messages: `sensitivity`, `up`, `down`, `mute`. Use to turn shaking or waving a sensor into an intensity value.

mo.sig~.digest: If the number of channels change, the DSP must be restarted.
mo.sig~.use_when: Multi-channel sig~ wrapper. DSP must restart on channel-count changes. Use as the mo.* signal source.

mo.slide.digest: Set up and down slide motion, and poll data if necessary.
mo.slide.use_when: Smooths each value of a list with separate slide-up and slide-down amounts, polling at a set rate in ms (the patch runs the list through jit.slide in a matrix, driven by qmetro). Use to smooth parallel sensor or controller channels where rising and falling should respond differently.

mo.sliders.digest: Output data can either be unipolar (0. - 1.) or bipolar (-1. - 1.).
mo.sliders.use_when: Multi-voice slider array. Output unipolar (0–1) or bipolar (-1 to 1). Use as the standard multi-slider UI in mo.* patches.

mo.smooth.digest: Smooth a list of values through a leaky integrator.
mo.smooth.use_when: Multi-voice leaky-integrator smoother. Up/down ramp in ms, optional polling, auto-adapts to voice count. Use for smoothing parallel parameter streams.

mo.snapshot~.digest: If the number of channels change, the DSP must be restarted.
mo.snapshot~.use_when: Multichannel snapshot~ with channel-count-restart caveat. Use as the mo.* snapshot abstraction.

mo.spectroscope~.digest: Display multichannel signals level through an spectroscope or sonogram.
mo.spectroscope~.use_when: Multichannel spectroscope/sonogram display. Use for multichannel spectral monitoring in mo.* patches.

mo.speedlim.digest: Limit the speed of a list of values throughput.
mo.speedlim.use_when: Throughput-limit on a list of values. Use as the multi-voice speedlim — limits update rate per-voice.

mo.split.digest: Output numbers within, below and above range.
mo.split.use_when: Split a number into within-range, below-range, and above-range outputs. Use as a 3-way split for value-band analysis.

mo.steer.digest: If both signals are equal to 0, the output will be 0.5.
mo.steer.use_when: Direction-biased two-input combiner. If both signals = 0, output = 0.5 (centred). Use for joystick-style steering math (combine two control axes into a normalised position).

mo.step.digest: Set steps composed of pitch, velocity, and duration (plus two additional steps).
mo.step.use_when: Step sequencer with per-step pitch, velocity, duration, plus two extra parameters. Use as a generative step-sequencer block.

mo.swatch.use_when: Colour-picker UI — control by hue/saturation/lightness. Send list (1st inlet) or message (2nd). Use for colour-control in jit.gl / video output patches.

mo.tabs.digest: Set the number of tabs and each item's name.
mo.tabs.use_when: Tab-bar UI — set tab count and per-item names. Use as a horizontal tab control with named tabs.

mo.theremin~.use_when: Theremin synth abstraction. Drive with normalised list or messages. Parameters: pitch, volume, timbre. Use as a self-contained theremin voice.

mo.transport.digest: Keep track of the Global Transport.
mo.transport.use_when: Global Transport tracker. Use to expose Max's global transport state to in-patch logic.

mo.udpreceive.use_when: Network UDP receive. Use as the mo.* wrapper around udpreceive with consistent UI.

mo.udpsend.use_when: Network UDP send. Default host=localhost, port=7400. Use as the mo.* wrapper around udpsend.

mo.vector.digest: Combine a list of control signals into speherical coordinates (vector sum).
mo.vector.use_when: Combine a list of control values into spherical / vector-sum coordinates. Outputs combined xy axes plus per-node values. Use for vector-summing N inputs into a single 2D position (e.g. multi-fader → trajectory point).

mo.vrslider.use_when: Vertical range slider (low-high pair). Range default (0., 1.). Use as the vertical complement to mo.hrslider.

mo.vslider.digest: Map this object to a MIDI controller.
mo.vslider.use_when: Vertical slider — map to MIDI controller. Use as the standard vertical slider in mo.* patches.

mo.vtab.digest: Set the number of tabs and each item's name.
mo.vtab.use_when: Vertical tab UI with named items. Use for vertical tabs alongside mo.htab's horizontal layout.

mo.xbendout.digest: Send continuous control change values to a MIDI device.

rytm.digest: Enables communication with Elektron Analog Rytm MKII which is
rytm.use_when: Read and edit an Elektron Analog Rytm MKII (OS 1.70) over SysEx. Connect sysexin to the inlet and the left outlet (serialized SysEx) to midiout; @sysex_id sets the device ID. query <object> [index] loads patterns, kits and other objects from the device; send <object> [index] writes them back; get and set read and change values; load and save use project files; copy duplicates patterns or kits; reset restores defaults. Outlet 2: query responses; outlet 3: status 0 success, 1 error, 2 warning. Not for CC or NRPN control.

mcs.spectrogram.player~.use_when: spectrogram.player~ with its channel outlets replaced by one multichannel (MC) outlet, for feeding mc.* chains. Everything else is identical: same Link outlet to spectrogram~, messages (`play`, `stop`, int, `position <ms>`, `set`), loop inlets, attributes and help patch (the object file is spectrogram.player~, mapped by init/spectrogram-objectmappings.txt). The second argument, or `@chans`, fixes the MC channel count (0-1024); the default 0 follows the referenced buffer~'s channel count. The count is read when the DSP chain compiles, so a change takes effect only after audio is turned off and on; with no buffer bound at compile time the outlet carries one silent channel.

spectrogram.colorbar.digest: Colorbar displaying magnitude-to-color mappings used in a connected
spectrogram.colorbar.use_when: Colour legend showing how magnitudes map to colours in a spectrogram~. Attach it with a patch cord from its outlet to any spectrogram~ inlet (cords may pass through subpatcher and bpatcher inlets/outlets, not send/receive); it follows rewiring automatically. `textsize`, `textjustification`, `textcolor` style the labels; `write` saves it as a PNG.

spectrogram.player~.use_when: Play, loop and spectrally filter the buffer~ shown in a spectrogram~. Link it by wiring the rightmost (Link) outlet to any spectrogram~ inlet; the cord may pass through subpatcher/bpatcher inlets and outlets but not send/receive or poly~. While linked, the buffer name follows the spectrogram~'s @buffer_name, the loop region follows the selection rectangle (or the drawn shapes' time span), a draggable playhead and loop markers appear on the display, and `@filter 1` passes only audio inside the selection and shapes (outside them with the spectrogram~'s @edit_inverted), silent when the playhead is outside every region. Args: `[buffer-name] [channel-count]` (groove~ order; 1-64 signal outlets, default 1). Left inlet: `play`, `stop`, int nonzero/0 (1 resumes, does not restart), `position <ms>`, `set <buffer>` (ignored while linked), or a signal that replaces @speed. Inlets 2 and 3 set `@loop_start` / `@loop_end` in ms (negative end = buffer end). Attributes: `@speed` (signed, unclamped, groove~ semantics, no anti-aliasing), `@gain` dB (-40..20), `@loop` 0 off / 1 on / 2 pendulum, `@filter_fft_size` 32-8192 (power of 2, default 2048; the filter delays output by this many samples). Outlets: channel signals, a 0-1 loop sync ramp (drive wave~ or edge~ for loop-start bangs, as in the help), Link. Unlinked it is a plain buffer~ player and @filter is inert, so use groove~ unless you want the spectrogram~ link.

spectrogram~.use_when: Buffer~-based spectrogram viewer and editor with mouse zoom, pan, selection and drawing. Name the buffer~ with `@buffer_name` (and `@buffer_chan`). Analysis: `@win_size`, `@win_overlap`, `@win_zero_pad`, `@win_type`, `@mag_scale`, `@freq_reassign`, `@mag_min` / `@mag_max`, `@color_scheme`. Navigation messages: `zoom_in`, `zoom_out`, `view_all`, `view_selected`, `select_all`, `select_none` (plus `_time` / `_freq` variants). Destructive spectral edits on the buffer~: `edit_selection_delete`, `edit_selection_isolate`, `edit_selection_gain`, `edit_selection_pitch_shift`, `edit_selection_freq_shift`, the same for drawn shapes (`edit_shapes_…`), with `undo`, `redo`, `clear_history`; `render` writes the selection to another buffer~. Inlets/outlets 0-7 set and report display and selection ranges (ms, Hz); outlet 9 reports time, frequency and magnitude under the mouse. Link spectrogram.player~ for playback and spectrogram.colorbar for a legend. `write` saves a PNG.
